options.B: To split a single prefix into many smaller, more-specific prefixes automatically, the opposite of what BGP route aggregation actually accomplishes into the routing table
options.C: To combine multiple more-specific prefixes into a single summarized prefix advertised to neighbors, reducing the size of the routing table advertised externally
options.D: To disable the advertisement of any routes at all, effectively creating a full BGP route filter

questions.explanation_es: La agregación de rutas en BGP (comando 'aggregate-address') combina múltiples prefijos más específicos en un único prefijo resumido que se anuncia a los vecinos, reduciendo el tamaño de la tabla de rutas anunciada externamente y simplificando la topología vista por otros AS.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: In a Policy-Based Routing (PBR) route-map, which of the following is a typical 'match' criterion used to identify traffic for special routing treatment?

options.A: PBR route-maps only support matching on VLAN ID, with no ability to match Layer 3 or Layer 4 criteria
options.B: An access-list matching specific source addresses, or the packet length, among other criteria defined in the route-map
options.C: PBR route-maps can only match on destination IP address, exactly like normal routing, offering no additional flexibility
options.D: PBR cannot use access-lists as match criteria within a route-map

questions.explanation_es: En un route-map de PBR, un criterio de 'match' típico es una access-list que identifica el tráfico según su dirección de origen (u otros campos permitidos por la ACL), o también se puede hacer match por longitud de paquete, entre otros criterios; luego se define un 'set' para indicar el tratamiento especial (por ejemplo, el next-hop a usar) para ese tráfico coincidente.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: Why is NTP authentication (e.g., using MD5 or SHA keys) recommended in a production network?

options.A: It encrypts all network traffic passing through the router, not just NTP, providing full payload confidentiality for every protocol traversing the device, including HTTP and SSH
options.B: It prevents a malicious or unauthorized source from injecting false time information, which could otherwise disrupt logging correlation, certificate validation, or other time-sensitive processes
options.C: It is required for NTP to function at all, even in a lab environment with no external time source configured
options.D: It encrypts the NTP time value itself so that an eavesdropper cannot read the synchronized time, but it does not protect the router against a spoofed source injecting a false time update

questions.explanation_es: La autenticación NTP (usando claves MD5/SHA) previene que una fuente maliciosa o no autorizada inyecte información de tiempo falsa, lo cual podría afectar procesos sensibles al tiempo como la correlación de logs, validación de certificados digitales, o el registro correcto de eventos de seguridad.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What is the role of the 'grandmaster clock' in a PTP (Precision Time Protocol) domain?

options.A: It refers to any client device receiving time from the network, regardless of its position in the PTP hierarchy or its distance from the grandmaster
options.B: It is a backup clock that only activates if all other clocks fail, remaining completely passive otherwise
options.C: It performs no synchronization function in PTP, serving only as a passive monitoring device on the network
options.D: It is the primary time reference source for the entire PTP domain, from which all other clocks in the hierarchy synchronize (directly or indirectly)

questions.explanation_es: El grandmaster clock es la fuente de referencia de tiempo principal para todo el dominio PTP; todos los demás relojes en la jerarquía (boundary clocks, ordinary clocks) sincronizan su tiempo directa o indirectamente a partir de este reloj maestro, seleccionado mediante el Best Master Clock Algorithm (BMCA).

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: What is the difference between Static NAT and Dynamic NAT?

options.A: They are functionally identical, differing only in configuration syntax
options.B: Static NAT can only be used with IPv6, and Dynamic NAT only with IPv4
options.C: Static NAT selects an address from a pool on a first-come, first-served basis, while Dynamic NAT always maps a host to one fixed address configured in advance, meaning Dynamic NAT actually behaves more predictably in address assignment
options.D: Static NAT creates a fixed, permanent one-to-one mapping between a specific inside local and inside global address; Dynamic NAT maps addresses from a pool on a first-come, first-served basis, without a fixed permanent mapping

questions.explanation_es: Static NAT crea un mapeo fijo y permanente uno-a-uno entre una dirección local interna específica y una dirección global externa específica (útil por ejemplo para servidores que deben ser siempre alcanzables en la misma IP pública). Dynamic NAT, en cambio, asigna direcciones de un pool de forma dinámica, por orden de llegada, sin una asignación fija permanente.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: In Cisco NAT terminology, what does 'inside local' refer to, as opposed to 'inside global'?

options.A: 'Inside local' and 'inside global' both refer to addresses on the external network, differing only in whether the address belongs to a remote host or to the NAT device's own outside interface
options.B: 'Inside global' refers to an external host's address, not an internal host's translated address, a distinction that only applies under PAT and not under static or dynamic NAT configurations on the router, with static and dynamic NAT instead using the term interchangeably
options.C: These terms only apply to IPv6 NAT, not IPv4
options.D: 'Inside local' is the address of an internal host as seen within the internal (private) network; 'inside global' is the translated address that represents that same internal host as seen from the external (public) network

questions.explanation_es: 'Inside local' es la dirección de un host interno tal como se ve dentro de la red privada (típicamente una IP privada RFC 1918); 'inside global' es la dirección traducida que representa a ese mismo host interno visto desde la red externa/pública, después de aplicar NAT.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: What is the standard virtual MAC address format used by HSRP (version 1) for a given group?

options.A: The real burned-in MAC address of the active router's physical interface, with no virtual MAC
options.B: FFFF.FFFF.FFFF, the standard broadcast MAC
options.C: A completely random MAC address generated at each failover
options.D: 0000.0C07.ACxx, where 'xx' represents the HSRP group number in hexadecimal

questions.explanation_es: HSRP versión 1 utiliza una dirección MAC virtual con el formato estándar 0000.0C07.ACxx, donde 'xx' representa el número de grupo HSRP en hexadecimal, permitiendo que los hosts sigan usando la misma MAC virtual sin importar cuál router físico esté actualmente activo.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Regarding default preemption behavior, how do HSRP and VRRP differ?

options.A: In HSRP, preemption is enabled by default and takes effect immediately once a higher-priority router comes online; in VRRP, preemption must be explicitly enabled, since it is disabled by default
options.B: In VRRP, preemption is enabled by default; in HSRP, preemption is disabled by default and must be explicitly configured
options.C: Both protocols disable preemption by default with no differences between their default configurations at all
options.D: Neither protocol supports preemption at all, requiring a completely manual failover process every time

questions.explanation_es: Una diferencia clave a tener presente: en VRRP la preferencia (preemption) está habilitada por defecto, mientras que en HSRP está deshabilitada por defecto y debe configurarse explícitamente si se desea que un router de mayor prioridad reclame el rol activo al recuperarse.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol)?

options.A: It allows hosts to inform their local multicast router about which multicast groups they want to receive traffic for, enabling the router to determine where to forward multicast traffic on the local segment
options.B: It only operates between routers, never between a host and its local router, making it purely a router-to-router protocol used for multicast tree maintenance across an entire routed enterprise domain and its RP
options.C: It replaces the need for PIM entirely across a routed network
options.D: It is used to encrypt multicast traffic between the source and every receiver in the group

questions.explanation_es: IGMP es el protocolo que permite a los hosts informar a su router multicast local a qué grupos multicast desean unirse (join), permitiendo que el router determine si debe reenviar tráfico multicast hacia ese segmento local. PIM, en cambio, se encarga del enrutamiento de multicast entre routers a través de la red.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of MSDP (Multicast Source Discovery Protocol)?

options.A: It replaces PIM entirely as the multicast routing protocol, eliminating the need for any RP configuration
options.B: It is used only within a single PIM-SM domain, never between domains, making it purely an intra-domain protocol with no role across separate autonomous multicast networks
options.C: It is used for IGMP snooping on Layer 2 switches, with no role in Layer 3 multicast routing at all
options.D: It allows Rendezvous Points (RPs) in different PIM-SM domains to share information about active multicast sources, enabling inter-domain multicast source discovery

questions.explanation_es: MSDP permite que los Rendezvous Points (RP) de distintos dominios PIM-SM compartan información sobre fuentes multicast activas, habilitando el descubrimiento de fuentes multicast entre dominios independientes (inter-domain), algo que PIM-SM por sí solo no resuelve dentro de un único dominio.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: How does traceroute determine the sequence of hops (routers) along a path to a destination?

options.A: It sends probe packets with progressively increasing TTL values; each router that decrements the TTL to zero returns an ICMP 'Time Exceeded' message, revealing each hop along the path
options.B: It requires manual configuration of every hop in advance
options.C: It relies on SNMP queries to each router along the path, requiring SNMP to be pre-configured and reachable across the entire routed topology in advance across the entire routed topology in advance
options.D: It uses a single packet with a fixed TTL of 255 for the entire path

questions.explanation_es: Traceroute envía paquetes de prueba con valores de TTL incrementales (empezando en 1); cada router que decrementa el TTL a cero descarta el paquete y responde con un mensaje ICMP 'Time Exceeded', revelando así, salto por salto, la ruta hacia el destino a medida que se incrementa el TTL en cada iteración.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: What underlying mechanism does the 'ping' utility use to test basic reachability to a destination?

options.A: DNS queries
options.B: TCP three-way handshake
options.C: ICMP Echo Request and Echo Reply messages
options.D: SNMP GET requests

questions.explanation_es: Ping utiliza mensajes ICMP Echo Request (enviados al destino) y Echo Reply (respondidos por el destino) para probar la conectividad básica y medir el tiempo de ida y vuelta (RTT), sin necesidad de establecer una sesión TCP.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: How does NetFlow fundamentally differ from SPAN in terms of what data is collected?

options.A: NetFlow collects summarized flow metadata/statistics (such as source/destination, byte and packet counts) rather than full packet copies; SPAN mirrors complete copies of the actual packets to an analysis destination
options.B: SPAN only provides summarized statistics, never full packets, which is the exact reverse of how SPAN actually mirrors complete packets to its destination port for analysis by an external tool for later offline analysis by an external tool
options.C: They are functionally identical mechanisms
options.D: NetFlow copies every full packet, exactly like SPAN

questions.explanation_es: NetFlow recopila metadatos y estadísticas resumidas de los flujos de tráfico (direcciones origen/destino, conteos de bytes/paquetes, etc.) sin capturar el contenido completo de cada paquete; SPAN, en cambio, refleja copias completas de los paquetes reales hacia un destino de análisis, siendo mucho más pesado en términos de ancho de banda pero ofreciendo visibilidad total del contenido.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What is a key limitation of local SPAN compared to RSPAN or ERSPAN?

options.A: Local SPAN has no limitations compared to RSPAN or ERSPAN
options.B: Local SPAN can only mirror traffic to a destination port on the same physical switch where the source traffic is located
options.C: Local SPAN can mirror traffic to any destination across a routed WAN without any limitation, exactly the same way ERSPAN does
options.D: Local SPAN requires GRE encapsulation, just like ERSPAN

questions.explanation_es: Una limitación clave de SPAN local es que solo puede reflejar tráfico hacia un puerto destino ubicado en el mismo switch físico donde está el tráfico origen; para monitorear tráfico y enviarlo a un destino en otro switch (dentro del mismo dominio L2) se necesita RSPAN, y para atravesar una red enrutada se necesita ERSPAN.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What constraint does RSPAN traffic have regarding how it can be transported across the network?

options.A: RSPAN traffic is carried over a dedicated RSPAN VLAN that must remain within a single Layer 2 (bridged) domain — it cannot be routed across a Layer 3 boundary, which is where ERSPAN would be needed instead
options.B: RSPAN traffic is automatically encrypted with IPsec
options.C: RSPAN requires no dedicated VLAN and can use any regular data VLAN interchangeably
options.D: RSPAN traffic can be routed across any number of Layer 3 hops with no special encapsulation, exactly like a normal unicast IP packet would be forwarded across any WAN link across any WAN link without any special handling at all

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico de RSPAN se transporta sobre una VLAN dedicada de RSPAN que debe permanecer dentro de un único dominio de Capa 2 (puenteado); no puede ser enrutado a través de un límite de Capa 3. Cuando se necesita llevar tráfico espejado a través de una red enrutada, se debe usar ERSPAN, que lo encapsula en GRE.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: What is the purpose of an IP SLA 'responder' configured on the target device of a probe?

options.A: It is required only for ICMP-based operations, never for UDP-based ones
options.B: It converts the target device into an IP SLA source itself, allowing it to originate its own independent probes toward other devices on the network without any additional configuration
options.C: It improves measurement accuracy (especially for jitter and latency) by timestamping the probe packets on the target device itself, rather than relying solely on round-trip estimates from the source
options.D: It blocks all IP SLA probes from reaching that device

questions.explanation_es: El IP SLA Responder, configurado en el dispositivo destino de la prueba, mejora la precisión de la medición (especialmente para jitter y latencia) al marcar con timestamp los paquetes de prueba en el propio dispositivo destino, en lugar de depender únicamente de estimaciones basadas en el tiempo de ida y vuelta medido solo desde el origen.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: Which IP SLA operation type is commonly used to measure jitter, useful for validating voice/video quality over a path?

options.A: FTP operation
options.B: UDP jitter operation
options.C: DNS lookup operation
options.D: HTTP GET operation

questions.explanation_es: La operación de tipo UDP jitter de IP SLA está diseñada específicamente para medir jitter (variación en el retardo), latencia y pérdida de paquetes de forma similar al tráfico de voz/video real, siendo comúnmente usada para validar la calidad esperada de esos servicios sobre una ruta determinada antes o durante su despliegue.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: How does Catalyst Center's Assurance capability typically obtain near-real-time visibility into network and client health, as opposed to relying solely on periodic polling?

options.A: By disabling all monitoring capabilities on the managed devices
options.B: By requiring the administrator to manually run 'show' commands on every device and paste the output into a spreadsheet for later analysis into a spreadsheet for later manual analysis
options.C: By leveraging telemetry streaming from network devices and clients, in addition to traditional data collection methods, to provide more timely insight than polling alone
options.D: By relying on SNMP polling every 24 hours

questions.explanation_es: Catalyst Center Assurance aprovecha el streaming de telemetría desde los dispositivos de red y clientes (además de métodos de recolección más tradicionales), lo que permite una visibilidad mucho más cercana al tiempo real sobre la salud de la red y de los clientes, comparado con depender únicamente de polling periódico tradicional.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: What does Cisco Catalyst Center's Plug and Play (PnP) capability enable?

options.A: It disables all automatic configuration, requiring fully manual setup for every new device added to the network, one device at a time by an on-site engineer by an on-site engineer every time
options.B: It replaces the need for any IP addressing on new devices
options.C: It is used only for wireless access points, never for switches or routers
options.D: Zero-touch or near-zero-touch onboarding of new network devices, which automatically contact Catalyst Center upon first boot to receive their configuration and software image

questions.explanation_es: Plug and Play (PnP) permite el onboarding de nuevos dispositivos de red con mínima o nula intervención manual: los dispositivos nuevos, al arrancar por primera vez, contactan automáticamente a Catalyst Center para recibir su configuración inicial e imagen de software correspondiente, simplificando el despliegue a gran escala.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Over which transport and default port does NETCONF typically operate?

options.A: UDP on port 161, the same as SNMP
options.B: Plain unencrypted Telnet on port 23
options.C: SSH, using the dedicated 'netconf' SSH subsystem, typically on TCP port 830
options.D: HTTP on port 80, exactly like RESTCONF uses by default in most deployments, though RESTCONF typically runs over HTTPS on port 443

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF típicamente opera sobre SSH, utilizando un subsistema SSH dedicado llamado 'netconf', normalmente en el puerto TCP 830, estableciendo una sesión persistente y segura para el intercambio de mensajes RPC en XML.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: Which of these correctly reflects an advantage of NETCONF's transaction-based approach using candidate/running datastores over RESTCONF's typical single-datastore model?

options.A: There is no meaningful difference between the two approaches
options.B: RESTCONF can optionally stage changes in a candidate datastore similar to NETCONF, but unlike NETCONF it provides no explicit validate operation to check those changes before the commit is applied
options.C: NETCONF has no concept of validating changes before applying them
options.D: NETCONF's candidate datastore allows a set of changes to be staged and validated before an explicit commit is applied to the running configuration, supporting more controlled, transactional configuration changes

questions.explanation_es: El uso del datastore 'candidate' en NETCONF permite preparar y validar un conjunto de cambios antes de aplicarlos formalmente (commit) a la configuración en ejecución (running), soportando un flujo de cambios más controlado y transaccional; RESTCONF, en cambio, opera típicamente de forma directa sobre un único datastore equivalente a running, sin ese paso intermedio de candidate/commit.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: What is the key security difference between the 'enable password' and 'enable secret' commands on a Cisco device?

options.A: Neither command has any impact on device security
options.B: 'enable secret' stores the password using a strong hash by default, while the older 'enable password' stores it in a much weaker, reversible/plaintext-like form; 'enable secret' should always be preferred
options.C: They are identical in security, differing only in command syntax
options.D: 'enable password' is always more secure than 'enable secret', since it uses a stronger and more modern hashing algorithm by default on every current Cisco IOS release regardless of platform or software version

questions.explanation_es: 'enable secret' almacena la contraseña usando un hash fuerte por defecto, mientras que el comando más antiguo 'enable password' la almacena de una forma mucho más débil (tipo 7, fácilmente reversible), por lo que 'enable secret' siempre debe preferirse; si ambos están configurados, 'enable secret' tiene prioridad.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: Why is SSH generally preferred over Telnet for remote device management access?

options.A: SSH and Telnet both support optional session encryption, but Telnet enables it by default while SSH requires the administrator to explicitly generate a crypto key before encryption actually takes effect
options.B: SSH cannot be used for CLI access, only for file transfer
options.C: Telnet encrypts sessions, and SSH does not
options.D: SSH encrypts the entire session (including credentials), while Telnet transmits data, including usernames and passwords, in plaintext, making it vulnerable to eavesdropping

questions.explanation_es: SSH cifra toda la sesión, incluyendo las credenciales de acceso, mientras que Telnet transmite todo en texto plano (incluyendo usuario y contraseña), haciéndolo vulnerable a ser interceptado (eavesdropping) por cualquiera con acceso a la ruta de red. Por eso SSH es el estándar recomendado para gestión remota.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which transport protocol and port does TACACS+ use by default, as opposed to RADIUS?

options.A: TACACS+ uses TCP port 49; RADIUS uses UDP ports 1812/1813 (authentication/accounting) — reflecting TACACS+'s reliance on TCP's connection-oriented delivery versus RADIUS's use of UDP
options.B: TACACS+ uses UDP port 49 for faster, connectionless delivery of authentication requests, while RADIUS uses TCP ports 1812 and 1813 to guarantee reliable delivery of accounting records
options.C: TACACS+ uses HTTP as its transport
options.D: Both protocols use TCP port 49 by default, differing only in how they separate authentication from authorization within that single session

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ utiliza TCP en el puerto 49, aprovechando la entrega orientada a conexión de TCP; RADIUS utiliza UDP, típicamente en los puertos 1812 (autenticación/autorización) y 1813 (accounting), reflejando un enfoque más liviano pero sin las garantías de entrega de TCP.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: What happens to a packet that does not match any explicit permit or deny statement in a Cisco ACL?

options.A: It is always permitted by default if no explicit match occurs, since Cisco ACLs assume permit rather than deny at the end
options.B: It is denied, due to the implicit 'deny any' at the end of every ACL, even though it is not visibly configured
options.C: The packet causes the router to reboot
options.D: The ACL is automatically disabled

questions.explanation_es: Toda ACL de Cisco tiene un 'deny any' implícito al final, aunque no aparezca explícitamente en la configuración; cualquier paquete que no coincida con ninguna sentencia permit/deny explícita configurada será denegado por este comportamiento implícito por defecto.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: What is a practical advantage of using named ACLs over numbered ACLs?

options.A: There is no functional difference between named and numbered ACLs
options.B: Named ACLs cannot be applied to any interface
options.C: Numbered ACLs support far more entries than named ACLs, which is their only advantage over the more descriptive naming scheme used by named access lists on modern platforms
options.D: Named ACLs allow individual entries to be added or removed (edited) more easily by line/sequence, and the name itself can be more descriptive of the ACL's purpose

questions.explanation_es: Las ACLs nombradas (named ACLs) permiten agregar o eliminar entradas individuales de forma más flexible (usando números de secuencia), sin tener que recrear toda la lista, además de que el nombre puede ser descriptivo del propósito de la ACL, facilitando su identificación y mantenimiento frente a una ACL puramente numerada.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is using HTTPS (TLS) essential for securing REST API communications, such as those with Cisco Catalyst Center?

options.A: HTTP and HTTPS provide identical security for API traffic
options.B: HTTPS eliminates the need for any authentication token
options.C: HTTPS encrypts the data in transit between the client and the API server, protecting credentials, tokens, and payload data from being intercepted or tampered with over the network
options.D: HTTPS is only relevant for browser-based access, not for API calls made by automated scripts or applications talking directly to a REST endpoint without any browser involved at all

questions.explanation_es: HTTPS (HTTP sobre TLS) cifra los datos en tránsito entre el cliente y el servidor de la API, protegiendo credenciales, tokens de autenticación y datos del payload de ser interceptados o manipulados por un atacante en la red, algo que HTTP plano no ofrece.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: What does the principle of 'least privilege' mean when applied to API access scopes/roles?

options.A: An API client or user should only be granted the minimum permissions/scopes necessary to perform its intended function, rather than broad or administrative access by default
options.B: Least privilege only applies to human users, never to API service accounts
options.C: It means API calls should always be rate-limited to one request per minute
options.D: Every API client should be granted full administrative access by default for convenience, since revoking access later is always simple and low-risk regardless of how the client authenticates

questions.explanation_es: El principio de menor privilegio (least privilege) establece que a un cliente de API o usuario se le deben otorgar solo los permisos/scopes mínimos necesarios para cumplir su función prevista, en lugar de otorgar acceso amplio o administrativo por defecto, reduciendo el impacto potencial si esas credenciales son comprometidas.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: In 802.1X port-based authentication, what are the three key roles involved?

options.A: Router, Switch, and Access Point, with no client-side role
options.B: Only two roles exist: Supplicant and Authenticator, with no separate Authentication Server required in any 802.1X deployment, regardless of vendor or RADIUS backend used, a claim contradicted by the 802.1X standard itself
options.C: Client, Server, and Firewall — with no other roles defined
options.D: Supplicant (the client device requesting access), Authenticator (the switch/AP enforcing the port state), and Authentication Server (e.g., RADIUS server, which validates credentials)

questions.explanation_es: 802.1X define tres roles clave: el Supplicant (el dispositivo cliente que solicita acceso a la red), el Authenticator (típicamente el switch o access point, que controla el estado del puerto según el resultado de la autenticación), y el Authentication Server (por ejemplo, un servidor RADIUS/ISE, que valida las credenciales del supplicant).

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What is the purpose of MAB (MAC Authentication Bypass) in a NAC deployment?

options.A: It completely replaces 802.1X for all devices, including those capable of doing 802.1X
options.B: It disables all authentication for devices matching a MAC address whitelist without any verification, bypassing every security check entirely regardless of the device's actual compliance posture
options.C: It allows devices that cannot perform 802.1X authentication (such as printers or IoT devices) to be authenticated based on their MAC address instead, as a fallback mechanism
options.D: It is used only for wireless guest networks, never for wired ports

questions.explanation_es: MAB (MAC Authentication Bypass) permite que dispositivos incapaces de realizar autenticación 802.1X (como impresoras, cámaras IP, o ciertos dispositivos IoT) sean autenticados basándose en su dirección MAC como mecanismo alternativo (fallback), en lugar de quedar completamente sin acceso o requerir excepciones manuales complejas.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What is the primary role of Cisco Firepower Management Center (FMC) in a Cisco NGFW deployment?

options.A: It provides centralized policy management, monitoring, and reporting for one or more Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) NGFW devices
options.B: It is used for wireless controller management
options.C: It only manages licensing, with no policy or monitoring capability for any connected Firepower device, despite FMC actually serving as the primary policy console for connected devices
options.D: It is a hardware appliance that replaces the FTD firewall itself

questions.explanation_es: FMC (Firepower Management Center) provee gestión centralizada de políticas, monitoreo y reportes para uno o varios dispositivos NGFW Firepower Threat Defense (FTD), permitiendo administrar de forma consistente múltiples firewalls desde una única consola en lugar de configurarlos individualmente.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What does Application Visibility and Control (AVC) provide within a Cisco NGFW or router?

options.A: AVC is used for physical cable diagnostics
options.B: AVC replaces the need for any firewall rules
options.C: Only the ability to see interface bandwidth utilization, with no application-level detail beyond simple byte and packet counters per interface across the entire managed network, since AVC's DPI engine identifies the application behind a flow
options.D: The ability to identify specific applications generating traffic (beyond just port/protocol) and apply granular policy (allow, block, QoS treatment) based on that application identity

questions.explanation_es: AVC (Application Visibility and Control) permite identificar qué aplicación específica está generando cierto tráfico (más allá de simplemente el puerto/protocolo usado, ya que muchas apps modernas comparten puertos como 443), y aplicar políticas granulares (permitir, bloquear, dar cierto tratamiento de QoS) basadas en esa identidad de aplicación.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: In Python, what keyword is used to define a reusable function?

options.A: function
options.B: func
options.C: lambda is the only way to define any function
options.D: def

questions.explanation_es: En Python, una función se define usando la palabra clave 'def', seguida del nombre de la función y sus parámetros entre paréntesis, por ejemplo: 'def mi_funcion(parametro):'. 'lambda' se usa para funciones anónimas de una sola expresión, pero no es la forma estándar de definir una función reutilizable con nombre.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which of these data types is NOT natively supported directly by the JSON specification?

options.A: Strings
options.B: Comments (JSON has no native syntax for comments within the document)
options.C: Boolean values (true/false), since JSON only natively supports strings and numbers as primitive data types
options.D: Numbers

questions.explanation_es: JSON no soporta comentarios de forma nativa dentro del documento; a diferencia de YAML u otros formatos, no existe una sintaxis estándar para agregar comentarios en un archivo JSON válido. Sí soporta strings, números, booleanos, null, objetos y arreglos.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: What is the key difference between an HTTP 401 Unauthorized and a 403 Forbidden response?

options.A: Both codes only apply to POST requests, never to GET requests
options.B: 403 indicates the credentials were invalid or expired, while 401 indicates the client authenticated successfully but lacks permission for the requested resource, so a script receiving a 401 should simply refresh its stored token
options.C: 401 indicates the request lacks valid authentication credentials (or they were rejected); 403 indicates the client is authenticated but does not have permission to access the requested resource
options.D: 401 and 403 mean exactly the same thing and are used interchangeably

questions.explanation_es: 401 Unauthorized indica que la solicitud carece de credenciales de autenticación válidas (o fueron rechazadas) — el cliente no está autenticado correctamente. 403 Forbidden indica que el cliente SÍ está autenticado, pero no tiene permiso para acceder al recurso solicitado — es un problema de autorización, no de autenticación.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: When interpreting a paginated JSON response from an API (such as Catalyst Center's Intent APIs), what is a typical purpose of metadata fields often included in the response envelope?

options.A: To encrypt the response body
options.B: To store the API's licensing key
options.C: To specify which programming language the client must use when parsing the JSON response body returned by the server for that endpoint, regardless of the client's own platform
options.D: To indicate details such as whether more results exist beyond the current page, so the client knows whether to make additional requests to retrieve the full dataset

questions.explanation_es: En respuestas paginadas, los metadatos incluidos (por ejemplo, indicadores de si hay más resultados disponibles) le indican al cliente si debe realizar solicitudes adicionales para obtener el conjunto de datos completo, en lugar de asumir que la primera página contiene todos los resultados.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: What is a common 'action' type used within an EEM applet once a defined event triggers it?

options.A: EEM applets can only reboot the device as their sole possible action, with no ability to run any other CLI command or generate any log message or configuration, because IOS rejects any 'action X cli command' line if entered
options.B: Actions such as 'action X cli command' (to execute a CLI command) or 'action X syslog' (to generate a syslog message), used to automate a remediation or notification step
options.C: EEM applets cannot perform any actions, only detect events
options.D: Actions in EEM are limited to sending SNMP traps only

questions.explanation_es: Una vez que un evento definido dispara un applet EEM, se pueden configurar distintas acciones, como 'action X cli command' (para ejecutar un comando de CLI de forma automática) o 'action X syslog' (para generar un mensaje de syslog), permitiendo automatizar pasos de remediación, notificación, o recolección de datos de diagnóstico sin intervención manual.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Why do agentless automation tools (like Ansible) tend to be particularly well-suited for managing network devices (routers, switches) compared to agent-based tools?

options.A: Most network devices do not support running third-party software agents, so agentless tools that connect via standard protocols (SSH, NETCONF, RESTCONF) fit naturally without requiring vendor support for an installed agent
options.B: There is no practical difference between agent-based and agentless approaches for network devices, since both require exactly the same amount of vendor support and installed software on every single managed device in the network
options.C: Agent-based tools are always faster and simpler to use on network devices than agentless tools
options.D: Network devices always have full support for running any third-party agent software natively

questions.explanation_es: La mayoría de los dispositivos de red (routers, switches) no soportan la instalación de agentes de software de terceros como sí lo hacen los servidores; por eso las herramientas agentless (como Ansible), que se conectan usando protocolos estándar (SSH, NETCONF, RESTCONF) sin requerir un agente instalado, encajan naturalmente mejor para la automatización de infraestructura de red.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What does it mean for the HTTP PUT method to be 'idempotent', and how does this compare to POST?

options.A: Idempotency in HTTP refers only to whether a method's response can be cached by an intermediary proxy, which is why GET and PUT are both considered idempotent while a POST response is never eligible for caching
options.B: PUT is never idempotent, while POST always is
options.C: Sending the same PUT request multiple times results in the same final state (the resource is simply replaced with the same content each time); POST is generally NOT idempotent, since repeating it may create multiple new resources
options.D: Both PUT and POST are always non-idempotent by definition

questions.explanation_es: Que PUT sea idempotente significa que enviar la misma solicitud PUT múltiples veces produce el mismo estado final (el recurso queda reemplazado con el mismo contenido cada vez, sin efectos adicionales acumulativos). POST generalmente NO es idempotente, ya que repetir la misma solicitud POST puede crear múltiples recursos nuevos (por ejemplo, múltiples entradas duplicadas) en lugar de producir el mismo resultado.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: Which statement best describes how Policy-Based Routing (PBR) makes forwarding decisions compared to standard destination-based routing?

options.A: PBR only functions on Layer 2 switches, having no applicability to Layer 3 routers at all
options.B: PBR can forward packets based on criteria such as source address, packet size, or protocol, overriding the routing table before the normal lookup occurs
options.C: PBR only considers the destination IP address, exactly like the routing table, offering no additional classification criteria based on source or packet attributes
options.D: PBR requires BGP to be configured on the router before any route-map can be applied to an interface

questions.explanation_es: PBR usa route-maps para clasificar el tráfico por múltiples criterios (IP origen, tamaño de paquete, protocolo, etc.) y aplicar un next-hop distinto al que indicaría la tabla de enrutamiento normal. Se evalúa antes de la búsqueda estándar en la RIB.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: In a PBR route-map, what is the difference between the 'set ip next-hop' and 'set ip default next-hop' commands?

options.A: They are functionally identical, differing only in the order the keywords appear in the command
options.B: 'set ip default next-hop' overrides BGP routes only, having no effect on static, connected, or any other type of route present in the routing table at the time the route-map is evaluated
options.C: 'set ip next-hop' only works with static routes, and has no effect when used with any dynamic routing protocol
options.D: 'set ip next-hop' forwards to the specified address unconditionally when the route-map matches, while 'set ip default next-hop' is used only as a fallback when the routing table has no explicit route for the destination

questions.explanation_es: 'set ip next-hop' fuerza el next-hop indicado sin importar la tabla de enrutamiento. 'set ip default next-hop' solo se usa como respaldo, cuando el router no tiene una ruta explícita hacia el destino más allá de la default.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: On which interface direction is Policy-Based Routing typically applied with the 'ip policy route-map' command?

options.A: Only on loopback interfaces, since those are the only interfaces PBR is designed to support
options.B: Outbound, after the routing table lookup has already determined the next hop
options.C: It applies globally to the router regardless of interface, affecting every packet the router processes
options.D: Inbound, before the normal routing table lookup is performed

questions.explanation_es: PBR se aplica con 'ip policy route-map' en el sentido entrante de la interfaz; el router evalúa el route-map sobre el tráfico que ingresa, antes de hacer la búsqueda normal en la tabla de enrutamiento.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: A company wants traffic from the Finance subnet (10.10.10.0/24) to always exit via ISP-A, while all other traffic uses the normal default route via ISP-B, regardless of destination. Which technology best achieves this without changing destination-based routing for other traffic?

options.A: OSPF route redistribution between ISP-A's and ISP-B's separate routing domains
options.B: VRRP configured to load-balance traffic between ISP-A and ISP-B based on router priority
options.C: A static default route pointing all traffic toward ISP-A regardless of source subnet
options.D: Policy-Based Routing matching source address 10.10.10.0/24

questions.explanation_es: PBR permite clasificar el tráfico según el origen (entre otros criterios) y forzar un next-hop distinto solo para ese tráfico, dejando el resto sujeto al enrutamiento normal — algo que una ruta estática o un protocolo de enrutamiento por destino no logran por sí solos.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: What distinguishes PAT (Port Address Translation) from standard dynamic NAT?

options.A: PAT translates only the destination address, never the source, which is the opposite of how PAT actually operates on a Cisco router configured for NAT overload
options.B: PAT allows multiple internal hosts to share a single public IP address by also translating the Layer 4 port number
options.C: PAT requires a one-to-one mapping between inside and outside addresses, exactly like static NAT does
options.D: PAT only works with UDP traffic, having no support for TCP-based sessions at all

questions.explanation_es: PAT (NAT overload) traduce dirección IP y puerto, permitiendo que muchos hosts internos compartan una sola IP pública, distinguiéndose entre sí por el número de puerto de origen traducido.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: Why must both an 'ip nat inside' and an 'ip nat outside' interface be configured on a router for NAT to actually take effect?

options.A: These commands configure DNS resolution for NAT and have nothing to do with interface direction
options.B: Only 'ip nat inside' needs to be configured, on the private-facing interface; the router then automatically infers which remaining interface is 'outside' based on its current default route
options.C: These commands tell the router which interfaces face the private ('inside') network and which face the public ('outside') network, which NAT needs to know to determine the direction of translation
options.D: NAT works identically with no interface designation at all; these commands are optional legacy syntax with no real effect, superseded in this mistaken view by automatic direction detection based on which interface first receives a DHCP lease

questions.explanation_es: Estos comandos le indican al router qué interfaces dan hacia la red privada ('inside') y cuáles hacia la red pública ('outside'), lo cual NAT necesita saber para determinar la dirección de la traducción.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: Which statement about static NAT is correct?

options.A: It always requires PAT to function, since static NAT cannot operate independently on a Cisco router
options.B: It creates a temporary one-to-one mapping only when traffic is initiated from the inside, expiring once the session ends
options.C: It creates a permanent one-to-one mapping between an inside local and an inside global address, allowing outside hosts to initiate connections to the inside host
options.D: It cannot be used for servers that must be reachable from the internet, since it never allows externally-initiated connections regardless of firewall configuration

questions.explanation_es: El NAT estático crea un mapeo fijo 1:1 entre una IP interna y una IP pública, permitiendo que hosts externos inicien conexiones hacia el host interno (por ejemplo, un servidor web) — a diferencia del NAT dinámico o PAT, que dependen de que la conexión se inicie desde adentro.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: In HSRP, which router becomes the Active router by default?

options.A: The router with the highest HSRP priority (default 100); if tied, the highest IP address on the HSRP interface breaks the tie
options.B: Whichever router boots up last, regardless of its configured priority or interface IP address
options.C: The router with the lowest priority value, since HSRP always favors the most conservative router configuration in the group in the group
options.D: The router with the lowest IP address, used only as a tiebreaker when priorities are equal

questions.explanation_es: En HSRP, el router con mayor prioridad (por defecto 100) se convierte en el Active. Si hay empate en la prioridad, se decide por la IP más alta en la interfaz HSRP.

questions.name: HSRP/VRRP
questions.question: Unlike HSRP, which is a Cisco proprietary protocol, VRRP has what key characteristic?

options.A: VRRP does not support preemption, unlike HSRP which enables it by default in every configuration
options.B: VRRP is an IETF standard protocol and can use the real interface IP address of one of the group's routers as the virtual IP
options.C: VRRP only supports 2 routers per group, unlike HSRP which has no such limit on group size
options.D: VRRP requires a dedicated virtual IP separate from all physical interfaces, exactly like HSRP always does in every configuration

questions.explanation_es: VRRP es un estándar IETF (RFC), y permite que uno de los routers del grupo use su propia IP física de interfaz como la IP virtual (ese router se vuelve el Master 'IP owner'), algo que HSRP no hace, ya que siempre usa una IP virtual separada.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Besides statically configuring the same Rendezvous Point (RP) address on every PIM router, what dynamic mechanisms exist for RP discovery in a PIM Sparse Mode network?

options.A: RP discovery is always handled by OSPF flooding RP information as a special LSA type, with no dedicated PIM mechanism, treating RP reachability like an opaque LSA type 10 payload the way MPLS traffic-engineering data is flooded
options.B: Auto-RP (a Cisco-proprietary protocol) and BSR (Bootstrap Router, a standards-based protocol) both let routers learn the active RP dynamically, without static per-router configuration
options.C: Only DHCP can dynamically assign an RP address to PIM routers; there is no PIM-native discovery mechanism
options.D: Dynamic RP discovery is not possible in PIM Sparse Mode; static RP configuration is the only supported method

questions.explanation_es: Auto-RP (protocolo propietario de Cisco) y BSR (Bootstrap Router, basado en estándares) permiten que los routers aprendan el RP activo dinámicamente, sin necesidad de configuración estática en cada router.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: In PIM Sparse Mode, what is the role of the Rendezvous Point (RP)?

options.A: It is only used in PIM Dense Mode, having no equivalent role or function in PIM Sparse Mode
options.B: It acts as a meeting point where multicast sources register and receivers initially join, before the network potentially shifts to a more optimal shortest-path tree
options.C: It replaces the need for IGMP entirely, since receivers register directly with the RP instead of communicating with their local multicast router, bypassing the last-hop router's own group-membership tracking process entirely
options.D: It is the only device allowed to send multicast traffic, with all sources required to route through it directly

questions.explanation_es: El RP en PIM-SM funciona como un punto de encuentro: las fuentes se registran ahí y los receptores se unen inicialmente al árbol compartido (RPT) a través del RP; luego el tráfico puede migrar al árbol de ruta más corta (SPT) hacia la fuente para mayor eficiencia.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What does an NTP stratum value of 16 signify about a device's clock?

options.A: Stratum 16 is reserved for GPS-based reference clocks
options.B: Stratum 16 is used by convention to indicate that the device is unsynchronized, rather than indicating 16 hops from a reference clock
options.C: Stratum values above 15 are invalid and NTP rejects any device reporting stratum 16
options.D: Stratum 16 indicates the highest possible precision, better even than a stratum 1 reference clock, as though a higher stratum number meant added oscillator redundancy rather than hop count

questions.explanation_es: Por convención, el stratum 16 se usa para indicar que el dispositivo está desincronizado, en lugar de indicar 16 saltos desde un reloj de referencia.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: What does a PTP 'domain number' identify, and why might a network run multiple separate PTP domains?

options.A: The domain number sets the priority1 value used by the Best Master Clock Algorithm, so changing a device's domain number can directly shift which clock in the network gets elected grandmaster
options.B: A domain number groups a set of PTP clocks that synchronize together under one grandmaster; running multiple domains lets independent groups of devices (e.g., different applications or tenants) maintain separate time synchronization on the same physical network
options.C: The domain number determines the physical cable length PTP messages can travel before requiring a repeater
options.D: Only one PTP domain can ever exist per organization, regardless of network size or the number of applications requiring synchronization

questions.explanation_es: Un número de dominio agrupa un conjunto de relojes PTP que se sincronizan juntos bajo un grandmaster; correr múltiples dominios permite que grupos independientes de dispositivos mantengan sincronización de tiempo separada sobre la misma red física.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which statement about LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) EtherChannel modes is correct?

options.A: 'passive' mode actively sends LACP packets to initiate negotiation, exactly the opposite of what 'active' mode actually does in a real deployment during the initial handshake
options.B: A channel will form if at least one side is set to 'active' and the other side is set to 'active' or 'passive'; two 'passive' sides will never form a channel
options.C: Setting both ends to 'active' will not form a channel, since LACP requires exactly one side to be passive
options.D: LACP requires PAgP to be enabled first on both switches before any channel negotiation can begin

questions.explanation_es: LACP forma el canal si al menos un extremo está en modo 'active' (y el otro en 'active' o 'passive'). Si ambos extremos están en 'passive', ninguno inicia la negociación y el canal nunca se forma, porque 'passive' espera recibir paquetes LACP en lugar de enviarlos.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python data type is immutable and therefore commonly used as a dictionary key?

options.A: list
options.B: dict, since dictionaries are the only built-in Python type that can never be modified after creation
options.C: set
options.D: tuple

questions.explanation_es: Las tuplas son inmutables, por lo que pueden usarse como claves de diccionario (los dicts requieren claves hashables). Las listas y los propios dicts son mutables y no son hashables, así que no pueden usarse como claves.

questions.name: Python básico

options.A: status
options.B: None
options.C: unknown
options.D: KeyError

questions.explanation_es: dict.get(key, default) retorna el valor default indicado si la clave no existe, en vez de lanzar KeyError como haría data["status"]. Como "status" no está en el dict, imprime "unknown".

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: In a Python script using the 'requests' library to call a REST API, which method sends an HTTP GET request?

options.A: requests.fetch()
options.B: requests.get()
options.C: requests.query()
options.D: requests.send()

questions.explanation_es: La librería requests usa requests.get(url) para solicitudes GET y requests.post() para POST. Las otras opciones no son métodos reales de la librería.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: How must a JSON boolean value be written, and how does this differ from Python's boolean literals?

options.A: JSON booleans must be capitalized exactly like Python's ('True'/'False'), with no difference between the two, a mix-up that arises because Python's 'json' module accepts either capitalization as a convenience when encoding custom objects
options.B: JSON booleans must be written in all uppercase ('TRUE'/'FALSE') to be considered valid
options.C: JSON booleans must be lowercase ('true'/'false'), while Python's native booleans are capitalized ('True'/'False') — a library like json.loads() handles the conversion between the two automatically
options.D: JSON has no boolean type at all; booleans must be represented as the strings '1' and '0'

questions.explanation_es: Los booleanos de JSON deben ir en minúscula ('true'/'false'), mientras que los booleanos nativos de Python van capitalizados ('True'/'False') — una librería como json.loads() maneja la conversión automáticamente.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: What Python type does the JSON value 'null' map to when parsed with json.loads()?

options.B: False
options.C: "" (empty string)
options.D: None

questions.explanation_es: Al parsear JSON en Python, el valor null se convierte en el objeto None, no en 0, cadena vacía ni False.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which JSON structure correctly represents an array of two interface objects?

options.A: {"interfaces": [{"name": "Gi0/1", "status": "up"}, {"name": "Gi0/2", "status": "down"}]}
options.B: {"interfaces": ("Gi0/1": "up", "Gi0/2": "down")}
options.C: {"interfaces": ["Gi0/1", "up", "Gi0/2", "down"]}
options.D: {"interfaces": {"Gi0/1": "up", "Gi0/2": "down"}}, which is exactly equivalent to an array of interface objects in JSON

questions.explanation_es: Un array JSON de objetos usa corchetes conteniendo objetos {} separados por comas. La opción A es un objeto (no array), la B mezcla claves y valores en una lista plana, y la D usa paréntesis, que no es sintaxis JSON válida.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When integrating a traditional (non-fabric) campus network with an SD-Access fabric, which device role connects the two domains?

options.A: Control Plane Node
options.B: Fabric Border Node
options.C: Fabric WLC
options.D: Fabric Edge Node

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node es el punto de interoperabilidad entre la fabric SD-Access y las redes externas o tradicionales; traduce entre el encapsulado VXLAN/LISP de la fabric y el enrutamiento IP tradicional fuera de ella.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: A host in a traditional VLAN-based segment needs to reach a host inside an SD-Access fabric. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The traditional host must also run LISP and register its own EID with the fabric's Map Server before any traffic can pass
options.B: The Control Plane Node performs all packet forwarding for external traffic, in addition to maintaining the host-tracking database directly
options.C: SD-Access cannot interoperate with traditional networks requiring a full fabric-wide migration first
options.D: Traffic enters/exits the fabric through the Border Node, which translates between the fabric overlay and traditional routing/switching

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node traduce el tráfico entre el overlay de la fabric (VXLAN con políticas basadas en SGT) y una red tradicional externa; el host tradicional no necesita ejecutar LISP ni ningún protocolo especial de la fabric.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: During a phased migration from a traditional 3-tier campus to SD-Access, which approach is commonly recommended?

options.A: Migrate site by site or IP pool by IP pool, using the Border Node to maintain connectivity between migrated and non-migrated segments
options.B: Migration must begin at the core and distribution layers first, since access switches cannot be converted to fabric mode until every upstream device has already been migrated
options.C: Only wireless clients can be migrated to SD-Access; wired endpoints must remain on the traditional network permanently due to a hard platform limitation in fabric-enabled switching
options.D: Migrate the entire campus in a single maintenance window, converting every switch to fabric mode simultaneously

questions.explanation_es: Una migración típica hacia SD-Access se hace de forma incremental (por sitio, por IP pool o por switch), aprovechando el Border Node para mantener conectividad entre las partes ya migradas y las que siguen en la red tradicional, evitando un corte total.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: On platforms that support fine-grained CoPP, what do the 'host', 'transit', and 'CEF-exception' control-plane sub-interfaces each classify?

options.A: 'Host' classifies traffic destined to the device itself, 'transit' classifies traffic passing through the device that still reaches the CPU, and 'CEF-exception' classifies traffic punted to the CPU due to a forwarding exception
options.B: All three sub-interfaces are functionally identical and exist only for redundancy
options.C: These sub-interfaces classify traffic by physical port only, not by traffic type or destination
options.D: 'Host' and 'transit' both refer to traffic destined to the device itself, while 'CEF-exception' refers only to multicast traffic, a mix-up that overlooks how 'transit' refers to traffic merely passing through the device toward another destination while still reaching the CPU

questions.explanation_es: 'Host' clasifica el tráfico destinado al propio dispositivo, 'transit' clasifica el tráfico que pasa a través del dispositivo pero igual llega a la CPU, y 'CEF-exception' clasifica el tráfico desviado a la CPU por una excepción de reenvío.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: In which direction does Control Plane Policing apply its policy?

options.A: Only to transit traffic passing through the device
options.B: To traffic between two VLANs on the same switch
options.C: To traffic destined TO the device's control plane (the CPU itself)
options.D: Only to traffic sourced by the device toward external hosts, never to traffic destined toward the CPU itself

questions.explanation_es: CoPP se aplica específicamente al tráfico destinado a la CPU del propio dispositivo (control plane), no al tráfico de tránsito que solo pasa por el plano de datos sin involucrar a la CPU.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: Which Cisco IOS mechanism is used to configure CoPP?

options.A: A service-policy applied under the 'control-plane' context, using class-maps and a policy-map
options.B: QoS marking with 'mls qos trust'
options.C: A VACL (VLAN ACL) configuration
options.D: An access-list applied directly to a physical interface with 'ip access-group', which is functionally identical to CoPP configuration

questions.explanation_es: CoPP se configura definiendo class-maps para clasificar el tráfico, un policy-map con las acciones (police/drop), y aplicándolo con 'service-policy input <nombre>' bajo el contexto 'control-plane', que representa lógicamente a la CPU del dispositivo.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Which of these automation tools is classified as agentless (no software needs to be installed on the managed device)?

options.A: Ansible
options.B: Puppet
options.C: Chef
options.D: SaltStack running in agent mode

questions.explanation_es: Ansible es agentless: se conecta a los dispositivos gestionados vía SSH o APIs sin instalar software permanente en ellos. Puppet y Chef típicamente requieren un agente instalado en el nodo gestionado.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What is a key operational advantage of an agentless automation approach for network devices?

options.A: It typically completes large-scale changes faster than agent-based tools because connections to each device in the batch can be established and torn down in parallel, rather than relying on a persistent agent process on every device
options.B: It guarantees real-time push notifications from every managed device
options.C: It eliminates the need for any credentials to connect to devices
options.D: It avoids installing, updating, and maintaining agent software on each device — useful since many network devices cannot run third-party agents

questions.explanation_es: Muchos dispositivos de red no pueden ejecutar software de terceros como un agente; el enfoque agentless evita esa necesidad, conectándose bajo demanda (SSH/API) sin instalar ni mantener nada persistente en el dispositivo.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: In an agent-based orchestration model (e.g., Puppet), what role does the agent play on the managed node?

options.A: It runs persistently, periodically pulling configuration from a central server and applying it locally
options.B: It only serves as a passive log collector with no configuration capability, forwarding events to a central server without ever applying any changes
options.C: It only functions during initial provisioning and is then uninstalled
options.D: It replaces the need for a central server entirely

questions.explanation_es: En un modelo basado en agentes, el agente se instala de forma persistente en el nodo gestionado y contacta periódicamente a un servidor central (master) para obtener y aplicar la configuración deseada.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Cisco Embedded Event Manager (EEM)?

options.A: To detect an event on a device (CLI command, syslog message, CPU threshold, etc.) and automatically trigger a defined action in response
options.B: To provide a GUI for network monitoring, replacing the need for any CLI-based scripting or event detection logic entirely across every supported Cisco IOS platform
options.C: To replace SNMP entirely
options.D: To encrypt configuration files

questions.explanation_es: EEM permite definir applets que combinan un evento disparador (event detector) con una acción automática a ejecutar en respuesta, como enviar un email, correr un comando o generar un log.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM event detector triggers an applet when a specific CLI command is entered by a user?

options.A: event cli
options.B: event snmp
options.C: event syslog
options.D: event timer

questions.explanation_es: 'event cli' detecta cuando se ingresa un patrón de comando CLI específico (con 'match' sobre una expresión regular), disparando el applet antes o después de ejecutarse ese comando.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: An EEM applet is configured with 'event syslog pattern "%LINK-3-UPDOWN"' and an action to send an email. What triggers this applet?

options.A: A scheduled timer
options.B: The router generating a syslog message matching that pattern, such as an interface changing state
options.C: A manual CLI command entered by the administrator immediately before the applet is configured on the device
options.D: An SNMP trap received from another device

questions.explanation_es: 'event syslog' dispara el applet cuando el dispositivo genera internamente un mensaje de syslog que coincide con el patrón indicado, en este caso un cambio de estado de una interfaz.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: In RESTful API design, which HTTP method is idempotent and used to completely replace an existing resource?

options.A: GET
options.B: POST
options.C: PUT
options.D: PATCH

questions.explanation_es: PUT reemplaza por completo el recurso indicado con el cuerpo enviado y es idempotente. POST no es idempotente (crea un nuevo recurso cada vez) y PATCH aplica una modificación parcial, no un reemplazo completo.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Which HTTP method is typically used to apply a partial update to an existing resource, modifying only specific fields?

options.A: PATCH
options.B: OPTIONS
options.C: PUT
options.D: DELETE

questions.explanation_es: PATCH se usa para aplicar una modificación parcial a un recurso existente (cambiar solo algunos campos), a diferencia de PUT, que reemplaza el recurso completo.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Which statement about the HTTP GET method is correct?

options.A: GET should be safe and idempotent, retrieving a representation of a resource without side effects on the server
options.B: GET is the only method that can return a 201 Created status, since every other HTTP method is forbidden from creating new resources
options.C: GET requires a request body containing the resource data
options.D: GET is used to create new resources on the server

questions.explanation_es: GET es un método seguro (no debería modificar el estado del servidor) e idempotente, usado para leer un recurso. Crear un recurso, que puede devolver 201 Created, es responsabilidad típica de POST.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: Before 802.1X authentication completes, what kind of access does a switch port typically allow the connecting endpoint?

options.A: Restricted access via a pre-authentication ACL, allowing only what's needed for the authentication process itself (e.g., DHCP, ISE communication)
options.B: Trunk-level access to all VLANs
options.C: No traffic, including DHCP
options.D: Full, unrestricted access to the network, exactly as if 802.1X authentication had already completed successfully on that switch port regardless of the connected device's identity

questions.explanation_es: Antes de completarse la autenticación 802.1X, el puerto suele permitir un acceso restringido mediante una ACL de pre-autenticación, habilitando solo el tráfico necesario para el propio proceso (DHCP, DNS, comunicación con ISE), no acceso completo.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes TACACS+ from RADIUS?

options.A: TACACS+ encrypts only the password in the packet, while RADIUS encrypts the entire packet body
options.B: TACACS+ encrypts the entire packet body, while RADIUS encrypts only the password field
options.C: Both encrypt the entire packet identically
options.D: Neither protocol encrypts any part of the packet

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ cifra todo el cuerpo del paquete, mientras que RADIUS solo cifra el campo de contraseña, dejando el resto del paquete (como el username) sin cifrar.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: Which AAA protocol separates authentication and authorization into distinct processes, making it well suited for granular per-command authorization on network devices?

options.A: Kerberos
options.B: LDAP
options.C: TACACS+
options.D: RADIUS

questions.explanation_es: TACACS+ separa claramente autenticación, autorización y accounting en procesos independientes, permitiendo un control granular como autorizar comandos individuales en el CLI — algo que RADIUS, al combinar autenticación y autorización, no maneja tan bien.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: In a standard IPv4 ACL, which criterion can be used to match traffic?

options.A: Destination MAC address
options.B: Source IP address only
options.C: Source and destination IP address plus Layer 4 port
options.D: VLAN tag

questions.explanation_es: Las ACL estándar de IPv4 solo pueden filtrar según la dirección IP de origen. Para filtrar por IP destino, protocolo o puertos de Capa 4 se necesita una ACL extendida.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: By default, what happens to a packet that matches no explicit statement in an ACL applied to an interface?

options.A: It is queued until an administrator manually decides how to handle it during the next maintenance window
options.B: It is denied, due to an implicit 'deny all' at the end of every ACL
options.C: It is permitted, since ACLs default to permit
options.D: It is forwarded using the next ACL in sequence

questions.explanation_es: Toda ACL de Cisco tiene una sentencia implícita de 'deny all' al final (aunque no se muestre en la configuración), por lo que el tráfico que no coincide explícitamente con un 'permit' se descarta.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What does a CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) score help an organization do when triaging discovered vulnerabilities?

options.A: It provides a standardized numeric severity rating, helping prioritize which vulnerabilities to remediate first based on relative risk
options.B: It only classifies vulnerabilities by which vendor reported them, not by their actual severity or exploitability
options.C: It has no practical use in prioritization; every vulnerability must be treated as equally urgent regardless of score, ignoring that CVSS scores exist to differentiate urgency
options.D: It automatically patches the vulnerability once scored, removing the need for manual remediation planning

questions.explanation_es: Provee una calificación numérica estandarizada de severidad, ayudando a priorizar qué vulnerabilidades remediar primero según su riesgo relativo.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Which authentication mechanism involves the client sending a token in the 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' HTTP header on each API request?

options.A: IPsec
options.B: OAuth 2.0 token-based authentication
options.C: Basic authentication with username/password on every request

questions.explanation_es: En OAuth 2.0, tras autenticarse el cliente recibe un token de acceso que envía en el header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' en cada solicitud posterior, sin reenviar usuario/contraseña cada vez.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is HTTPS (TLS) considered essential for securing REST API calls that carry authentication credentials or tokens?

options.A: HTTPS encrypts the data in transit, preventing credentials/tokens from being intercepted in cleartext
options.B: HTTPS is only needed for GET requests
options.C: HTTPS makes the API respond faster
options.D: HTTPS replaces the need for any authentication mechanism entirely, since TLS alone verifies the identity of every client

questions.explanation_es: HTTPS cifra el tráfico entre cliente y servidor, protegiendo credenciales y tokens de ser interceptados en texto plano (por ejemplo en un ataque man-in-the-middle); no reemplaza la autenticación, la complementa.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: What does IP SLA 'scheduling' (using the 'ip sla schedule' command) allow an administrator to configure for a defined operation?

options.A: It has no effect; all IP SLA operations start immediately and run forever by default with no way to change that, though an operation without an explicit life value still eventually stops on its own
options.B: It controls when the operation starts and how long it runs (its 'life'), including whether it runs once, for a fixed duration, or indefinitely
options.C: It configures which VRF the operation's probe traffic uses, unrelated to timing
options.D: It only allows renaming the operation; timing must be configured elsewhere

questions.explanation_es: Controla cuándo inicia la operación y cuánto tiempo corre (su 'life'), incluyendo si corre una sola vez, por una duración fija, o indefinidamente.

questions.name: IP SLA
questions.question: How can IP SLA be combined with object tracking to improve network resiliency?

options.A: A 'track' object can monitor an IP SLA operation and trigger actions like removing a static route from the routing table if the tracked path fails
options.B: IP SLA replaces the need for a routing protocol entirely
options.C: IP SLA automatically reconfigures BGP neighbor relationships whenever a monitored path degrades below a defined threshold whenever a monitored path degrades in quality
options.D: IP SLA cannot be combined with any other feature

questions.explanation_es: Un objeto 'track' puede monitorear el estado de una operación de IP SLA (por ejemplo, alcanzabilidad de un gateway) y, si falla, disparar acciones automáticas como retirar una ruta estática, logrando una conmutación por falla más rápida.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: How does NetFlow version 9 (and by extension Flexible NetFlow) differ from the older, fixed-format NetFlow version 5 in terms of exported record structure?

options.A: Version 9 removed the ability to export any flow data at all, using it only for device health monitoring
options.B: Version 9 and version 5 use an identical fixed record format, with version 9 only changing the UDP port used for export
options.C: Version 5 introduced the template-based record format that allows customizable fields, while version 9 reverted to a fixed record layout for backward compatibility with older collectors
options.D: Version 9 uses a template-based export format, where the set of fields in a record is defined by a separate template message, allowing customizable and extensible records — unlike version 5's fixed, non-configurable field set

questions.explanation_es: La versión 9 usa un formato de exportación basado en templates, donde el conjunto de campos de un registro se define mediante un mensaje de template separado, permitiendo registros personalizables y extensibles — a diferencia del conjunto de campos fijo y no configurable de la versión 5.

questions.name: Flexible NetFlow
questions.question: Which components must be configured and associated to enable Flexible NetFlow on an interface?

options.A: A route-map and a class-map
options.B: A SPAN session and a VLAN ACL
options.C: Only an access-list applied to the interface, with no need for any record, monitor, or exporter configuration at all
options.D: A flow record and a flow monitor (with an optional flow exporter), with the flow monitor applied to the interface

questions.explanation_es: Flexible NetFlow se arma con un flow record (define qué campos se recolectan) y un flow monitor (asocia el record con una caché, opcionalmente con un exporter) que se aplica a la interfaz; el exporter es opcional para enviar los datos a un collector externo.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: What is the key difference between SPAN and RSPAN?

options.A: RSPAN can mirror traffic across multiple switches over a dedicated RSPAN VLAN, while SPAN is limited to a single switch
options.B: SPAN encrypts mirrored traffic; RSPAN does not
options.C: SPAN can span traffic across multiple switches using a dedicated VLAN, while RSPAN cannot do this at all, since mirrored traffic is assumed to flood across any trunk link
options.D: There is no functional difference; RSPAN is just a newer name for SPAN

questions.explanation_es: SPAN copia tráfico de un puerto/VLAN origen a un puerto destino dentro del mismo switch. RSPAN extiende esa capacidad usando una VLAN dedicada para transportar el tráfico espejado a través de múltiples switches.

questions.name: SPAN/RSPAN/ERSPAN
questions.question: Why would an administrator choose ERSPAN over SPAN or RSPAN?

options.A: ERSPAN encapsulates the mirrored traffic in GRE, allowing it to be transported over a routed Layer 3 network to a remote destination
options.B: ERSPAN cannot be used with Cisco Catalyst switches
options.C: ERSPAN is required whenever mirroring traffic within the same switch, since SPAN cannot handle that scenario at all since plain SPAN cannot handle that scenario
options.D: ERSPAN only works on a single VLAN within one switch

questions.explanation_es: ERSPAN encapsula el tráfico espejado en GRE, permitiendo enviarlo a través de una red enrutada de Capa 3 hacia un destino remoto (por ejemplo, una herramienta de monitoreo en otro sitio), algo que SPAN y RSPAN no pueden hacer al estar limitados a Capa 2.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: Which command creates a local username/password database entry for authentication on a Cisco device?

options.A: line vty 0 4
options.B: enable secret Cisco123, which also creates a full local username database entry automatically
options.C: aaa new-model
options.D: username admin password Cisco123

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'username <nombre> password <clave>' crea una entrada en la base de datos local de usuarios del dispositivo, usada para autenticación local en líneas configuradas con 'login local'.

questions.name: Líneas y autenticación local
questions.question: What is the effect of the 'login local' command applied under 'line vty 0 4'?

options.A: It applies only to console line access, not VTY
options.B: It requires users connecting via those VTY lines to authenticate using the local username database configured on the device
options.C: It forces authentication through a RADIUS server, bypassing the local username database entirely regardless of configuration
options.D: It disables authentication entirely for VTY lines

questions.explanation_es: 'login local' bajo las líneas VTY indica que la autenticación debe validarse contra la base de datos local de usuarios (creada con 'username'), en lugar de usar solo una contraseña de línea genérica o un servidor AAA externo.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
questions.question: What is the difference between NETCONF's '<get>' and '<get-config>' operations?

options.A: '<get>' retrieves configuration data only from the candidate datastore, while '<get-config>' retrieves both configuration and operational state data from the running datastore
options.B: They are two identical aliases for the same operation, with no functional difference between them
options.C: '<get-config>' retrieves configuration data from a specified datastore (such as running or candidate), while '<get>' retrieves both configuration and operational state data
options.D: '<get-config>' is used only to delete configuration, unrelated to retrieving any data

questions.explanation_es: '<get-config>' obtiene datos de configuración de un datastore especificado (como running o candidate), mientras que '<get>' obtiene tanto datos de configuración como de estado operativo.

questions.name: NETCONF/RESTCONF
