questions.question: Which encoding format does NETCONF use to structure its messages, such as <get-config> and <edit-config> operations?

options.A: CSV
options.B: XML
options.C: Only JSON
options.D: Only plain text

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF utiliza XML para codificar sus mensajes y operaciones, a diferencia de RESTCONF, que soporta tanto XML como JSON.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center) feature provides end-to-end visibility into network health and can proactively identify issues affecting client connectivity?

options.A: Plug and Play
options.B: Assurance
options.C: Path Trace
options.D: Template Editor

questions.explanation_es: Assurance en Catalyst Center recopila telemetría de la red y los clientes para dar visibilidad de salud end-to-end, detectando proactivamente problemas y sugiriendo posibles causas raíz.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: What does the Catalyst Center 'Path Trace' tool do?

options.A: It only shows historical CPU utilization graphs
options.B: It automatically remediates any configuration errors found and can even suggest likely root causes for connectivity problems along that path automatically
options.C: It is used for wireless site surveys
options.D: It simulates and traces the actual path a packet would take between two endpoints, showing each hop and potential issues along the way

questions.explanation_es: Path Trace traza la ruta real (hop por hop) que seguiría o está siguiendo el tráfico entre un origen y un destino, mostrando el estado de cada salto y ayudando a identificar dónde ocurre un problema.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: How does managing an FTD device via FDM (Firepower Device Manager) differ from managing it via FMC (Firepower Management Center)?

options.A: FDM and FMC both run as separate centralized platforms capable of managing multiple FTD devices, differing mainly in licensing tier rather than in their overall scope of management
options.B: FDM can manage multiple FTD devices centrally, while FMC can only manage a single device at a time
options.C: FDM is a locally hosted, single-device web UI built into the FTD appliance itself, while FMC is a centralized platform that manages policy across many FTD devices at once
options.D: FDM requires a separate physical appliance, while FMC runs directly on each FTD device with no separate platform needed, a description that reverses which of the two products actually needs its own dedicated platform

questions.explanation_es: FDM es una interfaz web local, de un solo dispositivo, integrada en el propio equipo FTD, mientras que FMC es una plataforma centralizada que gestiona política a través de muchos dispositivos FTD a la vez.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: Beyond QoS shaping, how can AVC's application-visibility reporting help with a security use case like detecting 'shadow IT'?

options.A: AVC can only detect applications that are already known and pre-approved, making it unable to surface anything unexpected
options.B: AVC has no visibility-reporting capability at all; it can only apply QoS marking, not generate reports
options.C: AVC reporting can reveal applications actually running on the network that weren't expected or sanctioned, helping identify unauthorized software or services in use
options.D: Shadow IT detection requires a completely separate product; AVC's application data cannot be used for this purpose in any way, overlooking that AVC's per-flow data would surface an unsanctioned cloud app

questions.explanation_es: Los reportes de AVC pueden revelar aplicaciones que realmente corren en la red y que no eran esperadas o autorizadas, ayudando a identificar software o servicios no sancionados en uso.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: In a virtualized environment (e.g., VMware vSphere), what does Fault Tolerance (FT) provide?

options.A: Scheduled nightly backups of VM disk images to external storage
options.B: A live, continuously synchronized secondary copy of a VM on a different host, which takes over instantly with zero downtime if the primary host fails
options.C: Encryption of VM network traffic between hosts
options.D: Automatic load balancing of VMs across hosts based on current resource usage, migrating them live whenever CPU or memory contention is detected, which is how FT is sometimes marketed alongside DRS

questions.explanation_es: Fault Tolerance mantiene una VM secundaria sincronizada en tiempo real en otro host; si el host primario falla, la secundaria toma el control de inmediato sin pérdida de estado — a diferencia de HA, que reinicia la VM tras la falla.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: What is the purpose of Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) in a virtualization cluster?

options.A: It performs VM backups automatically on a fixed schedule
options.B: It provides zero-downtime failover identical to Fault Tolerance, maintaining a fully synchronized secondary copy of every VM at all times
options.C: It manages physical firewall rules on the network perimeter
options.D: It automatically balances VM workloads across hosts in a cluster by migrating VMs to optimize resource utilization

questions.explanation_es: DRS monitorea el uso de recursos de los hosts en un clúster y migra VMs automáticamente (vía migración en vivo) entre hosts para balancear la carga, sin proveer la tolerancia a fallas instantánea que sí ofrece FT.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What distinguishes a Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor from a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor?

options.A: There is no meaningful architectural difference between them at all
options.B: Type 1 requires a host OS to function; Type 2 does not need one
options.C: Type 1 runs directly on the physical hardware; Type 2 runs as an application on top of a host operating system
options.D: Type 2 hypervisors always provide better performance than Type 1 does, since they benefit from optimizations built into the host operating system

questions.explanation_es: Un hypervisor tipo 1 (bare-metal, como VMware ESXi) se ejecuta directamente sobre el hardware físico sin un sistema operativo host intermedio. Un tipo 2 se ejecuta como aplicación dentro de un SO host ya existente, agregando overhead.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Why are Type 1 hypervisors generally preferred in enterprise data center environments over Type 2 hypervisors?

options.A: Type 1 hypervisors do not support live migration between hosts
options.B: Type 1 hypervisors are always free of charge to license
options.C: Type 1 hypervisors offer better performance and lower overhead since they interact directly with hardware, without an extra host OS layer
options.D: Type 2 hypervisors cannot run more than one VM at a time on a host, unlike Type 1 hypervisors which support many simultaneous guest operating systems side by side

questions.explanation_es: Al ejecutarse directamente sobre el hardware sin un sistema operativo host de por medio, los hypervisors tipo 1 tienen menor overhead y mejor rendimiento, por lo que son preferidos en centros de datos que ejecutan múltiples VMs de producción.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What does it mean for a service like DHCP relay or NTP to be 'VRF-aware' on a router with multiple VRFs configured?

options.A: VRF-awareness has no practical effect on how these services function
options.B: The service can only operate in the global routing table and cannot be associated with any VRF
options.C: The service automatically replicates its configuration identically into every VRF with no per-VRF customization possible, meaning a single DHCP relay address configured once is automatically applied unchanged across every VRF on the router
options.D: The service can be configured to operate within a specific VRF's context, such as relaying DHCP requests or reaching an NTP server that is only reachable through that VRF's routing table

questions.explanation_es: El servicio puede configurarse para operar dentro del contexto de una VRF específica, como reenviar solicitudes DHCP o alcanzar un servidor NTP que solo es alcanzable a través de la tabla de ruteo de esa VRF.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: For two devices in different VRFs on the same router to communicate with each other, what is typically required?

options.A: VRF automatically bridges all instances together at Layer 2
options.B: Nothing extra is required; VRFs communicate with each other by default because they all still share the router's single global routing table underneath
options.C: Both devices must be configured in the same VLAN
options.D: Route leaking (importing/exporting routes between VRFs) or an intermediate device connecting them, since VRFs are isolated by design

questions.explanation_es: Las VRFs están aisladas entre sí por diseño; para que se comuniquen se necesita una técnica explícita como route leaking (por ejemplo vía route-targets con MP-BGP) o un dispositivo intermedio como un firewall.

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: In LISP (Locator/ID Separation Protocol), what do the EID and RLOC represent?

options.A: EID identifies the device's identity, while RLOC identifies where that device is topologically reachable
options.B: RLOC identifies the device's identity, while EID identifies its location within the network topology at any given moment
options.C: EID and RLOC are simply two different names for the same address
options.D: EID is used only for IPv6 addressing, and RLOC only for IPv4

questions.explanation_es: LISP separa identidad y ubicación: el EID identifica quién es el dispositivo (no cambia aunque se mueva), mientras que el RLOC identifica dónde está topológicamente alcanzable (el router de borde que lo conecta a la red de tránsito).

questions.name: LISP
questions.question: What is the role of the LISP Map Server/Map Resolver system?

options.A: It replaces the need for BGP in the underlay routing entirely, since EID-to-RLOC mappings are distributed using LISP's own dedicated routing protocol
options.B: It maintains and answers mapping queries between EIDs and their current RLOCs, similar in concept to how DNS maps names to IP addresses
options.C: It encrypts LISP-encapsulated packets between sites
options.D: It performs NAT translation for LISP-encapsulated traffic

questions.explanation_es: El sistema Map Server/Map Resolver mantiene la base de datos de mapeos EID-a-RLOC y resuelve consultas sobre dónde está alcanzable un EID, de forma conceptualmente similar a cómo DNS resuelve nombres a direcciones IP.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which statement about GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunnels is correct?

options.A: GRE can only encapsulate TCP traffic inside it
options.B: GRE requires IPsec to function at all as a tunnel
options.C: GRE provides encryption of the encapsulated payload by default using AES, negotiating keys automatically the moment the tunnel first comes up, using keys derived from the tunnel endpoints
options.D: GRE encapsulates a wide variety of protocols (including multicast and non-IP protocols) inside an IP packet, but provides no encryption on its own

questions.explanation_es: GRE encapsula una amplia variedad de protocolos (incluido tráfico multicast) dentro de paquetes IP, creando un túnel; pero por sí solo no cifra ni autentica el tráfico, por eso suele combinarse con IPsec.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Why is GRE often combined with IPsec (GRE over IPsec) instead of using IPsec alone for certain deployments?

options.A: Because IPsec cannot encrypt any IP traffic at all without GRE
options.B: Because GRE is required for IPsec to establish a Security Association, since IPsec cannot negotiate one without a GRE tunnel already established and passing traffic
options.C: Because GRE improves the encryption strength used by IPsec
options.D: Because IPsec alone cannot transport multicast or dynamic routing protocol traffic well, while GRE can encapsulate that traffic before IPsec encrypts it

questions.explanation_es: IPsec en modo túnel puro no soporta bien tráfico multicast ni protocolos de enrutamiento dinámico que dependen de multicast (como OSPF). GRE puede encapsular ese tráfico dentro de un túnel IP unicast que luego IPsec cifra, combinando la flexibilidad de GRE con la seguridad de IPsec.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: Which statement about the 'debug' command on a Cisco IOS device is correct?

options.A: 'debug' commands permanently alter the device's running configuration
options.B: 'debug' output is only visible via SNMP
options.C: 'debug' commands can consume significant CPU resources and should be used cautiously in production, narrowed and disabled promptly after troubleshooting
options.D: 'debug' commands have no impact on device CPU and can always be left running safely, even on a heavily loaded production router

questions.explanation_es: Los comandos 'debug' generan y procesan mucha información en tiempo real, lo que puede consumir CPU significativa; se recomienda acotarlos (por ejemplo con listas de acceso) y desactivarlos ('undebug all') apenas se termina el troubleshooting.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: What does an HTTP 204 No Content response typically indicate?

options.A: The request succeeded, but there is no content to return in the response body (common after a successful DELETE)
options.B: The request failed due to a client error
options.C: The requested resource was permanently moved to a new URL that the client must follow for all future requests, generated by the same framework middleware
options.D: The server is temporarily unavailable

questions.explanation_es: HTTP 204 No Content indica que la solicitud se procesó exitosamente pero no hay contenido para devolver — es común, por ejemplo, como respuesta a un DELETE exitoso donde no hace falta retornar datos.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In a spine-leaf (Clos) fabric design commonly used in data centers, what is a defining architectural principle?

options.A: Spine switches connect only to each other in a ring, while leaf switches form a separate independent mesh with no connection to the spine at all
options.B: Only a single spine switch is permitted per fabric, with all leaf switches connecting to that one central device
options.C: Leaf switches connect directly to each other in a full mesh, and the spine layer is used only as a passive Layer 1 patch panel
options.D: Every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, and leaf switches never connect directly to each other, giving predictable equal-cost paths between any two leaves

questions.explanation_es: En un diseño spine-leaf (topología Clos), cada switch leaf se conecta a todos los switches spine, y los leaves nunca se conectan directamente entre sí. Esto da caminos de igual costo (ECMP) predecibles entre cualquier par de leaves, con latencia y ancho de banda consistentes independientemente de qué leaf a leaf se comunique.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: Why do modern data center fabrics favor a spine-leaf design over a traditional 3-tier (core/distribution/access) design?

options.A: Spine-leaf requires fewer total switch ports than a 3-tier design of equivalent scale
options.B: Spine-leaf eliminates the need for any IP addressing within the data center
options.C: Spine-leaf was designed specifically to eliminate the need for any Layer 3 routing in the data center, relying instead on a flat Layer 2 fabric where every leaf switch forwards frames purely by MAC address lookup across the spine, the same flooding-and-learning behavior found in a basic hub
options.D: Spine-leaf provides predictable, low-latency East-West bandwidth between any two leaf switches, which suits the high server-to-server traffic patterns typical of modern data centers, better than a hierarchical design optimized for North-South traffic

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico en los data centers modernos es mayormente East-West (servidor a servidor, por ejemplo entre microservicios), a diferencia del tráfico North-South típico de un campus. El diseño spine-leaf ofrece ancho de banda y latencia predecibles entre cualquier par de leaves, algo que un diseño jerárquico de 3 capas (optimizado para tráfico hacia/desde un borde central) no logra tan eficientemente.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What does 'oversubscription ratio' refer to in the context of a spine-leaf or hierarchical network design?

options.A: The percentage of ports on a switch that are administratively shut down for security reasons
options.B: The ratio of downlink (access-facing) bandwidth to uplink bandwidth toward the next layer, indicating how much traffic could theoretically be blocked if every downlink were fully utilized simultaneously
options.C: The number of physical switches purchased compared to the number actually installed in the rack, a procurement metric tracked by asset management teams rather than something configured within the switching or routing infrastructure itself
options.D: The ratio of IPv4 addresses to IPv6 addresses configured on a given VLAN

questions.explanation_es: El ratio de oversubscription compara el ancho de banda total disponible hacia los downlinks (por ejemplo, hacia los servidores o el access) contra el ancho de banda de los uplinks hacia la capa siguiente. Un ratio de 3:1, por ejemplo, significa que si los tres downlinks estuvieran saturados simultáneamente, el uplink no podría cursar todo ese tráfico sin congestión.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: Which statement accurately distinguishes 'North-South' traffic from 'East-West' traffic in network design terminology?

options.A: North-South traffic refers only to traffic between two racks within the same data center row, while East-West traffic refers only to traffic crossing between two separate data center sites
options.B: East-West traffic refers only to traffic between two different physical data center sites, and North-South refers only to traffic within a single rack, terminology that originated from how DCI links were labeled on early data center topology diagrams
options.C: North-South traffic only occurs on IPv6 networks, while East-West traffic only occurs on IPv4 networks
options.D: North-South traffic flows between clients and servers/services (often crossing the network's edge toward users or the internet), while East-West traffic flows between servers or workloads within the data center itself

questions.explanation_es: El tráfico North-South es el que entra o sale del data center/campus hacia los clientes o internet (cliente-servidor). El tráfico East-West es el que ocurre entre servidores o cargas de trabajo dentro del mismo data center (por ejemplo, entre microservicios) — este patrón ha crecido mucho con arquitecturas distribuidas y es la razón principal detrás del diseño spine-leaf.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: When comparing public cloud, private cloud, and hybrid cloud deployment models, what best characterizes a 'hybrid cloud'?

options.A: A deployment model that is defined solely by whether the organization pays a monthly subscription instead of buying hardware outright
options.B: A combination of private (on-premises or dedicated) infrastructure and public cloud resources, typically interconnected so that workloads or data can move between the two as needed
options.C: A cloud model where a single public cloud provider hosts all workloads for multiple, entirely unrelated customers on strictly isolated hardware, a configuration more accurately referred to as a single-tenant public cloud deployment
options.D: A deployment that uses on-premises infrastructure with no connection to any public cloud provider

questions.explanation_es: Una nube híbrida combina infraestructura privada (propia o dedicada) con recursos de nube pública, típicamente interconectados para que las cargas de trabajo o los datos puedan moverse entre ambos entornos según convenga (por ejemplo, picos de demanda desbordando hacia la nube pública).

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In the traditional 3-tier campus model, what functional separation exists between the access layer and the distribution layer regarding VLANs?

options.A: The distribution layer only ever operates at Layer 1, with all VLAN tagging and routing decisions made at the access layer
options.B: VLANs are configured at the core layer, and neither the access nor the distribution layer has any VLAN awareness at all
options.C: The access layer typically terminates end-user VLANs at the switch port, while the distribution layer often serves as the Layer 2/Layer 3 boundary, aggregating multiple access-layer VLANs and routing between them
options.D: Access and distribution layers must always use exactly the same single VLAN throughout the entire campus for the design to function

questions.explanation_es: En el modelo tradicional de 3 capas, el access layer conecta a los usuarios finales dentro de sus VLANs, mientras que la distribution layer suele actuar como el límite Capa 2/Capa 3, agregando las VLANs de múltiples switches de acceso y enrutando entre ellas — de ahí su rol central en el diseño jerárquico.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What is a key limitation of a traditional 3-tier VLAN-based campus design that fabric-based designs (like SD-Access) aim to address?

options.A: 3-tier designs cannot support any wireless access points at all, since the access layer in a traditional 3-tier model is defined as wired-only by the original hierarchical design specification
options.B: 3-tier designs require the distribution layer to run only a single routing protocol across the entire campus, since the original hierarchical model did not anticipate redistribution between multiple IGPs occurring at that layer
options.C: VLANs in a 3-tier design are often tied to specific physical switches/subnets, making network-wide segmentation and consistent policy enforcement across the whole campus difficult without extending Layer 2 broadly (which introduces its own risks, like large broadcast domains)
options.D: 3-tier designs cannot use any dynamic routing protocol other than static routes, since the core/distribution boundary in the original hierarchical model was defined around manually configured routes only

questions.explanation_es: En un diseño tradicional, las VLANs suelen estar atadas a switches/subredes físicas, lo que dificulta aplicar segmentación y políticas consistentes en toda la red sin extender Capa 2 ampliamente (lo cual trae riesgos, como dominios de broadcast grandes). Las fabrics como SD-Access resuelven esto desacoplando la política (SGT) de la topología/IP.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: Which statement about Cisco Validated Designs (CVDs) is accurate?

options.A: CVDs are a certification that individual network engineers must obtain before configuring any Cisco device, similar to a CCNA or CCNP credential, and engineers who lack an active CVD certification are blocked from deploying validated designs in production
options.B: A CVD is a proprietary hardware component that must be physically installed in every Cisco switch
options.C: CVDs eliminate the need for any site-specific customization or planning
options.D: CVDs are tested, documented reference architectures published by Cisco that provide design guidance and best practices for specific network scenarios, helping reduce design risk compared to building a fully custom architecture from scratch

questions.explanation_es: Los Cisco Validated Designs (CVD) son arquitecturas de referencia probadas y documentadas por Cisco que ofrecen guías de diseño y mejores prácticas para escenarios específicos, ayudando a reducir el riesgo de diseño frente a construir una arquitectura completamente a medida desde cero.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In a 2-tier (collapsed core) design, what operational trade-off is typically accepted compared to a full 3-tier design?

options.A: By merging the core and distribution functions into one layer, the design reduces cost and complexity for smaller networks, but may offer less separation of failure domains and less room to scale to very large campus sizes compared to a dedicated 3-tier design
options.B: A 2-tier design requires strictly more physical switches than an equivalent 3-tier design
options.C: A 2-tier design always provides strictly higher total bandwidth than any 3-tier design of the same physical size, because removing the distribution layer eliminates an entire hop of oversubscription that would otherwise reduce uplink capacity, regardless of how many access switches are ultimately connected
options.D: A 2-tier design cannot support any form of Layer 3 routing

questions.explanation_es: Al fusionar las funciones de core y distribución en una sola capa, un diseño de 2 niveles reduce costo y complejidad para redes más pequeñas, pero típicamente ofrece menos separación de dominios de falla y menos margen de crecimiento hacia campus muy grandes, comparado con un diseño de 3 niveles dedicado.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What does 'IaaS' (Infrastructure as a Service) refer to in the context of cloud service models relevant to network design?

options.A: A cloud model where the provider offers fundamental computing resources — virtual machines, storage, and networking — while the customer manages the operating system, applications, and much of the network configuration on top of that infrastructure
options.B: A licensing term that refers to the physical hardware warranty period offered by a vendor
options.C: A cloud model where the provider delivers fully finished, ready-to-use business applications, and the customer has no infrastructure to manage at all, a description that actually corresponds to SaaS rather than IaaS in most provider catalogs, a distinction Cisco exam objectives test directly
options.D: A protocol used specifically for encrypting traffic between two IaaS providers

questions.explanation_es: IaaS (Infraestructura como Servicio) es un modelo donde el proveedor ofrece recursos de cómputo fundamentales (VMs, almacenamiento, redes), mientras que el cliente gestiona el sistema operativo, las aplicaciones y buena parte de la configuración de red sobre esa infraestructura — a diferencia de PaaS o SaaS, donde el proveedor gestiona más capas.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In the context of intent-based networking (IBN) as a design philosophy, what is the general idea behind expressing network configuration as 'intent'?

options.A: Intent-based networking means the administrator declares a high-level desired outcome (e.g., 'this group of users should have access to that group of resources'), and the system translates that intent into the detailed low-level device configuration needed to achieve it, often verifying that the actual network state matches the intent
options.B: Intent-based networking eliminates the need for any network monitoring, since the network is assumed to always work correctly once intent is declared, because the declared intent itself is treated as a permanent guarantee of the resulting state rather than something the controller checks again after the initial deployment, making ongoing verification unnecessary once deployed
options.C: Intent-based networking means every configuration must be typed manually into each device's CLI one command at a time, with no automation involved
options.D: Intent-based networking refers to naming conventions used for VLAN IDs

questions.explanation_es: En redes basadas en intención, el administrador declara un resultado deseado de alto nivel (por ejemplo, 'este grupo de usuarios debe tener acceso a aquel grupo de recursos'), y el sistema traduce esa intención a la configuración detallada de bajo nivel necesaria, a menudo verificando continuamente que el estado real de la red coincida con esa intención declarada.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares a traditional CLI-driven, box-by-box network design approach to a controller-based (e.g., Catalyst Center or SD-WAN vManage) design approach?

options.A: A controller-based approach still requires each device to be configured individually through its own CLI, with the controller mainly providing a centralized dashboard for reviewing configuration state after the fact
options.B: A controller-based approach centralizes configuration and policy definition, pushing consistent configuration to many devices from a single source of truth, whereas a traditional box-by-box approach requires configuring and maintaining consistency across each device individually via its own CLI
options.C: A controller-based approach can only ever manage a single device at a time, exactly like box-by-box CLI configuration
options.D: Box-by-box CLI configuration is always faster to deploy at scale than any controller-based approach, regardless of the number of devices involved, since each device's configuration can be typed and applied in parallel by a large enough team of engineers working simultaneously across the network with no coordination overhead between them

questions.explanation_es: Un enfoque basado en controlador centraliza la definición de configuración y política, empujando configuración consistente a muchos dispositivos desde una única fuente de verdad, mientras que el enfoque tradicional caja por caja requiere configurar y mantener la consistencia en cada dispositivo individualmente vía su propio CLI — una diferencia clave de escalabilidad operativa.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: What is a common reason a network designer would choose to keep certain workloads on-premises (private cloud/traditional data center) rather than migrating them fully to a public cloud?

options.A: On-premises infrastructure typically achieves a lower total cost of ownership than public cloud once the initial hardware investment is fully depreciated, even for workloads with highly variable, bursty utilization patterns
options.B: Public cloud providers are legally prohibited from hosting any type of business application
options.C: On-premises infrastructure requires no operational staff or maintenance once installed
options.D: Regulatory, data sovereignty, latency-sensitive, or legacy application compatibility requirements may make it impractical or non-compliant to move certain workloads to a public cloud provider

questions.explanation_es: Requisitos regulatorios, de soberanía de datos, sensibilidad a la latencia, o compatibilidad con aplicaciones legacy pueden hacer poco práctico o no conforme migrar ciertas cargas de trabajo a la nube pública — una consideración de diseño real detrás de mantener algunos workloads on-premises o en nube privada.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In a 3-tier hierarchical design, why is it generally recommended to keep detailed security/QoS policy enforcement closer to the access layer edge rather than centralizing all of it at the core?

options.A: Because access-layer switches always have more CPU resources available than core switches
options.B: Because the core layer is physically incapable of running any software newer than five years old
options.C: Because switches at the access layer are not designed to applying any policy at all
options.D: Because enforcing policy as close as possible to the traffic's origin filters or shapes unwanted/misclassified traffic before it consumes bandwidth deeper in the network, and keeps the core layer focused on fast, low-latency forwarding rather than heavy per-flow inspection

questions.explanation_es: Aplicar la política (seguridad, QoS) lo más cerca posible del origen del tráfico filtra o clasifica el tráfico no deseado antes de que consuma ancho de banda más adentro de la red, y mantiene a la capa core enfocada en reenvío rápido y de baja latencia en vez de inspección pesada por flujo — un principio clásico del diseño jerárquico.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: Which best describes the relationship between the underlay network and the overlay network in a fabric-based design (such as SD-Access or a VXLAN data center fabric)?

options.A: The overlay must be built first, and the underlay is generated automatically afterward with no IP addressing plan required, since VXLAN tunnel endpoints negotiate their own routed connectivity dynamically through the overlay's control-plane protocol
options.B: The underlay and overlay are two unrelated networks that never interact or depend on each other in any way
options.C: The overlay refers to the physical routed infrastructure connecting the fabric nodes, while the underlay refers to the logical VXLAN tunnels built on top of it to carry segmented traffic between endpoints
options.D: The underlay provides basic IP reachability (routed connectivity) between fabric nodes, and the overlay (e.g., VXLAN) is built logically on top of that underlay to carry segmented, policy-aware traffic between endpoints

questions.explanation_es: El underlay provee conectividad IP básica (enrutada) entre los nodos de la fabric, y el overlay (por ejemplo, VXLAN) se construye lógicamente encima de ese underlay para transportar tráfico segmentado y consciente de políticas entre endpoints — el underlay es la base de transporte, el overlay es donde vive la lógica de la fabric.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: When designing network redundancy at the distribution/core layer of a campus, what is the general goal of deploying redundant links and redundant devices together?

options.A: Redundant links and devices are purely a cosmetic requirement with no actual availability benefit
options.B: To intentionally introduce Layer 2 loops that STP can then be tested against during a scheduled maintenance window, verifying that the spanning-tree topology converges correctly before the redundant links are placed into production service
options.C: To eliminate any single point of failure, so that the failure of one link or one device does not disrupt overall connectivity, ideally with automatic failover handled by protocols like STP, FHRP, or dynamic routing
options.D: To ensure that the network requires manual intervention to reroute traffic after every single link failure

questions.explanation_es: El objetivo de desplegar enlaces y dispositivos redundantes es eliminar puntos únicos de falla, de forma que la caída de un enlace o un dispositivo no interrumpa la conectividad general, idealmente con conmutación automática manejada por protocolos como STP, FHRP o enrutamiento dinámico — sin necesitar intervención manual.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What is the relationship between NSF (Non-Stop Forwarding) and SSO (Stateful Switchover)?

options.A: NSF replaces the need for SSO entirely, making SSO obsolete on any modern platform
options.B: NSF works together with SSO: while SSO synchronizes control-plane state between supervisors so a switchover doesn't require a reboot, NSF allows the data plane to continue forwarding packets during that switchover using the last known-good routing information, minimizing packet loss
options.C: NSF only applies to wireless controllers, while SSO only applies to routers
options.D: NSF and SSO are unrelated features that cannot be used together on the same device, because NSF depends on a separate hot-standby routing engine that runs its own independent copy of the routing database rather than sharing state with the active supervisor, requiring the standby engine to rebuild its entire routing table from scratch

questions.explanation_es: NSF y SSO trabajan juntos: SSO sincroniza el estado del plano de control entre supervisoras para que un switchover no requiera reinicio, mientras que NSF permite que el plano de datos siga reenviando paquetes durante ese switchover usando la última información de enrutamiento conocida, minimizando la pérdida de paquetes durante la transición.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: In an HSRP deployment, what does the 'standby' router do while the 'active' router is functioning normally?

options.A: The standby router actively forwards half of the traffic for the group at all times, sharing the load equally with the active router, a load-sharing behavior that some engineers mistakenly assume HSRP inherited from GLBP's multiple Active Virtual Forwarder design
options.B: The standby router monitors the active router's hello messages and is prepared to take over the active role if the active router fails or stops sending hellos, but does not forward traffic for the virtual IP while in standby state
options.C: The standby router is completely powered off until a failover event occurs
options.D: The standby router only monitors DNS server reachability and has no role related to gateway redundancy

questions.explanation_es: El router en estado Standby monitorea los mensajes hello del Active y está listo para asumir el rol activo si este falla o deja de enviar hellos, pero no reenvía tráfico para la IP virtual mientras está en estado standby — solo un router reenvía tráfico para el grupo HSRP a la vez (a diferencia de GLBP).

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: Which FHRP tracking mechanism allows a router to lower its own HSRP/VRRP priority if a specific uplink interface goes down, encouraging failover to a peer router?

options.A: Interface tracking (e.g., 'standby track' in HSRP), which decrements the local priority by a configured amount when the tracked interface fails, potentially causing another router to become active instead
options.B: Spanning Tree root guard, which blocks any FHRP hello messages received on a non-root port
options.C: VTP pruning, which automatically reassigns the active role based on VLAN database revision numbers
options.D: CDP neighbor discovery, which can be configured to automatically decrement HSRP priority whenever a directly connected CDP neighbor stops sending advertisements

questions.explanation_es: El tracking de interfaz (por ejemplo, 'standby track' en HSRP) permite que un router disminuya su propia prioridad si una interfaz rastreada (típicamente un uplink) cae, lo que puede provocar que otro router con mayor prioridad relativa se vuelva Active — así el failover ocurre no solo si el router entero falla, sino también si pierde conectividad ascendente.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: How many virtual MAC addresses does GLBP typically use for a single group, compared to HSRP?

options.A: GLBP requires a unique virtual MAC per VLAN interface on every router in the network, regardless of group membership, meaning every router must be assigned a distinct virtual MAC even for interfaces not participating in any GLBP group, a hardware allocation requirement that some engineers believe explains why GLBP is deployed less often
options.B: GLBP uses a single shared virtual MAC for the entire group, exactly the same as HSRP, with no per-router distinction
options.C: GLBP does not use any virtual MAC address at all, relying purely on virtual IP addressing
options.D: GLBP can assign up to four different virtual MAC addresses (one per AVF, Active Virtual Forwarder) within a group, allowing different client default gateways to be load-balanced across multiple physical routers, whereas HSRP uses a single virtual MAC shared by only one active forwarder at a time

questions.explanation_es: GLBP puede asignar hasta cuatro MAC virtuales distintas (una por AVF, Active Virtual Forwarder) dentro de un mismo grupo, permitiendo balancear las respuestas ARP del gateway virtual entre varios routers físicos. HSRP, en cambio, usa una única MAC virtual asociada a un solo router activo por vez.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What is the purpose of the HSRP or VRRP 'hello timer' and 'hold timer' (or 'dead timer')?

options.A: The hello timer determines how often the physical link light blinks on the switch port
options.B: The hello timer controls how often status messages are sent between group members, and the hold/dead timer defines how long a peer can go without receiving a hello before declaring the other router dead and initiating failover
options.C: The hold timer must always be set to a value smaller than the hello timer, or the protocol will fail to start, since the router's finite-state machine is designed to reject any configuration where the dead interval is shorter than the hello interval
options.D: Both timers control how often DHCP leases are renewed for end hosts using the virtual gateway

questions.explanation_es: El hello timer controla cada cuánto se envían los mensajes de estado entre los miembros del grupo FHRP, y el hold/dead timer define cuánto tiempo puede pasar sin recibir un hello del peer antes de considerarlo caído e iniciar el failover. Por buena práctica, el hold timer debe ser mayor (típicamente 3-4 veces) que el hello timer.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: Why might a network designer choose to configure multiple HSRP groups across different VLANs, each with a different router as the active gateway, instead of always making the same router active for every VLAN?

options.A: This configuration mainly simplifies troubleshooting by keeping the same router active for all VLANs during a failure event, rather than providing any real load-sharing benefit across uplinks
options.B: HSRP technically requires a different active router for every VLAN, or the protocol will refuse to start
options.C: Doing this disables the ability to use interface tracking on any of the HSRP groups involved
options.D: Distributing the active role across different routers for different VLANs allows the uplink traffic load to be spread more evenly across multiple routers/paths, rather than concentrating all forwarding on a single device

questions.explanation_es: Distribuir el rol Active entre distintos routers para distintas VLANs permite repartir la carga de tráfico de uplink entre varios dispositivos/rutas, en lugar de concentrar todo el reenvío en un solo equipo — una técnica común para aprovechar mejor el ancho de banda disponible en un diseño con dos routers de distribución.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What does it mean for a router to be the VRRP 'IP address owner' in a given VRRP group?

options.A: It means the router has purchased a static public IP address from an internet registry specifically for that VRRP group, a registration requirement distinct from the addressing normally used for a group's virtual IP address, which the router obtains through its own regional internet registry
options.B: It means the router must be physically located in the same rack as every other member of the VRRP group
options.C: It means the router is the only device on the network permitted to send any traffic at all
options.D: It means the router physically owns the actual interface IP address that is also being used as the group's virtual IP address, which affects certain default behaviors such as automatically preempting and responding to ICMP pings sent to the virtual IP

questions.explanation_es: El 'IP address owner' es el router cuya IP real de interfaz coincide con la IP virtual del grupo VRRP. Esto afecta ciertos comportamientos por defecto, como preemption automática y responder directamente a pings ICMP dirigidos a la IP virtual — un concepto propio de VRRP que no existe de la misma forma en HSRP.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: How does a client host typically use an FHRP virtual IP address (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP) in its own configuration?

options.A: FHRP virtual IP addresses can never be used as a default gateway; they exist purely for internal router-to-router communication, with the hello messages exchanged over that address used only to negotiate active/standby role priority
options.B: The client is configured with the FHRP virtual IP address as its default gateway, so it always sends off-subnet traffic to that virtual IP, regardless of which physical router is currently active behind it
options.C: The client must be manually reconfigured with a new default gateway IP address every time an FHRP failover occurs
options.D: The client uses the FHRP virtual IP only for DNS resolution, never as a default gateway

questions.explanation_es: El host cliente se configura con la IP virtual del FHRP como su default gateway, por lo que siempre envía el tráfico fuera de subred a esa IP virtual, sin importar qué router físico esté actualmente activo detrás de ella — esto es justamente lo que hace transparente el failover para los endpoints.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: What potential issue can arise if 'preempt' is enabled on an HSRP group but the returning higher-priority router's uplink is not yet fully converged (e.g., routing protocol still reconverging) when it reclaims the active role?

options.A: This scenario only affects VRRP, and HSRP is immune to it entirely
options.B: The router could become the HSRP active for the group and start receiving traffic for the virtual IP before its own upstream routing is fully functional, potentially causing a brief black-holing of traffic until convergence completes
options.C: Preemption automatically disables itself if the uplink is not fully converged, so this scenario is not possible by design
options.D: No issue can ever occur, since preemption always guarantees a perfectly seamless transition with zero risk under every condition

questions.explanation_es: Si un router con mayor prioridad reclama el rol Active antes de que su propio enrutamiento ascendente haya convergido completamente, puede empezar a recibir tráfico para la IP virtual sin poder reenviarlo correctamente todavía, causando una breve pérdida de tráfico (black-holing) hasta que termine de converger — por eso a veces se retrasa la preemption con temporizadores.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how GLBP achieves load balancing of outbound traffic from clients, given that clients only ever point to a single default gateway IP?

options.A: GLBP cannot perform any load balancing; it only provides simple failover exactly like HSRP
options.B: GLBP achieves load balancing by forcing every client to periodically change its own configured default gateway IP address
options.C: GLBP achieves load balancing by responding to different clients' ARP requests for the virtual IP with different virtual MAC addresses (belonging to different AVFs), so different clients end up sending their traffic to different physical routers even though they share one virtual gateway IP
options.D: GLBP achieves load balancing only by adjusting DHCP lease times for each client

questions.explanation_es: GLBP logra balanceo de carga respondiendo a las solicitudes ARP de distintos clientes con distintas MAC virtuales (correspondientes a distintos AVFs), de forma que distintos clientes terminan enviando su tráfico a distintos routers físicos aunque todos compartan la misma IP virtual de gateway — el 'truco' está en la respuesta ARP, no en la IP.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: Which of these is a valid reason to prefer VRRP over HSRP in a specific network design scenario?

options.A: The environment includes non-Cisco routers that need to participate in the same first-hop redundancy group, requiring an open, multi-vendor standard rather than Cisco's proprietary protocol
options.B: VRRP is the only FHRP that supports more than two routers in a single group
options.C: VRRP provides significantly stronger encryption of user data traffic than HSRP under every configuration, because its advertisement packets are secured using an AES-based cipher suite that HSRP's hello mechanism was never designed to support
options.D: VRRP eliminates the need for any IP addressing on the routers participating in the group

questions.explanation_es: Si el entorno incluye routers de otros fabricantes que necesitan participar del mismo grupo de redundancia de primer salto, se necesita un estándar abierto y multi-vendor como VRRP en lugar del protocolo propietario de Cisco (HSRP) — ese es un motivo válido y común para elegir VRRP.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: Which statement about FHRP authentication (e.g., HSRP or VRRP plaintext or MD5 authentication) is correct?

options.A: FHRP authentication is used to verify that hello/advertisement packets are coming from a legitimate group member, helping prevent a rogue device from injecting itself into the group (e.g., claiming to be the active router) without providing the correct shared key
options.B: FHRP authentication encrypts all user data traffic passing through the virtual gateway, functioning as a full IPsec tunnel between the active and standby routers that also protects every client packet forwarded through the group's virtual IP address, the same way IPsec protects traffic between two VPN peers
options.C: FHRP authentication only works over IPv6 and has no equivalent for IPv4 deployments
options.D: FHRP authentication is mandatory and the protocol cannot start without it configured

questions.explanation_es: La autenticación FHRP (texto plano o MD5) se usa para verificar que los mensajes hello/advertisement provienen de un miembro legítimo del grupo, ayudando a prevenir que un dispositivo no autorizado se inserte en el grupo (por ejemplo, haciéndose pasar por el router activo) sin conocer la clave compartida correcta.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: In Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, what does OMP (Overlay Management Protocol) run over between the vSmart controller and WAN Edge routers?

options.A: OMP requires a separate physical out-of-band cable connecting every WAN Edge directly to vSmart
options.B: OMP runs inside a DTLS or TLS-secured control connection between vSmart and each WAN Edge, similar in spirit to how BGP runs over TCP between peers
options.C: OMP runs directly over raw unencrypted UDP with no session-layer protection
options.D: OMP only operates over satellite links and cannot function over standard MPLS or broadband transport, because those transports lack the specific latency profile that OMP was originally tuned for

questions.explanation_es: OMP corre dentro de una conexión de control asegurada con DTLS o TLS entre vSmart y cada WAN Edge, de forma conceptualmente similar a cómo BGP corre sobre TCP entre peers — esto protege el intercambio de rutas, TLOCs y políticas del overlay.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is a TLOC (Transport Locator) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN terminology?

options.A: A TLOC identifies a specific transport attachment point on a WAN Edge router (combining its system IP, color, and encapsulation), used to represent where and how that router can be reached over a given underlay transport
options.B: A TLOC refers to the geographic GPS coordinates of a branch site
options.C: A TLOC is a licensing token required before a WAN Edge router can boot for the first time
options.D: A TLOC is the physical MAC address burned into every WAN Edge router's motherboard

questions.explanation_es: Un TLOC identifica un punto específico de conexión de transporte en un WAN Edge (combinando su system-ip, el 'color' del transporte y la encapsulación), representando dónde y cómo se puede alcanzar ese router sobre un underlay de transporte determinado — es una pieza clave que OMP distribuye para armar el overlay.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What does the 'color' attribute assigned to a TLOC represent in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN?

options.A: A field that determines the physical LED color displayed on the router's chassis
options.B: A field that determines the DSCP marking applied to packets leaving that TLOC, used by intermediate service providers to prioritize traffic but not itself evaluated by centralized policy on vSmart
options.C: A field that selects which IPsec cipher suite (such as AES-256 versus AES-128) is used for the DTLS/TLS control connection to that TLOC, independent of the underlying transport type, and renegotiated automatically each time the WAN Edge re-establishes its control connection to vSmart
options.D: A tag identifying the type/identity of the underlying transport (e.g., mpls, biz-internet, lte, public-internet), which can be used in centralized policy to influence path selection, restrict certain traffic to certain transports, or control which TLOCs form control connections with each other

questions.explanation_es: El 'color' de un TLOC identifica el tipo/identidad del transporte subyacente (por ejemplo, mpls, biz-internet, lte, public-internet). Se usa en políticas centralizadas para influir en la selección de camino, restringir cierto tráfico a ciertos transportes, o controlar qué TLOCs forman conexiones de control entre sí.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: Which SD-WAN controller component is primarily responsible for storing and analyzing historical performance data and providing predictive analytics (in deployments that include it)?

options.A: vAnalytics (or an equivalent analytics/telemetry component), which collects and analyzes network and application performance data over time to provide insights, trends, and predictive recommendations beyond real-time monitoring
options.B: The WAN Edge router's local flash storage, which is the sole location where all analytics are permanently retained
options.C: vSmart, since analytics is a core function of the control-plane protocol itself
options.D: vBond, since it is responsible for all historical data storage in every SD-WAN deployment

questions.explanation_es: vAnalytics (o un componente de analítica/telemetría equivalente) recopila y analiza datos históricos de rendimiento de red y aplicaciones a lo largo del tiempo, ofreciendo insights, tendencias y recomendaciones predictivas más allá del monitoreo en tiempo real que ya provee vManage.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: In a typical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN control-plane sequence, what is the general order in which a new WAN Edge router establishes connectivity to the overlay?

options.A: The WAN Edge first contacts vBond for initial authentication and orchestration (including learning about vSmart/vManage), then establishes secure control connections to vSmart and vManage, and finally begins exchanging OMP routes
options.B: The WAN Edge only ever contacts vSmart, and vBond/vManage play no role in the onboarding process
options.C: The WAN Edge must be manually pre-configured with every other WAN Edge's IP address before it can join the overlay
options.D: The WAN Edge contacts vManage directly first with no prior orchestration step, skipping vBond and vSmart entirely

questions.explanation_es: Típicamente el WAN Edge primero contacta a vBond para autenticación inicial y orquestación (incluyendo aprender sobre vSmart/vManage), luego establece conexiones de control seguras hacia vSmart y vManage, y finalmente comienza a intercambiar rutas OMP — vBond actúa como el punto de entrada inicial al overlay.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: Why is vBond often deployed with a publicly reachable IP address, even when vSmart and vManage may sit behind NAT or in a private address space?

options.A: Because vBond needs to be reachable by every new/unknown WAN Edge device across the internet (often from behind NAT at a branch site) so it can perform initial orchestration and help with NAT traversal, before those devices have learned how to reach the other controllers
options.B: Because a public IP address is a licensing requirement unrelated to any functional need
options.C: vBond is never deployed with a public IP address ; this scenario does not occur in practice
options.D: Because vBond is the only controller that requires internet access to receive periodic software updates, while vManage and vSmart instead receive their software images through an out-of-band USB transfer process shipped physically to each site, bypassing the need for any network-based transport entirely

questions.explanation_es: vBond necesita ser alcanzable por cualquier WAN Edge nuevo/desconocido a través de internet (a menudo detrás de NAT en la sucursal) para realizar la orquestación inicial y ayudar con el traspaso de NAT, antes de que esos dispositivos hayan aprendido cómo alcanzar a los demás controladores — por eso suele tener una IP pública alcanzable.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: How many vSmart controllers are typically deployed in a production Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN environment, and why?

options.A: Typically two or more vSmart controllers are deployed for redundancy, so that the loss of a single vSmart controller does not disrupt the control plane's ability to distribute OMP routing and policy information to WAN Edge routers
options.B: vSmart controllers are never deployed redundantly because OMP itself provides all necessary control-plane redundancy without needing multiple controllers, since each WAN Edge caches the last-received route table locally and can continue operating indefinitely without a controller
options.C: Exactly one vSmart controller per individual WAN Edge router, requiring as many vSmarts as there are branch sites
options.D: Exactly one vSmart controller only, since the architecture technically forbids deploying more than one

questions.explanation_es: Típicamente se despliegan dos o más controladores vSmart por redundancia, de forma que la pérdida de un vSmart no interrumpa la capacidad del plano de control de distribuir rutas OMP y políticas a los WAN Edge — un principio básico de alta disponibilidad en el diseño de controladores de SD-WAN.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: In Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, what is a 'localized policy' as opposed to a 'centralized policy'?

options.A: A localized policy can only be applied to vBond, never to any WAN Edge device
options.B: Localized policies are deprecated and no longer supported in any current release of the SD-WAN software
options.C: A localized policy is applied and pushed directly to a specific device's data-plane/control-plane configuration (e.g., ACLs, QoS, routing policy on that device), as opposed to a centralized policy which shapes overlay-wide routing/topology behavior via vSmart
options.D: A localized policy and a centralized policy are exactly the same concept, differing only in naming convention between different vManage software versions, with the terminology having simply changed after the platform's rebrand from Viptela to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, a rename that took effect company-wide

questions.explanation_es: Una política localizada se aplica y empuja directamente a la configuración de un dispositivo específico (por ejemplo, ACLs, QoS, política de enrutamiento local en ese router), a diferencia de una política centralizada que moldea el comportamiento de enrutamiento/topología de todo el overlay a través de vSmart.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: Which statement about the data plane in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN is correct regarding how WAN Edge routers protect traffic between sites?

options.A: WAN Edge routers can only exchange traffic via GRE tunnels with no encryption capability
options.B: Data-plane encryption in SD-WAN is handled by vManage, with WAN Edge routers having no role in encrypting or decrypting traffic
options.C: WAN Edge routers exchange traffic between sites in plaintext by default, with encryption being an optional add-on that is rarely used in practice, similar to how a plain GRE tunnel operates without IPsec unless separately configured
options.D: WAN Edge routers establish IPsec tunnels between each other (built and keyed using information distributed via OMP/vSmart) to protect data-plane traffic as it crosses the underlay transport between sites

questions.explanation_es: Los WAN Edge establecen túneles IPsec entre sí (construidos y con claves distribuidas vía OMP/vSmart) para proteger el tráfico del plano de datos mientras cruza el transporte del underlay entre sitios — la seguridad del data plane es una función distribuida entre los propios WAN Edges, no centralizada en un solo dispositivo.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is a common deployment option for vManage, vSmart, and vBond controllers in terms of hosting location?

options.A: Controllers can only run as a mobile application installed on an administrator's personal smartphone
options.B: Controllers must be deployed as a single combined virtual machine running vManage, vSmart, and vBond together as one integrated process on customer premises
options.C: Controllers can only ever be deployed as physical hardware appliances shipped directly to the customer's headquarters, with no cloud-hosted option available, since cloud hosting was reserved solely for the Meraki product line
options.D: Controllers are commonly hosted either in a cloud-hosted model managed by Cisco, or on-premises/self-hosted as virtual machines within the customer's own data center, depending on the organization's requirements

questions.explanation_es: Los controladores suelen alojarse ya sea en un modelo hospedado en la nube gestionado por Cisco, o de forma on-premises/auto-alojada como máquinas virtuales dentro del propio data center del cliente, según los requisitos de la organización (regulatorios, de control, etc.).

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What role does the WAN Edge router's local configuration (as opposed to controller-pushed policy) typically still play in a Catalyst SD-WAN deployment?

options.A: WAN Edge routers download their entire configuration fresh from vBond on every single reboot, discarding all controller-pushed policy each time, since vBond is treated as the sole persistent configuration repository during any period of prolonged controller unavailability
options.B: WAN Edge routers download their entire configuration fresh from vBond on every single reboot, discarding all controller-pushed policy each time
options.C: WAN Edge routers still maintain some local device-specific configuration (such as interface settings, local system parameters, or device templates applied via vManage), which works alongside centrally-pushed policy rather than being fully replaced by it
options.D: Local configuration on a WAN Edge router is only relevant for wireless access points, never for the router's own routing behavior

questions.explanation_es: Los WAN Edge mantienen cierta configuración local específica del dispositivo (ajustes de interfaz, parámetros locales del sistema, o plantillas de dispositivo aplicadas vía vManage), que trabaja junto con la política empujada centralmente en lugar de ser completamente reemplazada por ella.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: Which statement best describes how a WAN Edge router determines which remote WAN Edge TLOCs it should attempt to build BFD sessions and data-plane tunnels with?

options.A: WAN Edge routers determine tunnel peers purely at random, with no influence from any controller
options.B: A WAN Edge router builds a data-plane tunnel and BFD session to literally every other TLOC that has ever existed anywhere on the internet
options.C: vSmart, guided by centralized control policy, determines and advertises via OMP which TLOCs a given WAN Edge should learn about and establish connections/tunnels with, effectively controlling the resulting overlay topology (full mesh, hub-and-spoke, etc.)
options.D: Each WAN Edge router must be manually configured with the exact IP address of every other WAN Edge router it should ever connect to, since vSmart plays no role in this decision at all, requiring administrators to maintain static peer lists by hand as sites are added or removed

questions.explanation_es: vSmart, guiado por la política de control centralizada, determina y anuncia vía OMP qué TLOCs debe conocer un WAN Edge determinado y con cuáles debe establecer conexiones/túneles, controlando efectivamente la topología resultante del overlay (malla completa, hub-and-spoke, etc.) sin necesidad de configuración manual por sitio.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) used for between WAN Edge routers in an SD-WAN data-plane tunnel?

options.A: BFD is used to negotiate the initial IPsec encryption keys between two WAN Edge routers
options.B: BFD replaces the need for any IP addressing on WAN Edge transport interfaces
options.C: BFD is used to rapidly detect data-plane path failures or degraded conditions (such as high loss/latency) between two WAN Edge tunnel endpoints, enabling fast failover to an alternate path, faster than relying solely on higher-level routing protocol timers
options.D: BFD only operates between vManage and a single WAN Edge router, never between two WAN Edge routers directly, since path liveness between WAN Edges is instead inferred solely from OMP route withdrawal timers, relying on the same 30-second default hold-down used by OSPF and EIGRP neighbor adjacencies

questions.explanation_es: BFD se usa para detectar rápidamente fallas o condiciones degradadas (alta pérdida/latencia) en el camino del plano de datos entre dos extremos de túnel WAN Edge, permitiendo una conmutación rápida hacia un camino alternativo — mucho más rápido que depender únicamente de los temporizadores de un protocolo de enrutamiento de capa superior.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: Why does Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN separate the control plane (vSmart/OMP) from the data plane (WAN Edge-to-WAN Edge tunnels), similar in philosophy to how traditional SDN architectures separate control and data planes?

options.A: This separation exists only to comply with a specific national telecommunications regulation and serves no technical purpose otherwise
options.B: This separation is purely a marketing distinction with no actual architectural or operational significance
options.C: vSmart terminates the IPsec data tunnels between sites and forwards the decrypted traffic onward toward each WAN Edge router's LAN interface, meaning the control plane still participates directly in per-packet data forwarding
options.D: Separating control and data planes allows routing/policy decisions to be centralized and managed consistently from vSmart, while the actual forwarding of user traffic remains distributed across WAN Edge routers, avoiding a single point of failure for data forwarding and improving scalability of policy management

questions.explanation_es: Separar el plano de control (vSmart/OMP) del plano de datos (túneles WAN Edge a WAN Edge) permite centralizar y gestionar las decisiones de enrutamiento/política de forma consistente desde vSmart, mientras el reenvío real del tráfico de usuario permanece distribuido entre los WAN Edge, evitando un punto único de falla para el forwarding y mejorando la escalabilidad de la gestión de políticas.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How does application-aware routing in SD-WAN typically benefit a business-critical application such as VoIP or video conferencing?

options.A: Application-aware routing can continuously monitor per-tunnel metrics like loss, latency, and jitter, and dynamically steer a specific application's traffic toward whichever available path currently meets that application's defined SLA, rather than using a single static path regardless of quality
options.B: Application-aware routing requires disabling all encryption for the application being prioritized
options.C: Application-aware routing eliminates the need for any WAN bandwidth at each site
options.D: Application-aware routing only works for file transfer protocols and has no effect on real-time applications like VoIP, because real-time UDP flows are classified generically as best-effort traffic by the underlying transport and cannot be individually matched by the application-recognition engine that SD-WAN policy relies on

questions.explanation_es: El enrutamiento consciente de aplicación monitorea continuamente métricas por túnel (pérdida, latencia, jitter) y puede dirigir dinámicamente el tráfico de una aplicación específica hacia el camino disponible que actualmente cumpla el SLA definido para ella, en vez de usar siempre un único camino estático sin importar su calidad actual.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What is a realistic operational limitation to consider when using low-cost broadband internet as a transport in an SD-WAN design, compared to a traditional MPLS circuit?

options.A: Broadband internet transport requires a completely separate WAN Edge hardware platform from MPLS transport, since a standard WAN Edge router cannot terminate a broadband circuit directly
options.B: Broadband internet transport typically comes with no SLA (or a much weaker one) from the ISP regarding bandwidth, latency, or uptime, compared to a carrier-backed MPLS circuit, so application-aware routing and redundancy across multiple transports become more important to compensate
options.C: Broadband internet transport always costs strictly more than an equivalent MPLS circuit in every market and every country
options.D: SD-WAN cannot technically function over broadband internet

questions.explanation_es: El internet de banda ancha suele venir sin SLA (o con uno mucho más débil) del ISP respecto a ancho de banda, latencia o disponibilidad, comparado con un circuito MPLS respaldado por el carrier — por eso el enrutamiento consciente de aplicación y la redundancia entre múltiples transportes se vuelven más importantes para compensar esa incertidumbre.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why is centralized, template-based device configuration considered a significant operational benefit of SD-WAN compared to manually configuring each branch router's CLI individually?

options.A: Template-based configuration guarantees that no branch site will ever experience an outage
options.B: Templates eliminate the need for any IP addressing plan across the organization
options.C: Templates are purely a cosmetic feature of the vManage GUI with no actual configuration impact on the underlying devices, since the actual running configuration on each WAN Edge router must still be entered manually through the CLI, with the template serving only as a visual record of intended settings
options.D: Templates let an administrator define configuration once and apply it consistently across many devices, reducing manual configuration errors and the time needed to provision or update a large number of branch sites, compared to logging into and configuring each router's CLI one at a time

questions.explanation_es: Las plantillas permiten definir la configuración una sola vez y aplicarla de forma consistente en muchos dispositivos, reduciendo errores de configuración manual y el tiempo necesario para aprovisionar o actualizar un gran número de sitios, en comparación con entrar al CLI de cada router uno por uno.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What is a legitimate concern regarding the SD-WAN controllers (vManage, vSmart, vBond) representing a form of centralized dependency in the architecture?

options.A: If any controller goes down for even one second, every single WAN Edge router immediately loses all connectivity to every other WAN Edge instantly and permanently, because the IPsec tunnels between WAN Edge routers are re-keyed continuously through vSmart and cannot remain established without an active control connection refreshing their security associations every few seconds.
options.B: There is no such concern; centralizing control has literally zero downside in any SD-WAN design
options.C: Controller unavailability has no effect on the network at all, since WAN Edge routers do not depend on controllers in any meaningful case
options.D: Because vSmart distributes routing/policy and vManage handles configuration and monitoring, sustained unavailability of these controllers can impair the ability to make new configuration changes or have new routing/policy changes take effect, even though already-established WAN Edge data-plane tunnels generally continue forwarding traffic independently for some time

questions.explanation_es: Dado que vSmart distribuye enrutamiento/política y vManage maneja configuración y monitoreo, la falta de disponibilidad sostenida de estos controladores puede afectar la capacidad de hacer nuevos cambios de configuración o que nuevos cambios de política surtan efecto, aunque los túneles de datos ya establecidos entre WAN Edges generalmente sigan reenviando tráfico de forma independiente por un tiempo — de ahí la importancia de desplegar controladores redundantes.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How can SD-WAN's transport-independent design help an organization during a migration away from an expensive legacy MPLS circuit?

options.A: SD-WAN requires MPLS to be present at every site and cannot function if MPLS is removed
options.B: Because SD-WAN can run its overlay across any mix of transports, an organization can gradually introduce broadband/LTE alongside or instead of MPLS at each site, migrating transport-by-transport or site-by-site without having to redesign the entire overlay policy each time
options.C: SD-WAN transport independence means the organization no longer needs any physical WAN circuit at all, because the overlay fabric is assumed to establish tunnels directly over the public internet backbone using bandwidth provided inherently by the WAN Edge router's software license even on entirely unmanaged connections.
options.D: Transport independence only applies to data centers and has no relevance to branch site migrations

questions.explanation_es: Como SD-WAN puede correr su overlay sobre cualquier combinación de transportes, una organización puede introducir gradualmente banda ancha/LTE junto con o en reemplazo del MPLS en cada sitio, migrando transporte por transporte o sitio por sitio sin tener que rediseñar toda la política del overlay cada vez — una ventaja concreta de la independencia de transporte.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What operational skill-set shift does adopting SD-WAN typically require from a networking team accustomed to purely traditional box-by-box router configuration?

options.A: Teams typically need to build familiarity with controller-based/centralized policy concepts, templates, and the overlay's control-plane abstractions (like OMP, TLOCs, and centralized policy), in addition to (not instead of) traditional networking fundamentals
options.B: SD-WAN requires the entire team to become expert C++ software developers before any configuration can be performed
options.C: No shift is required at all; SD-WAN configuration is byte-for-byte identical to traditional router CLI configuration with no new concepts involved
options.D: SD-WAN eliminates the need for networking staff to understand IP addressing or routing concepts ever again

questions.explanation_es: Los equipos suelen necesitar familiarizarse con conceptos de política centralizada/basada en controlador, plantillas, y las abstracciones del plano de control del overlay (OMP, TLOCs, política centralizada), además de (no en reemplazo de) los fundamentos tradicionales de networking — es un salto de habilidades real a considerar en la adopción.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why might Direct Internet Access (DIA) combined with local security inspection at the branch (SD-WAN 'secure branch' design) be preferred over backhauling all internet-bound traffic to a central data center for inspection?

options.A: Backhauling is always not supported to configure in an SD-WAN environment
options.B: DIA with local security inspection avoids adding the extra latency and WAN bandwidth cost of backhauling every SaaS/internet request through a central hub, which can meaningfully improve the user experience for cloud applications, provided adequate security controls are deployed at each branch
options.C: Backhauling internet traffic to a central site always provides lower latency than accessing the internet locally at the branch, because the central data center's internet edge is provisioned with a higher-bandwidth circuit than any individual branch could economically justify on its own, offsetting the additional latency of the backhaul path
options.D: DIA eliminates the need for any firewall or security inspection anywhere in the network

questions.explanation_es: El acceso directo a internet (DIA) con inspección de seguridad local evita agregar la latencia extra y el costo de ancho de banda WAN de retroceder cada solicitud SaaS/internet hacia un hub central, lo cual puede mejorar notablemente la experiencia de usuario para aplicaciones en la nube, siempre que se desplieguen controles de seguridad adecuados en cada sucursal.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What is a potential risk of enabling Direct Internet Access (DIA) at many branch sites without adequate local security controls?

options.A: DIA automatically disables all encryption for every application at the branch
options.B: DIA can only be enabled if the branch site has zero users connected to it
options.C: There is no risk; DIA is always strictly safer than centralized internet access under every circumstance, because each branch firewall automatically inherits the same threat-intelligence feed and IPS signature set as the central data center edge without any separate licensing or update process.
options.D: DIA with weak local security expands the organization's attack surface, since each branch now has its own path to the internet that must be independently secured (e.g., firewall, DNS security, malware inspection), rather than relying on a single, more heavily fortified central internet edge

questions.explanation_es: Habilitar DIA sin controles de seguridad locales adecuados amplía la superficie de ataque de la organización, ya que cada sucursal pasa a tener su propio camino a internet que debe asegurarse de forma independiente (firewall, seguridad DNS, inspección de malware), en vez de depender de un único borde de internet central más fortificado.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How does SD-WAN's ability to define policy centrally help with consistent security segmentation across many branch offices?
