options.A: Centralized policy defines segmentation only at the transport layer by assigning different TLOC colors to each VRF, rather than through actual VPN/VRF-based separation of the traffic itself
options.B: A segmentation policy (e.g., isolating guest traffic from corporate traffic via VPN/VRF segmentation) can be defined once centrally and pushed consistently to every site, rather than requiring an administrator to manually replicate the same segmentation configuration correctly on each individual branch router
options.C: Segmentation can only be applied to a single branch at a time and cannot be defined centrally
options.D: Centralized policy requires every branch to have physically separate cabling for each segment, which SD-WAN cannot avoid

questions.explanation_es: Una política de segmentación (por ejemplo, aislar tráfico de invitados del tráfico corporativo vía segmentación VPN/VRF) puede definirse una sola vez de forma centralizada y aplicarse de forma consistente a cada sitio, en lugar de requerir que un administrador replique manualmente esa misma configuración de segmentación correctamente en cada router de sucursal.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What total cost of ownership (TCO) benefit does SD-WAN's ability to combine cheaper broadband transport with intelligent path selection commonly offer, compared to relying purely on MPLS?

options.A: SD-WAN always costs more in total than an equivalent pure-MPLS design, with no scenario where it reduces spend
options.B: TCO benefits only apply if an organization completely eliminates all WAN circuits and relies solely on satellite internet
options.C: SD-WAN guarantees that broadband internet will always be technically superior to MPLS in every performance metric with no trade-offs, because the SD-WAN overlay itself allocates dedicated last-mile bandwidth that is functionally equivalent to a carrier SLA, a claim vendors sometimes make when comparing raw throughput benchmarks in isolation
options.D: By blending lower-cost broadband/LTE transport with MPLS (or replacing MPLS at some sites) while using application-aware routing to protect critical traffic, organizations can often reduce overall WAN transport spend while maintaining acceptable performance for important applications

questions.explanation_es: Combinando transporte de menor costo (banda ancha/LTE) con MPLS (o reemplazándolo en algunos sitios) y usando enrutamiento consciente de aplicación para proteger el tráfico crítico, las organizaciones suelen poder reducir el gasto total en transporte WAN manteniendo un rendimiento aceptable para las aplicaciones importantes — un argumento de TCO frecuente a favor de SD-WAN.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why is it important to plan bandwidth and licensing sizing carefully on SD-WAN controllers (especially vManage/vSmart) as the number of managed WAN Edge sites grows significantly?

options.A: Licensing for SD-WAN controllers has nothing to do with the number of WAN Edge devices under management
options.B: Controller sizing is only relevant for the physical color of the rack the controllers are mounted in
options.C: Controller sizing mainly affects how many simultaneous administrator GUI sessions vManage can support, while the OMP route-processing load stays roughly constant regardless of how many WAN Edge sites are added
options.D: As the number of WAN Edge devices, control connections, and routes grows, the controllers require adequate compute/scale sizing to handle the increased control-plane load (OMP route processing, template pushes, telemetry ingestion), or performance and responsiveness can degrade

questions.explanation_es: A medida que crece el número de dispositivos WAN Edge, conexiones de control y rutas, los controladores necesitan un dimensionamiento de cómputo/escala adecuado para manejar la mayor carga del plano de control (procesamiento de rutas OMP, envío de plantillas, ingestión de telemetría), o el rendimiento y la capacidad de respuesta pueden degradarse — una consideración real de diseño al escalar.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What benefit does zero-touch provisioning (ZTP) offer when deploying SD-WAN to many new branch sites?

options.A: ZTP requires an experienced network engineer to be physically on-site at every branch to manually type the full configuration before the device can join the overlay, since the zero-touch process only pre-stages the device's serial number in vBond's whitelist, leaving every routing, interface, and policy setting to be entered by hand
options.B: ZTP allows a WAN Edge device to be shipped to a branch, connected to power and a transport link by non-technical local staff, and then automatically contact vBond/vManage to receive its identity, software, and configuration with minimal or no manual CLI configuration required on-site
options.C: ZTP only functions for wireless access points and has no application to WAN Edge routers
options.D: ZTP eliminates the need for the device to ever have any IP addressing configured, even automatically

questions.explanation_es: El aprovisionamiento sin intervención (ZTP) permite que un dispositivo WAN Edge se envíe a una sucursal, lo conecte a energía y a un enlace de transporte personal no técnico local, y luego contacte automáticamente a vBond/vManage para recibir su identidad, software y configuración con mínima o ninguna configuración manual de CLI en el sitio — un beneficio operativo clave para desplegar muchas sucursales rápidamente.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In Cisco SD-Access, what happens when a wired endpoint first connects to a Fabric Edge Node and sends its first packet?

options.A: The endpoint's traffic is immediately flooded unencapsulated to every other switch in the entire campus
options.B: The Fabric Edge Node authenticates/onboards the endpoint (e.g., via 802.1X or MAB), then registers the endpoint's identity (EID) and location with the Fabric Control Plane node, so other nodes can learn how to reach it
options.C: The endpoint must first manually register itself with the Fabric Control Plane using a dedicated software client installed on the endpoint, similar to how a LISP xTR would register manually before EID-to-RLOC mappings become active
options.D: The Fabric Border Node handles all endpoint registration directly, and the Fabric Edge Node has no role in this process

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Edge Node autentica/incorpora al endpoint (por ejemplo, vía 802.1X o MAB) y luego registra la identidad (EID) y ubicación de ese endpoint ante el Fabric Control Plane node, para que otros nodos de la fabric puedan aprender cómo alcanzarlo — este registro es análogo a cómo un ITR de LISP registra mapeos EID-a-RLOC.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What role does the LISP protocol play specifically in the SD-Access control plane?

options.A: LISP provides the mapping mechanism (EID-to-RLOC) that the Fabric Control Plane node uses to track and resolve where endpoints are currently located within the fabric, similar to how LISP is used in a standalone LISP deployment for identity/location separation
options.B: LISP is used to assign VLAN IDs to fabric-enabled switch ports
options.C: LISP has been fully replaced by BGP EVPN as the control-plane protocol in newer SD-Access fabric software releases, though older releases retain LISP for backward compatibility
options.D: LISP is used only for encrypting data-plane traffic between Fabric Edge Nodes, with no role in the control plane at all, a function that in SD-Access is actually handled separately through a dedicated IPsec tunnel negotiated directly between the two Fabric Edge Nodes themselves

questions.explanation_es: LISP provee el mecanismo de mapeo (EID-a-RLOC) que el Fabric Control Plane node usa para rastrear y resolver dónde está actualmente ubicado un endpoint dentro de la fabric, de forma similar a cómo se usa LISP en un despliegue LISP independiente para separar identidad de ubicación.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: How does SGT (Scalable/Security Group Tag) information get carried across the SD-Access fabric data plane?

options.A: SGT information can only be applied if MACsec encryption is also enabled on every link in the fabric
options.B: SGT information is carried inside the VXLAN header alongside the encapsulated frame, allowing the Fabric Edge Node at the destination to apply SGACL policy based on the source SGT without needing a separate lookup or out-of-band signaling
options.C: SGT information is carried via a separate SNMP trap sent to each Fabric Edge Node for every single packet
options.D: SGT information is never transmitted across the network at all; it exists only as a label in the ISE database and has no bearing on actual forwarded packets, with enforcement instead performed entirely through periodic pxGrid queries made by each Fabric Edge Node

questions.explanation_es: La información de SGT viaja dentro del encabezado VXLAN junto con el frame encapsulado, permitiendo que el Fabric Edge Node en el destino aplique política SGACL basándose en el SGT de origen sin necesitar una consulta separada ni señalización fuera de banda — esto es lo que hace posible la microsegmentación consistente en toda la fabric.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What is the function of the 'Map-Server/Map-Resolver' role within the SD-Access Fabric Control Plane node?

options.A: The Map-Server/Map-Resolver role is solely responsible for issuing DHCP leases to every endpoint in the fabric
options.B: The Map-Server/Map-Resolver role only functions for wireless endpoints and has no relevance to wired endpoints in the fabric
options.C: The Map-Server/Map-Resolver role encrypts all traffic between the Fabric Border Node and external networks
options.D: The Map-Server/Map-Resolver role stores and answers queries about EID-to-RLOC mappings, similar in concept to how a DNS server resolves names to IP addresses, allowing other fabric nodes to discover the current location of any registered endpoint

questions.explanation_es: El rol de Map-Server/Map-Resolver almacena y responde consultas sobre mapeos EID-a-RLOC, de forma conceptualmente similar a cómo un servidor DNS resuelve nombres a direcciones IP, permitiendo que otros nodos de la fabric descubran la ubicación actual de cualquier endpoint registrado.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In SD-Access, what is a 'virtual network' (VN), and how does it relate to a VRF?

options.A: A virtual network is simply another name for an SGT, mapping directly to a security group tag rather than to a separate Layer 3 VRF instance
options.B: A virtual network and a VRF are mutually exclusive concepts that cannot be used together in the same fabric
options.C: A virtual network in SD-Access is a macro-segmentation construct that maps to an underlying VRF instance, providing a fully isolated Layer 3 routing domain (for example, separating a 'Guest' virtual network from an 'Employee' virtual network) on top of which SGT-based micro-segmentation can further be applied within each VN
options.D: A virtual network is used to identify a specific wireless SSID, with no relevance to wired fabric segmentation

questions.explanation_es: Una virtual network (VN) en SD-Access es un constructo de macro-segmentación que se mapea a una instancia VRF subyacente, proveyendo un dominio de enrutamiento de Capa 3 completamente aislado (por ejemplo, separando una VN 'Invitados' de una VN 'Empleados'), sobre el cual además se puede aplicar micro-segmentación basada en SGT dentro de cada VN.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: How does the SD-Access data plane (VXLAN) support carrying Layer 2 traffic across what is fundamentally a routed (Layer 3) underlay?

options.A: VXLAN requires the underlay itself to be a pure Layer 2 network with no routing at all, contradicting SD-Access's routed-access design
options.B: VXLAN cannot carry Layer 2 traffic ; SD-Access data plane traffic is always purely Layer 3
options.C: VXLAN only supports carrying IP multicast traffic and cannot transport regular unicast Ethernet frames
options.D: VXLAN encapsulates the original Ethernet frame (including its Layer 2 header) inside a UDP/IP packet, allowing that Layer 2 frame to be transported across the routed underlay between Fabric Edge Nodes, effectively creating an overlay Layer 2 segment (per VNI) on top of Layer 3 transport

questions.explanation_es: VXLAN encapsula el frame Ethernet original (incluyendo su encabezado de Capa 2) dentro de un paquete UDP/IP, permitiendo que ese frame de Capa 2 se transporte a través del underlay enrutado entre Fabric Edge Nodes, creando efectivamente un segmento Capa 2 de overlay (por VNI) sobre transporte de Capa 3.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What happens from a control-plane perspective when a wired endpoint roams from one Fabric Edge Node to another within the same SD-Access fabric?

options.A: The old Fabric Edge Node continues to receive all traffic for the endpoint indefinitely, with no update ever propagated to the Control Plane node, because RLOC bindings in SD-Access are statically provisioned during fabric onboarding and are not designed to be updated after an endpoint's initial registration
options.B: Roaming is not supported at all for wired endpoints in SD-Access; only wireless clients can move between access points
options.C: The new Fabric Edge Node updates the Fabric Control Plane node with the endpoint's new location (RLOC), so that subsequent traffic destined for that endpoint is directed to the new Fabric Edge Node instead of the old one, without requiring the endpoint to change its own IP address
options.D: The endpoint is forced to obtain a completely new IP address every time it roams to a different Fabric Edge Node

questions.explanation_es: El nuevo Fabric Edge Node actualiza al Fabric Control Plane node con la nueva ubicación (RLOC) del endpoint, de forma que el tráfico subsiguiente dirigido a ese endpoint se enrute hacia el nuevo Fabric Edge Node en lugar del anterior, sin que el endpoint necesite cambiar su propia dirección IP — esto es posible gracias a la separación identidad/ubicación que provee LISP.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: Why does SD-Access use a routed access design (Layer 3 all the way to the Fabric Edge Node) in its underlay, rather than a traditional Layer 2 access-to-distribution design?

options.A: Routed access is used only because it is a mandatory requirement for connecting wireless access points, with no benefit for wired forwarding
options.B: A routed underlay avoids large Layer 2 broadcast domains and STP-related convergence concerns in the underlay, providing fast, predictable IP-based convergence, while all the segmentation/policy flexibility traditionally requiring Layer 2 extension is instead handled by the VXLAN overlay and SGTs
options.C: A routed access design was chosen purely because it requires less IP addressing than a Layer 2 design
options.D: A routed underlay was chosen because Layer 3 protocols cannot experience any form of network loop, making STP entirely irrelevant to the design's benefits

questions.explanation_es: Un underlay enrutado evita dominios de broadcast de Capa 2 grandes y preocupaciones de convergencia relacionadas con STP en el underlay, dando una convergencia rápida y predecible basada en IP, mientras que toda la flexibilidad de segmentación/política que tradicionalmente requería extender Capa 2 la maneja en cambio el overlay VXLAN junto con los SGT.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What is the significance of an 'anycast gateway' in SD-Access, configured identically on every Fabric Edge Node for a given subnet/VN?

options.A: An anycast gateway requires manually configuring a different gateway IP per Fabric Edge Node, defeating the purpose of a consistent addressing scheme
options.B: An anycast gateway means every Fabric Edge Node in the fabric uses the exact same default gateway IP and virtual MAC for a given subnet, allowing an endpoint to roam to any Fabric Edge Node within that subnet's virtual network and keep using the exact same default gateway address, without needing any FHRP protocol like HSRP or VRRP
options.C: Anycast gateway is a wireless-only concept and has no meaning for wired Fabric Edge Nodes
options.D: An anycast gateway refers to a single, physically centralized router that all fabric traffic must always pass through no matter where the endpoint is located, similar to the Border Node's role in aggregating traffic destined outside the fabric before it reaches an external routed network, rather than being distributed identically across every edge switch

questions.explanation_es: El anycast gateway significa que todos los Fabric Edge Node de la fabric usan la misma IP y MAC virtual de gateway para una subred dada, permitiendo que un endpoint pueda estar conectado (o moverse) a cualquier Fabric Edge Node de esa virtual network y seguir usando exactamente la misma dirección de gateway, sin necesitar un protocolo FHRP tradicional como HSRP o VRRP.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: When SD-Access enforces SGACL (Security Group ACL) policy, at which point in the data path is that policy typically enforced?

options.A: SGACL enforcement typically occurs at the egress Fabric Edge Node (closest to the destination endpoint), which evaluates the source SGT carried in the VXLAN header against the destination SGT/policy matrix before forwarding the traffic to the destination
options.B: SGACL enforcement requires a separate physical firewall appliance inserted between every pair of communicating endpoints
options.C: SGACL policy is enforced only at the Fabric Border Node, regardless of where the source and destination endpoints are actually located within the fabric
options.D: SGACL policy is only ever enforced centrally on the Fabric Control Plane node, which physically intercepts every packet before it reaches any Fabric Edge Node

questions.explanation_es: La aplicación de SGACL típicamente ocurre en el Fabric Edge Node de egreso (el más cercano al endpoint destino), que evalúa el SGT de origen transportado en el encabezado VXLAN contra la matriz de política/SGT destino antes de reenviar el tráfico al destino final.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: How does SD-Access typically integrate wireless traffic into the fabric's data plane when using a fabric-enabled Wireless LAN Controller (WLC)?

options.A: Wireless traffic is always sent unencapsulated in plaintext directly onto the underlay with no VXLAN involvement
options.B: Wireless clients must obtain a completely separate, non-fabric IP addressing scheme that is entirely disconnected from the wired fabric's virtual networks, because fabric-enabled APs are only capable of bridging traffic locally onto a dedicated management VLAN that exists outside any of the fabric's defined virtual networks
options.C: Wireless traffic in a fabric-enabled deployment is VXLAN-encapsulated at the fabric-enabled Access Point (or at the Fabric Edge Node it connects through) and carried over the same fabric overlay used for wired traffic, rather than being tunneled back to the WLC using traditional CAPWAP data tunneling
options.D: Wireless traffic can never be integrated into an SD-Access fabric ; SD-Access is a wired-only architecture

questions.explanation_es: En un despliegue con fabric habilitada, el tráfico inalámbrico se encapsula en VXLAN en el access point (o en el Fabric Edge Node al que se conecta) y se transporta sobre el mismo overlay de la fabric usado para tráfico cableado, en lugar de tunelizarse de vuelta al WLC vía CAPWAP tradicional — así unifica el tratamiento de política entre cableado e inalámbrico.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What advantage does separating the control plane (LISP-based mapping) from the data plane (VXLAN forwarding) provide in SD-Access, similar to the general SDN philosophy?

options.A: This separation provides no practical advantage and exists purely for historical/legacy reasons carried over from older Cisco products
options.B: This separation exists only to allow SD-Access to be marketed as 'software-defined' with no actual technical benefit
options.C: This separation means the data plane no longer needs any IP addressing at all
options.D: Separating control and data planes allows endpoint location/identity information to be managed and updated centrally and efficiently (via the Control Plane node), while actual packet forwarding remains distributed and fast at each Fabric Edge Node, avoiding the need for every switch to flood-and-learn or maintain a full picture of every endpoint in the fabric

questions.explanation_es: Separar el plano de control (mapeo basado en LISP) del plano de datos (reenvío VXLAN) permite gestionar y actualizar la información de identidad/ubicación de endpoints de forma centralizada y eficiente (vía el Control Plane node), mientras el reenvío real de paquetes permanece distribuido y rápido en cada Fabric Edge Node, evitando que cada switch tenga que hacer flood-and-learn o mantener una imagen completa de cada endpoint de la fabric.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When an SD-Access fabric needs to advertise its internal virtual network subnets to a traditional routed core outside the fabric, what typically happens at the Fabric Border Node?

options.A: The Border Node requires every external router to run LISP natively before any interoperability is possible
options.B: The Border Node redistributes or advertises the fabric's VXLAN-encapsulated routes into standard IP routing (e.g., via BGP or OSPF) toward the external network, translating the fabric's internal reachability information into a form the traditional routed network understands
options.C: The Border Node simply drops all traffic destined for any address outside the fabric, since fabrics are designed to be fully isolated from external networks by default, requiring a separate non-fabric device that is provisioned and maintained completely independently of the fabric's own control-plane infrastructure
options.D: The Border Node converts all external traffic into VXLAN before it even reaches the fabric boundary, regardless of whether the external device supports VXLAN

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node redistribuye o anuncia las rutas internas de la fabric (VXLAN) hacia el enrutamiento IP estándar (por ejemplo, vía BGP u OSPF) hacia la red externa, traduciendo la información de alcanzabilidad interna de la fabric a una forma que la red enrutada tradicional entienda — es el punto de traducción entre ambos mundos.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why is a Fusion Router (or Fusion Firewall) often needed when SD-Access virtual networks (VRFs) need to communicate with resources in a shared services VRF or the traditional network's global routing table?

options.A: VRFs are isolated from each other and from the global routing table by design; a Fusion device performs controlled route leaking (importing/exporting routes) between the VRFs and the external network, since simply attaching them to the same Border Node does not automatically merge their routing tables
options.B: A Fusion Router is required only when the fabric has exactly one virtual network configured, and becomes unnecessary once a second VN is added
options.C: Fusion Routers exist purely to physically convert copper cabling into fiber cabling at the fabric boundary
options.D: A Fusion Router is needed only to relay DHCP requests between virtual networks, since attaching multiple VRFs to the same Border Node is otherwise enough to automatically merge their routing tables for all other traffic

questions.explanation_es: Las VRFs están aisladas entre sí y de la tabla de enrutamiento global por diseño; un dispositivo Fusion realiza route leaking controlado (importando/exportando rutas) entre las VRFs y la red externa, ya que simplemente conectarlas al mismo Border Node no fusiona automáticamente sus tablas de enrutamiento.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: How can SGT information be preserved when traffic needs to leave the SD-Access fabric and cross a segment of traditional (non-fabric) network before reaching another fabric-aware or ISE-integrated device?

options.A: SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) can be used to propagate IP-address-to-SGT bindings to devices that lack inline SGT tagging support, allowing policy enforcement to be extended (in a limited, IP-binding-based way) even across parts of the network that don't natively carry SGTs in the data plane
options.B: SGT information can only be preserved by re-encapsulating traffic into a new VXLAN tunnel across the non-fabric segment, since SXP is limited to propagating SGT bindings within a single fabric site and cannot extend into traditional network segments
options.C: SGT information can only be preserved if the entire traditional network segment is physically replaced with fabric-capable switches first
options.D: SGT information is automatically converted into a VLAN ID whenever it crosses into a non-fabric segment, with no configuration required

questions.explanation_es: SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) permite propagar los bindings de IP-a-SGT hacia dispositivos que no soportan tagging inline de SGT, permitiendo extender la aplicación de política (de forma limitada, basada en bindings de IP) incluso a través de partes de la red que no transportan SGTs nativamente en el plano de datos.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: In a phased SD-Access migration, why might an organization choose to migrate by 'IP pool' rather than migrating an entire physical site all at once?

options.A: IP pool-based migration requires renumbering the entire campus to a single subnet before any migration can begin
options.B: IP pool-based migration is purely a licensing requirement with no operational reasoning behind it
options.C: IP pools are only relevant to wireless clients and have no bearing on how wired migration is phased
options.D: Migrating by IP pool allows specific groups of endpoints (e.g., a particular department or VLAN's address range) to be moved into the fabric incrementally, limiting the blast radius and complexity of each migration step, while other pools continue operating on the traditional network until they too are migrated

questions.explanation_es: Migrar por IP pool permite mover grupos específicos de endpoints (por ejemplo, el rango de direcciones de un departamento o VLAN en particular) a la fabric de forma incremental, limitando el radio de impacto y la complejidad de cada paso de migración, mientras el resto sigue operando en la red tradicional hasta que también se migre.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What consideration is important when connecting a traditional Layer 2 access switch (non-fabric) to a Fabric Edge Node as part of an interoperability/migration design?

options.A: Connecting a traditional switch to a Fabric Edge Node automatically disables SGACL enforcement fabric-wide
options.B: The traditional switch's VLANs and trunking need to be properly mapped/extended to correspond with the correct IP pools and virtual networks configured on the fabric side, since the traditional switch itself has no awareness of VXLAN, SGTs, or the fabric's LISP control plane
options.C: Traditional switches can never be connected to a Fabric Edge Node ; only fabric-capable hardware may connect there
options.D: No special consideration is needed at all; a traditional switch can be plugged directly into a Fabric Edge Node with zero configuration and instantly gains full fabric capabilities, including VXLAN encapsulation, automatically

questions.explanation_es: Las VLANs y el trunking del switch tradicional deben mapearse/extenderse correctamente para corresponder con los IP pools y virtual networks configurados del lado de la fabric, ya que el switch tradicional en sí no tiene conocimiento de VXLAN, SGTs, ni del plano de control LISP de la fabric — la traducción ocurre en el Fabric Edge Node al que se conecta.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why is it generally recommended to plan IP addressing/subnetting carefully before beginning an SD-Access migration from a traditional network?

options.A: Careful IP planning is only necessary if the organization plans to use IPv6, with no relevance to IPv4-only deployments
options.B: SD-Access typically maps subnets to IP pools associated with specific virtual networks, so a clean, well-planned addressing scheme makes it easier to logically group endpoints into the correct virtual networks and simplifies the eventual mapping between legacy VLANs/subnets and fabric IP pools
options.C: IP addressing has little bearing on SD-Access migration planning, since the fabric automatically renumbers every device transparently with zero pre-planning required, drawing new addresses on demand from a default pool shared across every virtual network in the fabric, with no coordination against the legacy VLAN plan required
options.D: IP addressing only matters for wireless clients in an SD-Access deployment and has no relevance to wired endpoint migration

questions.explanation_es: SD-Access típicamente mapea subredes a IP pools asociados a virtual networks específicas, así que un esquema de direccionamiento limpio y bien planeado facilita agrupar lógicamente a los endpoints en la virtual network correcta y simplifica el mapeo eventual entre VLANs/subredes legacy y los IP pools de la fabric.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What role can a traditional distribution-layer switch play temporarily during a phased migration, before it is eventually replaced or converted into a Fabric Border/Edge role?

options.A: A traditional distribution switch must be physically powered off the instant any part of the campus begins migrating to SD-Access, with no coexistence period possible
options.B: A traditional distribution switch can only interoperate with the fabric if it is manually added as an unmanaged Fabric Edge Node within Catalyst Center, rather than simply connecting to the Border Node in its existing role
options.C: It can continue serving non-migrated access switches and VLANs exactly as before, connecting into the fabric via the Border Node so that migrated and non-migrated portions of the campus remain interconnected throughout the transition period
options.D: Traditional distribution switches automatically gain full SD-Access fabric awareness the moment SD-Access is enabled anywhere in the campus, with no configuration required, through an automatic discovery process broadcast by the Fabric Control Plane node

questions.explanation_es: Un switch de distribución tradicional puede seguir sirviendo a los switches de acceso y VLANs aún no migrados exactamente como antes, conectándose a la fabric a través del Border Node, de forma que las porciones migradas y no migradas del campus permanezcan interconectadas durante todo el período de transición.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When extending shared services (such as DNS, DHCP, or an ISE server) that live in the traditional network's global routing table to be reachable from within SD-Access virtual networks, what is a common design approach?

options.A: Shared services can only be reached by manually connecting a physical Ethernet cable from every access switch directly to the DHCP server
options.B: Shared services become reachable by extending each virtual network's VRF directly onto the same VLAN as the global routing table, merging the two broadcast domains at Layer 2 so that DHCP relay alone provides connectivity without any Fusion device or route import/export configuration
options.C: Route leaking is configured (often via a Fusion device or route-target import/export) so that each virtual network's VRF can reach the shared services subnet in the global table, without fully merging every VN's routing table together
options.D: Shared services must be physically duplicated and re-hosted separately inside every single virtual network, since cross-VN or cross-VRF reachability is not supported under any configuration

questions.explanation_es: Se configura route leaking (a menudo vía un dispositivo Fusion o import/export de route-targets) para que la VRF de cada virtual network pueda alcanzar la subred de servicios compartidos en la tabla global, sin fusionar completamente la tabla de enrutamiento de cada VN — un patrón de diseño común para servicios como DNS, DHCP o ISE.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What is a key reason SD-Access migrations are typically done incrementally rather than as a single 'flash cut' across an entire large campus?

options.A: An incremental approach limits risk by validating fabric behavior, policy, and interoperability on a smaller scale first, allows lessons learned to inform later phases, and reduces the potential impact/blast radius if an issue is discovered, compared to converting an entire large campus in one maintenance window
options.B: Incremental migration is required because SD-Access fabrics are limited to a maximum of exactly one switch per fabric, so every additional switch must be onboarded as a completely separate fabric site with its own dedicated Control Plane and Border Node pair rather than joining an existing one, and cannot be added as a member of that site's existing switch stack.
options.C: Flash-cut migrations are not supported for any Cisco product due to a hard-coded software limitation
options.D: Incremental migration is purely a marketing recommendation with no real operational benefit over a single flash cut

questions.explanation_es: Un enfoque incremental limita el riesgo al validar el comportamiento de la fabric, la política y la interoperabilidad a menor escala primero, permite que las lecciones aprendidas informen fases posteriores, y reduce el impacto potencial si se descubre un problema, comparado con convertir todo un campus grande en una sola ventana de mantenimiento.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: How does a Fabric Border Node typically handle a default route or 'internet-bound' traffic originating from inside the SD-Access fabric?

options.A: Internet-bound traffic from inside the fabric is always silently dropped, since fabrics have no concept of a default route by design
options.B: The Border Node commonly advertises a default route (or specific external routes) into the fabric's control plane, so that internal fabric traffic destined for unknown/external destinations (like the internet) is directed toward the Border Node for handoff to the traditional network/internet edge
options.C: The Border Node requires every endpoint to manually configure its own static default route pointing directly at an ISP router
options.D: Every individual Fabric Edge Node must have its own direct physical connection to the internet, with no role for the Border Node in internet connectivity at all, requiring a separate ISP handoff to be provisioned at every wiring closet throughout the campus, since Border Nodes are assumed to only handle traffic already destined for known internal prefixes

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node comúnmente anuncia una ruta default (o rutas externas específicas) hacia el plano de control de la fabric, de forma que el tráfico interno de la fabric destinado a destinos desconocidos/externos (como internet) se dirija hacia el Border Node para su entrega hacia la red tradicional/borde de internet.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why might an organization deploy more than one Fabric Border Node in an SD-Access design that interoperates with a traditional network?

options.A: Deploying redundant Border Nodes avoids a single point of failure for external/interoperability connectivity, so the fabric can continue reaching external networks and shared services even if one Border Node fails or needs maintenance
options.B: Multiple Border Nodes are required purely to increase the total VLAN ID range available anywhere in the fabric
options.C: Multiple Border Nodes exist solely to allow different wireless SSIDs to be broadcast from different physical locations
options.D: A fabric can technically have only one Border Node ever, so 'multiple Border Nodes' is not a real deployment option in SD-Access

questions.explanation_es: Desplegar Border Nodes redundantes evita un punto único de falla para la conectividad externa/de interoperabilidad, de forma que la fabric pueda seguir alcanzando redes externas y servicios compartidos aunque un Border Node falle o requiera mantenimiento — un patrón de alta disponibilidad habitual en diseños de producción.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the DiffServ (Differentiated Services) QoS model, as opposed to IntServ (Integrated Services)?

options.A: DiffServ requires every router along the path to reserve dedicated bandwidth for every individual flow before any traffic can be sent, exactly like IntServ, using the same RSVP signaling messages to establish and maintain each flow's reservation state hop by hop, requiring the same per-flow admission control that makes IntServ difficult to scale
options.B: DiffServ only applies to wireless networks and has no relevance to wired QoS design
options.C: DiffServ classifies and marks traffic into a small number of forwarding classes (using DSCP) and applies per-hop behaviors at each device, providing scalable QoS without requiring per-flow signaling or reservation across the entire path, unlike IntServ's RSVP-based per-flow reservation model
options.D: DiffServ and IntServ both rely on RSVP to signal reservations hop-by-hop along the path, differing mainly in how many priority levels each model supports, with DiffServ simply defining more granular per-hop classes than IntServ's coarser reservation levels

questions.explanation_es: DiffServ clasifica y marca el tráfico en un número pequeño de clases de reenvío (usando DSCP) y aplica comportamientos por salto (per-hop behavior) en cada dispositivo, dando QoS escalable sin necesitar señalización o reserva por flujo a lo largo de todo el camino — a diferencia de IntServ, que usa RSVP para reservar recursos por flujo individual, lo cual escala mucho peor en redes grandes.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the general purpose of NBAR (Network-Based Application Recognition) as a QoS traffic classification mechanism, as opposed to simple port-number-based classification?

options.A: NBAR replaces the need for any QoS marking or queuing configuration entirely, handling traffic prioritization on its own with no policy-map required, since it was designed to fully automate end-to-end QoS without any administrator-defined class-map
options.B: NBAR only works for traffic using well-known, fixed TCP/UDP ports, offering no advantage over simple port-based ACL matching
options.C: NBAR inspects traffic characteristics beyond just the port number (such as packet payload signatures) to identify the actual application, which is useful for applications that don't use a fixed, predictable port
options.D: NBAR classification only applies to encrypted traffic and cannot classify any unencrypted flow

questions.explanation_es: NBAR inspecciona características del tráfico más allá del número de puerto (como firmas del payload) para identificar la aplicación real, lo cual es útil para aplicaciones que no usan un puerto fijo y predecible.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which queuing mechanism is specifically designed to give strict priority to a designated class of traffic (such as voice), ensuring it is always serviced first, ahead of other queues, up to a configured bandwidth limit?

options.A: Round-robin queuing, which services every queue in strict rotating order 's latency sensitivity
options.B: FIFO (First In, First Out) queuing, which treats every packet from every class identically with no prioritization
options.C: WRED (Weighted Random Early Detection), which is a congestion avoidance mechanism, not a queuing/scheduling mechanism, though its IP-precedence-based drop profiles are sometimes configured under the assumption that they also grant higher-priority queuing treatment to marked traffic on lower-end platforms.
options.D: LLQ (Low Latency Queuing), which adds a strict-priority queue on top of CBWFQ, so traffic assigned to that priority queue (like voice) is always serviced ahead of the other CBWFQ classes, within a configured policed bandwidth limit to prevent it from starving other traffic

questions.explanation_es: LLQ (Low Latency Queuing) agrega una cola de prioridad estricta sobre CBWFQ, de forma que el tráfico asignado a esa cola de prioridad (como voz) siempre se atienda antes que las demás clases de CBWFQ, dentro de un límite de ancho de banda policiado configurado para evitar que ahogue al resto del tráfico.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does CBWFQ (Class-Based Weighted Fair Queuing) provide that basic WFQ (Weighted Fair Queuing) does not?

options.A: CBWFQ removes the ability to guarantee any bandwidth at all, while WFQ guarantees 100% of bandwidth to every flow simultaneously, because WFQ's fair-queuing scheduler recalculates an equal byte-level share of link bandwidth across every currently active flow on the interface each time a new flow starts or an existing flow finishes transmitting, without any administrator input.
options.B: CBWFQ and WFQ are identical mechanisms, differing only in which IOS command is used to configure them
options.C: CBWFQ allows the administrator to explicitly define traffic classes (via class-maps matching specific criteria) and assign a guaranteed minimum bandwidth or percentage to each class, whereas basic WFQ automatically classifies flows based on characteristics like IP address/port with no administrator-defined classes or guaranteed bandwidth allocation
options.D: CBWFQ can only be applied to wireless interfaces, while WFQ can only be applied to wired interfaces

questions.explanation_es: CBWFQ permite que el administrador defina explícitamente clases de tráfico (mediante class-maps que hacen match con criterios específicos) y asigne un ancho de banda mínimo garantizado o un porcentaje a cada clase, mientras que el WFQ básico clasifica flujos automáticamente según características como IP/puerto, sin clases definidas por el administrador ni garantía de ancho de banda por clase.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the general purpose of Cisco's 'AutoQoS' feature on IOS switches/routers?

options.A: It only applies to wireless controllers and has no equivalent capability for wired switches or routers, since wired platforms instead rely solely on manually written MQC policy-maps with no auto-generation option
options.B: It automatically detects and blocks all non-business traffic without any administrator configuration
options.C: It disables all QoS functionality on the device to simplify troubleshooting
options.D: It automatically generates a baseline QoS configuration (classification, marking, queuing) based on Cisco-recommended best practices, reducing the manual effort of building a QoS policy from scratch

questions.explanation_es: Genera automáticamente una configuración QoS base (clasificación, marcado, colas) según las mejores prácticas recomendadas por Cisco, reduciendo el esfuerzo manual de construir una política QoS desde cero.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What problem does WRED (Weighted Random Early Detection) address, and how does it work at a high level?

options.A: WRED guarantees that no packet will ever be dropped under any level of network congestion, no matter how severe
options.B: WRED only operates on wireless interfaces and has no application to wired congestion avoidance
options.C: WRED works by physically reducing the interface's link speed whenever congestion is detected
options.D: WRED prevents TCP global synchronization and worsening congestion by proactively and randomly dropping some packets before a queue becomes completely full, with the drop probability increasing (and weighted by factors like DSCP/IP precedence) as the queue fills, rather than waiting until the queue overflows and dropping many packets from many flows all at once (tail drop)

questions.explanation_es: WRED previene la sincronización global de TCP y el empeoramiento de la congestión, descartando de forma proactiva y aleatoria algunos paquetes antes de que la cola se llene completamente, con probabilidad de descarte creciente (ponderada por factores como DSCP/IP precedence) a medida que la cola se llena, en lugar de esperar a que la cola desborde y descartar muchos paquetes de muchos flujos de golpe (tail drop).

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: According to Cisco's QoS best-practice marking recommendations, which DSCP class is typically used to mark call-signaling traffic (e.g., SCCP/SIP), as distinct from the voice bearer (RTP) traffic itself?

options.A: CS3 (Class Selector 3) is the commonly recommended marking for call-signaling traffic, which is treated with a lower priority guarantee than the EF-marked voice bearer traffic but still receives preferential treatment over best-effort data
options.B: Call-signaling traffic cannot be marked with DSCP at all and must rely on Layer 2 CoS marking
options.C: Call-signaling traffic is typically marked AF31 rather than a Class Selector value, placing it in the same assured-forwarding band used for multimedia streaming instead of being given its own dedicated signaling class
options.D: Call-signaling traffic is always marked with the lowest possible DSCP value (0, best-effort), identical to ordinary web browsing traffic, since Cisco's marking recommendations only assign non-default DSCP values to the voice bearer itself, leaving signaling traffic to go unprioritized

questions.explanation_es: CS3 (Class Selector 3) es la marca comúnmente recomendada para tráfico de señalización de llamadas, que recibe un trato con menor prioridad garantizada que el tráfico portador de voz marcado con EF, pero aún así recibe trato preferencial frente al tráfico de datos best-effort.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the Cisco-recommended best-practice DSCP marking for interactive video (e.g., video conferencing) traffic, as distinct from voice?

options.A: Interactive video cannot be marked with any DSCP value under any Cisco best-practice recommendation and must rely solely on physical bandwidth reservation
options.B: Interactive video is typically marked CS4 rather than AF41, placing it in a Class Selector queue that receives the same strict-priority scheduling as voice but without AF41's drop-precedence subclasses
options.C: Interactive video is always marked as best-effort (DSCP 0), identical to ordinary web browsing, since video is considered non-critical by Cisco best practice, with only the voice bearer stream ever receiving preferential treatment under the current QoS baseline model
options.D: AF41 (Assured Forwarding class 4, low drop precedence) is the commonly recommended marking for interactive video, giving it strong (though not strict-priority-queue-guaranteed like EF) preferential treatment distinct from voice bearer traffic

questions.explanation_es: AF41 (Assured Forwarding clase 4, baja precedencia de descarte) es la marca comúnmente recomendada para video interactivo, dándole un trato preferencial fuerte (aunque no con la garantía de cola de prioridad estricta que sí tiene EF), distinto del tráfico portador de voz.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: In QoS policy configuration on Cisco IOS, what is the relationship between a class-map, a policy-map, and a service-policy?

options.A: A class-map defines the traffic classification criteria (what to match); a policy-map defines the QoS actions (e.g., bandwidth, priority, marking) to apply to one or more classes referenced from class-maps; and a service-policy applies a given policy-map to a specific interface (inbound or outbound)
options.B: A policy-map can only be applied globally to the entire router and can never be applied to an individual interface
options.C: A class-map and a policy-map are configured together as a single combined statement applied directly under interface configuration mode, while the service-policy command is actually used to define the traffic-matching criteria itself, reversing the roles the two commands perform in Cisco's Modular QoS CLI
options.D: A service-policy defines traffic classification, while class-map and policy-map are only used for interface speed/duplex negotiation, unrelated to QoS

questions.explanation_es: El class-map define los criterios de clasificación del tráfico (qué hacer match); el policy-map define las acciones de QoS (ancho de banda, prioridad, marcado) a aplicar a una o más clases referenciadas desde los class-maps; y el service-policy aplica un policy-map determinado a una interfaz específica (entrante o saliente) — la jerarquía típica de configuración de QoS en Cisco IOS.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why does Cisco best practice generally recommend classifying and marking traffic as close to the source as possible (e.g., at the endpoint or access-layer switch), rather than only at a central point like the WAN edge?

options.A: Cisco best practice actually recommends the opposite: never marking traffic until it reaches the WAN edge, to avoid any risk of early misclassification, since access-layer switches are assumed to lack the CPU capacity needed to perform NBAR-based classification reliably at line rate, a limitation that supposedly persists even on modern multigigabit access switches with dedicated TCAM resources
options.B: Marking traffic early allows every downstream device along the path to make consistent QoS decisions (queuing, dropping, shaping) based on that marking from the very first hop, rather than treating all traffic as best-effort until it reaches a distant central point, which could allow congestion to occur before any prioritization is ever applied
options.C: Marking traffic close to the source is only relevant for wireless traffic and has no bearing on wired network design at all
options.D: Marking close to the source has no actual benefit and is purely a stylistic convention with no operational reasoning behind it

questions.explanation_es: Marcar el tráfico temprano permite que todos los dispositivos aguas abajo en el camino tomen decisiones de QoS consistentes (colas, descartes, shaping) basadas en esa marca desde el primer salto, en lugar de tratar todo el tráfico como best-effort hasta que llegue a un punto central lejano, lo cual podría permitir que ocurra congestión antes de que se aplique cualquier priorización.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does 'admission control' typically refer to in the context of voice/video QoS design (e.g., via CAC — Call Admission Control)?

options.A: Admission control refers to which VLANs are permitted to trunk across a given switch port, unrelated to voice or video traffic
options.B: Admission control guarantees unlimited simultaneous calls of any quality on any link, regardless of available bandwidth
options.C: Admission control (CAC) limits the number of simultaneous voice/video calls/sessions allowed over a given constrained-bandwidth link, rejecting or redirecting new call attempts once the configured bandwidth threshold for that traffic class would be exceeded, protecting the quality of calls already in progress
options.D: Admission control refers to a physical security badge reader that grants employees access to the building where network equipment is stored, a physical-security control that is sometimes confused with CAC due to both sharing the same 'admission control' terminology in unrelated Cisco documentation, and is unrelated to any bandwidth-based call limiting function

questions.explanation_es: El control de admisión de llamadas (CAC) limita el número de llamadas/sesiones de voz o video simultáneas permitidas sobre un enlace de ancho de banda limitado, rechazando o redirigiendo nuevos intentos de llamada una vez que se superaría el umbral de ancho de banda configurado para esa clase de tráfico, protegiendo la calidad de las llamadas ya en curso.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is a key QoS design consideration specific to wireless LANs (e.g., using WMM — Wi-Fi Multimedia) compared to wired QoS?

options.A: Wireless networks are not designed to supporting any form of QoS marking or prioritization
options.B: Because wireless is a shared, contention-based medium (unlike a dedicated switched Ethernet link), wireless QoS mechanisms like WMM adjust channel access parameters (such as contention window sizes) to give higher-priority traffic classes a statistically better chance of gaining access to the shared airtime, in addition to queuing/marking concepts similar to wired QoS
options.C: Wireless QoS relies on the same strict-priority queuing and CoS-to-DSCP mapping tables used on wired switches, applying them directly at the RF layer without needing separate channel-access parameters such as contention window adjustments
options.D: WMM only applies to wired Ethernet ports and has no relevance to actual over-the-air wireless transmissions

questions.explanation_es: Como el medio inalámbrico es compartido y basado en contención (a diferencia de un enlace Ethernet conmutado dedicado), mecanismos de QoS inalámbrico como WMM ajustan parámetros de acceso al canal (como el tamaño de la ventana de contención) para darle a las clases de tráfico de mayor prioridad una probabilidad estadísticamente mejor de acceder al medio compartido, además de conceptos de colas/marcado similares a los del QoS cableado.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why is it generally considered a QoS design mistake to mark a large portion of an organization's traffic (e.g., most applications) as high priority or EF?

options.A: There is no downside to marking most traffic as high priority; doing so always improves the performance of every application simultaneously with no trade-off
options.B: QoS marking is limited to exactly one single traffic class per router globally, so marking multiple applications as high priority is not technically possible in the first place
options.C: Marking additional applications as high priority mainly changes how traffic is displayed in NetFlow and monitoring tools, while the actual queuing and dropping behavior on the interface continues to be governed by the interface's default FIFO queue regardless of the DSCP or CoS values applied
options.D: If most traffic is marked as high priority, the priority marking loses its meaning as a differentiator — during actual congestion, a priority queue that is itself oversubscribed with too much 'high priority' traffic can no longer reliably protect the truly latency-sensitive applications (like voice) it was meant to protect

questions.explanation_es: Si la mayor parte del tráfico se marca como alta prioridad, la marca pierde su valor como diferenciador — durante congestión real, una cola de prioridad sobre-suscrita con demasiado tráfico 'de alta prioridad' ya no puede proteger de forma confiable a las aplicaciones realmente sensibles a la latencia (como voz) que se suponía debía proteger. Por eso EF debe reservarse estrictamente para voz.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does the term 'tail drop' refer to in the context of interface queuing, and why is it generally considered less desirable than WRED for TCP-heavy traffic?

options.A: Tail drop happens when a queue is completely full and any newly arriving packet is simply discarded because there is no room left; for TCP flows, this can cause many flows to experience loss and reduce their send rate at roughly the same time (TCP global synchronization), leading to oscillating underutilization and re-congestion of the link
options.B: Tail drop refers to physically disconnecting the last few centimeters of an Ethernet cable to intentionally reduce signal quality, a legacy troubleshooting practice once used on shared-media Ethernet segments to deliberately induce collisions for testing purposes and measure how quickly a network interface card recovers throughput after sustained frame loss under controlled laboratory conditions
options.C: Tail drop guarantees that TCP flows will never reduce their sending rate, regardless of how full the queue becomes
options.D: Tail drop only occurs on wireless interfaces and has no equivalent behavior on any wired interface queue

questions.explanation_es: Tail drop ocurre cuando una cola está completamente llena y cualquier paquete nuevo que llega simplemente se descarta porque no queda espacio; para flujos TCP, esto puede hacer que muchos flujos experimenten pérdida y reduzcan su tasa de envío casi al mismo tiempo (sincronización global de TCP), provocando una oscilación de subutilización y recongestión del enlace — por eso WRED suele preferirse para tráfico dominado por TCP.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: In an end-to-end QoS design spanning a campus LAN and a WAN edge, why is it important that DSCP markings be preserved (not stripped or reset) as traffic crosses from the LAN into the WAN?

options.A: DSCP markings are automatically regenerated identically at every hop, making preservation an automatic, unavoidable behavior with nothing to design for, since every IOS device is assumed to re-derive the original classification from the packet's payload rather than simply forwarding the existing marking unchanged, making any WAN-edge remarking policy redundant by design
options.B: If markings are stripped or reset at the LAN/WAN boundary, the WAN edge device and every downstream device across the WAN would be unable to apply the correct differentiated treatment to that traffic, effectively defeating the purpose of having classified and marked it consistently within the campus in the first place
options.C: DSCP markings only matter within a single VLAN and have no relevance once traffic leaves that VLAN, regardless of whether it crosses into a WAN
options.D: Preserving DSCP markings across the LAN/WAN boundary is prohibited by RFC 2474 and must always be explicitly reset

questions.explanation_es: Si las marcas se eliminan o reinician en el límite LAN/WAN, el equipo de borde WAN y todos los dispositivos aguas abajo a través de la WAN no podrían aplicar el trato diferenciado correcto a ese tráfico, anulando efectivamente el propósito de haberlo clasificado y marcado de forma consistente dentro del campus — por eso preservar DSCP de extremo a extremo es un principio de diseño clave.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is a 'conform-action' and 'exceed-action' in the context of a Cisco policing configuration (e.g., using CIR — Committed Information Rate)?

options.A: The conform-action specifies what to do with traffic that stays within the configured committed rate (e.g., transmit as-is), while the exceed-action specifies what to do with traffic that goes above that rate (e.g., drop it, or re-mark it to a lower-priority DSCP/CoS value before transmitting)
options.B: Conform-action only applies to inbound traffic, and exceed-action only applies to traffic that has already been dropped, making it moot, since Cisco's policing implementation only evaluates the thresholds once per interface at configuration time, storing the result as a static flag that is never revisited for the life of the policy-map
options.C: Conform-action and exceed-action determine which egress interface queue a packet is placed into based on its VLAN tag, selecting a queue independently of the packet's measured rate against the configured CIR
options.D: Conform-action and exceed-action both apply only to traffic that exceeds the configured CIR, differing in that conform-action re-marks the DSCP value while exceed-action re-marks the CoS value of that same excess traffic

questions.explanation_es: El conform-action especifica qué hacer con el tráfico que se mantiene dentro de la tasa comprometida configurada (por ejemplo, transmitirlo tal cual), mientras que el exceed-action especifica qué hacer con el tráfico que supera esa tasa (por ejemplo, descartarlo, o remarcarlo a un valor DSCP/CoS de menor prioridad antes de transmitirlo) — la base de una configuración de policing con CIR en Cisco IOS.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why might a service provider apply policing (rather than shaping) at the ingress of their network for a customer's traffic entering via an MPLS or internet circuit?

options.A: Policing at ingress lets the provider enforce a hard contracted rate limit (e.g., a customer's purchased bandwidth) immediately, without the provider's own network having to buffer/delay a customer's excess traffic — protecting the provider's shared infrastructure from a single customer exceeding their agreed rate, at the cost of dropping (rather than smoothing) that excess traffic
options.B: A service provider typically applies shaping rather than policing at ingress because shaping can buffer and smooth a customer's bursts above the contracted rate without ever dropping packets, making it the preferred mechanism for protecting shared core bandwidth from oversubscription
options.C: Policing is only technically possible on customer-owned equipment and can never be applied on provider-owned equipment
options.D: Policing at ingress guarantees that a customer's traffic will never experience any packet loss

questions.explanation_es: El policing en el ingreso le permite al proveedor aplicar de inmediato un límite de tasa contratado (por ejemplo, el ancho de banda comprado por el cliente), sin que la propia red del proveedor tenga que hacer buffer/retrasar el tráfico excedente del cliente — protegiendo la infraestructura compartida del proveedor de que un solo cliente exceda su tasa acordada, a costa de descartar (en vez de suavizar) ese tráfico excedente.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: According to Cisco's QoS baseline marking recommendations, roughly how many traffic classes (application categories) does the model typically define for consistent enterprise-wide marking?

options.A: Exactly two classes only: 'important' and 'unimportant', with no further granularity defined by Cisco
options.B: The number of classes is fixed permanently at exactly 256, matching the maximum possible DSCP value
options.C: Exactly one single class, since Cisco best practice recommends treating all traffic identically with no differentiation
options.D: Cisco's QoS baseline defines a fairly granular set of traffic classes (covering categories such as voice, broadcast video, real-time interactive, multimedia conferencing, network control, signaling, and various data classes like transactional/bulk/best-effort/scavenger), each intended to receive consistent marking and treatment across the enterprise

questions.explanation_es: El QoS baseline de Cisco define un conjunto bastante granular de clases de tráfico (voz, video broadcast, tiempo real interactivo, conferencia multimedia, control de red, señalización, y varias clases de datos como transaccional/bulk/best-effort/scavenger), cada una pensada para recibir marcado y trato consistente en toda la empresa — no es simplemente 'importante vs no importante'.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the 'scavenger' traffic class typically used for in a Cisco QoS marking scheme, and how is it usually marked?

options.A: The scavenger class is used for the organization's most business-critical, latency-sensitive applications, and is always marked with EF, identical to voice
options.B: The scavenger class (commonly marked with CS1) is used for traffic that is explicitly considered 'less than best-effort' — such as recreational or non-business applications — so that during periods of congestion, this traffic is the first to be starved/dropped, protecting bandwidth for all other legitimate business traffic classes
options.C: The scavenger class refers to network management/monitoring traffic like SNMP and syslog, which Cisco recommends marking with the highest possible priority
options.D: Scavenger-class traffic is always given strictly more guaranteed bandwidth than any other class in the QoS baseline

questions.explanation_es: La clase scavenger (comúnmente marcada con CS1) se usa para tráfico explícitamente considerado 'menos que best-effort' — como aplicaciones recreativas o no relacionadas con el negocio — de forma que durante períodos de congestión, ese tráfico sea el primero en verse limitado/descartado, protegiendo el ancho de banda para el resto de las clases de tráfico legítimas del negocio.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: In a hub-and-spoke WAN topology with a high-bandwidth hub and lower-bandwidth spoke links, why is shaping commonly applied at the hub site toward each spoke, even though the hub's own physical interface may have plenty of bandwidth available?

options.A: Shaping at the hub is mainly used to enforce consistent QoS marking across all spokes rather than to prevent the hub from overrunning any individual spoke's lower-bandwidth access circuit, since spoke-side policing alone is generally treated as sufficient to prevent oversubscription
options.B: Even though the hub interface itself may be fast, each individual spoke's actual access-circuit bandwidth is typically much lower; shaping outbound traffic at the hub toward each spoke's rate prevents overrunning that spoke's slower link and causing uncontrolled tail drops or excessive queuing delay at the spoke's ingress
options.C: Shaping at the hub is required only to comply with a licensing restriction, with no actual traffic-management purpose
options.D: Shaping at the hub is only relevant if every spoke has identical bandwidth to the hub itself, with no benefit in a mixed-bandwidth topology

questions.explanation_es: Aunque la interfaz del hub sea rápida, el ancho de banda real del circuito de acceso de cada spoke suele ser mucho menor; aplicar shaping saliente en el hub ajustado a la tasa de cada spoke evita saturar ese enlace más lento y causar tail drops descontrolados o retardo de cola excesivo en el ingreso del spoke — un patrón de diseño clásico en topologías hub-and-spoke con enlaces de spoke más lentos que el hub.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Which of these is an example of a Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor commonly used in enterprise data centers?

options.A: VMware ESXi, which installs directly on server hardware without requiring a separate general-purpose host operating system underneath it
options.B: Oracle VirtualBox, which is designed to run as a desktop application on top of an existing consumer operating system
options.C: VMware Workstation, which requires a full Windows or Linux desktop operating system installed first before it can run any virtual machine
options.D: A standard web browser, since modern browsers can virtualize an entire operating system natively

questions.explanation_es: VMware ESXi es un ejemplo clásico de hypervisor tipo 1 (bare-metal): se instala directamente sobre el hardware del servidor, sin necesitar un sistema operativo host de propósito general debajo de él. VMware Workstation y VirtualBox, en cambio, son hypervisors tipo 2 que corren como aplicación sobre un SO existente.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What resource-management responsibility does a hypervisor take on when running multiple virtual machines on a single physical server?

options.A: The hypervisor has no involvement in resource allocation at all; each VM directly and owns a physically separate copy of the server's CPU and memory, a design inherited from early hardware-partitioning where physical blades were assigned whole to one OS without any shared scheduler
options.B: The hypervisor only manages network connectivity and has little role in CPU or memory allocation
options.C: Resource management is handled entirely by the guest operating system inside each VM, with the hypervisor playing no role at all
options.D: The hypervisor schedules and allocates the physical server's CPU, memory, storage, and network I/O among the various virtual machines, presenting each VM with the illusion of dedicated hardware while actually sharing the underlying physical resources

questions.explanation_es: El hypervisor programa y asigna la CPU, memoria, almacenamiento y E/S de red del servidor físico entre las distintas máquinas virtuales, dándole a cada VM la ilusión de hardware dedicado mientras en realidad comparte los recursos físicos subyacentes — esta es la función central de cualquier hypervisor.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Which scenario is a more typical use case for a Type 2 hypervisor rather than a Type 1 hypervisor?

options.A: Providing the underlying virtualization layer for a public cloud provider's compute service
options.B: Hosting a large-scale, highly available private cloud infrastructure for an entire organization
options.C: A developer running a single test virtual machine on their personal laptop, alongside their normal desktop applications, to test software in an isolated environment
options.D: Running dozens of production virtual machines in an enterprise data center serving thousands of end users, since Type 2's tighter desktop-OS integration is said to simplify managing large production VM fleets

questions.explanation_es: Un caso de uso típico de hypervisor tipo 2 es un desarrollador ejecutando una VM de prueba en su laptop personal, junto a sus aplicaciones de escritorio normales, para probar software en un entorno aislado — los escenarios de producción a gran escala (a), (c) y (d) son el dominio típico de los hypervisors tipo 1.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What does 'hardware-assisted virtualization' (e.g., Intel VT-x or AMD-V) provide that improves hypervisor performance?

options.A: Hardware-assisted virtualization eliminates the need for a hypervisor altogether, allowing guest operating systems to run directly on bare metal, since VT-x/AMD-V are described as providing a complete built-in scheduler and memory manager in the CPU microcode that replaces the hypervisor's own functions entirely
options.B: A guarantee that every virtual machine will always run at exactly the same clock speed as the physical host regardless of load
options.C: A dedicated physical network card reserved for hypervisor management traffic, unrelated to CPU virtualization
options.D: CPU-level extensions that allow the processor itself to more efficiently trap and handle privileged instructions from guest operating systems, reducing the overhead the hypervisor would otherwise need in pure software to emulate privileged CPU operations

questions.explanation_es: Las extensiones de virtualización asistida por hardware (Intel VT-x, AMD-V) son extensiones a nivel de CPU que permiten al propio procesador interceptar y manejar de forma más eficiente las instrucciones privilegiadas de los sistemas operativos huésped, reduciendo el overhead que el hypervisor de otro modo necesitaría emular por software.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: In terms of the attack surface, why is a Type 1 hypervisor generally considered to have a smaller/more controlled attack surface than a Type 2 hypervisor?

options.A: A Type 1 hypervisor runs directly on hardware with a comparatively minimal, purpose-built codebase, whereas a Type 2 hypervisor runs as an application on top of a full general-purpose host operating system, which itself has a much larger codebase and its own set of potential vulnerabilities that could also affect the hypervisor running on top of it
options.B: Attack surface has no relevance to hypervisor architecture and depends solely on the guest operating systems installed inside the VMs
options.C: Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisors have exactly identical attack surfaces in every measurable respect, with no meaningful security distinction between them
options.D: Type 2 hypervisors are always more secure than Type 1 hypervisors because they include a built-in antivirus engine by default

questions.explanation_es: Un hypervisor tipo 1 corre directamente sobre el hardware con una base de código comparativamente mínima y de propósito específico, mientras que un hypervisor tipo 2 corre como aplicación sobre un sistema operativo host de propósito general completo, que tiene una base de código mucho más grande y sus propias vulnerabilidades potenciales que también podrían afectar al hypervisor que corre encima.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What is a 'virtual machine monitor' (VMM), and how does this term relate to 'hypervisor'?

options.A: A VMM is the guest-side driver installed inside each virtual machine that translates the VM's hardware calls into hypervisor API calls, distinct from the hypervisor itself which runs independently on the physical host
options.B: VMM and hypervisor are essentially synonymous terms — the VMM/hypervisor is the software layer responsible for creating, running, and managing virtual machines by abstracting and allocating the underlying physical hardware to each guest
options.C: A VMM is a type of guest operating system that can only run inside a Type 2 hypervisor, never a Type 1
options.D: A VMM is a dedicated physical hardware device that has no software component and is unrelated to the concept of a hypervisor at all, similar to how a physical KVM switch handles multiple servers, except a VMM is said to be installed as a rack-mounted appliance

questions.explanation_es: VMM (Virtual Machine Monitor) y 'hypervisor' son términos esencialmente sinónimos — es la capa de software responsable de crear, ejecutar y gestionar máquinas virtuales, abstrayendo y asignando el hardware físico subyacente a cada huésped.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: How does a hypervisor typically provide virtual networking connectivity to the VMs it hosts?

options.A: The hypervisor requires every VM to have its own dedicated physical network interface card installed inside the physical server chassis
options.B: VMs hosted by a hypervisor can never communicate with the external physical network ; they are always fully isolated from anything outside the host
options.C: The hypervisor includes or integrates with a vSwitch (virtual switch) component, which the hypervisor uses to switch traffic between VMs on the same host and to bridge that traffic out to the host's physical NICs toward the external physical network
options.D: Virtual networking is provided by a separate physical switch that must be directly cabled to each individual VM, bypassing the hypervisor entirely

questions.explanation_es: El hypervisor incluye o se integra con un componente vSwitch (switch virtual), que el hypervisor usa para conmutar tráfico entre VMs del mismo host y para conectar ese tráfico hacia las NICs físicas del host, hacia la red física externa — así es como las VMs obtienen conectividad de red sin necesitar hardware dedicado por VM.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What is 'CPU overcommitment' in a hypervisor environment, and what risk does it carry if pushed too far?

options.A: CPU overcommitment refers to allocating more total virtual CPUs to VMs than the number of physical CPU cores actually available on the host, betting that not all VMs will demand their full CPU allocation simultaneously; if too many VMs do demand CPU at once, contention can degrade performance across all of them
options.B: CPU overcommitment refers to a licensing violation with no actual technical or performance meaning
options.C: CPU overcommitment only becomes a genuine risk once the ratio of virtual to physical cores exceeds roughly 4:1, since hypervisor schedulers are generally designed to guarantee every VM full, uncontended CPU access below that specific ratio regardless of how many VMs are simultaneously demanding cycles
options.D: CPU overcommitment means physically installing more CPU sockets in the server chassis than the motherboard supports

questions.explanation_es: El overcommitment de CPU consiste en asignar más vCPUs totales a las VMs que la cantidad de núcleos físicos realmente disponibles en el host, apostando a que no todas las VMs demandarán su asignación completa simultáneamente; si demasiadas VMs sí lo hacen al mismo tiempo, la contención puede degradar el rendimiento de todas ellas.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Why is compatibility with a broad range of certified physical server hardware an important consideration when selecting a Type 1 hypervisor for production use?

options.A: A Type 1 hypervisor interacts directly with physical hardware, so using hardware from the vendor's hardware compatibility list (HCL) helps ensure proper driver support, stability, and vendor support, reducing the risk of unexpected hardware-related issues in production
options.B: Hardware compatibility only matters for Type 2 hypervisors, since Type 1 hypervisors are hardware-agnostic by definition
options.C: Selecting compatible hardware is only a cosmetic preference with no bearing on system stability or vendor support
options.D: Hardware compatibility has little relevance to hypervisor selection, since every Type 1 hypervisor runs identically on any hardware without any driver or firmware considerations

questions.explanation_es: Como un hypervisor tipo 1 interactúa directamente con el hardware físico, usar equipos de la lista de compatibilidad de hardware (HCL) del fabricante ayuda a asegurar soporte de drivers adecuado, estabilidad y soporte del proveedor, reduciendo el riesgo de problemas inesperados relacionados con el hardware en producción.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: How does a Type 1 hypervisor's console/management interface (e.g., a direct console UI or a remote management client) typically differ from how a Type 2 hypervisor is managed?

options.A: Management interface design has no actual difference between Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisors in any real-world product
options.B: A Type 1 hypervisor is typically managed remotely (via a dedicated management client, web interface, or centralized platform) since it has no traditional desktop of its own, while a Type 2 hypervisor is typically managed through an application window running inside the host operating system's own desktop environment
options.C: Type 1 hypervisors can never be managed remotely and always require direct physical console access for every single operation
