questions.question: What is the maximum number of usable VLAN IDs typically available in a standard 802.1Q VLAN ID space, and why does this sometimes matter for very large environments (like some data center or service provider designs)?

options.A: 802.1Q's 12-bit VLAN ID field theoretically supports up to 4094 usable VLANs (0 and 4095 reserved), which can become a practical scaling limitation in very large multi-tenant environments, motivating the use of technologies like VXLAN (with its 24-bit VNI space)
options.B: 802.1Q VLAN IDs are capped at exactly 16 usable values on every Cisco platform, a limitation inherited from an early revision of the 802.1Q standard that was later superseded but is sometimes still assumed to apply
options.C: VXLAN's 24-bit VNI field was primarily introduced to add native encryption to Layer 2 traffic crossing the underlay network, with its larger identifier space being an incidental side effect rather than the main design motivation
options.D: 802.1Q's 12-bit VLAN tag field theoretically allows up to 8192 usable VLAN IDs since the top bit is reserved for extended-range signaling, giving most data center fabrics enough headroom that VXLAN's larger VNI space is rarely needed purely for ID-count reasons

questions.explanation_es: El campo de 12 bits de VLAN ID de 802.1Q soporta teóricamente hasta 4094 VLANs utilizables (0 y 4095 reservados), lo cual puede convertirse en una limitación práctica de escala en entornos multi-tenant muy grandes, motivando el uso de tecnologías como VXLAN (con su espacio de VNI de 24 bits) que soportan una cantidad de segmentos lógicos muchísimo mayor.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What potential security issue does 'double-tagging' (also called 'VLAN double-encapsulation') exploit in a VLAN hopping attack?

options.A: Double-tagging is a legitimate diagnostic technique network engineers use intentionally to test QoS marking behavior across a trunk, with no security implications for the VLANs involved
options.B: Double-tagging can only occur on Layer 3 switches performing inter-VLAN routing, since the attack is assumed to depend on the routing process itself re-examining and re-tagging a frame's VLAN ID as it passes between VLANs
options.C: Double-tagging requires physically connecting two separate Ethernet cables to the same switch port simultaneously, since a single cable is assumed to only be capable of carrying one 802.1Q tag layer at a time, overlooking that 802.1Q tagging is carried entirely within the frame header of a single physical link rather than requiring any second physical cable.
options.D: An attacker crafts a frame with two stacked 802.1Q tags: the outer tag matches the trunk's native VLAN (which gets stripped by the first switch that treats it as untagged-native traffic), exposing the inner tag (targeting the victim VLAN) to be forwarded onward by the next switch

questions.explanation_es: Un atacante fabrica un frame con dos etiquetas 802.1Q apiladas: la etiqueta externa coincide con la VLAN nativa del trunk (que el primer switch quita al tratarla como tráfico nativo sin etiquetar), exponiendo la etiqueta interna (apuntando a la VLAN víctima) para que el siguiente switch la reenvíe — saltando efectivamente de la VLAN del atacante a una VLAN objetivo distinta sin pasar por un router. Por eso se recomienda no usar VLAN 1 como nativa y evitar que coincida con VLANs de usuario.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Why do some organizations choose to explicitly configure an unused VLAN ID (rather than VLAN 1 or any actively used data VLAN) as the native VLAN on trunk links, as part of hardening against VLAN hopping?

options.A: Using an unused VLAN as the native VLAN has little security benefit and is done purely for cosmetic labeling reasons
options.B: An unused native VLAN automatically and disables 802.1Q tagging on the entire trunk, removing the need for any further configuration
options.C: Choosing an unused native VLAN is a mandatory requirement of the 802.1Q standard itself, with no flexibility to use any other VLAN as native
options.D: Using an unused, dedicated VLAN as the native VLAN means that even if a double-tagging attack strips the outer tag, the frame is effectively dropped into a VLAN with no real hosts, limiting the practical impact of that class of attack, and it avoids accidentally mixing untagged native-VLAN traffic in with a VLAN that actually carries production traffic

questions.explanation_es: Usar una VLAN dedicada sin uso real como VLAN nativa significa que, aunque un ataque de doble etiquetado quite la etiqueta externa, el frame termine efectivamente en una VLAN sin hosts reales, limitando el impacto práctico de ese tipo de ataque, y evita mezclar accidentalmente tráfico nativo sin etiquetar con una VLAN que realmente transporta tráfico de producción.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is the relationship between a trunk link's configured 'allowed VLAN' list and the VLAN database (VLAN configuration) that must also exist on the switch?

options.A: The allowed-VLAN list on a trunk automatically creates every listed VLAN in the switch's VLAN database, with no separate VLAN configuration step ever required — provisioning each VLAN with default parameters the moment the 'switchport trunk allowed vlan' command is entered on the interface
options.B: The VLAN database only needs to be configured on the switch acting as the VTP server, while any other switch's trunk allowed-VLAN list can reference VLAN IDs that were never locally created in that switch's own VLAN database
options.C: A VLAN must generally exist in the switch's VLAN database before it can be meaningfully carried across a trunk's allowed-VLAN list; listing a VLAN as 'allowed' on a trunk does not itself create that VLAN if it was never configured/active on the switch
options.D: There is no relationship between the two; a trunk can carry any VLAN ID at all, whether or not that VLAN exists anywhere in the switch's configuration

questions.explanation_es: Generalmente una VLAN debe existir en la base de datos VLAN del switch antes de que pueda transportarse de forma significativa a través de la lista de VLANs permitidas de un trunk; listar una VLAN como 'permitida' en un trunk no crea esa VLAN por sí sola si nunca se configuró/activó en el switch.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: How does VLAN pruning (whether manual via allowed-VLAN lists, or automatic via VTP pruning where supported) benefit STP and overall broadcast traffic on a trunk?

options.A: VLAN pruning always increases the total number of broadcast domains flooded across every trunk in the topology, since removing a VLAN from one trunk's allowed list is assumed to force that traffic onto every other trunk instead, a claim that ignores how flooding is scoped per-VLAN rather than redistributed onto unrelated VLANs on other trunks.
options.B: Restricting a trunk to only carry VLANs that are actually needed on the far end reduces unnecessary broadcast/multicast flooding and STP BPDU processing for VLANs that have no active devices on that particular link, improving efficiency across the switched topology
options.C: VLAN pruning has little effect on broadcast traffic or STP processing and exists purely as a documentation convenience for tracking which VLANs an administrator intends to use on a given trunk
options.D: VLAN pruning can only be applied to Layer 3 routed links, since the allowed-VLAN concept is assumed to be a routing-table construct rather than a Layer 2 trunk-interface setting

questions.explanation_es: Restringir un trunk para que solo transporte las VLANs realmente necesarias del otro lado reduce el flooding innecesario de broadcast/multicast y el procesamiento de BPDUs de STP para VLANs que no tienen dispositivos activos en ese enlace en particular, mejorando la eficiencia y reduciendo el overhead innecesario de plano de control y de datos en toda la topología conmutada.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is the effect of the 'switchport trunk pruning vlan' command, in environments where VTP pruning is used?

options.A: It immediately removes the listed VLANs from that trunk's allowed-VLAN list, functioning identically to the 'switchport trunk allowed vlan remove' command rather than only affecting which VLANs are eligible for automatic VTP pruning
options.B: It defines which VLAN is treated as that trunk's native VLAN for untagged traffic, and has no effect on which VLANs VTP is allowed to automatically prune from the link
options.C: It is only relevant on Layer 3 routed interfaces and cannot be applied to a Layer 2 trunk port at all
options.D: It restricts which VLANs are eligible to be automatically pruned by VTP pruning on that specific trunk, refining the default set of prunable VLANs rather than statically hardcoding the entire allowed-VLAN list the way 'switchport trunk allowed vlan' does

questions.explanation_es: Restringe qué VLANs son elegibles para ser podadas automáticamente por VTP pruning en ese trunk específico, refinando el conjunto por defecto de VLANs podables, en lugar de fijar de forma estática toda la lista de VLANs permitidas como hace 'switchport trunk allowed vlan'.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Why might a network engineer prefer to disable Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) entirely on end-user-facing access ports, even though those ports are not intended to become trunks?

options.A: Disabling DTP on access ports is required before any VLAN can ever be assigned to that port, with the port otherwise remaining in an unusable, unconfigured state
options.B: DTP, if left enabled on an access port, automatically and immediately converts every connected end-user device into a Layer 3 router capable of forwarding traffic for other VLANs, an outcome far more disruptive than anything DTP negotiation itself is actually capable of triggering on a connected end-user device.
options.C: Explicitly configuring access ports as 'switchport mode access' and disabling DTP negotiation closes off the possibility that a connected device attempting to speak DTP could ever trick the port into becoming a trunk, a defensive best practice regardless of whether an attack is actually anticipated
options.D: DTP has little relevance to access ports since it is assumed to exist only on Layer 3 routed interfaces, where trunking negotiation would be meaningless in the first place

questions.explanation_es: Configurar explícitamente los puertos de acceso como 'switchport mode access' y deshabilitar la negociación DTP en ellos cierra la posibilidad de que un dispositivo conectado que intente hablar DTP pueda engañar al puerto para que se vuelva trunk — una buena práctica defensiva independientemente de si se anticipa un ataque específico en ese puerto en particular.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What does the 'show etherchannel summary' command on a Cisco switch primarily help an administrator verify?

options.A: It shows the configured EtherChannel bundles, their protocol (LACP/PAgP/none), and the status of each member port (e.g., bundled 'P', suspended 's', individual 'I'), helping quickly identify whether all expected member links are actually bundled and forwarding as part of the channel
options.B: It can only be used to verify wireless access point associations and has no application to wired EtherChannel bundles
options.C: It displays each member port's SFP/transceiver type and cable diagnostics, rather than the port's actual bundling and negotiation-protocol status codes such as bundled, suspended, or individual
options.D: It shows the Layer 3 EtherChannel interface's assigned IP address and subnet mask, but does not report the bundling protocol or per-port status of the individual member links themselves

questions.explanation_es: Muestra los bundles de EtherChannel configurados, su protocolo (LACP/PAgP/ninguno), y el estado de cada puerto miembro (por ejemplo, bundled 'P', suspended 's', individual 'I'), ayudando a identificar rápidamente si todos los enlaces miembro esperados están realmente agrupados y reenviando como parte del canal.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is the general purpose of configuring a specific load-balancing hashing method (e.g., 'src-dst-ip' vs 'src-dst-mac') on an EtherChannel bundle?

options.A: Load-balancing hashing methods only apply to wireless EtherChannel-like bundles and have no relevance to wired switch EtherChannel configuration
options.B: Configuring a hashing method mainly determines the overall aggregate bandwidth limit of the bundle rather than which specific member link an individual flow gets placed on, since Cisco platforms are said to distribute flows using a separate, non-configurable round-robin mechanism underneath
options.C: The load-balancing hashing method controls how fast each individual physical link runs, unrelated to which link carries which flow
options.D: The chosen hashing method determines which fields of a packet/frame are used as input to select which physical member link a given flow is placed on, and selecting a method that produces good entropy across many distinct flows (rather than always hashing to the same result) helps more evenly distribute traffic across all the bundle's physical links

questions.explanation_es: El método de hashing elegido determina qué campos de un paquete/frame se usan como entrada para seleccionar qué enlace físico miembro lleva un flujo determinado, y elegir un método que produzca buena entropía entre muchos flujos distintos (en vez de siempre hashear al mismo resultado) ayuda a distribuir el tráfico de forma más pareja entre todos los enlaces físicos del bundle.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why can EtherChannel load balancing sometimes appear 'unbalanced' even though the hashing algorithm is functioning correctly, particularly when there are relatively few distinct traffic flows?

options.A: Uneven load balancing indicates that LACP has failed entirely and none of the member links are actually part of the bundle any longer
options.B: EtherChannel load balancing is always perfectly even across every member link at every single moment in time, regardless of the number or size of active flows, making this scenario not supported — the hashing algorithm recalculates a fresh output for every individual frame transmitted rather than pinning a flow to one link for its duration, so even a handful of large flows would still be redistributed across every member link rather than settle on just one of them
options.C: Unbalanced EtherChannel load distribution can only ever be caused by a hardware failure on one of the member ports, never by the number or characteristics of the actual traffic flows
options.D: With very few distinct flows (e.g., just two or three large flows), the hashing algorithm's output can happen to place multiple large flows onto the same physical link purely due to how the hash values distribute for that specific small set of flows, resulting in uneven utilization across the bundle even though the algorithm itself is working as designed — this is a statistical/flow-count limitation rather than a malfunction

questions.explanation_es: Con muy pocos flujos distintos (por ejemplo, solo dos o tres flujos grandes), el resultado del algoritmo de hashing puede coincidir en colocar varios flujos grandes en el mismo enlace físico simplemente por cómo se distribuyen los valores de hash para ese conjunto pequeño específico de flujos, resultando en utilización despareja del bundle aunque el algoritmo en sí funcione como fue diseñado — es una limitación estadística/de cantidad de flujos, no un mal funcionamiento.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is the relationship between an EtherChannel's logical 'Port-channel' interface and its physical member interfaces, in terms of Layer 3 configuration (for a routed EtherChannel)?

options.A: A Layer 3 EtherChannel cannot have any IP address configured anywhere, on either the Port-channel interface or its members
options.B: The logical Port-channel interface and its physical members must always be assigned to two entirely different, unrelated VRFs
options.C: For a Layer 3 EtherChannel, IP addressing and most Layer 3 configuration is applied to the logical Port-channel interface itself, not to each individual physical member interface, since the member interfaces operate as part of the single logical bundled link represented by the Port-channel
options.D: Layer 3 IP addressing must always be configured identically and separately on every individual physical member interface, with no IP configuration ever applied to the logical Port-channel interface

questions.explanation_es: Para un EtherChannel de Capa 3, el direccionamiento IP y la mayor parte de la configuración de Capa 3 se aplica a la interfaz lógica Port-channel en sí, no a cada interfaz física miembro individualmente, ya que las interfaces miembro operan como parte del único enlace agrupado lógico representado por el Port-channel.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: How does STP typically treat a properly formed EtherChannel bundle in terms of the spanning-tree topology?

options.A: STP has little interaction with EtherChannel bundles and is automatically and permanently disabled the moment any EtherChannel is configured anywhere on the switch
options.B: STP treats the entire EtherChannel bundle as a single logical link/port in its topology calculations, meaning it does not run a separate STP instance per physical member link; this avoids STP blocking individual member links (which would defeat the purpose of the bundle) while still allowing STP to block or forward the bundle as a whole relative to other paths in the topology
options.C: STP treats every physical member link of the bundle as a completely separate, independent port in its calculations, often blocking most of the member links individually and defeating the purpose of bundling them together — since the Port-channel interface is generally assumed to be purely a CLI grouping construct, with each physical port still sending its own BPDUs and occupying its own spot in the topology
options.D: EtherChannel bundles can never participate in a spanning-tree topology at all and must always be manually excluded from STP calculations

questions.explanation_es: STP trata todo el bundle de EtherChannel como un único enlace/puerto lógico en sus cálculos de topología, es decir, no corre una instancia de STP separada por cada enlace físico miembro; esto evita que STP bloquee enlaces miembro individuales (lo cual anularía el propósito del bundle) mientras sigue permitiendo que STP bloquee o reenvíe el bundle como un todo respecto a otros caminos en la topología.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is 'Cross-Stack EtherChannel' (or similar multi-chassis EtherChannel technologies like StackWise or VSS-based EtherChannel), and what availability benefit does it provide over a standard single-switch EtherChannel?

options.A: Cross-stack EtherChannel allows member links to terminate on separate switches only when those switches are running completely independent control planes, without requiring any StackWise or VSS synchronization between the chassis involved
options.B: This technology is used for wireless access point redundancy and has no application to wired switch-to-switch EtherChannel links
options.C: Cross-stack EtherChannel eliminates the need for any physical cabling between the two switches involved in the bundle entirely
options.D: It allows the individual physical member links of a single logical EtherChannel bundle to terminate on two (or more) physically separate switches that act as one logical switching entity, so that the failure of one entire physical chassis does not take down the whole EtherChannel bundle, only the member links that happened to terminate on the failed chassis

questions.explanation_es: Permite que los enlaces físicos individuales miembro de un único bundle lógico de EtherChannel terminen en dos (o más) switches físicamente separados que actúan como una única entidad de switching lógica, de forma que la falla de un chasis físico completo no derribe todo el bundle de EtherChannel, solo los enlaces miembro que terminaban en el chasis que falló — una mejora de disponibilidad importante sobre un EtherChannel de un solo switch.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why must the member interfaces of an EtherChannel bundle generally be removed from any existing Layer 3 IP configuration before they can be added to a Layer 2 (switched) EtherChannel bundle?

options.A: There is no such requirement; a member port can retain a fully independent IP address and simultaneously participate in a Layer 2 EtherChannel bundle with no conflict — since copper Gigabit Ethernet ports are generally assumed to support a hybrid mode forwarding routed Layer 3 traffic on their own IP address while simultaneously bundling as a Layer 2 member, a capability fiber interfaces are believed to lack
options.B: This requirement only applies to fiber-optic member interfaces and never to copper Ethernet member interfaces
options.C: EtherChannel bundling permanently and irreversibly deletes the physical interface from the switch's hardware inventory the moment it is added to a bundle
options.D: A given physical interface cannot simultaneously have its own independent Layer 3 IP address configuration and also participate as a Layer 2 switched member of an EtherChannel bundle, since bundling a port into a Layer 2 channel converts that port's role into one governed by the logical Port-channel, not by any individually configured Layer 3 settings on that specific member port

questions.explanation_es: Un puerto físico dado no puede tener simultáneamente su propia configuración de dirección IP de Capa 3 independiente y participar como miembro conmutado de Capa 2 de un bundle de EtherChannel, ya que agrupar un puerto en un canal de Capa 2 convierte el rol de ese puerto en uno gobernado por el Port-channel lógico, no por ninguna configuración de Capa 3 configurada individualmente en ese puerto miembro específico.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is a common recommended practice regarding the physical diversity of the individual links that make up an EtherChannel bundle, when availability is a priority?

options.A: Best practice generally treats line-card placement of member links as having negligible impact on availability, since a modular chassis's supervisor is expected to reroute a failed line card's traffic internally to a backup card before the EtherChannel protocol itself would ever detect a member-link failure
options.B: Where practical, spreading member links across different physical line cards/modules (on a modular chassis) or different physical paths reduces the risk that a single hardware fault (like one line card failing) takes down every member link of the bundle simultaneously, preserving the redundancy benefit the bundle is meant to provide
options.C: Physical diversity of member links has little bearing on EtherChannel availability, since all member links are logically treated identically regardless of which physical hardware they terminate on
options.D: EtherChannel technology itself physically prevents an administrator from ever placing member links on different line cards or modules

questions.explanation_es: Cuando es práctico, distribuir los enlaces miembro entre distintas tarjetas de línea/módulos físicos (en un chasis modular) o distintos caminos físicos reduce el riesgo de que una sola falla de hardware (como una tarjeta de línea cayéndose) derribe todos los enlaces miembro del bundle simultáneamente, preservando el beneficio de redundancia que el bundle está pensado para dar.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: How does LACP's 'system priority' and 'port priority' influence which links are actively used when more links are configured in a bundle than the maximum number of active links supported (e.g., more than 8)?

options.A: LACP can never support more member links than the maximum number of simultaneously active links; any extra configured link is immediately and permanently rejected with no standby capability — since the port-channel interface is generally assumed to hard-code its maximum bundle size at creation and simply refuse configuration of a ninth or later member link
options.B: System priority and port priority have no functional effect in LACP and exist purely as unused legacy fields with no bearing on which links are active
options.C: These priority values are used to determine the color of the status LED on each member port, unrelated to which links actively forward traffic
options.D: LACP uses these priority values (combined with system/port ID) to determine which links become the 'active' bundled members versus which are placed into a 'hot-standby' state, so that if an active member fails, one of the standby links can automatically take its place without requiring an administrator to manually reconfigure the bundle

questions.explanation_es: LACP usa estos valores de prioridad (combinados con el ID de sistema/puerto) para determinar qué enlaces se vuelven miembros activos del bundle versus cuáles quedan en estado de 'hot-standby', de forma que si un miembro activo falla, uno de los enlaces en espera pueda tomar su lugar automáticamente sin que un administrador tenga que reconfigurar manualmente el bundle.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why is EtherChannel commonly used on the uplinks between an access-layer switch and a pair of redundant distribution-layer switches, in designs that support it (such as with a switch stack or VSS/StackWise at the distribution layer)?

options.A: EtherChannel on access-to-distribution uplinks is used purely as a licensing requirement with no actual bandwidth or redundancy benefit
options.B: EtherChannel across those uplinks combines the bandwidth of multiple physical links into one logical link while also providing redundancy, all without STP needing to block any of the redundant physical paths (since they appear as a single logical link to STP), which is more bandwidth-efficient than a design where STP simply blocks one of two separate redundant uplinks entirely
options.C: Using EtherChannel on these uplinks provides redundancy without any real bandwidth benefit, since STP still selects only one of the bundle's member links as forwarding at any given time and blocks the rest, the same way it would block a separate redundant standalone uplink
options.D: EtherChannel can only be used on downlinks toward end-user devices and is technically incompatible with switch-to-switch uplink connections

questions.explanation_es: El EtherChannel en esos uplinks combina el ancho de banda de varios enlaces físicos en un único enlace lógico mientras también provee redundancia, todo sin que STP necesite bloquear ninguno de los caminos físicos redundantes (ya que aparecen como un único enlace lógico ante STP), lo cual es más eficiente en ancho de banda que un diseño donde STP simplemente bloquea uno de dos uplinks redundantes por completo.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What does the term 'min-links' configuration on an LACP EtherChannel bundle control?

options.A: 'min-links' specifies the minimum physical cable length allowed for any member link in the bundle, measured in meters
options.B: 'min-links' controls the minimum number of VLANs that must be allowed across the bundle's trunk configuration
options.C: 'min-links' specifies the minimum LACP system priority value that a neighboring switch must advertise before its ports are allowed to join the bundle, rather than controlling how many active member links are required to keep the Port-channel interface up
options.D: It specifies the minimum number of member links that must be actively bundled and up for the entire Port-channel interface itself to be considered up; if the number of active links drops below that configured minimum, the whole logical Port-channel interface goes down, which can be used to ensure a minimum guaranteed bandwidth threshold is always met whenever the channel is considered operational

questions.explanation_es: Especifica el número mínimo de enlaces miembro que deben estar activamente agrupados y up para que la propia interfaz Port-channel se considere up; si el número de enlaces activos cae por debajo de ese mínimo configurado, toda la interfaz Port-channel lógica cae, lo cual puede usarse para asegurar que siempre se cumpla un umbral mínimo de ancho de banda garantizado cuando el canal se considere operativo.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why is it generally recommended to configure EtherChannel member ports consistently for STP-related settings (such as PortFast, BPDU Guard) at the Port-channel interface level rather than trying to configure them differently per individual physical member port?

options.A: Because STP treats the bundle as a single logical port, STP-related settings are meant to apply to that logical Port-channel interface as a whole; attempting to configure conflicting STP settings on individual member ports could lead to inconsistent or unintended behavior, since STP does not actually process each member port as an independent, separately-controlled STP port
options.B: LACP requires every member port to have identical STP settings, such as PortFast and BPDU Guard, before it will allow that port to bundle, verifying this compatibility as part of its marker-protocol exchange during channel formation, similar to how it verifies speed and duplex
options.C: STP-related settings have no relevance to EtherChannel bundles at all and can be safely ignored entirely in any EtherChannel design
options.D: PortFast and BPDU Guard can only ever be configured on access ports and can never be associated with any EtherChannel Port-channel interface

questions.explanation_es: Como STP trata el bundle como un único puerto lógico, los ajustes relacionados con STP están pensados para aplicarse a esa interfaz Port-channel lógica como un todo; intentar configurar ajustes de STP en conflicto en puertos miembro individuales podría llevar a comportamiento inconsistente o no deseado, ya que STP en realidad no procesa cada puerto miembro como un puerto STP independiente y controlado por separado.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What common troubleshooting step should be taken if an EtherChannel bundle configured with LACP fails to form (all member ports remain individual/independent rather than bundled)?

options.A: An LACP bundle failing to form is almost always caused by a hardware fault in the switch's forwarding ASIC, so the recommended first troubleshooting step is to reload the switch rather than checking for a mode, speed/duplex, or VLAN mismatch between the two ends
options.B: The only fix for a failed LACP bundle is to physically replace every switch involved with new hardware
options.C: The only possible cause of an LACP bundle failing to form is a completely dead physical cable; no other configuration mismatch could ever prevent bundling
options.D: Verify that both ends are running a compatible LACP mode combination (at least one side active, or active+passive), and that basic Layer 2 parameters (speed, duplex, trunk encapsulation/allowed VLANs, access VLAN if applicable) are consistent across all intended member ports on both switches, since a mismatch in any of these is a common cause of ports being suspended or failing to bundle

questions.explanation_es: Verificar que ambos extremos corran una combinación de modos LACP compatible (al menos un lado active, o active+passive), y que los parámetros básicos de Capa 2 (velocidad, duplex, encapsulación de trunk/VLANs permitidas, VLAN de acceso si aplica) sean consistentes en todos los puertos miembro pretendidos en ambos switches, ya que un desajuste en cualquiera de estos es una causa común de puertos suspendidos o que no logran agruparse.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: How does PAgP's 'desirable' and 'auto' negotiation modes compare conceptually to LACP's 'active' and 'passive' modes?

options.A: PAgP has no negotiation modes at all and always forms a channel unconditionally
options.B: PAgP 'desirable' behaves similarly to LACP 'active' (it actively initiates negotiation), and PAgP 'auto' behaves similarly to LACP 'passive' (it only responds to negotiation initiated by the other side); as with LACP, two ports both set to the passive-equivalent mode (auto+auto) will not form a channel, since neither side initiates
options.C: PAgP 'desirable' and 'auto' are both equivalent to LACP 'active', meaning any combination of PAgP modes will always successfully negotiate a channel
options.D: PAgP and LACP negotiation modes are entirely unrelated concepts with no conceptual parallel between them

questions.explanation_es: PAgP 'desirable' se comporta de forma similar a LACP 'active' (inicia activamente la negociación), y PAgP 'auto' se comporta de forma similar a LACP 'passive' (solo responde a una negociación iniciada por el otro lado); igual que con LACP, dos puertos configurados en el modo equivalente a pasivo (auto+auto) no formarán un canal, ya que ninguno de los dos inicia.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What advantage does LACP's ability to negotiate and dynamically detect a misconfigured or miswired member link provide, compared to a statically configured EtherChannel with no negotiation protocol ('mode on')?

options.A: With LACP, if a link is accidentally cabled to the wrong switch/port or otherwise doesn't match the expected bundle configuration, LACP's negotiation can detect the mismatch and keep that specific link out of the active bundle (avoiding it being blindly included), whereas a statically configured 'mode on' EtherChannel has no negotiation protocol running at all and will simply attempt to treat any physically connected, correctly-numbered member port as bundled, without any protocol-level verification that the far end agrees
options.B: Static 'mode on' EtherChannel configuration performs its own local verification of the neighbor's system ID and port priority before adding a link to the bundle, providing essentially the same miscabling protection LACP negotiation provides, just without exchanging control frames
options.C: LACP only detects a miscabled link after that link has already begun forwarding traffic as part of the bundle, briefly permitting a small amount of misdirected traffic before pulling the port back out once the mismatch is identified
options.D: LACP negotiation and static 'mode on' configuration provide functionally identical protection against miscabling, with no meaningful safety difference between them — both methods are believed to ultimately rely on the switch's own port-channel load-balancing hash to silently exclude any link whose traffic patterns look abnormal, so a technician who miscables a port would still see that link automatically pulled out of active forwarding within seconds, without LACP's own negotiation frames ever needing to detect a system-ID or port mismatch in the first place

questions.explanation_es: Con LACP, si un enlace se cablea accidentalmente al switch/puerto equivocado o de algún modo no coincide con la configuración de bundle esperada, la negociación de LACP puede detectar el desajuste y mantener ese enlace específico fuera del bundle activo (evitando incluirlo ciegamente), mientras que un EtherChannel configurado estáticamente con 'mode on' no corre ningún protocolo de negociación e intentará simplemente tratar como agrupado a cualquier puerto miembro físicamente conectado y correctamente numerado, sin ninguna verificación a nivel de protocolo de que el otro extremo esté de acuerdo.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why is using 'mode on' (static, unconditional EtherChannel with no negotiation protocol) generally discouraged in favor of LACP or PAgP negotiation, except in specific compatibility scenarios?

options.A: Because 'mode on' bypasses any negotiation entirely, both ends will unconditionally treat their configured ports as bundled even if there is a cabling mistake, a mismatched configuration, or the far end is not actually configured for a channel at all, which can silently cause a Layer 2 loop or other unexpected forwarding behavior that a negotiation protocol like LACP would have caught and prevented
options.B: 'mode on' cannot be configured on any modern Cisco switch platform and has been completely removed from current IOS software
options.C: 'mode on' configuration is objectively faster and more reliable in every single deployment scenario, with negotiation protocols like LACP offering no benefit over it
options.D: There is no meaningful difference in risk between 'mode on' and LACP negotiation; the choice is purely a matter of personal preference with identical safety characteristics

questions.explanation_es: Como 'mode on' evita cualquier negociación por completo, ambos extremos tratarán sus puertos configurados como agrupados incondicionalmente aunque haya un error de cableado, una configuración desajustada, o el otro extremo ni siquiera esté configurado para un canal, lo cual puede causar silenciosamente un loop de Capa 2 u otro comportamiento de reenvío inesperado que un protocolo de negociación como LACP habría detectado y evitado.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What happens to the traffic currently being carried by a specific member link of an active EtherChannel bundle if that individual physical link fails, while other member links remain up?

options.A: The EtherChannel protocol (LACP/PAgP) or the underlying hardware forwarding logic redistributes the flows that were using the failed link across the remaining active member links, typically resulting in a brief re-hash/re-convergence for the affected flows rather than a full outage of the entire logical channel, since the other member links continue forwarding traffic uninterrupted
options.B: Traffic that was using the failed member link is permanently lost and can never be recovered or redistributed to any other member link
options.C: The failure of a single member link causes the entire Port-channel interface to renegotiate its LACP system ID with the remaining members, temporarily suspending all traffic on the bundle until that renegotiation completes
options.D: EtherChannel bundles are physically incapable of continuing to operate with fewer member links than were originally configured, and require a full manual reconfiguration after any single link failure

questions.explanation_es: El protocolo de EtherChannel (LACP/PAgP) o la lógica de reenvío de hardware subyacente redistribuye los flujos que usaban el enlace caído entre los demás enlaces miembro activos, típicamente resultando en un breve re-hash/reconvergencia para los flujos afectados en lugar de una interrupción total del canal lógico, ya que los demás enlaces miembro siguen reenviando tráfico sin interrupción.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a limitation of relying on a hash-based load-balancing algorithm for EtherChannel, in terms of per-flow bandwidth?

options.A: Because the hashing algorithm places an entire flow onto a single physical member link (rather than splitting a single flow's packets across multiple links simultaneously), a single flow's maximum achievable throughput is generally limited to the bandwidth of one member link, not the combined bandwidth of the whole bundle, even if the bundle as a whole has much higher aggregate capacity
options.B: Per-flow bandwidth limitations only apply to wireless EtherChannel-like technologies and have no relevance to wired switch EtherChannel bundles
options.C: Hash-based load balancing has little limitation regarding per-flow throughput, and every flow always achieves the combined bandwidth of the entire bundle regardless of the hashing algorithm used
options.D: EtherChannel hashing always splits every individual flow's packets evenly across all member links simultaneously, guaranteeing that a single flow can achieve the full combined bandwidth of the entire bundle

questions.explanation_es: Como el algoritmo de hashing coloca un flujo entero en un único enlace físico miembro (en lugar de dividir los paquetes de un mismo flujo entre varios enlaces simultáneamente), el rendimiento máximo alcanzable de un solo flujo generalmente está limitado al ancho de banda de un único enlace miembro, no al ancho de banda combinado de todo el bundle, aunque el bundle en su conjunto tenga una capacidad agregada mucho mayor — una limitación importante a tener en cuenta al diseñar para un solo flujo de alto ancho de banda.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How is the STP Root Bridge elected among a set of switches running standard 802.1D/RSTP Spanning Tree?

options.A: The Root Bridge election is based on which switch has the highest number of physical ports, with priority and MAC address playing no role
options.B: The Root Bridge is always the switch that was physically powered on most recently in the topology
options.C: Each switch compares Bridge IDs (a combination of a configurable bridge priority and the switch's MAC address) received in BPDUs, and the switch with the numerically lowest Bridge ID is elected as the Root Bridge; a lower priority value wins, and the MAC address acts as a tiebreaker when priorities are equal
options.D: Root Bridge election is based purely on which switch has been running the longest without interruption (highest uptime), with the Bridge ID priority and MAC address values carried in the BPDU playing no role in breaking ties between switches

questions.explanation_es: Cada switch compara los Bridge ID (una combinación de una prioridad de bridge configurable y la dirección MAC del switch) recibidos en BPDUs, y el switch con el Bridge ID numéricamente más bajo es elegido Root Bridge; un valor de prioridad más bajo gana, y la dirección MAC actúa como desempate cuando las prioridades son iguales.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Root Path Cost' in STP, and how does it influence which port on a non-root switch becomes the Root Port?

options.A: Root Path Cost is calculated solely from the number of switch hops between a given switch and the Root Bridge, without factoring in the configured or default per-port cost values associated with each link's speed
options.B: Root Path Cost only applies to ports that are already blocking, and has no relevance to any port that is actively forwarding traffic
options.C: Root Path Cost is evaluated only on a switch's directly connected link to the Root Bridge when one exists, and has no bearing on Root Port selection for any switch that isn't directly attached to the Root Bridge itself
options.D: Root Path Cost is the cumulative cost of all links along the path from a given switch back to the Root Bridge, and each non-root switch selects, as its Root Port, the port with the lowest total Root Path Cost toward the Root Bridge, since that represents the best (lowest-cost) path back to the root

questions.explanation_es: El Root Path Cost es el costo acumulado de todos los enlaces a lo largo del camino desde un switch dado hasta el Root Bridge, y cada switch no-raíz selecciona, como su Root Port, el puerto con el menor Root Path Cost total hacia el Root Bridge, ya que representa el mejor camino (de menor costo) de regreso a la raíz.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is a 'Designated Port' in classic 802.1D Spanning Tree, and how is it selected on a given LAN segment?

options.A: Designated Ports only exist on the Root Bridge itself; no other switch in the topology can ever have a Designated Port
options.B: For each LAN segment, the switch offering the lowest Root Path Cost to reach the Root Bridge through that segment has its port on that segment elected as the Designated Port, which is the port responsible for forwarding traffic onto and off of that particular segment (with Bridge ID as a tiebreaker for equal costs)
options.C: A Designated Port is selected based solely on which switch has the highest port number connected to that segment, with root path cost only used as a tiebreaker when port numbers are identical
options.D: Every port on every switch in the topology is always a Designated Port simultaneously, with no distinction ever made between forwarding and blocking ports

questions.explanation_es: Para cada segmento de LAN, el switch que ofrece el menor Root Path Cost para llegar al Root Bridge a través de ese segmento tiene su puerto en ese segmento elegido como Designated Port, que es el puerto responsable de reenviar tráfico hacia y desde ese segmento en particular (con el Bridge ID como desempate en caso de costos iguales).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: In classic 802.1D STP, what are the five possible port states a port can transition through, and roughly what does each represent?

options.A: The five port states are named after colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue, Purple) with no functional distinction between them, a mix-up that likely stems from confusing STP's port-state naming with the red/amber/green port LED indicators on many Catalyst chassis, even though those LED colors describe only link/duplex/error conditions and have no relationship to STP's Blocking, Listening, Learning, Forwarding, and Disabled states that STP actually defines during convergence
options.B: Blocking (not forwarding, only listening for BPDUs), Listening (preparing to forward, not yet learning MACs), Learning (building the MAC address table, still not forwarding user data), Forwarding (actively forwarding traffic), and Disabled (administratively shut down); a port typically moves through Blocking/Listening/Learning before reaching Forwarding, which is why classic 802.1D convergence can take tens of seconds
options.C: Every port state in 802.1D STP allows the port to immediately forward user data traffic with zero delay, making the concept of transitional states meaningless
options.D: 802.1D STP has only two possible port states, 'On' and 'Off', involved in convergence

questions.explanation_es: Blocking (no reenvía, solo escucha BPDUs), Listening (preparándose para reenviar, aún no aprende MACs), Learning (construyendo la tabla de direcciones MAC, todavía sin reenviar datos de usuario), Forwarding (reenviando tráfico activamente), y Disabled (apagado administrativamente); un puerto típicamente pasa por Blocking/Listening/Learning antes de llegar a Forwarding, por eso la convergencia del 802.1D clásico puede tardar decenas de segundos.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does RSTP's 'proposal/agreement' mechanism enable much faster convergence than classic 802.1D STP's timer-based transitions?

options.A: RSTP's proposal/agreement mechanism has nothing to do with convergence speed and exists purely for logging/auditing purposes
options.B: RSTP achieves faster convergence by disabling all STP calculations entirely and simply forwarding on every port unconditionally with no loop prevention at all, treating RSTP as though it traded away loop protection rather than merely replacing 802.1D's fixed timers with an explicit proposal/agreement handshake that still fully computes and enforces the spanning tree
options.C: The proposal/agreement mechanism only functions on the Root Bridge itself and has no effect on convergence anywhere else in the topology
options.D: RSTP allows a switch to actively propose that its port become the new designated forwarding port and receive an explicit agreement back from its neighbor, enabling both sides to synchronize and move directly to forwarding without waiting through the fixed listening/learning timer delays that classic 802.1D relies on

questions.explanation_es: RSTP permite que un switch proponga activamente que su puerto se convierta en el nuevo puerto designado de reenvío y reciba un acuerdo explícito de su vecino, permitiendo que ambos lados se sincronicen y pasen directamente a forwarding sin esperar los retrasos de temporizador fijos de listening/learning en los que se basa el 802.1D clásico.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is a 'backup port' role, specific to RSTP, and when does it typically appear?

options.A: A backup port refers to a completely separate physical switch kept powered off in a storage closet as a spare replacement unit — intended to be manually swapped in by an administrator if the primary switch fails, with the term 'backup port' generally understood by analogy to a cold-spare hardware unit rather than to any specific RSTP port-role designation assigned during normal spanning-tree operation
options.B: A backup port is a non-designated port role that appears when a switch has more than one port connected to the same shared LAN segment (e.g., via a hub), representing a redundant path to a segment the switch can already reach via its own designated port on that same segment; it is ready to take over the designated role if the current designated port on that segment fails
options.C: A backup port is simply another name for the Root Port, with the two terms being fully interchangeable
options.D: Backup ports only exist in classic 802.1D STP and were entirely removed from RSTP, with no equivalent role present in RSTP

questions.explanation_es: Un puerto backup es un rol de puerto no designado que aparece cuando un switch tiene más de un puerto conectado al mismo segmento de LAN compartido (por ejemplo, vía un hub), representando un camino redundante hacia un segmento que el switch ya puede alcanzar por su propio puerto designado en ese mismo segmento; está listo para asumir el rol designado si el puerto designado actual de ese segmento falla.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What does 'BackboneFast' (a legacy Cisco STP enhancement) address, and why is it generally unnecessary once a network has migrated fully to RSTP?

options.A: BackboneFast reduced the time it took classic 802.1D STP to detect an indirect link failure (one not directly connected to the switch, discovered via the absence of expected BPDUs after the max-age timer), a scenario RSTP's more responsive BPDU-based mechanisms already handle quickly and natively without needing a separate feature
options.B: BackboneFast is required in every RSTP deployment and cannot be omitted, contrary to being a legacy 802.1D-era enhancement
options.C: BackboneFast works by having a switch immediately transition its blocking ports to forwarding as soon as it stops receiving BPDUs from any neighbor, without first confirming that an alternate path to the Root Bridge actually exists
options.D: BackboneFast primarily reduces the STP listening and learning state timers on directly connected access ports, rather than addressing the detection delay for an indirect link failure occurring elsewhere in the topology

questions.explanation_es: BackboneFast reducía el tiempo que le tomaba al 802.1D clásico detectar la falla de un enlace indirecto (uno no conectado directamente al switch, descubierto por la ausencia de las BPDUs esperadas tras el temporizador max-age), un escenario que los mecanismos más reactivos basados en BPDU de RSTP ya manejan rápida y nativamente sin necesitar una función separada.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does MST (Multiple Spanning Tree) group VLANs into 'MST instances' (MSTIs), and why does this grouping matter for scalability?

options.A: MST instances are created automatically based on numeric VLAN ranges, such as VLANs 1-100 mapping to instance 0 and 101-200 to instance 1, rather than through an administrator-defined 'instance vlan' mapping statement in MST configuration mode
options.B: MST requires that every single VLAN always be mapped to its own unique, individual MST instance, providing no CPU savings compared to PVST+ — since the 'instance vlan' mapping statement inside MST configuration mode is generally believed to only accept a single VLAN per line and to implicitly create a new spanning-tree instance automatically for each one entered, unlike PVST+'s per-VLAN model, which instead maintains a fully separate instance for every configured VLAN
options.C: MST allows an administrator to map many VLANs onto a smaller number of MST instances, each running its own independent spanning-tree topology calculation; since the number of actual STP computations equals the (typically small) number of instances rather than the (potentially much larger) number of VLANs, this significantly reduces the CPU/control-plane load compared to running a fully separate STP instance for every single VLAN (as PVST+ does)
options.D: MST can only ever define a single instance total across the entire network, with no ability to run more than one spanning-tree topology anywhere

questions.explanation_es: MST permite que un administrador mapee muchas VLANs a una cantidad menor de instancias MST, cada una corriendo su propio cálculo de topología de spanning-tree independiente; como el número real de cálculos de STP es igual a la cantidad (típicamente pequeña) de instancias en lugar de la cantidad (potencialmente mucho mayor) de VLANs, esto reduce significativamente la carga de CPU/plano de control comparado con correr una instancia STP completamente separada por cada VLAN (como hace PVST+).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What must be configured identically across all switches within the same MST 'region' for them to be considered part of that same region?

options.A: MST regions are determined purely by the switches' physical geographic distance from each other, with no software configuration involved at all
options.B: Only the MST configuration name needs to match between switches for them to be considered part of the same region, while the revision number and VLAN-to-instance mapping table are exchanged informationally but don't actually affect region membership
options.C: Every switch in an MST region must have an identical hostname, with configuration name, revision, and VLAN mapping playing no role in region membership
options.D: All switches in an MST region must share the same configured MST configuration name, revision number, and VLAN-to-instance mapping table; if any of these differ between two switches, they are considered to be in different MST regions, which affects how BPDUs and topology information are exchanged between them

questions.explanation_es: Todos los switches en una región MST deben compartir el mismo nombre de configuración MST, número de revisión, y tabla de mapeo VLAN-a-instancia; si alguno de estos difiere entre dos switches, se consideran en regiones MST distintas, lo cual afecta cómo se intercambian entre ellos las BPDUs y la información de topología.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does MST interact with switches running a different spanning-tree variant (like PVST+) at the boundary between an MST region and a non-MST switch?

options.A: Boundary interoperability between MST and PVST+ requires manually disabling STP on the MST region entirely, defeating the purpose of running STP at all
options.B: MST cannot interoperate with any other STP variant requiring every single switch in an entire organization to be upgraded to MST simultaneously in one flash cut
options.C: MST regions automatically and permanently disable Spanning Tree entirely on every neighboring non-MST switch the moment they are connected
options.D: MST includes interoperability behavior at region boundaries (using an Internal Spanning Tree/Common Spanning Tree, or CIST) so that MST regions can present a single, compatible spanning-tree view to neighboring switches running PVST+ or other STP variants, allowing the two to interoperate without requiring every single switch in the network to run the exact same STP variant

questions.explanation_es: MST incluye comportamiento de interoperabilidad en los límites de región (usando un Internal Spanning Tree/Common Spanning Tree, o CIST) para que las regiones MST puedan presentar una vista de spanning-tree única y compatible a switches vecinos que corren PVST+ u otras variantes de STP, permitiendo que ambos interoperen sin requerir que absolutamente todos los switches de la red corran exactamente la misma variante de STP.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is the purpose of 'UplinkFast' (a legacy Cisco 802.1D enhancement), and why is its function largely built into RSTP natively?

options.A: UplinkFast is a mandatory feature that must be manually enabled even on switches already running RSTP, since RSTP does not provide any equivalent capability on its own — because although RSTP's alternate port role speeds convergence for direct link failures, documentation is often read as still requiring UplinkFast to preserve the original 802.1D root-path-cost decrement used for uplink load-sharing in current recommended designs
options.B: UplinkFast only applies to Layer 3 routed uplinks and has no relevance to Layer 2 STP-blocked redundant links
options.C: UplinkFast raises the port cost of the standby uplink so it becomes preferred, but the port still passes through the normal listening and learning delay before it starts forwarding traffic
options.D: UplinkFast allowed an access-layer switch with a blocked backup uplink to quickly transition that backup link to forwarding if its active uplink failed, bypassing the normal listening/learning delay; RSTP achieves a similar (and generally faster/more general) rapid-failover capability natively through its alternate port role and proposal/agreement mechanism, without needing a separate legacy feature

questions.explanation_es: UplinkFast permitía que un switch de capa de acceso con un uplink de respaldo bloqueado transicionara rápidamente ese enlace de respaldo a forwarding si su uplink activo fallaba, saltándose el retraso normal de listening/learning; RSTP logra una capacidad de conmutación rápida similar (y generalmente más rápida/general) de forma nativa a través de su rol de puerto alternate y el mecanismo de proposal/agreement, sin necesitar una función legacy separada.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What happens to a port protected by Root Guard if it receives a superior BPDU (one that would normally cause it to become a Root Port)?

options.A: The port is placed into a 'root-inconsistent' blocking state, preventing it from forwarding traffic (and from becoming the Root Port) as long as it continues receiving that superior BPDU; once the superior BPDUs stop being received, the port can automatically recover back to its normal STP-determined state
options.B: The port immediately and permanently becomes the new Root Port, exactly opposite to Root Guard's intended function
options.C: The entire switch (not just the affected port) is immediately and permanently powered off the moment any superior BPDU is received anywhere on it — a fail-safe modeled on how a fatal hardware error triggers a full chassis reload, on the reasoning that a superior BPDU indicates a topology change serious enough to prevent at any cost
options.D: Root Guard has no defined behavior for this scenario and simply ignores any BPDU received, superior or not

questions.explanation_es: El puerto se coloca en un estado de bloqueo 'root-inconsistent', impidiéndole reenviar tráfico (y convertirse en Root Port) mientras siga recibiendo esa BPDU superior; una vez que dejan de recibirse las BPDUs superiores, el puerto puede recuperarse automáticamente de vuelta a su estado normal determinado por STP.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why is PortFast specifically intended only for ports connected to end hosts (like PCs, printers, or IP phones) and not for ports connecting to other switches?

options.A: PortFast can be safely enabled on any port type, including switch-to-switch links
options.B: PortFast causes a port to skip the normal listening/learning delay and transition immediately to forwarding, which is safe for a port that will never receive a BPDU from a downstream switch (an end host doesn't run STP); if PortFast were enabled on a port actually connecting to another switch, it could create a temporary Layer 2 loop before STP has a chance to properly detect the topology and block a redundant path
options.C: PortFast is actually intended for switch-to-switch trunk links and was never designed to be used on end-host-facing access ports at all
options.D: PortFast primarily disables MAC address learning on the port until traffic is seen from the attached device, which relates to end-host detection rather than to skipping the listening and learning delay itself

questions.explanation_es: PortFast hace que un puerto se salte el retraso normal de listening/learning y pase inmediatamente a forwarding, lo cual es seguro para un puerto que nunca recibirá una BPDU de un switch aguas abajo (un host final no corre STP); si PortFast se habilitara en un puerto que en realidad conecta a otro switch, podría crear un loop temporal de Capa 2 antes de que STP tenga la oportunidad de detectar correctamente la topología y bloquear un camino redundante — por eso PortFast siempre debe combinarse con BPDU Guard en puertos de acceso.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is the difference between BPDU Guard and BPDU Filter, both of which relate to how a port reacts to receiving a BPDU?

options.A: BPDU Filter, when triggered, immediately places the port into a permanently disabled state that requires a manual 'shutdown' followed by 'no shutdown' to restore, whereas BPDU Guard simply drops the incoming BPDU frames at the port while still allowing the PortFast-enabled port to keep forwarding traffic normally, without ever moving the port into an err-disabled condition
options.B: Neither BPDU Guard nor BPDU Filter has any relationship to received BPDUs; both features instead control only the port's VLAN assignment
options.C: BPDU Guard and BPDU Filter are simply two different configuration command names for exactly the same underlying behavior, with no functional distinction
options.D: BPDU Guard, upon receiving any BPDU on a protected (typically PortFast) port, immediately puts that port into an err-disabled state to protect the topology, whereas BPDU Filter suppresses the sending and processing of BPDUs on that port entirely, which can be riskier since it silently prevents STP loop detection on that port rather than actively shutting it down when unexpected BPDUs appear

questions.explanation_es: BPDU Guard, al recibir cualquier BPDU en un puerto protegido (típicamente con PortFast), pone inmediatamente ese puerto en estado err-disabled para proteger la topología, mientras que BPDU Filter suprime el envío y procesamiento de BPDUs en ese puerto por completo, lo cual puede ser más riesgoso ya que silenciosamente impide la detección de loops de STP en ese puerto en lugar de apagarlo activamente cuando aparecen BPDUs inesperadas.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is 'UDLD' (UniDirectional Link Detection), and what specific failure scenario does it address that basic STP BPDU exchange might not reliably catch?

options.A: UDLD and STP are functionally identical protocols that perform exactly the same detection and prevention function, making UDLD entirely redundant wherever STP is already running — since both are considered to rely on periodically exchanging control frames between neighboring switches to confirm the link is healthy, with UDLD's hello messages viewed as functionally interchangeable with STP's own BPDUs for detecting a broken or degraded connection between two switch ports on the same segment
options.B: UDLD detects a unidirectional link failure — where traffic can flow in one direction on a fiber pair (e.g., due to a crossed or damaged fiber strand) but not the other — a condition that can confuse STP (since BPDUs might still be received in one direction) and potentially lead to a forwarding loop; UDLD actively exchanges its own hello messages in both directions to verify true bidirectional connectivity and can err-disable a port if unidirectional behavior is detected
options.C: UDLD only operates on copper Ethernet links and has little application to fiber-optic connections, where unidirectional failures are most common
options.D: UDLD is used to negotiate the duplex setting of a link between two neighboring switches, correcting a duplex mismatch before STP begins its normal listening and learning states

questions.explanation_es: UDLD detecta una falla de enlace unidireccional — donde el tráfico puede fluir en una dirección en un par de fibra (por ejemplo, por una hebra de fibra cruzada o dañada) pero no en la otra — una condición que puede confundir a STP (ya que las BPDUs podrían seguir recibiéndose en una dirección) y potencialmente llevar a un loop de reenvío; UDLD intercambia activamente sus propios mensajes hello en ambas direcciones para verificar conectividad bidireccional real y puede dejar el puerto err-disabled si detecta comportamiento unidireccional.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does 'err-disable recovery' functionality help operationally after a port has been automatically shut down by a protective feature like BPDU Guard or UDLD?

options.A: Err-disable recovery can be configured to automatically re-enable a port that was shut down due to a specific cause (like BPDU Guard or UDLD) after a configured timeout period, reducing the need for an administrator to manually intervene and re-enable the port every single time the protective feature triggers, while still preserving the initial protective shutdown behavior
options.B: Enabling err-disable recovery for a given cause also raises the violation threshold for that specific trigger, so a port tolerates several additional BPDU Guard or UDLD events before being shut down again, rather than the recovery feature simply re-enabling the port unconditionally once the configured timeout period has elapsed each time the same condition occurs
options.C: Err-disable recovery works by lowering the severity of the triggering violation so that subsequent identical events are merely logged rather than causing another shutdown, rather than by re-enabling the port itself after a timer expires
options.D: Err-disable recovery disables the affected port forever, with no possibility of it ever being automatically or manually re-enabled again

questions.explanation_es: La recuperación de err-disable puede configurarse para volver a habilitar automáticamente un puerto que fue apagado por una causa específica (como BPDU Guard o UDLD) después de un período de timeout configurado, reduciendo la necesidad de que un administrador intervenga manualmente y vuelva a habilitar el puerto cada vez que se dispara la función protectora, mientras sigue preservando el comportamiento inicial de apagado protectivo.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why might 'PVST+' (Per-VLAN Spanning Tree Plus) allow for more granular load balancing across redundant uplinks than a single common spanning-tree instance shared by all VLANs?

options.A: The '+' in PVST+ specifically denotes its ability to also tag BPDUs with an 802.1Q VLAN header so they can traverse standard trunks, but PVST+ still computes only one shared spanning-tree topology for all VLANs on that trunk rather than a separate instance per VLAN, meaning any per-VLAN load balancing must instead be achieved by manually adjusting EtherChannel load-balancing hash algorithms rather than through separate per-VLAN root elections
options.B: Load balancing across uplinks is only possible with EtherChannel and can never be achieved through any STP-based mechanism like PVST+
options.C: Because PVST+ runs a logically separate STP instance per VLAN, different VLANs can independently select different root bridges/root ports, allowing an administrator to intentionally make one uplink the forwarding path for some VLANs while a second redundant uplink forwards a different set of VLANs, spreading traffic across both physical uplinks rather than leaving one uplink completely blocked for every VLAN simultaneously
options.D: PVST+ achieves its load-balancing benefit by running a single shared spanning-tree instance but assigning each VLAN a different port cost automatically, rather than by computing a fully independent topology per VLAN

questions.explanation_es: Como PVST+ corre una instancia de STP lógicamente separada por VLAN, distintas VLANs pueden elegir de forma independiente distintos root bridges/root ports, permitiendo que un administrador haga intencionalmente que un uplink sea el camino de reenvío para algunas VLANs mientras un segundo uplink redundante reenvía un conjunto distinto de VLANs, repartiendo el tráfico entre ambos uplinks físicos en lugar de dejar un uplink completamente bloqueado para todas las VLANs simultáneamente.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What operational cost does PVST+'s per-VLAN STP instance model impose as the number of VLANs on a switch grows very large, which MST was specifically designed to avoid?

options.A: Under PVST+, CPU utilization scales primarily with the number of physical trunk ports rather than the number of configured VLANs, since each trunk port floods only one shared set of BPDUs regardless of how many VLANs it carries
options.B: PVST+ has no additional CPU or control-plane cost regardless of how many VLANs are configured, making MST's instance-mapping approach unnecessary from a scalability perspective
options.C: PVST+ automatically converts itself into MST once a switch exceeds a certain number of configured VLANs, with no administrator action required
options.D: Because PVST+ runs a fully separate STP computation and BPDU exchange for every single VLAN, a switch with hundreds of VLANs must perform hundreds of independent STP calculations and process a proportionally larger volume of BPDUs, consuming significantly more CPU and control-plane resources than MST's approach of mapping many VLANs onto a much smaller number of instances

questions.explanation_es: Como PVST+ corre un cálculo de STP y un intercambio de BPDUs completamente separado para cada VLAN, un switch con cientos de VLANs debe realizar cientos de cálculos de STP independientes y procesar un volumen proporcionalmente mayor de BPDUs, consumiendo significativamente más CPU y recursos de plano de control que el enfoque de MST de mapear muchas VLANs a una cantidad mucho menor de instancias — la razón principal detrás de la existencia de MST.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why is it important that STP timers (hello time, forward delay, max age) be consistent with the actual diameter (maximum switch-to-switch hop count) of the switched topology?

options.A: STP timers have no relationship to network diameter and can be set to any arbitrary value with zero risk regardless of how many switches are in the topology
options.B: STP timers are automatically and dynamically recalculated in real time based on diameter with no default assumptions or administrator consideration ever required
options.C: The default STP timers are calculated assuming a certain maximum network diameter; if the actual topology's diameter exceeds what the configured timers were designed to safely accommodate, BPDUs might age out or convergence calculations might not have propagated fully across the entire topology in time, risking a temporary loop or slower-than-expected, potentially unreliable convergence behavior
options.D: Network diameter only matters for Layer 3 routing protocols like OSPF and has no bearing on Layer 2 Spanning Tree behavior

questions.explanation_es: Los temporizadores por defecto de STP se calculan asumiendo un cierto diámetro máximo de red; si el diámetro real de la topología excede lo que esos temporizadores configurados fueron diseñados para acomodar de forma segura, las BPDUs podrían expirar o los cálculos de convergencia podrían no haberse propagado completamente por toda la topología a tiempo, arriesgando un loop temporal o un comportamiento de convergencia más lento de lo esperado y potencialmente poco confiable.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the role of the 'successor' route in EIGRP's DUAL algorithm?

options.A: EIGRP does not use the term 'successor' at all; this terminology is exclusive to OSPF's SPF algorithm
options.B: The successor is always a backup-only route that is never installed in the routing table
options.C: A successor route is selected based only on the lowest hop count to the destination, with the composite bandwidth/delay metric used only as a tiebreaker when two or more neighbors report an identical hop count to that destination, similar to how RIP falls back to additional criteria only after hop count fails to produce a single best path
options.D: The successor is the route with the lowest overall composite metric to a given destination, and it is the route that is actually installed in the routing table and used for forwarding, while a feasible successor (if one exists) is kept as a loop-free backup in the topology table

questions.explanation_es: El successor es la ruta con el menor costo compuesto general hacia un destino dado, y es la ruta que realmente se instala en la tabla de enrutamiento y se usa para reenviar tráfico, mientras que un feasible successor (si existe) se mantiene como respaldo libre de loops en la tabla de topología.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the 'Feasibility Condition' that a backup route must satisfy in EIGRP to be considered a valid feasible successor (and thus be loop-free)?

options.A: A neighbor's advertised distance (its own reported metric to the destination) to that destination must be strictly less than the current successor's feasible distance (the local router's own best metric to that destination); this guarantees the neighbor is not routing back through the local router itself, avoiding a loop
options.B: There is no such thing as a Feasibility Condition in EIGRP; any advertised route from any neighbor is automatically accepted as a feasible successor with no verification — this is because EIGRP is generally described as relying on the DUAL finite state machine's query/reply process for loop avoidance rather than an upfront metric check against the successor's feasible distance
options.C: The Feasibility Condition requires the backup route to have an identical metric to the successor route in every single case, with no tolerance for any difference
options.D: The Feasibility Condition only applies to OSPF's SPF calculation and has little equivalent concept in EIGRP

questions.explanation_es: La distancia anunciada de un vecino (su propio costo reportado hacia el destino) debe ser estrictamente menor que la distancia factible (feasible distance) actual del successor (el mejor costo propio del router local hacia ese destino); esto garantiza que el vecino no esté enrutando de vuelta a través del propio router local, evitando un loop.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: How does EIGRP behave when a successor route fails and no feasible successor exists in the topology table for that destination?

options.A: EIGRP immediately and permanently marks the entire routing process as failed and requires a full router reboot to recover from the loss of any single route — since the DUAL finite state machine is considered to have no recovery path once a destination loses both its successor and every feasible successor, forcing a restart from a clean table
options.B: EIGRP silently drops all traffic to that destination forever with no attempt to query neighbors or recompute an alternate path
options.C: EIGRP always has a feasible successor pre-computed for every possible destination in every topology, making this active-state query scenario not supported
options.D: EIGRP enters 'Active' state for that route and sends Query packets to its neighbors asking whether they have an alternate loop-free path to the destination, waiting for Reply packets before recalculating and re-installing a new best route (or declaring the destination unreachable if no neighbor has a valid path)

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP entra en estado 'Active' para esa ruta y envía paquetes Query a sus vecinos preguntando si tienen un camino alternativo libre de loops hacia el destino, esperando paquetes Reply antes de recalcular e instalar una nueva mejor ruta (o declarar el destino inalcanzable si ningún vecino tiene un camino válido).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What potential problem does a prolonged EIGRP 'Stuck-In-Active' (SIA) condition represent, and what generally causes it?

options.A: An SIA condition occurs when a router does not receive Reply packets from one or more neighbors within the configured active-state timer after sending Query packets, often caused by a slow, congested, or unreachable neighbor that fails to reply in time; this can significantly delay convergence and, in the worst case, cause the router to reset the neighbor relationship with the non-responding neighbor
options.B: Stuck-In-Active is a normal, desirable steady-state condition that every EIGRP route is expected to remain in permanently under healthy network operation
options.C: An SIA condition is typically resolved by the router immediately re-flooding Query packets to all other neighbors before the active timer expires, which usually restores convergence within a few hundred milliseconds regardless of the non-responding neighbor's delay
options.D: SIA is a condition specific to OSPF's LSA flooding process during an area's SPF recalculation, and the equivalent EIGRP condition is instead referred to simply as a stuck query without any active-state timer involved

questions.explanation_es: Una condición SIA (Stuck-In-Active) ocurre cuando un router no recibe paquetes Reply de uno o más vecinos dentro del temporizador de estado activo configurado, a menudo causado por un vecino lento, congestionado o inalcanzable que no responde a tiempo; esto puede retrasar significativamente la convergencia y, en el peor caso, causar que el router reinicie la relación de vecindad con el vecino que no respondió.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the purpose of OSPF's SPF (Shortest Path First / Dijkstra) algorithm, run by every router within an area?

options.A: OSPF routers never run SPF; instead they rely entirely on distance-vector-style periodic full routing table exchanges, identical to RIP
options.B: SPF is calculated only once by a single centralized router for the entire OSPF domain, with every other router simply copying that one router's routing table verbatim with no independent calculation of their own
