options.C: Because most network devices already support SSH natively as a standard management access method, Ansible can connect to and manage them using that same existing, already-present access mechanism, without needing any additional custom agent software to be separately installed on the device beforehand — the device's built-in SSH server effectively serves as the 'entry point' Ansible needs, rather than a purpose-built agent
options.D: Ansible's agentless characteristic actually comes from its use of SNMP rather than SSH to reach managed network devices, with SSH instead being reserved specifically for connecting to Linux/Unix servers where a lightweight temporary Python module is pushed and executed on each managed node

questions.explanation_es: Como la mayoría de los dispositivos de red ya soportan SSH nativamente como método estándar de acceso de gestión, Ansible puede conectarse y gestionarlos usando ese mismo mecanismo de acceso ya existente, sin necesitar que se instale por separado ningún software de agente adicional personalizado en el dispositivo de antemano — el servidor SSH integrado del dispositivo efectivamente sirve como el 'punto de entrada' que Ansible necesita, en lugar de un agente construido específicamente para ese propósito.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What is the purpose of an Ansible 'module' (such as the 'ios_config' or 'ios_command' modules used for Cisco IOS devices)?

options.A: An Ansible module's parameters can be customized per invocation using variables, but those variable values must be hard-coded directly within the playbook's own task definition, since a module is not designed to pull its parameter values from separate per-host inventory variables or a 'vars' file at runtime, which limits per-host customization to editing the playbook itself rather than simply adjusting inventory data
options.B: An Ansible module is a piece of compiled binary code that must be manually installed onto each managed target device before that device can be automated, similar in concept to how an agent-based tool would need matching software pre-installed on every node it manages
options.C: A module is a reusable unit of Ansible functionality designed to perform a specific, well-defined task (such as applying a specific configuration change, or running a specific command) against a target, abstracting the underlying platform-specific implementation details away from the playbook author, who can simply invoke the module with the relevant parameters rather than needing to write low-level connection/command logic themselves for every single task
options.D: Modules in Ansible can only ever be used to manage Linux servers, and are not designed to interacting with or being applied to any network device such as a Cisco IOS router or switch

questions.explanation_es: Un módulo es una unidad reutilizable de funcionalidad de Ansible diseñada para realizar una tarea específica y bien definida (como aplicar un cambio de configuración específico, o correr un comando específico) contra un destino, abstrayendo los detalles de implementación específicos de la plataforma subyacente para el autor del playbook, quien puede simplemente invocar el módulo con los parámetros relevantes en lugar de necesitar escribir lógica de conexión/comando de bajo nivel por su cuenta para cada tarea individual.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Why might an agent-based configuration management tool (like Puppet or Chef) be particularly well suited for managing a large fleet of general-purpose Linux/Windows servers, even though that same agent-based model is less commonly applied to network devices?

options.A: General-purpose servers are not designed to running any third-party software, including a management agent, making agent-based tools entirely unusable for managing servers and only viable for network devices instead
options.B: The choice between agent-based and agentless tooling for a given platform is mainly driven by available management-plane bandwidth rather than by whether the platform can host persistent third-party software: agent-based tools took hold on servers because data-center links had ample spare capacity for constant agent check-ins, while WAN-connected network devices stayed agentless mainly to conserve limited out-of-band bandwidth.
options.C: Agent-based tools were originally designed around the lighter resource footprint of embedded network operating systems, so an agent's overhead is typically smaller to run on a switch or router than on a general-purpose server, which is why the agent-based model is more commonly applied to network devices than to servers.
options.D: General-purpose servers can readily run arbitrary third-party software (including a persistent management agent), and the ongoing local presence of that agent allows it to continuously enforce desired state locally without needing a fresh remote connection initiated from a central controller for every single check/enforcement cycle, which is a natural fit for platforms designed to run general-purpose software — a capability many embedded network device operating systems traditionally don't offer to the same extent, making the agentless model more practical for network device management specifically

questions.explanation_es: Los servidores de propósito general pueden correr fácilmente software de terceros arbitrario (incluyendo un agente de gestión persistente), y la presencia local continua de ese agente le permite aplicar el estado deseado de forma continua sin necesitar una conexión remota fresca iniciada desde un controlador central para cada ciclo de verificación/aplicación, algo que se adapta naturalmente a plataformas diseñadas para correr software de propósito general — una capacidad que muchos sistemas operativos embebidos de dispositivos de red tradicionalmente no ofrecen en la misma medida, haciendo que el modelo agentless sea más práctico específicamente para la gestión de dispositivos de red.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What does 'orchestration' typically add on top of what basic configuration management alone (whether agent-based or agentless) provides?

options.A: Orchestration and configuration management are simply two different names for exactly the same single concept, with no meaningful distinction between coordinating a multi-step, multi-system workflow versus applying a configuration state to an individual device or set of devices, since both terms are defined by the same standards body using nearly identical wording, and vendor marketing materials frequently use the two words interchangeably without distinction
options.B: Orchestration can only ever apply to a single individual device at a time, making it functionally more limited in scope than configuration management rather than typically representing a broader, higher-level coordination capability
options.C: Orchestration typically coordinates a sequence of multiple, potentially interdependent tasks — often across multiple different systems or device types — in a defined order (such as first updating a firewall rule, then deploying an application, then verifying its health), going beyond simply pushing a configuration state to individual devices in isolation to instead managing a broader, multi-step, multi-system workflow
options.D: Orchestration is configuration management applied at a larger scale — the same single-device state-enforcement logic, simply replicated across more devices simultaneously, rather than introducing task sequencing or cross-system dependency ordering as a distinct capability.

questions.explanation_es: La orquestación típicamente coordina una secuencia de múltiples tareas potencialmente interdependientes — a menudo a través de múltiples sistemas o tipos de dispositivo distintos — en un orden definido (como primero actualizar una regla de firewall, luego desplegar una aplicación, luego verificar su salud), yendo más allá de simplemente empujar un estado de configuración a dispositivos individuales de forma aislada para en cambio gestionar un flujo de trabajo más amplio, de múltiples pasos y múltiples sistemas.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Why might 'agent sprawl' (having many different vendor-specific or tool-specific agents installed across an estate of devices) become an operational burden over time?

options.A: Each installed agent needs to be individually deployed, updated, monitored for its own health, and potentially licensed, and if an organization ends up running several different agents from different tools for different purposes across its device fleet, that cumulative overhead (patching multiple agent versions, troubleshooting agent-specific issues, managing multiple agent-specific credentials/certificates) can become a significant, growing operational burden compared to relying on fewer, more centralized/agentless mechanisms where practical
options.B: An organization can only ever install a maximum of exactly one single agent total across its entire device estate, making the scenario of 'agent sprawl' (many different agents) not supported to occur in practice
options.C: Agent sprawl is primarily a licensing cost issue rather than an operational one: since most modern agents self-update and self-monitor automatically, the main downside of running several different agents is the extra per-agent license fees rather than any additional patching or troubleshooting workload.
options.D: Agent sprawl has no meaningful operational burden, since every installed agent, regardless of how many different ones are deployed across an estate, is assumed to always update, monitor, and manage itself automatically with zero ongoing administrative overhead

questions.explanation_es: Cada agente instalado necesita desplegarse, actualizarse, y monitorearse individualmente por su propia salud, y potencialmente licenciarse, y si una organización termina corriendo varios agentes distintos de distintas herramientas para distintos propósitos en toda su flota de dispositivos, ese overhead acumulado (parchear múltiples versiones de agente, resolver problemas específicos de cada agente, gestionar múltiples credenciales/certificados específicos de agente) puede convertirse en una carga operativa significativa y creciente comparado con depender de menos mecanismos, más centralizados/agentless donde sea práctico.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What is a practical limitation of an agentless approach when the target device is completely unreachable over the network (such as during an initial zero-touch bootstrap before any IP connectivity has been established)?

options.A: An agentless tool generally still needs some form of network reachability (SSH, an API, or another remote management protocol) to the target device to actually connect and apply configuration; for a device with no network connectivity at all yet (like one still at factory defaults with no IP address configured), a different bootstrapping mechanism (such as DHCP-based zero-touch provisioning, or an initial console-based configuration step) is typically needed to first establish that basic reachability, before an agentless tool like Ansible could then take over for further ongoing configuration
options.B: A completely network-unreachable device can only be brought into an agentless tool's inventory by shipping it back to the vendor for factory reconfiguration before deployment, since neither a console cable nor DHCP-based provisioning can establish the initial reachability an agentless tool would need.
options.C: Agentless tools have no reachability requirement and can fully configure any device from a completely blank, network-unreachable factory-default state with zero prior connectivity or bootstrapping ever needed
options.D: This limitation applies to agent-based tools and has little relevance to any agentless tool, since agentless tools are assumed to always have some alternative, non-network-based mechanism available to reach and configure any device regardless of its current connectivity state, a belief that persists because some agentless tools do support an alternate out-of-band transport like a serial console cable or a vendor-specific USB provisioning port, which gets mistakenly generalized into assuming every agentless tool always has some non-network fallback mechanism available for reaching any device during that bootstrap window

questions.explanation_es: Una herramienta agentless generalmente igual necesita alguna forma de alcanzabilidad de red (SSH, una API, u otro protocolo de gestión remota) hacia el dispositivo destino para realmente conectarse y aplicar configuración; para un dispositivo sin ninguna conectividad de red todavía (como uno aún en valores de fábrica sin dirección IP configurada), típicamente se necesita un mecanismo de arranque distinto (como aprovisionamiento sin intervención basado en DHCP, o un paso inicial de configuración vía consola) para establecer primero esa alcanzabilidad básica, antes de que una herramienta agentless como Ansible pudiera entonces tomar el control para la configuración continua posterior.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Why might a network automation team choose to combine an agentless tool like Ansible with a source control system (like Git) storing the playbooks/configuration templates, rather than only running ad-hoc, one-off automation commands?

options.A: Combining Ansible with a source control system provides no practical benefit compared to running only undocumented, ad-hoc automation commands with no persistent record, version history, or change-tracking capability
options.B: Storing playbooks and configuration templates in source control provides version history, change tracking, peer review capability (via pull requests), and a documented, repeatable source of truth for what automation logic exists and how it has evolved over time, supporting a more disciplined, auditable 'infrastructure as code' practice compared to running undocumented, one-off ad-hoc commands with no persistent record of what was actually done
options.C: Storing playbooks in source control mainly serves as a backup in case a device fails, and doesn't meaningfully help with reviewing or tracking how the automation logic itself changes over time, since Git stores file snapshots rather than the reasoning behind a given configuration change.
options.D: Ansible playbooks are not designed to being stored in any source control system like Git, restricting them to being defined as one-time, non-persistent, interactively typed commands with no file-based, storable representation

questions.explanation_es: Almacenar playbooks y plantillas de configuración en control de versiones da historial de versiones, rastreo de cambios, capacidad de revisión por pares (vía pull requests), y una fuente de verdad documentada y repetible de qué lógica de automatización existe y cómo evolucionó a lo largo del tiempo, apoyando una práctica de 'infraestructura como código' más disciplinada y auditable comparado con correr comandos ad-hoc no documentados sin registro persistente de qué se hizo realmente.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What consideration around credential management is particularly important for an agentless tool that connects to many devices using centrally-stored SSH credentials or API tokens?

options.A: Since the agentless controller typically stores or has access to the credentials needed to connect to every managed device, that central credential store becomes a high-value target — protecting those credentials (through encryption at rest, a dedicated secrets/vault management system, and strict access control to the controller itself) is critical, since a compromise of the controller's credential store could potentially expose access to the entire managed device fleet at once
options.B: This credential-management consideration is unique and exclusive to agent-based tools, and has little relevance to any agentless automation architecture like Ansible
options.C: Every single managed device automatically and independently generates its own unique credentials with zero centralized storage ever required by the agentless controller, eliminating any possibility of a centralized credential-related risk, relying instead on a per-connection ephemeral key negotiated fresh with each device over an out-of-band channel that the controller itself never stores or caches once that particular session closes, since the key is regenerated independently for every new connection attempt
options.D: Credential management matters mainly for compliance reporting rather than for actual security risk, since an agentless controller typically only holds credentials in memory for the duration of a single playbook run and discards them immediately afterward, leaving little practical exposure if the controller itself were later compromised.

questions.explanation_es: Como el controlador agentless típicamente almacena o tiene acceso a las credenciales necesarias para conectarse a cada dispositivo gestionado, ese almacén central de credenciales se convierte en un objetivo de alto valor — proteger esas credenciales (mediante cifrado en reposo, un sistema dedicado de gestión de secretos/vault, y control de acceso estricto al propio controlador) es crítico, ya que un compromiso del almacén de credenciales del controlador podría potencialmente exponer el acceso a toda la flota de dispositivos gestionados de una vez.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What does it mean for an HTTP method to be 'safe', as HTTP specifications describe GET and HEAD as being?

options.A: A 'safe' method is one whose request must be authenticated before the server will process it, while an 'unsafe' method is one a server will generally process without requiring prior authentication, since access-control documentation sometimes uses 'safe' to describe a request that already passed an authentication check rather than HTTP's own formal 'safe method' term defined specifically for GET and HEAD.
options.B: Every single HTTP method, including POST, PUT, and DELETE, is considered 'safe' according to the HTTP specification, with GET and HEAD holding no special distinction from any other method in this regard
options.C: A 'safe' method is not expected to cause any meaningful change in the state of the server/resource — it's intended purely for retrieval, meaning a client (or an intermediary like a cache or proxy) can generally assume that simply making a safe request has no meaningful side effect on the server, unlike a method such as POST or DELETE which is expected to change server state as its normal, intended purpose
options.D: A 'safe' HTTP method is one whose request and response are automatically compressed by the server to reduce bandwidth, a labeling convention separate from whether the method is expected to modify server-side resource state.

questions.explanation_es: No se espera que un método 'safe' cause ningún cambio significativo en el estado del servidor/recurso — está pensado puramente para recuperación, lo que significa que un cliente (o un intermediario como un caché o proxy) generalmente puede asumir que simplemente hacer una solicitud safe no tiene efecto secundario significativo en el servidor, a diferencia de un método como POST o DELETE, del cual se espera que cambie el estado del servidor como su propósito normal y pretendido.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What does the HTTP 'OPTIONS' method typically allow a client to discover about a given resource/endpoint?

options.A: OPTIONS is primarily used to negotiate the character encoding and compression scheme for a subsequent request, rather than to discover which HTTP methods a given endpoint actually supports.
options.B: Calling OPTIONS on an endpoint typically returns the full representation of the resource in the response body, much like a GET request would, including the same caching headers such as ETag and Last-Modified, rather than simply listing which methods and capabilities the endpoint supports, since some client libraries reuse the identical body-parsing and cache-validation logic for both OPTIONS and GET requests to the same URI.
options.C: The OPTIONS method can only ever be used with an endpoint that supports the GET method, and is technically inapplicable to querying the capabilities of any endpoint that also supports POST, PUT, or DELETE
options.D: OPTIONS is commonly used to query which HTTP methods (and sometimes other capabilities, like CORS-related headers) are actually supported for a given resource/endpoint, allowing a client to programmatically determine what operations are valid before actually attempting one of them, rather than simply guessing or hardcoding an assumption about what methods a given endpoint accepts

questions.explanation_es: OPTIONS se usa comúnmente para consultar qué métodos HTTP (y a veces otras capacidades, como encabezados relacionados con CORS) realmente soporta un recurso/endpoint dado, permitiendo que un cliente determine programáticamente qué operaciones son válidas antes de realmente intentar alguna de ellas, en lugar de simplemente adivinar o asumir de forma hardcodeada qué métodos acepta un endpoint dado.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What does the HTTP 'HEAD' method do, and how does it typically differ from a GET request to the same resource?

options.A: HEAD retrieves the same response body a GET request would return, but strips out the response headers, which can be useful when a client only cares about the resource's content and not its metadata.
options.B: HEAD requests the same response headers that a GET request to that same resource would return, but without the actual response body, which can be useful for efficiently checking metadata about a resource (like its size, last-modified date, or simply whether it exists at all) without incurring the cost of transferring the potentially large full response body
options.C: A HEAD request typically triggers the same server-side processing as a POST request, such as updating a hit counter or logging an access event, but suppresses the response body afterward, rather than being a purely read-only operation.
options.D: HEAD shares the same routing and response-generation logic as GET on most servers, so a HEAD request typically returns a truncated portion of the resource's body — usually just its first few bytes — rather than omitting the body entirely.

questions.explanation_es: HEAD solicita los mismos encabezados de respuesta que devolvería una solicitud GET a ese mismo recurso, pero sin el cuerpo de la respuesta real, lo cual puede ser útil para verificar eficientemente metadatos sobre un recurso (como su tamaño, fecha de última modificación, o simplemente si existe) sin incurrir en el costo de transferir el cuerpo completo de la respuesta, potencialmente grande.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Why is POST generally considered 'not idempotent', in contrast to PUT which is idempotent?

options.A: POST is idempotent whenever it's used to update an existing resource identified in the URL, while PUT is only non-idempotent in the specific case where the request body omits a required field, so idempotency for both methods depends on how the request is constructed rather than being a fixed property of the method.
options.B: Idempotency is mainly a caching-layer concept rather than something tied to how many times a request is repeated: it describes whether an intermediate proxy is permitted to serve a cached copy of the response, which is why POST responses (rarely cached) are described as 'not idempotent' while PUT responses (sometimes cached) are described as idempotent.
options.C: Sending the exact same POST request multiple times is generally expected to create multiple separate new resources (or otherwise cause a cumulative effect) each time it's sent, since POST is typically used to 'create a new instance of something' rather than to update a specific, already-identified resource to a defined final state the way PUT does, meaning repeating a POST request doesn't reliably converge to the same single end result
options.D: POST and PUT are both non-idempotent by default in the HTTP specification, and PUT only becomes idempotent in practice when the server additionally implements optimistic concurrency control, such as an ETag/If-Match check, to reject a conflicting repeat request.

questions.explanation_es: Se espera generalmente que enviar la misma solicitud POST varias veces cree múltiples recursos nuevos separados (o de otro modo cause un efecto acumulativo) cada vez que se envía, ya que POST típicamente se usa para 'crear una nueva instancia de algo' en lugar de actualizar un recurso específico ya identificado hacia un estado final definido como sí hace PUT, lo que significa que repetir una solicitud POST no converge de forma confiable al mismo resultado final único.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What is the general REST API design convention regarding which HTTP method maps to each CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operation?

options.A: The conventional mapping uses GET for all four CRUD operations (Create, Read, Update, and Delete), with no distinction made between the different HTTP methods for any of those four distinct actions
options.B: PATCH is conventionally used for the Create operation, POST is reserved specifically for partial updates, and PUT conventionally handles the Delete operation instead of a full resource replacement.
options.C: There is no common convention mapping HTTP methods to CRUD operations; each individual API is assumed to always use a completely arbitrary, unpredictable, and non-standardized mapping between HTTP methods and CRUD actions with zero cross-API consistency, since the HTTP specification itself is claimed to define GET as the only method any compliant server may expose for a CRUD-capable resource
options.D: A common convention maps Create to POST, Read to GET, Update to PUT (full replace) or PATCH (partial update), and Delete to DELETE — providing a widely recognized, predictable pattern that helps API consumers infer the general purpose of an operation from its HTTP method alone, even before reading detailed documentation for a specific new endpoint

questions.explanation_es: Una convención común mapea Create a POST, Read a GET, Update a PUT (reemplazo completo) o PATCH (actualización parcial), y Delete a DELETE — dando un patrón ampliamente reconocido y predecible que ayuda a los consumidores de la API a inferir el propósito general de una operación solo a partir de su método HTTP, incluso antes de leer documentación detallada de un endpoint nuevo específico.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Why might a client's HTTP library or an intermediate proxy cache a GET response but never cache a POST response by default?

options.A: Because GET is defined as a safe, typically idempotent retrieval operation with no expected side effects, its response is generally considered safe to cache and reuse for a subsequent identical request; POST, by contrast, is expected to potentially cause a state change (like creating a new resource) each time it's called, so caching and reusing a previous POST response instead of actually sending the request again could produce incorrect or unintended behavior
options.B: GET and POST responses are treated with exactly identical caching behavior by every HTTP client and intermediate proxy, with no meaningful distinction in whether either method's response is typically eligible for caching by default
options.C: HTTP caching eligibility is determined mainly by the response's Content-Type header rather than by which HTTP method produced it, so a JSON response to a POST request is generally just as cacheable by default as a JSON response returned from an equivalent GET request.
options.D: PUT responses are commonly cached by default while GET responses generally require an explicit Cache-Control header before a proxy will store them, since PUT is treated as the safe, repeatable operation and GET is treated as the one expected to change server state.

questions.explanation_es: Como GET se define como una operación de recuperación segura y típicamente idempotente sin efectos secundarios esperados, generalmente se considera seguro cachear y reutilizar su respuesta para una solicitud idéntica posterior; POST, en cambio, se espera que potencialmente cause un cambio de estado (como crear un recurso nuevo) cada vez que se llama, así que cachear y reutilizar una respuesta POST previa en lugar de realmente enviar la solicitud de nuevo podría producir comportamiento incorrecto o no deseado.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What does it mean, in RESTful API terms, for the DELETE method to be considered idempotent even though calling it a second time on an already-deleted resource typically returns a 404 Not Found rather than the same success response as the first call?

options.A: DELETE is only considered idempotent for the first repeat call; a third or later repeated call is classified as breaking idempotency, since the guarantee is limited to a single retry rather than to an arbitrary number of repeated calls.
options.B: Idempotency requires that the HTTP status code family stay consistent across repeated calls — a 2xx success followed only by further 2xx responses — so DELETE returning a 404 on a repeat call after an initial 200 or 204 breaks idempotency under that stricter reading, even though the resource's deleted state hasn't changed between calls.
options.C: Idempotency here is really about whether the client receives an error at all: a well-designed API should return the same success status on every repeated DELETE call, and returning a 404 instead is considered a design flaw rather than something idempotency itself accounts for.
options.D: Idempotency is defined in terms of the end state of the resource on the server (the resource ends up deleted/absent) rather than requiring every single response to be byte-for-byte identical across repeated calls; since the resource remains deleted (absent) no matter how many additional times DELETE is called after the first successful deletion, the method is still considered idempotent even though the specific status code returned on a repeat call (like 404) may differ from the first call's response (like 200 or 204)

questions.explanation_es: La idempotencia se define en términos del estado final del recurso en el servidor (el recurso termina eliminado/ausente) en lugar de requerir que cada respuesta sea idéntica byte por byte entre llamadas repetidas; como el recurso permanece eliminado (ausente) sin importar cuántas veces más se llame a DELETE después de la primera eliminación exitosa, el método sigue considerándose idempotente aunque el código de estado específico devuelto en una llamada repetida (como 404) pueda diferir del de la primera llamada (como 200 o 204).

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Why might an automation script deliberately choose to use PATCH rather than PUT when it only needs to update a single specific field (like an interface's description) on an otherwise larger, multi-field resource?

options.A: PUT and PATCH are functionally and technically identical for this specific scenario, with no meaningful difference in risk or behavior between sending a full-resource PUT versus a partial-field PATCH when only one field actually needs to change
options.B: Using PATCH to send only the specific field(s) being changed avoids the risk (present with PUT's full-replace semantics) of accidentally omitting or overwriting other existing fields on that resource that weren't meant to be touched — if a script sent a PUT request with an incomplete representation of the resource (missing fields it wasn't actually trying to change), those omitted fields could be unintentionally cleared or reset, whereas PATCH is designed to merge in only the specified changes
options.C: Choosing PATCH over PUT for a single-field update generally prevents the API server from validating the submitted data in any meaningful case, removing any server-side validation that a PUT request would otherwise have received
options.D: PATCH can only ever be used to update every single field of a resource simultaneously, making it functionally identical to PUT rather than offering a genuinely more targeted, partial-update alternative for changing just one specific field

questions.explanation_es: Usar PATCH para enviar solo el/los campo(s) específico(s) que se está cambiando evita el riesgo (presente con la semántica de reemplazo completo de PUT) de omitir u sobrescribir accidentalmente otros campos existentes de ese recurso que no se pretendía tocar — si un script enviara una solicitud PUT con una representación incompleta del recurso (faltando campos que en realidad no intentaba cambiar), esos campos omitidos podrían borrarse o reiniciarse sin querer, mientras que PATCH está diseñado para fusionar solo los cambios especificados.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What is the purpose of the HTTP 'CONNECT' method, and in what typical scenario is it used rather than GET, POST, or the other more commonly discussed REST-oriented methods?

options.A: CONNECT establishes an HTTP-level session much like GET does, but instead of returning a resource representation, it returns the destination server's supported TLS cipher suites and certificate chain, which the proxy caches and uses to pre-negotiate the encrypted session on the client's behalf, functioning as a capability-discovery step that precedes regular request/response traffic rather than as a tunnel-establishment mechanism in its own right.
options.B: CONNECT is used to establish a tunnel through an HTTP proxy to a destination server, typically used to support HTTPS connections passing through a proxy (the client asks the proxy to open a raw, tunneled connection to the destination, after which encrypted TLS traffic flows through that tunnel directly between the client and destination), rather than being used for typical REST API resource operations like retrieving or modifying data
options.C: The CONNECT method can only ever be used to permanently delete a resource from a server, making it functionally identical to DELETE rather than serving any proxy-tunneling purpose
options.D: CONNECT is the standard, universally recommended method for a typical REST API's Create operation, functioning as a direct alternative to POST for creating new resources

questions.explanation_es: CONNECT se usa para establecer un túnel a través de un proxy HTTP hacia un servidor destino, típicamente usado para soportar conexiones HTTPS que pasan por un proxy (el cliente le pide al proxy que abra una conexión cruda y tunelizada hacia el destino, después de lo cual el tráfico TLS cifrado fluye a través de ese túnel directamente entre el cliente y el destino), en lugar de usarse para operaciones típicas de recurso de una API REST como recuperar o modificar datos.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Why might a REST API design choose to explicitly restrict which HTTP methods are permitted on a given endpoint (for example, allowing only GET on a read-only reporting endpoint), rather than allowing every possible HTTP method on every endpoint?

options.A: Restricting the allowed methods on a given endpoint enforces the endpoint's intended purpose at the API level (for example, ensuring a purely informational reporting endpoint can never accidentally or maliciously be used to modify data via an unintended POST/PUT/DELETE call), providing a layer of API-level access control that complements broader authentication/authorization mechanisms
options.B: Restricting allowed HTTP methods on an endpoint provides no meaningful security or design benefit, since every endpoint in any well-designed REST API is expected to always support every single possible HTTP method
options.C: HTTP method restriction is a capability unique to XML-based SOAP APIs and has little meaningful applicability to the design of any typical JSON-based REST API
options.D: Once an endpoint restricts which methods are permitted, that restriction always and disables the ability for a client to interact with that endpoint using the one specific method that IS actually permitted, effectively disabling the endpoint entirely, because HTTP is claimed to permanently bind each endpoint to exactly one allowed method the moment it's first registered, making a GET-only URL structurally incapable of change

questions.explanation_es: Restringir los métodos permitidos en un endpoint dado hace cumplir el propósito pretendido de ese endpoint a nivel de API (por ejemplo, asegurando que un endpoint de reportes puramente informativo nunca pueda usarse accidental o maliciosamente para modificar datos vía una llamada POST/PUT/DELETE no pretendida), dando una capa de control de acceso a nivel de API que complementa mecanismos más amplios de autenticación/autorización.

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: What does the term 'method not allowed' (associated with the HTTP 405 status code) indicate, and how does it relate to a resource that does exist but doesn't support the specific method that was attempted?

options.A: A 405 status code indicates that the request's Content-Type header didn't match a format the server accepts, rather than signaling anything about which specific HTTP method was used.
options.B: A 405 response indicates the request succeeded completely with no issue, functioning identically in meaning to a 200 OK response rather than signaling any kind of method-related error condition
options.C: A 405 response indicates that the targeted resource does exist and is reachable, but the specific HTTP method used in the request (such as attempting a DELETE on a resource that only supports GET and PUT) is not supported for that resource, which is a more specific and informative signal than a generic 404 (which would suggest the resource itself doesn't exist at all)
options.D: A 405 status code indicates the resource exists but requires authentication before any method can be attempted against it, typically accompanied by a WWW-Authenticate header specifying the expected credential scheme — a meaning more specifically associated with 401 Unauthorized than with 405, since both codes can appear when a client's initial request lacks valid credentials for a protected resource.

questions.explanation_es: Una respuesta 405 indica que el recurso destino existe y es alcanzable, pero el método HTTP específico usado en la solicitud (como intentar un DELETE en un recurso que solo soporta GET y PUT) no está soportado para ese recurso, lo cual es una señal más específica e informativa que un 404 genérico (que sugeriría que el propio recurso no existe en absoluto).

questions.name: Métodos HTTP
questions.question: Why is it important for API documentation to clearly specify not just which HTTP methods a given endpoint supports, but also the expected request body format and required fields for methods like POST, PUT, or PATCH?

options.A: The HTTP method name alone (such as 'POST') generally conveys every detail a client needs to construct a fully valid request body, making any additional documentation of expected fields, structure, or data types entirely redundant and unnecessary
options.B: Simply knowing that an endpoint 'accepts POST' isn't enough information for a developer or automation script to actually construct a valid request; without clear documentation of the expected body structure, required versus optional fields, and data types, a client is likely to send a malformed or incomplete request that the API would reject (typically with a 400 or 422 error), making that additional documentation essential for successfully integrating with the API rather than the HTTP method name alone being sufficient guidance
options.C: API documentation formats like OpenAPI are primarily intended to describe available endpoints and supported methods, with request body schemas treated as an optional, advanced feature most teams skip, since request body validation is generally left to server-side runtime error messages instead.
options.D: Request body format and required fields matter mainly for internal, service-to-service API calls, while public-facing POST, PUT, or PATCH endpoints are generally designed to accept a flexible body structure and infer the intended fields automatically.

questions.explanation_es: Simplemente saber que un endpoint 'acepta POST' no es suficiente información para que un desarrollador o script de automatización realmente construya una solicitud válida; sin documentación clara de la estructura de cuerpo esperada, los campos requeridos versus opcionales, y los tipos de dato, es probable que un cliente envíe una solicitud malformada o incompleta que la API rechazaría (típicamente con un error 400 o 422), haciendo que esa documentación adicional sea esencial para integrarse exitosamente con la API en lugar de que el nombre del método HTTP solo sea guía suficiente.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: What is the purpose of the RESTCONF 'Accept' request header, and what does it tell the server about how the client wants the response formatted?

options.A: The 'Accept' header tells the RESTCONF server which YANG datastore, such as running or candidate, the client intends to operate against, rather than specifying the client's preferred response encoding.
options.B: RESTCONF servers always ignore the 'Accept' header entirely and unconditionally return every response in a single fixed format, regardless of what the client actually specified in that header
options.C: The 'Accept' header can only ever be used with a GET request, and is technically invalid, unsupported syntax when included with a POST, PUT, or PATCH request to a RESTCONF server
options.D: The 'Accept' header tells the RESTCONF server which media type(s) the client is able to process in the response (such as 'application/yang-data+json' or 'application/yang-data+xml'), allowing the client to request its preferred response encoding rather than the server unilaterally choosing a format the client might not be prepared to parse

questions.explanation_es: El encabezado 'Accept' le dice al servidor RESTCONF qué tipo(s) de medio puede procesar el cliente en la respuesta (como 'application/yang-data+json' o 'application/yang-data+xml'), permitiendo que el cliente solicite su codificación de respuesta preferida en lugar de que el servidor elija unilateralmente un formato que el cliente podría no estar preparado para parsear.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Why does a RESTCONF request that modifies configuration (like a POST or PUT) typically need to include a 'Content-Type' header specifying the format of the request body?

options.A: A RESTCONF server always ignores the 'Content-Type' header entirely regardless of what value the client sends, and instead attempts to auto-detect the request body's format through some other undocumented mechanism, instead relying on inspecting the opening bytes of the payload itself, similar to a Unix 'file' command's magic-number sniffing, to guess between JSON, XML, or another encoding before validating the submitted YANG configuration data against the target schema
options.B: The 'Content-Type' header tells the server how to correctly parse/interpret the request body being sent (such as 'application/yang-data+json' indicating the body is JSON-formatted YANG data), which the server needs to know in order to correctly decode the submitted configuration data before validating and applying it, rather than the server having to guess or assume a single fixed format for every incoming request
options.C: 'Content-Type' tells the server which specific YANG datastore, such as running or candidate, the modifying request should be applied against, rather than describing the encoding format of the request body itself.
options.D: The 'Content-Type' header can only ever be included with a GET request, and is technically invalid, unsupported syntax when included with any configuration-modifying request like POST, PUT, or PATCH

questions.explanation_es: El encabezado 'Content-Type' le dice al servidor cómo parsear/interpretar correctamente el cuerpo de la solicitud que se está enviando (como 'application/yang-data+json' indicando que el cuerpo tiene formato JSON de datos YANG), lo cual el servidor necesita saber para decodificar correctamente los datos de configuración enviados antes de validarlos y aplicarlos, en lugar de que el servidor tenga que adivinar o asumir un único formato fijo para cada solicitud entrante.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: What does RESTCONF's reliance on standard HTTP status codes (rather than a completely custom, RESTCONF-specific error-reporting scheme) provide as a practical benefit for client development?

options.A: Since RESTCONF reuses the same well-understood HTTP status code semantics that developers are already broadly familiar with from working with countless other REST APIs (like 404 for not found, 401 for unauthorized, 400/422 for invalid input), a client library or developer doesn't need to learn an entirely new, RESTCONF-specific error-code scheme from scratch, easing the general learning curve and enabling reuse of existing HTTP-handling logic/tooling
options.B: RESTCONF actually uses a completely custom, proprietary error-code numbering scheme entirely unrelated to standard HTTP status codes, making this description of it reusing standard HTTP codes fundamentally inaccurate
options.C: Standard HTTP status codes provide no practical benefit for RESTCONF client development, since every developer would need to learn an entirely new set of codes regardless of whether RESTCONF reused standard HTTP codes or invented its own custom scheme
options.D: RESTCONF's use of HTTP status codes is limited to the 2xx success range, with the protocol relying on some other undocumented mechanism entirely separate from HTTP status codes to report any kind of error condition

questions.explanation_es: Como RESTCONF reutiliza la misma semántica de códigos de estado HTTP bien entendida con la que los desarrolladores ya están ampliamente familiarizados por trabajar con incontables otras APIs REST (como 404 para no encontrado, 401 para no autorizado, 400/422 para entrada inválida), una librería cliente o un desarrollador no necesita aprender un esquema de códigos de error completamente nuevo y específico de RESTCONF desde cero, facilitando la curva de aprendizaje general y permitiendo reutilizar lógica/herramientas de manejo de HTTP ya existentes.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'ietf-yang-patch' media type sometimes used with RESTCONF, as a more granular alternative to a plain PATCH request?

options.A: YANG Patch can only ever be used to perform a single edit operation identical to a plain PATCH request, providing no additional granularity or capability beyond what a standard PATCH request already offers
options.B: The YANG Patch media type allows a single RESTCONF request to describe multiple distinct edit operations (each potentially targeting a different specific location within the data tree, with its own operation type like merge, replace, or delete) in one structured request body, providing finer-grained control over a set of changes than a single, simpler PATCH request targeting just one resource path would allow
options.C: 'ietf-yang-patch' is primarily a mechanism for validating a proposed configuration change against the device's YANG schema before it's applied, rather than a format for describing multiple distinct edit operations within a single request.
options.D: Once a YANG Patch request is submitted, it generally replaces the device's entire running configuration in one operation, rather than allowing multiple distinct, more targeted edit operations to be described

questions.explanation_es: El media type YANG Patch le permite a una única solicitud RESTCONF describir múltiples operaciones de edición distintas (cada una potencialmente apuntando a una ubicación específica distinta dentro del árbol de datos, con su propio tipo de operación como merge, replace, o delete) en un único cuerpo de solicitud estructurado, dando un control más granular sobre un conjunto de cambios de lo que permitiría una única solicitud PATCH más simple apuntando a solo una ruta de recurso.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: Why might a RESTCONF client need to handle the possibility of receiving a response in either JSON or XML format, even when it specifically requested one particular format via the Accept header?

options.A: While a well-behaved RESTCONF server should honor the client's Accept header preference when possible, a client written robustly should still be prepared to handle the case where the server returns an error response (or otherwise cannot honor that preference) in the alternative supported format, or should explicitly verify the actual returned Content-Type in the response rather than blindly assuming the response format always exactly matches what the request's Accept header specified
options.B: A RESTCONF client specifies its preferred response format through the URI's file extension, such as appending '.json' or '.xml' to the resource path, rather than through a request header like Accept, which servers generally ignore for that purpose.
options.C: This consideration only applies to RESTCONF clients written in a compiled language like C++, and has little relevance to a client written in a scripting language like Python
options.D: RESTCONF servers are not designed to ever returning any format other than exactly what the client's Accept header specified, making this consideration around handling an unexpected format unnecessary and irrelevant in practice

questions.explanation_es: Aunque un servidor RESTCONF bien comportado debería respetar la preferencia del encabezado Accept del cliente cuando sea posible, un cliente escrito de forma robusta debería igual estar preparado para manejar el caso donde el servidor devuelve una respuesta de error (u de otro modo no puede respetar esa preferencia) en el formato alternativo soportado, o debería verificar explícitamente el Content-Type realmente devuelto en la respuesta en lugar de asumir ciegamente que el formato de respuesta siempre coincide exactamente con lo que especificó el Accept header de la solicitud.

questions.name: RESTCONF
questions.question: What does RESTCONF's stateless request/response model mean for how a client must handle a sequence of related configuration changes, compared to NETCONF's stateful, session-based candidate/commit workflow?

options.A: Because each RESTCONF request is generally treated as an independent, self-contained operation with no built-in server-side session state tying multiple requests together into one transaction, a client needing to apply several related changes together as a single atomic unit typically must either combine them into one structured request (such as via YANG Patch) or accept that RESTCONF's default model doesn't provide the same native multi-request staging/commit transaction that NETCONF's candidate datastore workflow offers
options.B: Because RESTCONF is stateless, it's not supported for a RESTCONF client to ever make more than a single configuration change in total to a device across its entire lifetime, making the very question of applying 'a sequence of related changes' inapplicable to RESTCONF, a restriction some engineers wrongly infer from RESTCONF's per-request statelessness itself, reasoning that because no session ties requests together, the underlying datastore must also reject any request arriving after the very first one has already been committed successfully
options.C: RESTCONF's stateless model provides the same candidate-datastore staging and two-phase commit workflow as NETCONF by default, so a client doesn't need to combine related changes into a single structured request the way it would with NETCONF's session-based model.
options.D: RESTCONF and NETCONF provide exactly identical native support for staging and atomically committing multiple related configuration changes together as a single transaction, with no meaningful difference in transactional capability between the two protocols

questions.explanation_es: Como cada solicitud RESTCONF generalmente se trata como una operación independiente y autocontenida sin estado de sesión del lado del servidor incorporado que ate varias solicitudes juntas en una transacción, un cliente que necesita aplicar varios cambios relacionados juntos como una unidad atómica típicamente debe combinarlos en una única solicitud estructurada (como vía YANG Patch) o aceptar que el modelo por defecto de RESTCONF no provee la misma transacción nativa de preparación/commit de múltiples solicitudes que ofrece el flujo de trabajo del datastore candidate de NETCONF.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What happens to an 802.1Q tag when a frame is forwarded from a trunk port onto an access port configured for that same VLAN?

options.A: The switch converts the tag into an MPLS label before forwarding it out the access port
options.B: The frame is dropped, since access ports can never receive tagged traffic from a trunk under any configuration, on the assumption that the port's VLAN ID must match an incoming tag value
options.C: The tag is left intact and the access port forwards the frame exactly as received, tag included
options.D: The switch strips the 802.1Q tag before forwarding the frame out the access port, since access ports carry only untagged traffic for their single assigned VLAN

questions.explanation_es: El switch quita la etiqueta 802.1Q antes de reenviar el frame por el puerto de acceso, ya que los puertos de acceso transportan tráfico sin etiquetar para su única VLAN asignada.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Why is running CDP or LLDP on trunk links useful for documenting and troubleshooting a VLAN trunking topology?

options.A: CDP/LLDP let neighboring switches automatically discover and display information about each other (device ID, port, capabilities), helping an engineer quickly verify actual physical topology and cabling against what's documented, without relying solely on manual diagrams
options.B: CDP/LLDP primarily negotiate which VLANs are permitted to traverse a trunk, similar to VTP pruning, rather than helping an engineer discover and verify the physical topology and cabling.
options.C: CDP/LLDP require every trunk to carry exactly one single VLAN, restricting trunking flexibility
options.D: CDP/LLDP replace the need for 802.1Q tagging entirely on any link where they are enabled

questions.explanation_es: CDP/LLDP permiten que switches vecinos se descubran automáticamente y compartan información (ID del dispositivo, puerto, capacidades), ayudando a un ingeniero a verificar rápidamente la topología física real contra lo documentado, sin depender solo de diagramas manuales.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is a potential downside of extending the same VLAN across many switches and a large geographic area within a campus?

options.A: Extending a VLAN across many switches always improves convergence time for every routing protocol running on those switches, since a larger Layer 2 domain is assumed to reduce the number of routing adjacencies that need to be maintained
options.B: There is no downside; VLANs are designed specifically to scale without limit across an arbitrarily large Layer 2 footprint, since STP's loop-prevention mechanism is assumed to also cap the underlying broadcast domain's physical size
options.C: Extending a VLAN automatically increases the maximum frame size that can be carried on every trunk in the topology, requiring every switch along the path to be reconfigured for a larger MTU
options.D: It expands the Layer 2 broadcast/failure domain, meaning a broadcast storm, MAC flapping issue, or STP problem in one part of that VLAN can potentially impact every switch carrying it, across the entire extended footprint

questions.explanation_es: Extender la misma VLAN entre muchos switches y un área geográfica grande amplía el dominio de broadcast/falla de Capa 2, lo que significa que una tormenta de broadcast, un problema de flapping de MAC, o un problema de STP en una parte de esa VLAN puede potencialmente impactar a cada switch que la transporta en todo ese alcance extendido.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Why might an engineer verify 'show interfaces trunk' output on both ends of a link during troubleshooting, rather than checking only one side?

options.A: A trunk's actual behavior depends on the configuration of both ends agreeing (native VLAN, allowed VLANs, trunk mode); checking only one side could miss a mismatch that's only visible by comparing both switches' configuration and status side by side
options.B: Checking both ends of a trunk link is only relevant when troubleshooting a routing protocol issue, and has little relevance to diagnosing a Layer 2 trunking problem
options.C: 'show interfaces trunk' output is always identical on both ends of any link regardless of actual configuration, making comparison between the two sides unnecessary
options.D: Trunk configuration only ever needs to be verified on a single side of a link, since Cisco IOS is assumed to automatically synchronize configuration between both ends of any trunk, treating native VLAN and allowed-VLAN lists as though they were negotiated like DTP mode

questions.explanation_es: El comportamiento real de un trunk depende de que la configuración de ambos extremos coincida (VLAN nativa, VLANs permitidas, modo de trunk); verificar solo un lado podría pasar por alto un desajuste que solo es visible comparando la configuración y el estado de ambos switches lado a lado.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What does it mean for a VLAN to be in the 'active' state but not currently 'forwarding' on a specific trunk, as shown in 'show interfaces trunk' output?

options.A: A VLAN shown as active but not forwarding has been permanently and irreversibly deleted from the switch's VLAN database entirely
options.B: This state indicates that a native VLAN mismatch on the trunk has caused the switch to block traffic for every VLAN on that link except the one carried untagged, rather than reflecting a per-VLAN STP instance's own forwarding state.
options.C: 'Active' means the VLAN is allowed on the trunk by its allowed-VLAN list, while 'forwarding' additionally requires that VTP has propagated that VLAN's database entry to every other switch in the domain, so a VLAN can show active-but-not-forwarding simply because VTP synchronization hasn't yet completed.
options.D: The VLAN exists and is allowed on that trunk, but STP has currently placed that VLAN's instance on that particular trunk port into a blocking state (to prevent a loop), so traffic for that VLAN is not actively being forwarded across that specific link at this moment

questions.explanation_es: La VLAN existe y está permitida en ese trunk, pero STP actualmente colocó la instancia de esa VLAN en ese puerto trunk en particular en estado de bloqueo (para evitar un loop), así que el tráfico de esa VLAN no se está reenviando activamente por ese enlace específico en este momento.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What EIGRP command displays the topology table, including successors and feasible successors for each destination?

options.A: 'show ip eigrp topology', which lists each known destination along with its feasible distance, reported distances from neighbors, and which entries qualify as successor or feasible successor
options.B: 'show cdp neighbors', which displays Layer 2 neighbor information unrelated to EIGRP's Layer 3 topology table
options.C: 'show ip route eigrp', which lists only the routes EIGRP has actually installed into the routing table, without showing the feasible successors or reported distances that make up the fuller topology table.
options.D: 'show ip protocols' only, which never displays any per-destination topology table information for EIGRP

questions.explanation_es: 'show ip eigrp topology' lista cada destino conocido junto con su distancia factible, las distancias reportadas por los vecinos, y cuáles entradas califican como successor o feasible successor.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why does EIGRP typically converge very quickly when a feasible successor already exists for a failed route?

options.A: EIGRP still waits for the full hold timer on the failed successor to expire before it will promote an existing feasible successor, since DUAL requires that timer to expire as its trigger for re-evaluating the topology table, even when a validated feasible successor is already present.
options.B: A feasible successor can only be used after a fixed delay of several minutes, regardless of how quickly the successor actually failed
options.C: Because the feasible successor was already validated as loop-free ahead of time and is already present in the topology table, EIGRP can immediately promote it to successor and install it in the routing table without needing to query neighbors or wait for any new computation
options.D: EIGRP has no concept of using a pre-computed backup route; every route change always requires a full topology recalculation

questions.explanation_es: Como el feasible successor ya fue validado como libre de loops de antemano y ya está presente en la tabla de topología, EIGRP puede promoverlo inmediatamente a successor e instalarlo en la tabla de enrutamiento sin necesitar consultar a los vecinos ni esperar ningún cálculo nuevo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the purpose of OSPF's 'router LSA' (Type 1) age field, and what happens when an LSA's age reaches MaxAge without being refreshed?

options.A: LSA age primarily affects SPF calculation priority rather than database retention — an older LSA is simply processed later in the SPF run, but every originated LSA otherwise persists in the database indefinitely regardless of its age value.
options.B: The age field tracks how long since the LSA was originated/refreshed; if it reaches MaxAge (typically 3600 seconds) without a fresh refresh from the originating router, the LSA is flushed from the database, since routers periodically refresh their own LSAs to keep them current
options.C: MaxAge is measured independently by each receiving router based on when it first received the LSA rather than when the originating router created it, so two routers that received the same LSA at different times flush it from their databases at different moments.
options.D: The age field only applies to External (Type 5) LSAs and has no relevance to Router (Type 1) LSAs

questions.explanation_es: El campo age rastrea cuánto tiempo pasó desde que la LSA se originó/refrescó; si llega a MaxAge (típicamente 3600 segundos) sin un refresco del router originador, la LSA se elimina de la base de datos, ya que los routers refrescan periódicamente sus propias LSAs para mantenerlas vigentes.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why might an engineer prefer EIGRP in a mixed-bandwidth WAN environment where per-neighbor path metrics vary significantly?

options.A: EIGRP's composite metric (heavily weighted by bandwidth and delay by default) can naturally reflect meaningful differences between paths of very different quality, and its unequal-cost load-balancing via variance offers additional flexibility not natively available with plain OSPF cost
options.B: Metric differences between paths have no bearing on which routing protocol might be preferred in a given WAN design
options.C: OSPF's cost metric always more accurately reflects true path quality than EIGRP's composite metric in every possible topology, making this scenario irrelevant
options.D: EIGRP's default composite metric weighs delay much more heavily than bandwidth, which can occasionally cause it to prefer a lower-bandwidth, low-delay path over a higher-bandwidth path with more accumulated delay, unlike OSPF's cost metric, which is derived purely from configured bandwidth.

questions.explanation_es: La métrica compuesta de EIGRP (fuertemente ponderada por ancho de banda y delay por defecto) puede reflejar naturalmente diferencias significativas entre caminos de calidad muy distinta, y su balanceo de carga de costo desigual vía variance ofrece flexibilidad adicional no disponible nativamente con el costo simple de OSPF.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What does the OSPF 'show ip ospf neighbor' command's 'State' column (e.g., FULL, 2WAY, INIT) indicate about a given adjacency?

options.A: State reflects which OSPF network type, such as broadcast or point-to-point, is configured on the local interface facing that neighbor, rather than the live progress of that specific adjacency's formation process.
options.B: A neighbor showing 'INIT' state means the adjacency has already fully synchronized and no further progress is possible or needed
options.C: It shows the current stage of the neighbor formation/synchronization process that adjacency has reached, with FULL indicating the two routers have fully synchronized their link-state databases and are considered fully adjacent, while an earlier state like INIT or 2WAY indicates the process hasn't yet completed
options.D: The State column only ever reports two possible values, UP or DOWN, collapsing the several intermediate stages like INIT, 2WAY, and EXSTART into a single binary status, which can make it harder to pinpoint exactly where a stuck neighbor relationship is failing.

questions.explanation_es: Muestra la etapa actual del proceso de formación/sincronización de vecino que alcanzó esa adyacencia, con FULL indicando que ambos routers sincronizaron completamente sus bases de datos de estado de enlace y se consideran totalmente adyacentes, mientras que un estado anterior como INIT o 2WAY indica que el proceso aún no terminó.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why might two OSPF routers get stuck in the 'EXSTART' or 'EXCHANGE' state and never reach FULL adjacency?

options.A: These states primarily reflect whether the two routers' OSPF process IDs match, rather than the actual progress of link-state database synchronization between the neighbors.
options.B: Getting stuck at EXSTART or EXCHANGE can only ever be caused by a physical cable being unplugged, never by any software-level configuration mismatch like MTU
options.C: A common cause is an MTU mismatch between the two routers' interfaces, since OSPF's database description packets carried during exchange can be dropped or rejected if their size exceeds what one side's interface MTU allows, preventing the link-state database synchronization from ever completing
options.D: EXSTART and EXCHANGE are purely transient logging entries that a router only displays for a few seconds regardless of underlying conditions, so a neighbor relationship shown stuck there in 'show ip ospf neighbor' output is actually already fully adjacent and the display simply hasn't refreshed yet.

questions.explanation_es: Una causa común es un desajuste de MTU entre las interfaces de ambos routers, ya que los paquetes de descripción de base de datos de OSPF transportados durante exchange pueden descartarse o rechazarse si su tamaño excede lo que permite el MTU de la interfaz de un lado, impidiendo que la sincronización de la base de datos de estado de enlace llegue a completarse.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What does 'show ip ospf interface' display that is useful for verifying OSPF interface-level configuration?

options.A: It displays the interface's configured MTU and bandwidth values used in OSPF's cost calculation, but does not show area assignment, DR/BDR status, or neighbor count, which require a separate command to view.
options.B: This command primarily reports Layer 1/2 interface statistics like speed, duplex, and error counters, with OSPF-specific fields such as area assignment and DR/BDR status only appearing when the 'detail' keyword is additionally specified.
options.C: 'show ip ospf interface' only ever displays information about interfaces not running OSPF, excluding any OSPF-enabled interface from its output entirely
options.D: It shows per-interface OSPF details such as the area assignment, network type, cost, timers, DR/BDR status, and neighbor count, helping verify that an interface is configured and participating in OSPF as expected

questions.explanation_es: Muestra detalles por interfaz de OSPF como la asignación de área, tipo de red, costo, temporizadores, estado de DR/BDR, y cantidad de vecinos, ayudando a verificar que una interfaz esté configurada y participando en OSPF como se espera.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Why must the OSPF 'area' assigned to a given interface match on both ends of a link for an adjacency to form?

options.A: OSPF adjacencies are formed per-area; if the two ends of a link disagree about which area that link belongs to, they'll consider the hello parameters mismatched and refuse to form an adjacency, since the area is a fundamental part of how OSPF hello packets are validated between neighbors
options.B: Area assignment is relevant only for OSPFv3, and OSPFv2 routers never check or require area agreement between neighbors on the same link
options.C: Area mismatch is automatically and silently corrected by OSPF itself, with the two routers each independently deciding to use whichever area was configured on the router with the lower router-id — similar to how OSPF is sometimes believed to resolve a duplicate router-id conflict automatically during adjacency formation
options.D: OSPF area assignment has little bearing on adjacency formation; two routers with mismatched area configuration on the same link will always form a full adjacency without any issue

questions.explanation_es: Las adyacencias de OSPF se forman por área; si los dos extremos de un enlace no están de acuerdo sobre a qué área pertenece ese enlace, considerarán que los parámetros del hello no coinciden y se negarán a formar una adyacencia, ya que el área es una parte fundamental de cómo se validan los paquetes hello de OSPF entre vecinos.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the effect of configuring 'default-information originate' on an OSPF router?

options.A: The command configures the default seed metric OSPF assigns to externally redistributed routes in general, rather than specifically originating a 0.0.0.0/0 default route into the OSPF domain.
options.B: This command disables all OSPF route advertisement on that router entirely, preventing it from originating any route, default or otherwise
options.C: 'default-information originate' can only be used within a stub area, and is technically invalid, unsupported syntax anywhere else in an OSPF configuration — since default-route origination is generally assumed to rely on the same implicit mechanism a stub area's ABR automatically injects, rather than being usable on any router regardless of area type
options.D: It causes that router to originate and advertise a default route (0.0.0.0/0) into the OSPF domain, which is commonly used on a router that connects to the internet or another external network, so other OSPF routers can learn a path toward destinations not otherwise present in the OSPF database

questions.explanation_es: Hace que ese router origine y anuncie una ruta default (0.0.0.0/0) hacia el dominio OSPF, comúnmente usado en un router que se conecta a internet u otra red externa, para que los demás routers OSPF puedan aprender un camino hacia destinos que de otro modo no estarían presentes en la base de datos OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Why might an engineer configure OSPF 'bfd' (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) on a link, in addition to standard OSPF hello/dead timers?

options.A: Configuring BFD on an OSPF-enabled link always and disables OSPF's own hello/dead timer mechanism entirely, replacing it rather than complementing it
options.B: BFD and OSPF hello/dead timers detect exactly the same failure condition using an identical mechanism, providing zero speed or detection benefit when used together, since both are assumed to rely on the same sub-second hello interval rather than BFD's independent, faster detection process
options.C: BFD can detect a link/neighbor failure much faster (often in tens to hundreds of milliseconds) than waiting for OSPF's own dead timer to expire, and can trigger OSPF to react to that failure faster than relying solely on missed OSPF hellos
options.D: BFD can only be used with EIGRP and has little applicability to detecting an OSPF neighbor or link failure

questions.explanation_es: BFD puede detectar una falla de enlace/vecino mucho más rápido (a menudo en decenas a cientos de milisegundos) que esperar a que expire el propio dead timer de OSPF, y puede hacer que OSPF reaccione a esa falla más rápido que depender únicamente de hellos de OSPF perdidos.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What does the 'ip ospf priority 0' command applied to an interface accomplish, in terms of DR/BDR election on that segment?

options.A: A priority of 0 always guarantees that router will become the DR on that segment, since a priority of 0 is treated as the highest possible value in the DR election algorithm
options.B: Configuring priority 0 disables OSPF entirely on that interface, preventing the interface from forming any adjacency at all
options.C: A priority of 0 only affects the tiebreaker used when two routers have an identical router-id, and otherwise has no bearing on whether a router is eligible to become DR or BDR on that segment.
options.D: A priority of 0 makes the router ineligible to ever become the DR or BDR on that segment, effectively guaranteeing it will always be a DROTHER 's priority or router-id, which can be useful to intentionally exclude a specific router from the DR/BDR role

questions.explanation_es: Una prioridad de 0 hace que el router sea inelegible para convertirse en DR o BDR en ese segmento, garantizando efectivamente que siempre sea un DROTHER sin importar la prioridad o router-id de cualquier otro router, lo cual puede ser útil para excluir intencionalmente a un router específico del rol de DR/BDR.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Why is understanding OSPF LSA types (Type 1 Router, Type 2 Network, Type 3 Summary, Type 5 External, etc.) important when troubleshooting why a specific route is missing from a router's routing table?

options.A: LSA type only matters for OSPFv3, and OSPFv2 does not use LSA types to categorize different pieces of routing information
options.B: LSA types mainly affect how a route appears in the routing table's output formatting, such as whether it's marked O, O IA, or E2, but every LSA type is flooded and filtered identically at area and domain boundaries, so an engineer troubleshooting a missing prefix should look at redistribution and access-list filtering rather than at which LSA type was technically involved.
options.C: There is only a single LSA type in OSPF, making the concept of distinguishing between different LSA types for troubleshooting purposes entirely inapplicable
options.D: Each LSA type conveys different information and propagates differently (some are confined to an area, others cross area/domain boundaries); understanding which LSA type should be carrying a given route helps an engineer determine where in the OSPF topology to look for a missing or unexpectedly filtered piece of routing information

questions.explanation_es: Cada tipo de LSA transporta información distinta y se propaga de forma distinta (algunas quedan confinadas a un área, otras cruzan límites de área/dominio); entender qué tipo de LSA debería estar transportando una ruta dada ayuda a un ingeniero a determinar dónde buscar en la topología OSPF una pieza de información de enrutamiento faltante o filtrada inesperadamente.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What command is commonly used to verify the current state of a BGP neighbor relationship (e.g., Idle, Active, Established)?

options.A: 'show ip bgp neighbors', which primarily displays the negotiated capabilities and configured timers for each peer, but does not report the current session state such as Idle, Active, or Established.
options.B: 'show interfaces status' displays BGP neighbor state directly alongside physical interface link status, with no separate BGP-specific command needed
options.C: 'show ip bgp summary' (or 'show bgp summary'), which lists each configured neighbor along with its current session state or, if Established, the number of prefixes received from that neighbor
options.D: BGP neighbor state can never be verified through any Cisco IOS command output, and must always be inferred solely by observing whether routes are present in the routing table, since the state machine is assumed to have no exposed show command

questions.explanation_es: 'show ip bgp summary' (o 'show bgp summary') lista cada vecino configurado junto con su estado de sesión actual o, si está Established, la cantidad de prefijos recibidos de ese vecino.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Why does BGP typically use a much longer default hold-down/keepalive interval compared to an IGP like OSPF or EIGRP?

options.A: The longer BGP timer mainly exists to accommodate the additional TCP session overhead and per-update path processing BGP requires compared to an IGP, rather than being chosen specifically to protect internet-scale routing stability from flapping caused by a faster timer.
options.B: BGP timers are always identical to OSPF's default timers, with no meaningful difference in typical default interval length between the two protocols
options.C: BGP cannot support any configurable timer at all; its keepalive/hold interval is a fixed, unchangeable constant on every implementation
options.D: BGP is designed for stability over the internet-scale routing table, where excessively fast reconvergence triggered by a transient blip could cause significant route-flapping/instability across many downstream networks; a longer timer trades off some convergence speed for greater overall stability at that massive scale

questions.explanation_es: BGP está diseñado para dar estabilidad sobre la tabla de enrutamiento a escala de internet, donde una reconvergencia excesivamente rápida disparada por un problema transitorio podría causar inestabilidad/flapping de rutas significativo en muchas redes aguas abajo; un temporizador más largo intercambia algo de velocidad de convergencia por mayor estabilidad general a esa escala masiva.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the purpose of BGP 'next-hop-self' configured on an iBGP router that receives a route from an eBGP peer and re-advertises it to other iBGP peers?

options.A: Configuring next-hop-self generally prevents that router from ever advertising any route learned via eBGP to any of its iBGP peers
