questions.explanation_es: Una ACL de interfaz del plano de datos filtra el tráfico de tránsito que pasa por el dispositivo, mientras que CoPP protege específicamente la propia CPU del dispositivo del tráfico destinado a ella, lo que significa que aunque el filtrado de tráfico de tránsito ya esté bien diseñado, el tráfico legítimamente destinado al propio dispositivo (o el tráfico que llega al plano de control por algún otro camino) igual se beneficia de CoPP como una capa dedicada y complementaria de protección específica del plano de control.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: Why might CoPP configuration differ meaningfully between an edge/internet-facing router and an internal core router within the same organization?

options.A: An edge router facing the internet is generally exposed to a much higher risk of receiving malicious or abusive traffic directly from untrusted external sources, so its CoPP policy might reasonably be tuned more conservatively/restrictively than an internal core router, which primarily sees traffic from already relatively trusted internal devices and routing peers
options.B: CoPP configuration must always be byte-for-byte identical across every single router in an organization regardless of that router's actual role, exposure, or position in the network topology
options.C: CoPP is only relevant for internal core routers and provides no meaningful protective benefit for an internet-facing edge router that's actually exposed to untrusted external traffic
options.D: CoPP tuning should generally be more permissive on an internet-facing edge router than on an internal core router, since the edge router's higher volume of legitimate customer eBGP sessions means an overly conservative policer is more likely to drop wanted routing traffic than genuinely malicious traffic

questions.explanation_es: Un router de borde que enfrenta internet generalmente está expuesto a un riesgo mucho mayor de recibir tráfico malicioso o abusivo directamente de fuentes externas no confiables, así que su política de CoPP razonablemente podría ajustarse de forma más conservadora/restrictiva que la de un router de core interno, que principalmente ve tráfico de dispositivos internos y peers de enrutamiento ya relativamente confiables.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: What does 'mutual TLS' (mTLS) provide in an API security context, beyond what standard one-way TLS already offers?

options.A: In standard one-way TLS, the client verifies the server's certificate but the server typically doesn't verify a client certificate; mTLS adds client-side certificate verification as well, so both parties cryptographically authenticate each other, providing stronger assurance of the client's identity than relying solely on an application-layer credential like a password or token
options.B: mTLS eliminates the need for any meaningful case, relying purely on certificate exchange with no actual data confidentiality provided at all
options.C: Mutual TLS and standard one-way TLS provide exactly identical security guarantees, with no meaningful distinction in whether the server also verifies a certificate presented by the client, a claim that overlooks how mTLS specifically adds a client certificate exchange and verification step during the TLS handshake itself, a step standard one-way TLS never performs since it only validates the server's certificate presented to the client
options.D: Mutual TLS can only be used for browser-based web traffic and has little applicability to programmatic API-to-API authentication

questions.explanation_es: En TLS unidireccional estándar, el cliente verifica el certificado del servidor pero el servidor típicamente no verifica un certificado de cliente; mTLS agrega también la verificación del lado del cliente, de forma que ambas partes se autentiquen criptográficamente entre sí, dando una garantía más fuerte de la identidad del cliente que depender únicamente de una credencial de capa de aplicación como una contraseña o token.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why might an API expose separate 'read' and 'write' scopes for the same underlying resource, rather than a single combined 'access' scope covering both?

options.A: Read and write scopes always grant exactly identical permissions with no meaningful distinction between the ability to retrieve versus modify a given resource
options.B: Separating read and write scopes allows a token to be issued with only read access for a client/integration that only needs to retrieve data (like a reporting dashboard), without also granting that same client the ability to modify data, following the principle of least privilege more precisely than a single combined scope that would grant both capabilities together regardless of actual need
options.C: OAuth 2.0 scopes are defined by the authorization server as a fixed, standardized set such as 'read' and 'write' that every API implementing OAuth 2.0 must expose identically, so an individual API is not able to define its own custom, resource-specific scope names beyond that standard set
options.D: Granting only a read scope to a token typically also grants that same token full write access, making the distinction between the two scope types meaningless in practice

questions.explanation_es: Separar los scopes de lectura y escritura permite emitir un token con solo acceso de lectura para un cliente/integración que solo necesita obtener datos (como un dashboard de reportes), sin también otorgarle a ese mismo cliente la capacidad de modificar datos, siguiendo el principio de mínimo privilegio de forma más precisa que un único scope combinado que otorgaría ambas capacidades juntas sin importar la necesidad real.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: What is the purpose of an API 'webhook' signature/secret, verified by the receiving application when it accepts an incoming webhook notification?

options.A: A webhook signature is only relevant for outbound API calls initiated by the receiving application, and has little relevance to an unsolicited inbound notification sent by another platform
options.B: Webhook signatures have no security relevance and exist purely to specify which programming language the receiving application's endpoint was written in
options.C: Since a webhook is typically an unsolicited inbound HTTP POST from the sending platform to the receiving application's own endpoint, a shared signing secret (used to compute a signature over the payload) lets the receiving application verify that the notification genuinely came from the legitimate sending platform and wasn't forged or tampered with by an unauthorized third party
options.D: Once a webhook signature is verified successfully, the receiving application caches the sending platform's source IP address and trusts subsequent notifications arriving from that same IP without needing to recompute the signature on each later request

questions.explanation_es: Como un webhook típicamente es un POST HTTP entrante no solicitado desde la plataforma emisora hacia el propio endpoint de la aplicación receptora, un secreto de firma compartido (usado para calcular una firma sobre el payload) le permite a la aplicación receptora verificar que la notificación realmente vino de la plataforma emisora legítima y no fue falsificada o manipulada por un tercero no autorizado.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why might an API design intentionally avoid including overly detailed internal error information (like a full stack trace or internal file path) in an error response returned to an external client?

options.A: Detailed internal error information can inadvertently reveal implementation details about the server's internal architecture, software versions, or file structure that could help an attacker plan a more targeted attack, so error responses returned to external/untrusted clients are often deliberately kept more generic, with detailed diagnostic information instead logged internally where only authorized personnel can access it
options.B: Detailed error information should always be included in every client-facing response regardless of the client's trust level, since withholding any diagnostic detail always harms legitimate API consumers with no offsetting security benefit, a position that overlooks how a legitimate client only needs a clear error code and human-readable message to resolve its issue, while a full stack trace offers little practical benefit beyond what an attacker could also exploit
options.C: APIs are not designed to ever including any error information beyond a generic HTTP status code, making the question of how much internal detail to include entirely moot
options.D: Including detailed internal error information in a client-facing response has little security implications, and API design has no legitimate reason to ever limit how much internal detail is exposed in an error response

questions.explanation_es: La información de error interna detallada puede revelar inadvertidamente detalles de implementación sobre la arquitectura interna del servidor, versiones de software, o estructura de archivos que podrían ayudar a un atacante a planear un ataque más dirigido, así que las respuestas de error devueltas a clientes externos/no confiables a menudo se mantienen deliberadamente más genéricas, con información de diagnóstico detallada registrada internamente donde solo personal autorizado puede acceder.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: Why is 'CORS' (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) configuration relevant to the security of an API that's intended to be called from JavaScript running in a web browser on a different origin/domain?

options.A: Browsers enforce a same-origin policy by default, blocking JavaScript on one origin from freely making requests to an API on a different origin unless that API explicitly opts in via CORS headers indicating which origins are permitted; correctly scoping CORS to only trusted origins (rather than allowing any origin with a wildcard) helps prevent an unrelated, potentially malicious website from making unauthorized browser-based requests to the API using a victim's own credentials/session
options.B: CORS configuration is only relevant for APIs called from a mobile application, and has little relevance to any API called from JavaScript running in a web browser
options.C: CORS has little security relevance and exists purely to control the visual styling applied to an API's JSON response when displayed in a browser's developer tools
options.D: Once CORS is configured to allow one specific trusted origin, that same configuration automatically and permanently allows every other origin on the internet to make requests to that API as well, with no way to restrict access to only that one trusted origin

questions.explanation_es: Los navegadores aplican una política de mismo origen por defecto, bloqueando que JavaScript de un origen haga solicitudes libremente hacia una API en un origen distinto a menos que esa API acepte explícitamente vía encabezados CORS indicando qué orígenes están permitidos; delimitar correctamente CORS solo a orígenes confiables (en lugar de permitir cualquier origen con un comodín) ayuda a prevenir que un sitio web no relacionado y potencialmente malicioso haga solicitudes no autorizadas basadas en navegador hacia la API usando las propias credenciales/sesión de una víctima.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What is the purpose of 'vulnerability scanning' as a proactive security practice, as distinct from an IDS/IPS's ongoing traffic monitoring?

options.A: Vulnerability scanners are not designed to identifying any missing patch or outdated software version, and can only ever detect a live, in-progress network attack identical to what an IDS/IPS detects
options.B: A vulnerability scanner proactively probes systems/devices for known weaknesses (missing patches, misconfigurations, outdated software versions) on a periodic basis, identifying issues before they're exploited, whereas an IDS/IPS monitors live network traffic for signs of an attack actually being attempted or in progress
options.C: Vulnerability scanning can only ever be performed once, at the moment a device is first deployed, and provides no ongoing, periodic value for already-deployed production systems
options.D: Vulnerability scanning and IDS/IPS monitoring are exactly the same activity performed by exactly the same tool, with no meaningful distinction between proactively identifying weaknesses versus monitoring live traffic for an active attack

questions.explanation_es: Un escáner de vulnerabilidades sondea proactivamente sistemas/dispositivos en busca de debilidades conocidas (parches faltantes, malas configuraciones, versiones de software desactualizadas) de forma periódica, identificando problemas antes de que se exploten, mientras que un IDS/IPS monitorea el tráfico de red en vivo en busca de señales de un ataque realmente siendo intentado o en curso.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: Why is 'least privilege' considered a foundational security principle applicable broadly across user accounts, service accounts, and network access policy alike?

options.A: Applying least privilege generally prevents any legitimate user or service from ever accomplishing their actual intended task, making the principle fundamentally incompatible with normal business operations
options.B: Least privilege mainly reduces the administrative overhead of managing accounts by keeping permission sets small and easy to audit, and its effect on limiting the impact of a compromised account is a secondary, largely incidental benefit rather than the principle's primary purpose
options.C: Least privilege is relevant only to human user accounts and has little applicability to automated service accounts or network-level access policy
options.D: Granting only the minimum access/permissions actually needed for a given role or function (rather than broad access by default) limits the potential damage or exposure if that account or access point is ever compromised, since an attacker who gains control of an over-privileged entity gains access to everything it was granted rather than just what was genuinely necessary

questions.explanation_es: Otorgar solo el mínimo acceso/permisos realmente necesarios para un rol o función dado (en lugar de acceso amplio por defecto) limita el daño o exposición potencial si esa cuenta o punto de acceso alguna vez se ve comprometido, ya que un atacante que obtiene control de una entidad sobre-privilegiada gana acceso a todo lo que se le otorgó en lugar de solo lo que era genuinamente necesario.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What does 'threat intelligence' feed integration typically add to an organization's existing security tools (like a firewall or IPS)?

options.A: Threat intelligence feeds can only ever be used by an IDS, and are technically incompatible with being consumed by any other type of security tool like a firewall or SIEM
options.B: A threat intelligence feed provides continuously updated information about known malicious indicators (IP addresses, domains, file hashes) gathered from external research/monitoring, which security tools can consume to improve their detection accuracy against currently active, real-world threats, rather than relying solely on static, infrequently-updated internal signature databases
options.C: Once a threat intelligence feed is integrated, it generally replaces every other detection mechanism a security tool previously used, rather than supplementing and improving those existing mechanisms
options.D: Threat intelligence feeds mainly provide vulnerability disclosure bulletins and CVE advisories for patch prioritization, rather than the specific malicious IP addresses, domains, or file hashes a firewall or IPS would consume directly to improve real-time detection

questions.explanation_es: Un feed de inteligencia de amenazas provee información continuamente actualizada sobre indicadores maliciosos conocidos (direcciones IP, dominios, hashes de archivo) recolectada de investigación/monitoreo externo, la cual las herramientas de seguridad pueden consumir para mejorar su precisión de detección contra amenazas reales actualmente activas, en lugar de depender únicamente de bases de datos de firmas internas estáticas y actualizadas con poca frecuencia.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: Why might an organization conduct periodic 'tabletop exercises' (simulated, discussion-based walkthroughs of a hypothetical security incident) as part of its threat defense readiness program?

options.A: Once an organization has conducted a single tabletop exercise one time, further exercises provide no additional value regardless of how much time has passed or how much the organization's infrastructure or team has changed since that first exercise
options.B: Tabletop exercises let the organization's incident response team practice and validate their documented response plan against a realistic scenario in a low-risk, discussion-based setting, surfacing gaps, unclear responsibilities, or communication breakdowns in the plan before those same issues could cause confusion or delay during an actual, real security incident
options.C: Tabletop exercises mainly serve as a compliance checkbox required for certain security audits, so any gaps or unclear responsibilities they surface in the incident response plan are treated as secondary to simply satisfying that documentation requirement
options.D: A tabletop exercise always and necessarily requires actually and deliberately compromising a production system to be meaningful, rather than being a purely discussion-based, non-disruptive simulation

questions.explanation_es: Los ejercicios de mesa (tabletop) le permiten al equipo de respuesta a incidentes de la organización practicar y validar su plan de respuesta documentado contra un escenario realista en un entorno de bajo riesgo y basado en discusión, revelando brechas, responsabilidades poco claras, o fallas de comunicación en el plan antes de que esos mismos problemas pudieran causar confusión o retraso durante un incidente de seguridad real.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What is the general purpose of 'security awareness training' for general (non-technical) employees, as a threat defense element complementary to technical controls?

options.A: Many successful attacks (such as phishing) target human behavior rather than a purely technical vulnerability; training employees to recognize and appropriately respond to common social-engineering tactics addresses a threat vector that purely technical controls like a firewall or IPS cannot fully address on their own, since a user can be tricked into taking an action that bypasses those technical protections entirely
options.B: Technical controls like firewalls and IPS devices are always fully sufficient on their own to prevent every possible attack, making any investment in security awareness training for employees unnecessary and redundant
options.C: Security awareness training has little meaningful relationship to an organization's overall threat defense posture, since every successful attack is assumed to always exploit a purely technical vulnerability with minimal involvement of human behavior or decision-making
options.D: Security awareness training is only relevant for IT/security staff themselves, and has little relevance to general, non-technical employees across the rest of the organization

questions.explanation_es: Muchos ataques exitosos (como el phishing) apuntan al comportamiento humano en lugar de a una vulnerabilidad puramente técnica; entrenar a los empleados para reconocer y responder apropiadamente a tácticas comunes de ingeniería social aborda un vector de amenaza que los controles puramente técnicos como un firewall o IPS no pueden abordar completamente por sí solos, ya que a un usuario se lo puede engañar para que tome una acción que evada por completo esas protecciones técnicas.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What show command on a Cisco switch is commonly used to check the current 802.1X authentication status/session details of a specific interface?

options.A: 'show authentication sessions interface <int>' (or 'show dot1x interface <int>'), which displays the current authentication method, status, and assigned attributes (like VLAN or dACL) for sessions on that port
options.B: 'show interface <int> switchport' shows the port's current access or trunk VLAN assignment and administrative mode, but it does not report which 802.1X authentication method or session status is currently active on that port
options.C: 'show ip route' displays 802.1X session status directly alongside routing table entries, with no separate authentication-specific command needed
options.D: 802.1X authentication session status can never be verified through any Cisco IOS command output, and can only be inferred by checking the ISE server's own logs, a claim that overlooks the dedicated local show commands built specifically for this purpose

questions.explanation_es: 'show authentication sessions interface <int>' (o 'show dot1x interface <int>') muestra el método de autenticación actual, el estado, y los atributos asignados (como VLAN o dACL) para las sesiones de ese puerto.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: Why might an organization configure a specific 'critical VLAN' or 'critical authentication' fallback for 802.1X ports, to be used if the RADIUS/AAA server becomes unreachable?

options.A: Critical VLAN/authentication fallback mainly determines which VLAN a port reverts to during a link-flap event or interface reset, rather than specifically addressing what happens to 802.1X authentication when the RADIUS/AAA server itself becomes unreachable
options.B: Configuring a critical VLAN always and disables 802.1X authentication permanently on that port, even after RADIUS/AAA server connectivity is restored
options.C: Without a defined fallback, an outage of the RADIUS/AAA server could leave every 802.1X-enabled port unable to authenticate any device at all, effectively causing a widespread network access outage; a critical-VLAN fallback lets devices still gain some defined level of access (even if reduced/restricted) during that server outage, rather than being completely denied connectivity
options.D: This feature can only be configured on wireless access points, and has little applicability to wired 802.1X-enabled switch ports

questions.explanation_es: Sin un fallback definido, una interrupción del servidor RADIUS/AAA podría dejar a cada puerto habilitado con 802.1X incapaz de autenticar a ningún dispositivo, causando efectivamente una interrupción de acceso a la red generalizada; un fallback de critical VLAN le permite a los dispositivos igual obtener cierto nivel de acceso definido (aunque reducido/restringido) durante esa interrupción del servidor, en lugar de que se les niegue completamente la conectividad.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What is the general purpose of 'endpoint compliance' status reported by ISE, as it relates to ongoing posture reassessment rather than just a one-time check at initial connection?

options.A: Once an endpoint is found compliant a single time, ISE automatically and disables all future posture reassessment for that specific device for the remainder of its operational lifetime
options.B: Endpoint compliance status primarily reflects whether the endpoint successfully completed 802.1X authentication at the moment it first connected, rather than tracking whether posture elements like antivirus definitions or patch level remain current afterward
options.C: Posture compliance is only ever checked exactly once, at the moment of initial connection, with ISE having no capability to reassess an endpoint's compliance status at any later point during that same ongoing session, a claim that overlooks ISE's periodic reassessment (PRA) feature, designed to re-check an already-connected endpoint's posture at configurable intervals so drift like an outdated antivirus can still be caught mid-session
options.D: ISE can be configured to periodically re-check an endpoint's posture compliance status even after its initial connection, so that a device that was compliant when it first connected but later drifts out of compliance (such as its antivirus becoming outdated) can be detected and potentially have its access adjusted, rather than compliance being assumed permanently valid based only on the very first check

questions.explanation_es: ISE se puede configurar para volver a verificar periódicamente el estado de cumplimiento de postura de un endpoint incluso después de su conexión inicial, de forma que un dispositivo que era conforme cuando se conectó por primera vez pero luego se desvía del cumplimiento (como que su antivirus se vuelva desactualizado) pueda detectarse y potencialmente ajustar su acceso, en lugar de asumir el cumplimiento como permanentemente válido basándose solo en la primera verificación.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: Why might an organization integrate its NAC platform (like ISE) with a Mobile Device Management (MDM) system for BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) endpoints?

options.A: This integration is only relevant for corporate-owned devices, and has little relevance to genuinely personally-owned BYOD devices, the actual scenario it's typically used to address
options.B: Integrating ISE with an MDM platform always and disables NAC's ability to make any access decision at all, deferring every single access decision to the MDM platform with minimal involvement from ISE itself, a claim that overlooks how ISE's policy engine is built to combine MDM posture attributes with its own authorization rules, not hand the decision entirely to the MDM platform
options.C: MDM integration lets ISE incorporate device-management/compliance status (such as whether a personal device is enrolled in MDM, has a passcode set, or is jailbroken/rooted) into its access policy decisions for BYOD devices, extending NAC's context-aware policy beyond what network-level information alone could determine about a personally-owned device
options.D: MDM integration mainly allows ISE to push its own separate posture-assessment agent onto the personal device through the MDM platform, rather than pulling the MDM's own existing compliance attributes into ISE's authorization policy directly

questions.explanation_es: La integración con MDM le permite a ISE incorporar el estado de gestión/cumplimiento del dispositivo (como si un dispositivo personal está inscrito en MDM, tiene un código de acceso configurado, o está jailbreak/rooteado) en sus decisiones de política de acceso para dispositivos BYOD, extendiendo la política de NAC consciente del contexto más allá de lo que la información a nivel de red por sí sola podría determinar sobre un dispositivo de propiedad personal.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What operational risk does deploying 802.1X on switch ports connecting to non-computer infrastructure devices (like a networked printer, badge reader, or IP camera) without proper accommodation (like MAB) typically create?

options.A: Such devices typically cannot run an 802.1X supplicant at all, so without MAB (or another accommodation) configured as a fallback, they would fail 802.1X authentication entirely and be denied network access, potentially disrupting a legitimate business function like physical security (badge readers) or printing services that depend on that device having connectivity
options.B: Deploying 802.1X on ports connecting to this type of device has little operational risk, since every such device is assumed to always authenticate successfully via 802.1X with minimal possibility of any connectivity disruption
options.C: This risk only applies to wireless-connected devices of this type, and has little relevance to a wired printer, badge reader, or camera connected via a standard switch port
options.D: Non-computer infrastructure devices always natively support full 802.1X supplicant functionality identical to a modern laptop, making any special accommodation like MAB unnecessary for this category of device

questions.explanation_es: Ese tipo de dispositivo típicamente no puede correr ningún supplicant de 802.1X en absoluto, así que sin MAB (u otra adaptación) configurado como respaldo, fallaría la autenticación 802.1X por completo y se le negaría el acceso a la red, potencialmente interrumpiendo una función de negocio legítima como seguridad física (lectores de tarjeta) o servicios de impresión que dependen de que ese dispositivo tenga conectividad.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What is the general purpose of an 'intrusion event' generated by an FTD device's IPS engine, and where can an administrator review these events?

options.A: An intrusion event is generated when traffic matches a signature/rule in the applied intrusion policy, and these events (with details like the triggering rule, source/destination, and severity) can be reviewed centrally in FMC's event viewer, helping an analyst investigate and respond to detected threats
options.B: Intrusion events can only ever be viewed directly on the FTD device's own local console, and are not designed to being centrally aggregated or reviewed through FMC
options.C: An intrusion event is generated only when traffic is permitted with no inspection, and is never generated in response to any actual signature match
options.D: Intrusion events are generated primarily by the FTD's file and malware inspection engine when a file transfer is blocked, rather than by the IPS engine's own rule and signature matching against traffic patterns

questions.explanation_es: Un evento de intrusión se genera cuando el tráfico coincide con una firma/regla de la política de intrusión aplicada, y estos eventos (con detalles como la regla que lo disparó, origen/destino, y severidad) se pueden revisar centralmente en el visor de eventos de FMC, ayudando a un analista a investigar y responder a amenazas detectadas.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: Why might an organization tune (rather than accept the default configuration of) an intrusion policy's rule set for their specific environment?

options.A: There is no meaningful reason an organization's specific environment or technology stack would ever warrant any tuning of a default intrusion policy rule set, since every organization is assumed to always have exactly identical traffic patterns and application usage, overlooking that FTD's inspected traffic mix, exposed applications, and OS/patch baseline genuinely differ across organizations, which is exactly why Cisco Talos periodically updates recommended rule sets per deployment profile
options.B: Tuning an intrusion policy always and disables every single rule in the entire rule set, leaving the policy with zero active detection capability regardless of the specific tuning performed
options.C: A default, broadly applicable rule set may include signatures for vulnerabilities/attacks not relevant to that organization's specific technology stack (generating unnecessary alert noise), while potentially not being specifically tuned for the applications and traffic patterns that are actually present, so tuning (disabling irrelevant rules, adjusting thresholds) helps focus detection on genuinely relevant threats and reduces false-positive alert volume
options.D: Intrusion policy rule sets can never be tuned or customized in any way from their default, out-of-the-box configuration on any Cisco Firepower/FTD platform

questions.explanation_es: Un conjunto de reglas por defecto y ampliamente aplicable puede incluir firmas para vulnerabilidades/ataques no relevantes a la pila tecnológica específica de esa organización (generando ruido de alertas innecesario), mientras potencialmente no está específicamente ajustado a las aplicaciones y patrones de tráfico que realmente están presentes, así que el ajuste (deshabilitando reglas irrelevantes, ajustando umbrales) ayuda a enfocar la detección en amenazas genuinamente relevantes y reduce el volumen de alertas de falsos positivos.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: What is the purpose of an FTD 'network discovery' policy, in terms of what it helps FMC learn about the hosts on a monitored network?

options.A: Network discovery builds its host profile primarily by actively querying each discovered host's SNMP agent for system information, rather than passively observing the traffic that host naturally generates on the network
options.B: Enabling network discovery always and disables the FTD's ability to perform any actual intrusion detection or access control function, replacing those capabilities entirely
options.C: Network discovery passively observes traffic to build a profile of hosts on the network (such as operating system, applications in use, and services running), which can then inform other capabilities like intrusion rule relevance assessment (prioritizing alerts relevant to the actual OS/applications present) and general network visibility/inventory
options.D: A network discovery policy can only ever be applied to a single specific host at a time, making it not designed to building any broader profile across an entire monitored network segment

questions.explanation_es: El descubrimiento de red observa pasivamente el tráfico para construir un perfil de los hosts de la red (como sistema operativo, aplicaciones en uso, y servicios corriendo), lo cual luego puede informar otras capacidades como la evaluación de relevancia de reglas de intrusión (priorizando alertas relevantes al SO/aplicaciones realmente presentes) y visibilidad/inventario de red general.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: Why might FMC's dashboard prominently surface 'top attackers' and 'top targets' summary views, rather than only presenting a flat, chronological list of every individual security event?

options.A: These summary views provide no practical analytical value beyond what a flat chronological event list alone already provides, since an analyst is assumed to always be able to just as easily identify significant patterns by manually scrolling through every individual event one at a time, an assumption that overlooks how quickly manual review becomes impractical once event volume exceeds what a human can scan
options.B: Top attackers/targets views are only relevant for wireless network traffic, and provide no meaningful analytical value for wired network traffic passing through an FTD device
options.C: FMC's dashboard summary views like top attackers and top targets are generated only once per day during a scheduled reporting job, so an analyst investigating an event as it happens must still work from the flat, real-time chronological event list instead
options.D: Aggregated summary views (like top attackers/targets) help an analyst quickly identify which sources or destinations are involved in the most significant volume of security-relevant activity, surfacing patterns that might not be immediately obvious when scrolling through potentially thousands of individual, chronologically-ordered event log entries one at a time

questions.explanation_es: Las vistas resumen agregadas (como top attackers/targets) ayudan a un analista a identificar rápidamente qué orígenes o destinos están involucrados en el mayor volumen de actividad relevante para la seguridad, revelando patrones que podrían no ser inmediatamente obvios al desplazarse por potencialmente miles de entradas de log de eventos individuales ordenadas cronológicamente una por una.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: Why might an organization apply different access control and intrusion policies to different security zones (such as a DMZ zone versus an internal trusted zone) on the same FTD device, rather than a single uniform policy across all zones?

options.A: Different zones typically carry traffic with different risk profiles and legitimate use cases (a DMZ hosting internet-facing services generally warrants stricter, more aggressive inspection than purely internal traffic between already-trusted internal hosts), so tailoring policy per zone allows security posture to be matched to each zone's actual risk level rather than applying a single one-size-fits-all policy that might be too permissive for a high-risk zone or unnecessarily restrictive for a lower-risk one
options.B: FTD access control policy can differ by security zone for basic permit or deny decisions, but a single intrusion policy must always be applied identically across every zone regardless of that zone's actual risk profile
options.C: Applying different policies per zone provides no meaningful security benefit, since every zone on a device is assumed to always carry traffic with exactly identical risk characteristics and legitimate use cases
options.D: Zone-based policy differentiation is only relevant for wireless traffic, and has little relevance to wired traffic zones like a DMZ or internal trusted network segment

questions.explanation_es: Distintas zonas típicamente transportan tráfico con distintos perfiles de riesgo y casos de uso legítimos (una DMZ hospedando servicios expuestos a internet generalmente amerita inspección más estricta y agresiva que el tráfico puramente interno entre hosts internos ya confiables), así que ajustar la política por zona permite que la postura de seguridad coincida con el nivel de riesgo real de cada zona en lugar de aplicar una única política uniforme que podría ser demasiado permisiva para una zona de alto riesgo o innecesariamente restrictiva para una de menor riesgo.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: What command is commonly used on a Cisco switch to verify whether MACsec is actually established and encrypting traffic on a given interface?

options.A: 'show ip route' displays MACsec session status directly alongside routing table entries, with no separate MACsec-specific command needed
options.B: 'show macsec summary' (or 'show macsec interface <int>'), which displays the MACsec status, cipher suite, and key/session information for that interface, confirming whether encryption is actually active rather than simply configured
options.C: MACsec status can never be verified through any Cisco IOS command output, and can only be inferred by physically inspecting the cable with a specialized optical tool, a claim that overlooks the dedicated show commands built specifically to display MACsec session and cipher status
options.D: 'show authentication sessions interface <int>' displays whether 802.1X authentication succeeded on that port, but it does not separately confirm whether the resulting MACsec encryption session itself is actually up and passing encrypted traffic

questions.explanation_es: 'show macsec summary' (o 'show macsec interface <int>') muestra el estado de MACsec, el conjunto de cifrado, y la información de clave/sesión de esa interfaz, confirmando si el cifrado realmente está activo en lugar de solo configurado.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Why might TrustSec's SGT enforcement be described as scaling better than maintaining equivalent IP-based ACLs as the number of endpoint groups grows in a large enterprise?

options.A: An SGACL policy is expressed in terms of a relatively small, stable number of groups (SGTs) rather than a potentially huge and constantly-changing number of individual IP addresses/subnets, so the policy matrix size grows with the number of groups rather than with the number of individual endpoints, keeping policy complexity more manageable as the endpoint population grows
options.B: Policy scalability mainly depends on how frequently endpoint IP addresses change through DHCP renewal, so an SGT-based policy still requires roughly the same ongoing maintenance as an IP-based ACL whenever the underlying IP addressing churns, regardless of how the policy itself is expressed
options.C: SGT-based policy and IP-based ACL policy scale in exactly identical ways as the number of endpoints grows, with no meaningful difference in policy complexity or maintenance burden between the two approaches at any scale
options.D: TrustSec's SGACL policy actually requires defining a completely separate, unique rule for every single individual endpoint IP address, making it inherently less scalable than a traditional IP-based ACL approach as endpoint count grows, a mix-up that overlooks how an SGACL rule is written once per SGT pair rather than once per individual host, keeping the matrix size tied to group count

questions.explanation_es: Una política SGACL se expresa en términos de una cantidad relativamente pequeña y estable de grupos (SGTs) en lugar de una cantidad potencialmente enorme y en constante cambio de direcciones IP/subredes individuales, así que el tamaño de la matriz de política crece con la cantidad de grupos en lugar de con la cantidad de endpoints individuales, manteniendo la complejidad de política más manejable a medida que crece la población de endpoints.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: What role does 802.1AE (the underlying IEEE standard for MACsec) play relative to 802.1X, in terms of the overall standards these technologies build on?

options.A: 802.1X (port-based network access control) and 802.1AE (MACsec, Layer 2 frame encryption) are related but distinct IEEE 802.1 standards that are commonly deployed together — 802.1X governs whether/how a device is authenticated onto the network, while 802.1AE governs whether the resulting traffic on that link is actually encrypted
options.B: 802.1AE and 802.1X are simply two different names for exactly the same single standard, with no meaningful distinction between network access authentication and Layer 2 frame encryption
options.C: 802.1X and 802.1AE were both originally developed as a single combined IEEE standard for port-based access control, with 802.1AE later split off specifically to add key-management extensions rather than to define a separate frame-encryption function
options.D: 802.1AE is a legacy standard that has been fully replaced by 802.1X, with 802.1AE no longer having any meaningful case to current MACsec deployments

questions.explanation_es: 802.1X (control de acceso a la red basado en puerto) y 802.1AE (MACsec, cifrado de frames de Capa 2) son estándares relacionados pero distintos del IEEE 802.1 que comúnmente se despliegan juntos — 802.1X gobierna si/cómo se autentica un dispositivo en la red, mientras que 802.1AE gobierna si el tráfico resultante en ese enlace realmente se cifra.

questions.name: TrustSec/MACsec
questions.question: Why might an organization phase in a TrustSec deployment by first enabling SGT classification and monitoring (without yet enforcing any SGACL policy), similar in spirit to 802.1X's monitor mode?

options.A: There is no meaningful benefit to observing SGT classification and traffic patterns before enabling SGACL enforcement; jumping directly to full enforcement with no prior observation period carries no additional risk in any deployment scenario
options.B: TrustSec technically requires that SGACL enforcement always be enabled simultaneously with SGT classification from the very first moment either feature is configured, with no ability to observe classification results before enforcement takes effect
options.C: Deploying classification/monitoring first lets the organization observe what SGTs are actually being assigned and what traffic patterns exist between groups in the real production environment, informing the design of an accurate, well-tuned SGACL policy before actually turning on enforcement, reducing the risk of an overly restrictive or incorrectly designed policy unexpectedly blocking legitimate business traffic once enforcement is enabled
options.D: This phased monitoring approach is only applicable to 802.1X specifically, and has little relevance to how a TrustSec/SGT-based deployment might similarly be phased in in a comparable way

questions.explanation_es: Desplegar clasificación/monitoreo primero le permite a la organización observar qué SGTs realmente se están asignando y qué patrones de tráfico existen entre grupos en el entorno de producción real, informando el diseño de una política SGACL precisa y bien ajustada antes de realmente activar la aplicación, reduciendo el riesgo de que una política demasiado restrictiva o mal diseñada bloquee inesperadamente tráfico de negocio legítimo una vez habilitada la aplicación.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: During a phased migration from a traditional campus network to SD-Access, why is a 'fusion router' (or fusion device) commonly deployed at the boundary between the SD-Access fabric and the traditional network?

options.A: A fusion router sits at the fabric border and handles route leaking/redistribution between the fabric's VRFs (virtual networks) and the traditional network's global routing table, allowing controlled interoperability and communication between fabric-enabled and non-fabric segments during the migration period
options.B: Fusion routers are only relevant for wireless SD-Access deployments and have no applicability to interoperability with a wired traditional campus network
options.C: A fusion router primarily provides centralized DHCP relay services for endpoints across the SD-Access fabric's various virtual networks, rather than performing route leaking or redistribution between those VRFs and the traditional network's global routing table
options.D: Deploying a fusion router generally eliminates the need for any border node in the SD-Access fabric, replacing that fabric role entirely

questions.explanation_es: Un fusion router se ubica en el borde del fabric y maneja la fuga/redistribución de rutas entre las VRFs (redes virtuales) del fabric y la tabla de ruteo global de la red tradicional, permitiendo interoperabilidad y comunicación controlada entre segmentos habilitados para fabric y no-fabric durante el período de migración.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why might an organization adopt an incremental, site-by-site migration strategy when converting a large traditional campus network to SD-Access, rather than a single simultaneous cutover across the entire enterprise?

options.A: An incremental, site-by-site approach limits the scope of risk and disruption from any single migration step, allows lessons learned at one site to inform and improve the process at subsequent sites, and avoids requiring the simultaneous availability of every resource (staff, hardware, maintenance windows) that a single enterprise-wide cutover would demand all at once
options.B: SD-Access technically requires that every single site in an enterprise be migrated simultaneously in one single cutover event, making any incremental, site-by-site approach not supported to implement
options.C: Incremental migration is only relevant for wireless infrastructure and has little applicability to migrating wired campus switching infrastructure to SD-Access
options.D: An incremental migration strategy provides no practical benefit compared to a single simultaneous enterprise-wide cutover, since both approaches are assumed to carry exactly identical risk and resource requirements, and Cisco's fabric provisioning tools are assumed to parallelize every site's conversion automatically regardless of staffing availability, requiring no additional maintenance windows

questions.explanation_es: Un enfoque incremental, sitio por sitio, limita el alcance del riesgo e interrupción de cualquier paso de migración individual, permite que las lecciones aprendidas en un sitio informen y mejoren el proceso en sitios subsecuentes, y evita requerir la disponibilidad simultánea de cada recurso (personal, hardware, ventanas de mantenimiento) que un corte simultáneo a nivel empresarial demandaría todo de una vez.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What role does an SD-Access 'border node' play specifically in enabling interoperability with networks and services outside the fabric (such as the traditional campus, data center, or internet)?

options.A: A border node can only ever exist in a fabric that has zero connectivity to any traditional or external network, making the concept of 'external interoperability' inapplicable to any fabric that actually contains a border node, since deploying one is treated as evidence the fabric was built with no outside connections at all
options.B: The border node's primary role is to provide additional physical port density for endpoint connections at the fabric edge, with route advertisement to the outside network instead being handled by the fabric's control-plane node
options.C: The border node is the fabric device responsible for advertising fabric-known routes/prefixes to the outside network and importing external routes into the fabric's control plane, acting as the gateway point where fabric-encapsulated traffic is translated to/from traditional, non-fabric traffic
options.D: Border node functionality is only relevant to SD-WAN deployments and has little applicability to an SD-Access campus fabric's interoperability with external networks

questions.explanation_es: El border node es el dispositivo del fabric responsable de anunciar las rutas/prefijos conocidos por el fabric hacia la red externa e importar rutas externas hacia el plano de control del fabric, actuando como el punto de entrada donde el tráfico encapsulado del fabric se traduce hacia/desde el tráfico tradicional no-fabric.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why might an organization choose to run SD-Access and a traditional campus network side by side for an extended coexistence period, rather than treating migration as a brief, momentary event?

options.A: A large campus network typically has many interdependent services, applications, and endpoint types, some of which may not be immediately ready for or compatible with the fabric; an extended coexistence period gives the organization time to validate fabric behavior, migrate applications/services at a manageable pace, and maintain a fallback to the traditional network if unexpected issues arise, rather than forcing every dependency to be resolved instantaneously at a single cutover moment
options.B: Coexistence periods are only relevant for data center network migrations and have no applicability to a campus network migration to SD-Access
options.C: Extended coexistence between SD-Access and a traditional campus network provides no practical benefit compared to an instantaneous, single-moment cutover, since every dependency and application is assumed to always be immediately compatible with the fabric with zero validation needed, and Cisco's fabric onboarding wizard automatically remediates any incompatible application or legacy protocol dependency the moment a switch is converted into fabric mode, without requiring any administrator review of application compatibility beforehand.
options.D: SD-Access requires that fabric-enabled switches be physically segregated onto a completely separate cable plant from the traditional network's switches, so any coexistence period is limited strictly to logically distinct, physically non-overlapping segments of the campus

questions.explanation_es: Una red de campus grande típicamente tiene muchos servicios, aplicaciones, y tipos de endpoint interdependientes, algunos de los cuales podrían no estar inmediatamente listos o ser compatibles con el fabric; un período de coexistencia extendido le da a la organización tiempo para validar el comportamiento del fabric, migrar aplicaciones/servicios a un ritmo manejable, y mantener un respaldo hacia la red tradicional si surgen problemas inesperados, en lugar de forzar que cada dependencia se resuelva instantáneamente en un único momento de corte.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which two protocols make up the IPsec header options used to protect a packet? (Select two)

options.A: ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)
options.B: AES
options.C: DES
options.D: AH (Authentication Header)

questions.explanation_es: AH (Authentication Header) y ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload) son los dos protocolos de cabecera de IPsec. AES y DES son algoritmos de cifrado usados dentro de ESP, no cabeceras de IPsec en sí.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What IP protocol number is assigned to ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)?
questions.explanation_es: ESP usa el número de protocolo IP 50. AH usa el 51, GRE usa el 47, y OSPF usa el 89.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which factors does a router evaluate, in order, when choosing the best route to install in the routing table? (Select three)

options.A: Administrative distance
options.B: Metric
options.C: Router ID
options.D: Prefix length (longest match)

questions.explanation_es: El router primero prefiere la ruta con el prefijo más específico (longest match), luego, entre rutas con el mismo prefijo, la de menor distancia administrativa, y finalmente, entre rutas de la misma distancia administrativa, la de menor métrica. El Router ID solo se usa como desempate en casos muy específicos (p. ej. OSPF), no como criterio general de selección de ruta.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In the output of 'show ip route', which code letter identifies a static route?

options.A: C
options.B: O
options.C: S
options.D: D

questions.explanation_es: 'S' identifica una ruta estática en la tabla de ruteo de Cisco IOS. 'C' es conectada, 'O' es OSPF, y 'D' es EIGRP.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which command correctly configures a static route to network 10.10.10.0/24 via next-hop 20.20.20.2?
questions.explanation_es: La sintaxis correcta en IOS es 'ip route <red> <máscara> <next-hop>', por lo que sería 'ip route 10.10.10.0 255.255.255.0 20.20.20.2'.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: If a router learns the same destination network via both OSPF and RIP, which route does it install by default?

options.A: Both routes, load-balanced equally
options.B: The RIP route, since RIP has a lower administrative distance — because RIP's default administrative distance of 100 is treated as lower than OSPF's 110
options.C: Neither route is installed until manually resolved
options.D: The OSPF route, since OSPF's default administrative distance (110) is lower than RIP's (120)

questions.explanation_es: OSPF tiene distancia administrativa 110 por defecto, menor que la de RIP (120), así que el router prefiere e instala la ruta OSPF.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which of these are commonly cited advantages of static routing over dynamic routing protocols? (Select two)

options.A: It consumes very little CPU and memory on the router
options.B: It requires essentially no extra bandwidth for route advertisements
options.C: It scales better than dynamic protocols on very large networks
options.D: It automatically adapts to any topology change

questions.explanation_es: Las rutas estáticas no generan tráfico de actualización entre routers (bajo consumo de ancho de banda) y no requieren cálculos de un algoritmo de ruteo (bajo consumo de CPU/memoria). No se adaptan automáticamente a cambios de topología, y en redes grandes escalan peor que un protocolo dinámico.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which of these statements about EIGRP are correct? (Select three)

options.A: Its default internal administrative distance is 90
options.B: It uses the DUAL algorithm to calculate loop-free paths
options.C: Its default IPv4 multicast address is 224.0.0.10
options.D: It uses Dijkstra's SPF algorithm to calculate paths

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP usa el algoritmo DUAL (no SPF, que es de OSPF), su dirección multicast IPv4 por defecto es 224.0.0.10, y su distancia administrativa interna por defecto es 90 (170 es la distancia administrativa externa de EIGRP, no la interna).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why is EIGRP sometimes described as having both distance-vector and link-state characteristics?

options.A: Because it only ever exchanges routes with directly connected neighbors, with no additional link-state-like behavior at all
options.B: Because it only calculates hop count, exactly like RIP, with no link-state traits
options.C: Because it floods the full network topology to every router just like OSPF does
options.D: Because it maintains neighbor and topology tables and reacts quickly to changes via DUAL, behaving like a distance-vector protocol with some link-state-like traits

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP se describe a veces como un protocolo 'híbrido avanzado': funciona fundamentalmente como vector-distancia (solo intercambia rutas con vecinos directos), pero mantiene tablas de vecinos y topología y reacciona rápido a cambios mediante DUAL, características que recuerdan a un protocolo de estado de enlace.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In the output of 'show ip route', what does the '>' symbol next to a route typically indicate?

options.A: That the route is currently the best route installed and used for forwarding
options.B: That the route is a summarized route
options.C: That the route is pending validation
options.D: That the route was learned via a default route

questions.explanation_es: El símbolo '>' junto a una ruta en la tabla de ruteo de Cisco indica que esa es la ruta actualmente instalada y utilizada para reenviar tráfico hacia ese destino.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What does it mean when an EIGRP route enters the 'Active' state in the topology table?

options.A: The route is currently being used to forward traffic normally
options.B: The route's successor and all feasible successors have failed, and the router is now actively querying neighbors for a new path
options.C: The route has been manually marked as preferred by the administrator
options.D: The route was just learned and is being validated for the first time — a transient status EIGRP assigns to a newly discovered route while it waits for a hold-down timer to expire

questions.explanation_es: Una ruta EIGRP entra en estado 'Active' cuando su sucesor y todos sus sucesores factibles fallan, y el router debe enviar consultas (queries) a sus vecinos para encontrar una nueva ruta. Mientras está en ese proceso, la ruta se considera activa (en contraste con 'Passive', su estado normal y estable).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which type of EIGRP packet is primarily responsible for carrying routing information used to build the topology and routing tables?

options.A: Hello packets
options.B: Update packets
options.C: Query packets
options.D: Acknowledgment packets

questions.explanation_es: Los paquetes Update llevan la información de ruteo que EIGRP usa para construir las tablas de topología y de ruteo. Los paquetes Hello sirven para descubrir y mantener vecinos, no para transportar rutas.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In a routing table entry like '10.10.20.0/24 [110/15] via 10.10.1.1', what does the second number (15) represent?

options.A: The administrative distance
options.B: The interface index
options.C: The hop count limit
options.D: The metric

questions.explanation_es: En la notación '[AD/metric]' de Cisco IOS, el primer número (110) es la distancia administrativa y el segundo (15) es la métrica de la ruta para ese protocolo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which command enables real-time debugging of EIGRP packets being sent and received on a Cisco router?

options.A: show eigrp packets
options.B: debug ip eigrp neighbors
options.C: clear eigrp packets
options.D: debug eigrp packets

questions.explanation_es: 'debug eigrp packets' habilita el debug en tiempo real de los paquetes EIGRP (Hello, Update, Query, etc.) enviados y recibidos por el router.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which type of OSPF router connects two or more OSPF areas together?

options.A: BDR (Backup Designated Router)
options.B: ABR (Area Border Router)
options.C: ASBR (Autonomous System Boundary Router)
options.D: DR (Designated Router)

questions.explanation_es: El ABR (Area Border Router) es el router que tiene interfaces en más de un área OSPF, conectándolas entre sí.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which interface command sets the OSPF hello interval to 20 seconds?

options.A: ospf hello time 20
options.B: ip ospf interval 20
options.C: ip hello-interval ospf 20
options.D: ip ospf hello-interval 20

questions.explanation_es: El comando de interfaz correcto es 'ip ospf hello-interval 20'. Al cambiarlo, normalmente también hay que ajustar el 'dead-interval' para que siga siendo consistente (por defecto 4x el hello).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: If an interface's OSPF priority is set to 0, what effect does this have on DR/BDR election?

options.A: The router will never be elected DR or BDR on that segment
options.B: The priority value has no effect on DR/BDR election at all
options.C: The router is guaranteed to become the DR on that segment
options.D: The router is guaranteed to become the BDR on that segment

questions.explanation_es: Una prioridad OSPF de 0 hace que el router quede excluido de la elección de DR/BDR en ese segmento: nunca será elegido como DR ni como BDR, aunque sigue participando como vecino normal (DROTHER).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: During which state of OSPF neighbor establishment does DR/BDR election take place?

options.A: Exchange
options.B: Full
options.C: 2-Way
options.D: Exstart

questions.explanation_es: La elección de DR/BDR ocurre en el estado 2-Way, una vez que los routers se reconocen mutuamente como vecinos (bidireccionalidad confirmada), antes de pasar al intercambio de bases de datos (Exstart/Exchange).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is OSPF's default administrative distance on a Cisco router?
questions.explanation_es: OSPF tiene una distancia administrativa por defecto de 110 en dispositivos Cisco.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which of the following are accurate descriptions of OSPF? (Select three)

options.A: It uses Cisco's proprietary DUAL algorithm
options.B: It uses Dijkstra's SPF algorithm to compute the shortest path
options.C: It is a link-state routing protocol
options.D: It supports a hierarchical, multi-area design

questions.explanation_es: OSPF es un protocolo de estado de enlace que usa el algoritmo de Dijkstra (SPF) y soporta un diseño jerárquico de múltiples áreas. DUAL es de EIGRP, no de OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which of these router roles are specific to OSPF terminology? (Select three)

options.A: DR (Designated Router)
options.B: Route Reflector
options.C: BDR (Backup Designated Router)
options.D: ABR (Area Border Router)

questions.explanation_es: ABR, DR y BDR son roles definidos específicamente dentro de OSPF. El Route Reflector es en cambio un concepto de BGP, no de OSPF.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the correct order of BGP peer states from initial connection to a fully established session?

options.A: Idle, Active, Connect, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established
options.B: Connect, Idle, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established
options.C: Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established
options.D: Active, Connect, Idle, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established

questions.explanation_es: El orden correcto de los estados de una sesión BGP es: Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Under 'router bgp 200', which command sets a weight of 150 for neighbor 1.2.1.2?

options.A: match neighbor 1.2.1.2 weight 150
options.B: set neighbor 1.2.1.2 weight 150
options.C: weight neighbor 1.2.1.2 150
options.D: neighbor 1.2.1.2 weight 150

questions.explanation_es: El comando correcto, dentro del modo de configuración 'router bgp 200', es 'neighbor 1.2.1.2 weight 150'.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which of the following are well-known BGP path attributes? (Select three)

options.A: AS-Path
options.B: Weight
options.C: Origin
options.D: Local Preference

questions.explanation_es: Origin, AS-Path y Local Preference son atributos 'well-known' de BGP (well-known mandatory los dos primeros, well-known discretionary Local Preference). Weight ni siquiera es un atributo BGP estándar: es un valor puramente local de Cisco IOS que nunca se anuncia a otros routers.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which BGP peer state indicates that the session has fully converged and the peers are exchanging routing updates?

options.A: OpenConfirm
options.B: Established
options.C: 2-Way
options.D: OpenSent

questions.explanation_es: El estado 'Established' indica que la sesión BGP convergió completamente y los peers ya están intercambiando actualizaciones de ruteo. '2-Way' no es un estado de BGP, sino de OSPF.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: What is the correct order (highest to lowest priority) of the main steps in Cisco's BGP best-path selection process?

options.A: Weight, Local Preference, Locally Originated, AS-Path length, Origin, MED
options.B: MED, Origin, AS-Path length, Local Preference, Weight, Locally Originated
options.C: Local Preference, Weight, AS-Path length, Locally Originated, Origin, MED
options.D: AS-Path length, Weight, Local Preference, Origin, MED, Locally Originated

questions.explanation_es: El orden (de mayor a menor prioridad) del algoritmo de selección de mejor ruta de BGP en Cisco es: Weight (mayor), Local Preference (mayor), rutas originadas localmente, AS-Path (más corto), Origin (menor), y MED (menor).

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which multicast address range is reserved for local-subnet-only traffic (link-local, not forwarded by routers)?
questions.explanation_es: El rango 224.0.0.0 a 224.0.0.255 está reservado para tráfico multicast local al segmento (link-local), como Hellos de protocolos de ruteo; los routers no reenvían ese tráfico fuera del subnet.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which global configuration command enables IGMP snooping on a Cisco switch?

options.A: igmp snooping start
options.B: igmp snooping enable
options.C: ip igmp snooping
options.D: ip snooping igmp

questions.explanation_es: El comando global correcto es 'ip igmp snooping' (en muchos Catalyst viene habilitado por defecto, pero el comando explícito es ese).

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the IPv6 multicast address range, identified by its leading hex bits?

options.A: FEC0 to FEFF
options.B: FFFF to FFFF only
options.C: FE80 to FEBF
options.D: FF00 to FFFF

questions.explanation_es: Las direcciones multicast IPv6 comienzan con el prefijo FF00::/8, es decir, el primer byte va de FF00 a FFFF. FE80 corresponde en cambio al rango de direcciones link-local unicast.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: Which command correctly configures extended ACL 120 to permit only ICMP traffic from network 192.168.1.0/24 to host 2.2.2.2?

options.A: access-list 120 deny icmp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 2.2.2.2
options.B: access-list 120 permit icmp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 2.2.2.2
options.C: access-list 120 permit icmp host 2.2.2.2 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255

questions.explanation_es: La sintaxis correcta es 'access-list 120 permit icmp <origen> <wildcard> host <destino>', es decir: 'access-list 120 permit icmp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 2.2.2.2'.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: Which command correctly configures standard ACL 10 to deny all traffic from network 10.10.10.0/24?

options.B: access-list 10 permit 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255

questions.explanation_es: En una ACL estándar la sintaxis es 'access-list <número> deny <red> <wildcard>', usando wildcard mask (no máscara de subred), por lo que sería 'access-list 10 deny 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255'.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python code correctly prompts the user for input and stores it in variable x?

options.A: x = input("Enter your value: ")
options.B: x == input("Enter your value: ")
options.C: input x = "Enter your value: "
options.D: x = ("Enter your value: ")

questions.explanation_es: La forma correcta es 'x = input("Enter your value: ")', que llama a la función input() y asigna el resultado (lo que el usuario escriba) a la variable x.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which line of Python code correctly prints 'Hello World!' to the console?

options.A: echo("Hello World!")
options.B: print("Hello World!")
options.C: print "Hello World!"
options.D: print(Hello World!)

questions.explanation_es: En Python 3, la forma correcta es 'print("Hello World!")', con el texto entre paréntesis y comillas.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python condition correctly checks whether integer variable X is even?
questions.explanation_es: 'if X % 2 == 0:' usa el operador módulo (%) para verificar si el resto de dividir X por 2 es cero, lo cual indica que X es par. '=' es asignación, no comparación, por lo que 'X % 2 = 0' sería un error de sintaxis.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which Python code correctly assigns the string 'ABC' to variable String1 and then prints it?

options.A: String1 = 'ABC'\nprint(String1)
options.B: print(String1)\nString1 = 'ABC'
options.C: String1 == 'ABC'\nprint(String1)
options.D: String1 = ABC\nprint(String1)

questions.explanation_es: Hay que encerrar el string entre comillas ('ABC', no ABC sin comillas, que Python interpretaría como un nombre de variable), asignarlo con '=', y luego imprimirlo con print(String1).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How many distinct BPDU (Bridge Protocol Data Unit) types does classic 802.1D Spanning Tree define?

options.A: Three: a hello BPDU, a topology-change BPDU, and a root-election BPDU, each with its own distinct format
options.B: Two: the Configuration BPDU used for normal tree-building, and the Topology Change Notification (TCN) BPDU used to signal a topology change
options.C: Four, one for each STP port state transition (blocking, listening, learning, forwarding)
options.D: One single BPDU type that carries both configuration and topology-change information in every message, with no separate TCN message ever defined

questions.explanation_es: 802.1D define dos tipos de BPDU: la Configuration BPDU (usada normalmente para construir y mantener el árbol) y la Topology Change Notification (TCN) BPDU, que un switch envía hacia el root cuando detecta un cambio de topología.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Which attribute is compared first when switches elect the STP root bridge?

options.A: The switch's serial number, since Cisco is sometimes assumed to encode it directly into the bridge ID to guarantee a globally unique tiebreak, when in fact the bridge ID is built from priority plus system MAC address, with serial number playing no role
options.B: The per-port priority configured on each switch's lowest-numbered interface
options.C: The bridge priority value encoded in each switch's bridge ID, with the lowest value winning (the system MAC address is used only as a tiebreaker when priorities are equal)
options.D: The cumulative root path cost each switch has calculated so far, before any bridge ID is even examined

questions.explanation_es: El root bridge se elige comparando primero la prioridad de puente (bridge priority) de cada switch; el valor más bajo gana. Si hay empate en prioridad, se usa la dirección MAC del sistema como desempate (la MAC más baja gana).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Under the original 802.1D short-mode STP cost table, what interface cost is assigned to a 1 Gbps link?

options.A: 1, since short mode uses a linear cost scale of 1 unit per Gbps of link speed
options.C: 100, matching the cost historically assigned to 10 Mbps Ethernet
options.D: 19, the same value used for 100 Mbps links, since short mode does not distinguish speeds above Fast Ethernet

questions.explanation_es: En la tabla de costos original de 802.1D (modo corto, 16 bits), un enlace de 1 Gbps tiene un costo de 4 (10 Mbps=100, 100 Mbps=19, 1 Gbps=4, 10 Gbps=2).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What STP port role do every one of the root bridge's own active ports hold?

options.A: Alternate port, because the root bridge does not forward traffic on any interface by design
options.B: Designated port
options.C: Root port, since the root bridge is the reference point that every root path cost is measured against
options.D: Backup port, reserved in case another switch takes over the root role

questions.explanation_es: El root bridge nunca tiene un puerto raíz (root port) propio, porque el concepto de puerto raíz es 'el puerto más cercano al root bridge' y el root bridge ya es el root. Por eso, todos sus puertos activos son puertos designados (designated ports).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Using 802.1D default timers, how long does a port normally remain in the listening state before moving to learning?

options.A: 50 seconds, the sum of the default max-age (20s) and forward delay (15s) timers combined, a total some engineers mistakenly cite for the listening state alone instead of the full non-forwarding window across listening and learning
options.B: 20 seconds, matching the default max-age timer
options.C: 15 seconds, matching the default forward delay timer
options.D: 2 seconds, matching the default hello timer

questions.explanation_es: Con los temporizadores por defecto, tanto el estado listening como el learning duran 15 segundos cada uno (el valor del forward delay), por lo que un puerto tarda un total de 30 segundos en pasar de blocking a forwarding tras perder su BPDU superior.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What actually happens on downstream switches when they receive a configuration BPDU with the Topology Change (TC) flag set?

options.A: They ignore the flag entirely unless BPDU Guard is also enabled on the receiving port
options.B: They temporarily shorten their MAC address table aging timer to the forward delay value, so stale entries age out and are flushed much faster than the normal aging period
options.C: They permanently disable MAC address learning on all trunk ports until an administrator manually re-enables it
options.D: They immediately reboot the STP process on every VLAN, forcing a full re-election of the root bridge network-wide, rather than the far lighter-weight response of shortening the MAC aging timer that RSTP and 802.1D actually perform on a topology change

questions.explanation_es: Al recibir una BPDU con el flag de Topology Change, los switches reducen temporalmente el tiempo de aging de la tabla MAC al valor del forward delay (normalmente 15 segundos), en vez del aging normal (300 segundos), logrando que las entradas viejas se depuren mucho más rápido tras un cambio de topología.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: RSTP (802.1w) consolidates the classic 802.1D port states into fewer active states. Which pair of 802.1D states no longer exist as distinct named RSTP states? (Choose two.)

options.A: Listening
options.B: Blocking
options.C: Forwarding
options.D: Learning

questions.explanation_es: RSTP fusiona blocking y listening (además del estado disabled) en un único rol llamado 'discarding', dejando efectivamente tres estados operativos: discarding, learning y forwarding, en lugar de los cinco de 802.1D.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Does a large Layer 2 topology running RSTP need to fully converge network-wide before any port can start forwarding traffic?

options.A: Yes, RSTP still requires the entire topology to reach a stable state before any single port transitions to forwarding, identical to 802.1D in this respect, since RSTP is often mistakenly treated as just a faster-timer version of 802.1D rather than a protocol with its own rapid-transition handshake
options.B: Only the root bridge's ports can forward before convergence; all non-root switches must always wait
options.C: Only edge ports can skip convergence, and only if BPDU Guard is also disabled on them
options.D: No — RSTP's proposal/agreement handshake on point-to-point links (and edge ports connected to end hosts) allows individual ports to transition to forwarding rapidly, without waiting for the whole topology to converge

questions.explanation_es: Una de las mejoras clave de RSTP es el mecanismo de proposal/agreement en enlaces punto a punto, que permite que puertos individuales pasen rápidamente a forwarding sin esperar la convergencia de toda la topología, a diferencia de 802.1D.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: In what increments can a switch's STP bridge priority be configured?

options.A: In increments of 1, since Cisco IOS allows any arbitrary integer between 0 and 65535
options.B: In increments of 4096
options.C: In increments of 100, matching the legacy port-cost scale
options.D: In increments of 256, matching the extended system ID field width

questions.explanation_es: La prioridad de puente STP se configura en incrementos de 4096 (0, 4096, 8192, ... hasta 61440), porque los 12 bits inferiores del campo de 16 bits están reservados para el extended system ID (el número de VLAN).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: When a switch calculates its root path cost from a received configuration BPDU, whose interface cost gets added into that calculation?

options.A: The average of the sending and receiving interfaces' costs
options.B: The cost of the port the BPDU was sent out of on the advertising (upstream) switch
options.C: The cost of the receiving switch's own interface on which the BPDU arrived
options.D: No interface cost is added at all; root path cost is purely a hop count between the local switch and the root bridge

questions.explanation_es: El switch que envía la BPDU anuncia el costo acumulado SIN incluir el costo de su propio puerto de salida. Es el switch receptor quien suma el costo de SU puerto de entrada (por el que recibió la BPDU) al valor recibido, para calcular su propio root path cost.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: When two ports are tied on root path cost during STP port role selection, which STP port priority value wins the tiebreak?

options.A: The lower numeric port priority value
options.B: Port priority is never used as a tiebreaker; ties are always broken using the port's physical slot/module number only
options.C: Whichever port came up first chronologically, regardless of any configured priority
options.D: The higher numeric port priority value, since STP treats port priority the opposite way it treats bridge priority
