questions.explanation_es: Igual que con la prioridad de puente, en STP un valor de prioridad de puerto más bajo es más preferido. Se usa como criterio de desempate cuando dos puertos tienen el mismo costo de camino hacia la raíz.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: In Multiple Spanning Tree (MST), a VLAN is directly mapped to which construct?

options.A: A physical switch, since VLAN-to-switch mapping determines MST behavior directly
options.B: An MST instance (MSTI)
options.C: An MST region, since each region is defined as containing exactly one VLAN
options.D: An MST area, borrowing the OSPF-style hierarchical terminology

questions.explanation_es: En MST, las VLANs se asocian directamente a instancias (MSTIs, MST Instances), no a regiones ni a switches. Una región es un grupo de switches con la misma configuración MST; dentro de esa región, muchas VLANs se agrupan en un número reducido de instancias.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is special about MST instance 0, known as the Internal Spanning Tree (IST)?

options.A: It runs on every switch port in the MST region regardless of VLAN membership, and carries the other MST instances' information nested inside its own BPDUs, so only one set of BPDUs needs to be exchanged
options.B: It only exists in networks with fewer than 16 VLANs; larger environments must renumber it out of instance 0
options.C: It only carries BPDUs for VLANs that have not been explicitly mapped to another MST instance, acting as a default catch-all rather than as an instance that runs on every port in the region regardless of VLAN mapping
options.D: It is optional and can be disabled if an administrator only wants to use instances 1-15

questions.explanation_es: La IST (instancia 0) corre en todos los puertos de switch de la región MST, sin importar qué VLANs tengan asociadas, y transporta anidada la información del resto de las MSTIs dentro de sus propias BPDUs, permitiendo que MST anuncie un solo conjunto de BPDUs en vez de uno por instancia.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: For two connected switches to be considered part of the same MST region, what must match between them?

options.A: The configured region name, the configuration revision number, and the VLAN-to-instance mapping table (compared via a digest) — a mismatch in any of these places the switches in different regions
options.B: Only the physical cabling topology; MST region membership is determined by Layer 1 adjacency, not configuration
options.C: The region name and revision number must match, but the VLAN-to-instance mapping table only needs to be compatible rather than identical, since MST is understood to reconcile any differing VLAN assignments automatically once adjacency forms
options.D: Only the priority configured for MST instance 0, since that alone determines the region boundary

questions.explanation_es: La pertenencia a una región MST se determina comparando tres elementos: el nombre de región configurado, el número de revisión, y el mapeo VLAN-a-instancia (comparado mediante un digest/hash). Si alguno de estos difiere entre dos switches conectados, quedan en regiones MST distintas aunque estén físicamente conectados.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What do legacy 802.1D and CST (Common Spanning Tree, as used by 802.1Q) have in common that PVST+ and MST were designed to improve on?

options.A: Both compute only a single spanning tree topology across the entire network, so per-VLAN load balancing across redundant links isn't possible
options.B: Both were deprecated by the IEEE before Cisco ever implemented them in IOS
options.C: Both require dedicated hardware ASICs not found on typical Cisco Catalyst switches, a hardware dependency that has nothing to do with why per-VLAN load balancing is unavailable under a single shared spanning tree topology
options.D: Both mandate that every switch in the topology run in transparent VTP mode

questions.explanation_es: 802.1D clásico y CST calculan una única topología de árbol para toda la red (todas las VLANs comparten el mismo árbol), por lo que no permiten balancear carga por VLAN entre enlaces redundantes. PVST+ (una instancia por VLAN) y MST (varias instancias agrupando VLANs) resuelven esta limitación.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Which of these is NOT a valid VTP switch role/mode?

options.A: Off
options.B: Proxy
options.C: Client
options.D: Transparent

questions.explanation_es: Los roles válidos de VTP son Server, Client, Transparent, y (desde VTPv3) Off. 'Proxy' no es un rol de VTP real.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What information does a VTP summary advertisement actually carry?

options.A: Header-level identification information such as the VTP version, domain name, and configuration revision number — the actual per-VLAN details are carried separately in subset advertisements
options.B: The full list of VLANs that were recently added, deleted, or renamed, encoded directly in the summary advertisement itself
options.C: Only the MD5 password used to authenticate the VTP domain, with no other fields
options.D: A complete copy of the switch's running configuration, compressed for transport over the VTP domain

questions.explanation_es: La summary advertisement de VTP transporta información de encabezado (versión de VTP, nombre de dominio, número de revisión de configuración, etc.), pero no el detalle de las VLANs en sí — eso viaja en las subset advertisements que la siguen cuando hay un cambio real.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Why can physically relocating an old, previously configured switch into an active VTP domain be dangerous?

options.A: If that switch's stored configuration revision number is higher than the domain's current revision, other switches can accept it as more current and overwrite their VLAN databases with its (possibly outdated) VLAN set — potentially deleting VLANs domain-wide
options.B: It has no effect at all as long as the switch is set to VTP client mode before being reconnected
options.C: The relocated switch always defaults to transparent mode automatically upon reboot, which fully isolates it from any risk
options.D: The relocated switch will refuse to send any VTP updates unless manually configured as a VTP server first

questions.explanation_es: Si el switch reubicado conserva un número de revisión de configuración más alto que el del dominio activo (por ejemplo, de una configuración vieja no reseteada), los demás switches lo aceptan como más reciente y sobrescriben su base de datos de VLANs con la de ese switch, pudiendo borrar VLANs en todo el dominio. Por eso se recomienda resetear la revisión a 0 antes de reconectar un switch.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: If both ends of a link are configured with 'switchport mode dynamic auto', what is the resulting port mode?

options.A: A trunk forms, since DTP treats the combination of two auto ports as a valid negotiation match
options.B: The link becomes a Layer 3 routed port automatically, bypassing DTP entirely
options.C: The link flaps continuously between trunk and access as both switches repeatedly try to negotiate
options.D: The link stays in access mode — neither side initiates DTP negotiation, so no trunk forms

questions.explanation_es: 'Dynamic auto' espera pasivamente a que el otro extremo inicie la negociación DTP. Si ambos extremos están en auto, ninguno toma la iniciativa, así que el enlace permanece como puerto de acceso y nunca se forma un trunk.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which port types can be bundled into an EtherChannel?

options.A: Only loopback and tunnel interfaces, since EtherChannel was designed specifically for logical interface types
options.B: Access, trunk, and routed (Layer 3) ports
options.C: Only access ports; trunk and routed ports cannot participate in any EtherChannel bundle
options.D: Only trunk ports; EtherChannel requires 802.1Q tagging on every member link

questions.explanation_es: Un EtherChannel puede agrupar puertos de acceso, puertos trunk, o puertos enrutados de Capa 3 (formando un port-channel L3). Las interfaces loopback no son elegibles para EtherChannel.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Beyond the obvious bandwidth increase, what STP-related benefit does bundling multiple physical links into a single EtherChannel provide?

options.A: STP sees the whole bundle as a single logical link, so an individual member link flapping up/down doesn't trigger a full STP topology change/recalculation the way a flapping standalone link would
options.B: It disables STP entirely on the bundled links, since STP is assumed to be unnecessary once redundancy exists inside the bundle
options.C: It forces the bundle to always become the STP root port on every VLAN, regardless of actual path cost
options.D: It doubles the default STP port cost for the logical interface compared to any single member link

questions.explanation_es: Al presentarse ante STP como una única interfaz lógica, la caída o recuperación de un enlace miembro individual dentro del bundle no dispara un topology change de STP en toda la red, a diferencia de lo que ocurriría si ese mismo enlace estuviera solo (sin EtherChannel). Esto reduce la inestabilidad de la topología además de sumar ancho de banda.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: In Cisco DNA/Catalyst Center's 'Know Your Network' request path, which of the following is NOT one of its subdomains?

options.A: Environment
options.B: Clients
options.C: Sites
options.D: Devices

questions.explanation_es: Los subdominios del 'Know Your Network' request path de DNA/Catalyst Center incluyen Devices, Clients y Sites, entre otros. 'Environment' no es uno de esos subdominios.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which HTTP method is used to submit a username and password when authenticating to the Cisco DNA/Catalyst Center or vManage REST API?

options.A: GET, with the credentials passed as URL query parameters
options.B: PUT, since authenticating is treated as replacing the prior session resource
options.C: POST
options.D: OPTIONS, to first discover which authentication schemes the server accepts

questions.explanation_es: La autenticación contra la API de DNA/Catalyst Center o vManage se realiza enviando el usuario y contraseña mediante una solicitud POST, que retorna un token que se usa en las solicitudes posteriores.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM event detector publishes an event when an administrator manually executes a policy using the 'event manager run' CLI command?

options.A: The counter event detector, which fires once an internal invocation counter increments
options.B: The none event detector
options.C: The syslog event detector, since manually invoking a policy is logged as a syslog message first
options.D: The CLI event detector, since it is the general-purpose detector for anything typed at the CLI

questions.explanation_es: El detector de eventos 'none' es el que se dispara cuando un administrador ejecuta manualmente una política con el comando 'event manager run', en vez de que la política se dispare por un evento real del sistema.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which command lets you observe, in real time, the CLI actions an EEM applet is executing while it runs?

options.A: show event manager detector all
options.B: event manager run applet-name
options.C: show event manager policy active
options.D: debug event manager action cli

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'debug event manager action cli' permite observar en tiempo real las acciones de CLI que un applet EEM va ejecutando mientras corre, útil para depurar un applet que no se comporta como se espera.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: How does an administrator manually trigger an already-configured EEM applet from the CLI, outside of its normal event trigger?

options.A: debug event manager action cli applet-name
options.B: show event manager policy registered applet-name
options.C: event manager apply applet-name
options.D: event manager run applet-name

questions.explanation_es: El comando 'event manager run applet-name' ejecuta manualmente un applet EEM ya configurado, sin esperar a que ocurra su evento disparador normal — útil para probarlo bajo demanda.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Puppet's three high-level architectural components?

options.A: Puppet master
options.B: Puppet target
options.C: Puppet database
options.D: Puppet agent

questions.explanation_es: Los tres componentes de alto nivel de Puppet son el master, el agent y la database. 'Puppet target' no es un componente real de la arquitectura de Puppet.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: In Chef, what does a 'cookbook' represent, in relation to a 'recipe'?

options.A: A cookbook is the packaged unit distributed and versioned through a Chef supermarket or server, while a recipe refers only to the human-readable documentation describing what that cookbook does, rather than to any executable resource definitions
options.B: A cookbook only exists on the Chef server and has no equivalent concept on the managed node itself
options.C: A cookbook is a single low-level instruction, while a recipe is the larger structure that groups many cookbooks together
options.D: A cookbook is the full scenario definition, bundling everything (recipes, templates, files, attributes) needed to support that scenario — a recipe is one of the smaller units inside it

questions.explanation_es: Un cookbook en Chef define un escenario completo y agrupa todo lo necesario para soportarlo (recipes, templates, archivos, atributos); una recipe es una unidad más pequeña dentro de ese cookbook, con instrucciones de configuración específicas.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: Puppet and Chef both build their configuration-management tooling on which programming language?

options.A: Python, the same language Ansible is built on
options.B: Go, chosen specifically for its concurrency model when managing many nodes in parallel
options.C: Ruby
options.D: Java, matching the JVM-based tooling common in enterprise configuration management

questions.explanation_es: Tanto Puppet como Chef están construidos sobre Ruby (sus DSLs de manifests/recipes y el propio motor son Ruby), a diferencia de Ansible, que está escrito en Python.

questions.name: Orquestación agent vs agentless
questions.question: What file format do Ansible playbooks use to describe plays and tasks?

options.A: A Ansible-specific binary format compiled ahead of time, unlike Puppet manifests or Chef recipes which are plain text
options.B: JSON, matching the format most REST APIs Ansible modules call also use natively
options.C: XML, since it needs strict schema validation for network device modules
options.D: YAML

questions.explanation_es: Los playbooks de Ansible se escriben en YAML (YAML Ain't Markup Language), un formato más simple de leer y escribir que XML, e incluyen una o más 'plays', cada una compuesta de tareas.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: In HSRP, if two routers end up with the same configured priority, which additional attribute breaks the tie to elect the active router?

options.A: The router with the lowest configured interface bandwidth wins, since HSRP favors conserving faster links for user traffic
options.B: Neither router becomes active until an administrator manually breaks the tie by adjusting priority
options.C: The router with the higher primary IP address on the HSRP interface wins
options.D: The router that has been up the longest (highest uptime) always wins, regardless of IP addressing

questions.explanation_es: Cuando dos routers HSRP tienen la misma prioridad configurada, el desempate se resuelve comparando la dirección IP primaria de la interfaz HSRP: el router con la IP más alta gana la elección como router activo.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: What is the distinction between Cisco Cloud OnRamp for SaaS and Cloud OnRamp for IaaS?

options.A: OnRamp for SaaS and OnRamp for IaaS both only apply to on-premises data center connectivity and have no relationship to any public cloud provider
options.B: OnRamp for SaaS and OnRamp for IaaS both function by deploying WAN Edge router instances directly inside the public cloud provider, differing mainly in which cloud marketplace listing each one is published and licensed through
options.C: OnRamp for SaaS chooses the optimal network path for a given SaaS application's traffic; OnRamp for IaaS automatically deploys WAN Edge router instances in the public cloud to join the SD-WAN overlay
options.D: OnRamp for SaaS automatically deploys WAN Edge router instances inside the public cloud provider; OnRamp for IaaS instead chooses the best path for SaaS application traffic

questions.explanation_es: Cloud OnRamp for SaaS elige el mejor camino de red para el tráfico de una aplicación SaaS específica; Cloud OnRamp for IaaS, en cambio, despliega automáticamente instancias de WAN Edge router dentro de la nube pública para que pasen a formar parte del overlay SD-WAN.

questions.name: SD-WAN componentes
questions.question: Can a Cisco SD-WAN WAN Edge router be deployed as something other than a dedicated physical appliance?

options.A: Yes — it can also be deployed as a software-based virtual router, hosted in a private cloud (e.g., VMware ESXi, KVM) or a public cloud (e.g., AWS, Azure)
options.B: Yes, but only as a container running directly inside vManage itself, sharing vManage's own compute resources rather than running as an independent router instance
options.C: No, a WAN Edge router must always be a dedicated physical hardware appliance; software-based deployment is not supported by the SD-WAN architecture
options.D: Yes, but only when paired with a physical vSmart controller located at the same site, since virtual WAN Edge routers cannot reach a cloud-hosted vSmart

questions.explanation_es: Un WAN Edge router puede ser un appliance físico o un router basado en software (virtual), pudiendo alojarse en una nube privada (VMware ESXi, KVM) o en una nube pública (AWS, Azure), sin requisito de coubicación física con el resto de los controladores.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Of the four SD-WAN planes of operation (control, data, orchestration, management), which one is responsible for the automatic onboarding of WAN Edge routers into the SD-WAN overlay fabric?

options.A: Management plane
options.B: Control plane
options.C: Orchestration plane
options.D: Data plane

questions.explanation_es: El plano de orquestación (implementado por vBond) es el responsable de la incorporación automática ('onboarding') de los routers WAN Edge al fabric overlay de SD-WAN, autenticándolos y ayudándolos a descubrir a los demás controladores.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In the four SD-Access operational planes (control, data, policy, management), which plane does VXLAN encapsulation belong to?

options.A: Policy plane, since the VXLAN header's reserved bits carry the SGT used for segmentation
options.B: Data plane
options.C: Management plane, since Cisco DNA Center generates the VXLAN configuration pushed to fabric nodes
options.D: Control plane, since VXLAN headers also carry the LISP mapping information used for control-plane lookups

questions.explanation_es: VXLAN es una técnica de encapsulamiento MAC-in-IP que efectivamente mueve los paquetes de datos a través del fabric — corresponde al data plane de SD-Access. El control plane usa LISP, el policy plane usa TrustSec (SGT), y el management plane lo provee Cisco DNA Center.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In SD-Access, assigning a Security Group Tag (SGT) to a packet as it enters the fabric is a function of which operational plane?

options.A: Control plane
options.B: Management plane
options.C: Data plane
options.D: Policy plane

questions.explanation_es: La asignación de un SGT a un paquete en su punto de ingreso al fabric es una función del policy plane, implementado con Cisco TrustSec — se usa luego para aplicar políticas (QoS, ACLs, segmentación) basadas en el SGT en lugar de direcciones de red.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In an SD-Access fabric, which fabric role does a fabric-mode access point directly connect to?

options.A: The control plane node, so it can register endpoints directly into the host-tracking database itself
options.B: The intermediate node, bypassing the edge layer entirely to reduce hop count for wireless traffic
options.C: The border node, since APs need direct reachability to the fabric's external connections
options.D: The fabric edge node

questions.explanation_es: Un access point en modo fabric debe conectarse directamente al switch de fabric edge node del sitio, que es quien maneja el registro del endpoint y su tráfico dentro del fabric — no se conecta directamente a un border node, control plane node, ni intermediate node.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which type of network delay specifically accounts for the time a router or switch takes to move a packet from an input interface into the output queue of the outbound interface?

options.A: Serialization delay, the time to clock all the bits of a frame onto the physical link
options.B: Processing delay
options.C: Queuing delay, the time a packet waits inside the output queue before being transmitted
options.D: Propagation delay, the time for a signal to physically travel across the transmission medium

questions.explanation_es: El 'processing delay' es el tiempo que le toma a un router o switch tomar un paquete desde la interfaz de entrada y colocarlo en la cola de salida de la interfaz de salida — distinto del queuing delay (tiempo de espera dentro de esa cola), la serialización (tiempo de clockear los bits al medio), o la propagación (tiempo de viaje de la señal por el medio).

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: Type 2 hypervisors (such as VMware Fusion or VMware Workstation) are typically deployed in which kind of environment?

options.A: Test/development environments
options.B: Production data center environments hosting business-critical VMs
options.C: Large-scale service provider multi-tenant environments
options.D: Cloud service provider environments offering IaaS to external customers

questions.explanation_es: Los hypervisors tipo 2 (que corren sobre un sistema operativo host, como VMware Fusion o Workstation) se usan típicamente en entornos de prueba/desarrollo, a diferencia de los tipo 1 (bare-metal, como ESXi), que son los usados en producción.

questions.name: Hypervisor tipo 1 y 2
questions.question: What is the primary benefit of achieving a higher server consolidation ratio (more VMs per physical host)?

options.A: Higher return on investment (ROI), since fewer physical hosts are needed to run the same overall workload
options.B: It allows each individual VM to be provisioned with unlimited vCPUs regardless of the host's physical core count
options.C: Higher power consumption per rack, which is treated as inherently desirable regardless of cost
options.D: It reduces the licensing cost of the hypervisor software itself, since most hypervisor vendors charge per physical host rather than per VM, independent of any actual hardware consolidation benefit achieved

questions.explanation_es: Un mayor ratio de consolidación (más VMs por host físico) mejora el retorno de la inversión (ROI), ya que se necesitan menos servidores físicos para correr la misma carga de trabajo total, reduciendo gasto de capital y espacio de datacenter.

questions.name: VMs / FT / DRS
questions.question: Which of these is NOT a valid way to manage a VMware ESXi host or vCenter Server environment?

options.A: The VMware Host Client (an HTML5-based client for managing a single ESXi host directly)
options.B: The vSphere HTML5 Web Client
options.C: vCenter Server (a centralized management server for multiple ESXi hosts)
options.D: Microsoft Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) client

questions.explanation_es: El cliente RDP de Microsoft no es un método de administración de un entorno VMware ESXi/vCenter. Se usa el VMware Host Client (para un solo host) o vCenter Server con sus distintos clientes web (para administración centralizada de múltiples hosts).

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: How does the Cisco Nexus 1000VE virtual switch improve on its predecessor, the Nexus 1000V?

options.A: It drops NX-OS CLI support entirely in favor of a GUI-only management model
options.B: It no longer depends on in-kernel hypervisor platform APIs (such as VMware's own APIs), unlike the original Nexus 1000V
options.C: It removes support for VMware vSphere environments entirely, targeting only KVM and Hyper-V instead
options.D: It can only be deployed with Open vSwitch as its underlying data plane, unlike the original Nexus 1000V which ran independently

questions.explanation_es: El Nexus 1000VE es la evolución del Nexus 1000V, y su mejora clave es que ya no depende de las APIs internas del hipervisor (como las APIs propias de VMware) para operar, a diferencia de su predecesor.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Which Cisco virtual switch is specifically used to provide switching and policy enforcement within a Cisco ACI environment?

options.A: Open vSwitch
options.B: Cisco Nexus 1000V
options.C: vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS)
options.D: Cisco ACI Virtual Edge

questions.explanation_es: Cisco ACI Virtual Edge es el virtual switch hypervisor-agnostic diseñado específicamente para manejar el switching y la aplicación de políticas dentro de un entorno Cisco ACI, a diferencia del Nexus 1000V (NX-OS genérico), Open vSwitch (multiplataforma general) o el vDS de VMware (nativo de vSphere, sin integración ACI).

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: Is Cisco NFV (Network Functions Virtualization) infrastructure restricted to specialized, vendor-proprietary hardware?

options.A: No, NFV infrastructure can be deployed on any general-purpose x86 platform, and can mix virtual and physical, Cisco and third-party devices and network services
options.B: No, but only ARM-based server platforms are supported, not x86
options.C: Yes, NFV requires SR-IOV-capable network interface cards in every host to achieve line-rate packet forwarding, since a purely software-based virtual switch data path is not considered viable for production NFV deployments
options.D: Yes, NFV strictly requires Cisco-proprietary ASICs and cannot run on generic hardware

questions.explanation_es: La infraestructura NFV puede desplegarse sobre cualquier plataforma x86 de propósito general, permitiendo una mezcla de dispositivos virtuales y físicos, tanto de Cisco como de terceros, dentro del mismo entorno de servicios de red.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: What distinguishes Cisco FlexVPN from a single specific VPN topology like DMVPN or a site-to-site VPN?

options.A: FlexVPN is a unified solution/framework that simplifies deploying multiple different VPN types (site-to-site, hub-and-spoke, remote access) using a common IKEv2-based configuration model
options.B: FlexVPN replaces IPsec entirely with a proprietary Cisco encryption scheme incompatible with standard IKE
options.C: FlexVPN only operates over GRE tunnels and has no direct IPsec-only mode
options.D: FlexVPN is strictly limited to remote-access VPNs and cannot be used for any site-to-site topology

questions.explanation_es: Cisco FlexVPN es un framework unificado, basado en IKEv2, que simplifica el despliegue de distintos tipos de VPN (site-to-site, hub-and-spoke, acceso remoto) bajo un mismo modelo de configuración, en vez de requerir enfoques separados para cada topología.

questions.name: GRE / IPsec / AH
questions.question: Which IKE version introduced native support for NAT traversal (NAT-T)?

options.A: IKEv2
options.B: Neither version supports NAT-T; it is implemented entirely outside of IKE
options.C: NAT-T is unrelated to IKE and is instead a function of ESP alone, independent of which IKE version negotiates the security association
options.D: IKEv1, with IKEv2 later dropping the feature for security reasons

questions.explanation_es: El soporte de NAT traversal (NAT-T) fue incorporado en IKEv2, facilitando el establecimiento de túneles IPsec/IKE cuando uno de los extremos está detrás de un dispositivo NAT.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: What command activates Guest Shell so a Python interpreter can run directly on a Cisco IOS XE platform?

options.A: guestshell run
options.B: iox enable
options.C: guestshell enable
options.D: guestshell run python

questions.explanation_es: Guest Shell se activa con el comando 'guestshell enable', habilitando un contenedor Linux en la plataforma IOS XE donde se puede correr un intérprete de Python, entre otras herramientas.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: What does 'native' or 'onboard' Python refer to, in the context of Cisco switching platforms?

options.A: A cloud-hosted Python runtime that Cisco DNA Center exposes on the administrator's behalf
options.B: A Python interpreter that only understands Cisco-proprietary syntax extensions, incompatible with standard Python code
options.C: Python scripts that must always run from an external management server, never on the device itself
options.D: Python installed natively on the switching platform itself (e.g., a Cisco Catalyst 9300), rather than run through a separate container or external host

questions.explanation_es: 'Native' u 'onboard' Python se refiere a tener Python instalado directamente en la plataforma de switching (por ejemplo, un Catalyst 9300), en vez de depender de un contenedor separado (como Guest Shell) o de un host externo.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: When handling exceptions in Python with a try/except/else block, when does the code inside the 'else' clause execute?

options.A: Every single time, unconditionally, regardless of whether an exception occurred or not, exactly like code placed after the whole try/except block
options.B: Only when no exception was raised in the 'try' block
options.C: Never — 'else' is not a valid keyword in Python's exception-handling syntax
options.D: Only when an exception was raised and successfully caught by the 'except' clause

questions.explanation_es: El bloque 'else' en una construcción try/except se ejecuta únicamente cuando el bloque 'try' terminó sin lanzar ninguna excepción — es decir, cuando todo salió bien y no se entró a ningún 'except'.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which three protocols make up the model-driven programmability stack commonly referenced for network automation?

options.A: Telnet, SSH, and HTTP
options.B: NETCONF, RESTCONF, and gRPC
options.C: BGP, OSPF, and EIGRP
options.D: SNMP, Syslog, and NTP

questions.explanation_es: El stack de programabilidad basado en modelos referenciado habitualmente está compuesto por NETCONF, RESTCONF y gRPC — los tres protocolos de transporte/gestión usados junto con modelos de datos (como YANG) para configurar y operar dispositivos de forma programática.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: What does the first line of a well-formed XML document typically indicate?

options.A: The first child element of the document, since XML has no concept of a distinct declaration line at all
options.B: The root element's name, which must always appear as the literal first line before any other content
options.C: The XML declaration, specifying the XML version and the character encoding used (e.g., version 1.0, ISO-8859-1)
options.D: A comment block documenting the schema author, required by the XML 1.0 specification

questions.explanation_es: La primera línea de un documento XML bien formado es la declaración XML, que especifica la versión de XML (por ejemplo 1.0) y la codificación de caracteres usada (por ejemplo ISO-8859-1), antes de que aparezca el elemento raíz.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: In a JSON object, what is the distinct role of the comma character, as opposed to the colon character?

options.A: The comma separates one key/value pair from the next; the colon separates a key from its own value within a pair
options.B: Comma and colon are fully interchangeable in JSON syntax, and a parser accepts either one in either position
options.C: The comma is only used inside JSON arrays and never appears inside a JSON object at all
options.D: The comma separates each key from its own value within a single pair; the colon separates one complete key/value pair from the next

questions.explanation_es: En JSON, la coma separa un par clave/valor del siguiente dentro de un objeto; los dos puntos (colon) separan la clave de su propio valor dentro de un mismo par. Omitir una coma entre pares es un error de sintaxis común.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Why is SNMP generally considered a poor fit as a 'data model' for modern network programmability, motivating the move toward YANG-based models instead?

options.A: SNMP cannot run over UDP, requiring a costly protocol translation layer for every request
options.B: SNMP represents its managed objects strictly as flat, unstructured scalar values with no hierarchical organization at all, unlike the hierarchical, tree-structured data models that YANG defines
options.C: SNMP requires a dedicated hardware appliance per managed device, unlike YANG-based management
options.D: SNMP does not distinguish between configuration data and operational (state) data, unlike YANG-based models which model them separately and explicitly

questions.explanation_es: Una limitación clave de SNMP frente a los modelos basados en YANG es que no distingue entre datos de configuración y datos operativos/de estado; los modelos YANG modelan ambos tipos de datos de forma separada y explícita, lo cual es una de las motivaciones para adoptar NETCONF/YANG en vez de depender solo de SNMP.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid SNMPv3 security level?

options.A: noAuthNoPriv
options.B: privNoAuth
options.C: authPriv
options.D: authNoPriv

questions.explanation_es: Los niveles de seguridad válidos de SNMPv3 son noAuthNoPriv (sin autenticación ni cifrado), authNoPriv (con autenticación, sin cifrado) y authPriv (con autenticación y cifrado). 'privNoAuth' no es un nivel real — el cifrado (priv) en SNMPv3 siempre requiere autenticación.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: In Cisco IOS traceroute output, what does an 'A' character next to a hop indicate?

options.A: The hop successfully forwarded the probe with no issues at all
options.B: The probe timed out waiting for a reply from that hop
options.C: The destination network is unreachable from that hop
options.D: The hop is administratively prohibited from responding, typically because an ACL is filtering the probe

questions.explanation_es: En la salida de traceroute de Cisco IOS, el carácter 'A' indica que el salto está administrativamente prohibido de responder, típicamente porque una ACL está filtrando el paquete de prueba.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: What advantage does the SNMP 'Get Bulk' operation offer over repeatedly issuing 'Get Next'?

options.A: Get Bulk retrieves a large amount of object variable data in a single request/response exchange, instead of requiring many repeated Get Next round-trips
options.B: Get Bulk retrieves values only for scalar objects and cannot walk a table's repeating rows the way repeated Get Next requests can, limiting its usefulness for retrieving tabular MIB data
options.C: Get Bulk works by internally issuing a sequence of Get Next requests in the background and returning their combined results as a single response, so its round-trip savings depend on the agent's own implementation rather than on the protocol itself
options.D: Get Bulk can only retrieve a single specific object, making it more limited than Get Next

questions.explanation_es: La operación 'Get Bulk' de SNMP permite recuperar una gran cantidad de variables de objeto en un solo intercambio de solicitud/respuesta, evitando tener que hacer muchas rondas repetidas de 'Get Next' para recorrer la misma cantidad de datos.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Cisco DNA/Catalyst Center's four main dashboard sections aligned to IT workflow?

options.A: Automation
options.B: Provision
options.C: Design
options.D: Assurance

questions.explanation_es: Las cuatro secciones principales del dashboard de DNA/Catalyst Center son Design, Policy, Provision y Assurance. 'Automation' no es una de esas cuatro secciones (aunque muchas de ellas habilitan tareas de automatización).

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: In Cisco DNA/Catalyst Center's Assurance section, what does the Device 360 / Client 360 view specifically provide?

options.A: The ability to push a new configuration template directly to the selected device or client
options.B: Machine-learning-driven context-aware baselining that models the relationship between metrics as network conditions change
options.C: Historical topology, throughput, and latency information for a specific device or client across different time windows and applications
options.D: A list of every ACL currently applied network-wide, unrelated to any single device

questions.explanation_es: La vista Device 360 / Client 360 de Catalyst Center Assurance muestra información histórica de topología, throughput y latencia para un dispositivo o cliente específico, a través de distintas ventanas de tiempo y aplicaciones — a diferencia del baselining por machine learning, que es otra capacidad distinta dentro de Assurance.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which of the following routing protocols is classified as an Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP) rather than an IGP?

options.A: OSPF
options.B: IS-IS
options.C: EIGRP
options.D: BGP

questions.explanation_es: BGP es el único protocolo de la lista clasificado como EGP, ya que se usa para enrutar entre sistemas autónomos distintos; OSPF, EIGRP e IS-IS son IGPs que operan dentro de un mismo sistema autónomo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which three of the following routing protocols are classified as Interior Gateway Protocols (IGPs)? (Choose three.)

options.A: EIGRP
options.B: OSPF
options.C: RIPv2
options.D: BGP

questions.explanation_es: RIPv2, EIGRP y OSPF operan dentro de un mismo sistema autónomo y por eso se clasifican como IGPs; BGP, en cambio, es un protocolo de puerta de enlace exterior (EGP) usado entre sistemas autónomos distintos.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: A path-vector routing protocol such as BGP selects the best loop-free path primarily by evaluating which of the following?

options.A: Total accumulated delay
options.B: Path attributes (such as AS_Path)
options.C: Interface cost
options.D: Hop count

questions.explanation_es: Los protocolos de vector de ruta, como BGP, no usan métricas tradicionales de distancia; en su lugar evalúan atributos de ruta como el AS_Path para determinar el mejor camino libre de bucles.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: A classic distance-vector routing protocol determines the best loop-free path mainly by comparing which metric?

options.A: Combined bandwidth and delay
options.B: AS path length
options.C: Hop count
options.D: Interface cost

questions.explanation_es: Los protocolos de vector de distancia clásicos, como RIP, seleccionan la mejor ruta basándose principalmente en el número de saltos hasta el destino.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: A link-state routing protocol such as OSPF determines the best loop-free path mainly by using which value?

options.A: Interface cost (link metric)
options.B: Hop count
options.C: Administrative distance
options.D: AS path attributes

questions.explanation_es: Los protocolos de estado de enlace, como OSPF, calculan la mejor ruta ejecutando el algoritmo SPF sobre el costo (métrica) de cada enlace, no sobre el número de saltos.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which IP protocol number does EIGRP use to identify its packets at Layer 3?
questions.explanation_es: EIGRP utiliza el número de protocolo IP 88, mientras que OSPF usa el 89.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: How many distinct packet types does EIGRP use for communication between routers?

options.A: Three
options.B: Five
options.C: Four
options.D: Six

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP define cinco tipos de paquetes: hello, update, query, reply y ack.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In EIGRP terminology, what is the successor for a given destination network?

options.A: Any neighbor that has advertised the destination prefix, regardless of metric
options.B: The next-hop router associated with the lowest-metric (feasible distance) path to that destination
options.C: A backup route that satisfies the feasibility condition
options.D: The router responsible for maintaining adjacencies on a broadcast segment

questions.explanation_es: El sucesor es el router del siguiente salto que se usa para reenviar tráfico porque ofrece la ruta con la distancia factible (FD) más baja hacia el destino.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which three of the following are pieces of information stored in an EIGRP topology table entry for a prefix? (Choose three.)

options.A: The total path delay reported for the route
options.B: The maximum bandwidth available along the path
options.C: The list of neighbors that advertised that prefix
options.D: The destination network prefix

questions.explanation_es: La tabla de topología de EIGRP guarda el prefijo de destino, el retraso total y los vecinos que anunciaron esa ruta; en realidad se registra el ancho de banda mínimo del trayecto, no el máximo, así que esa opción es incorrecta.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which two of the following destination addresses does EIGRP use, when possible, to communicate with neighbors? (Choose two.)

options.A: Multicast MAC address 01:00:5E:00:00:05
options.B: IP multicast address 224.0.0.5
options.C: IP multicast address 224.0.0.10
options.D: Multicast MAC address 01:00:5E:00:00:0A

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP usa la dirección multicast 224.0.0.10 y su correspondiente dirección MAC multicast 01:00:5E:00:00:0A; 224.0.0.5 y su MAC asociada pertenecen a OSPF.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which interface-level value can be tuned to influence EIGRP's path selection without affecting the metric calculations of other protocols such as OSPF?

options.A: Interface delay
options.B: Interface bandwidth
options.C: Interface MTU
options.D: Interface priority

questions.explanation_es: El retraso de interfaz (delay) es un valor propio del cálculo de métrica de EIGRP; modificarlo no afecta a OSPF, mientras que cambiar el ancho de banda de la interfaz sí impactaría a ambos protocolos, ya que OSPF también usa el ancho de banda para su costo.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: In the classic EIGRP metric formula, the bandwidth component is scaled relative to a reference link speed of how much?

options.A: 10 Gbps
options.B: 100 Mbps
options.C: 1 Gbps
options.D: 40 Gbps

questions.explanation_es: La fórmula clásica de EIGRP escala el ancho de banda mínimo del trayecto respecto a un enlace de referencia de 10 Gbps (10^7 kbps).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the default EIGRP hello interval on high-speed interfaces (above T1 speed)?

options.A: 1 second
options.B: 5 seconds
options.C: 30 seconds
options.D: 10 seconds

questions.explanation_es: En interfaces de alta velocidad, EIGRP envía paquetes hello cada 5 segundos por defecto.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: When an EIGRP route has a stable path with no ongoing recomputation, what state is that route considered to be in?

options.A: Held-down
options.B: Dead
options.C: Passive
options.D: Active

questions.explanation_es: Una ruta EIGRP estable se encuentra en estado pasivo (P); pasa a estado activo (A) solo cuando DUAL necesita recalcular el camino tras perder el sucesor.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: When an EIGRP router loses its successor route and has no feasible successor available, how does it signal that a path recomputation is needed?

options.A: It sends an update packet with a topology-change notification flag.
options.B: It marks the route as unreachable and sends query packets to its neighbors asking for alternate paths.
options.C: It sends a withdrawal message instructing neighbors to purge the route from their topology tables.
options.D: It sends an update packet advertising the route with a metric of zero.

questions.explanation_es: Sin sucesor factible, el router marca la ruta con métrica infinita (inalcanzable), pasa a estado activo y envía paquetes query a sus vecinos para buscar un camino alternativo, como parte del algoritmo DUAL.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: When you manually configure EIGRP route summarization on a specific interface, out of which interfaces is the resulting summary route advertised?

options.A: Only out the interface where the summarization command was applied
options.B: Out every EIGRP-enabled interface on the router
options.C: Only toward the neighbor holding the feasible successor
options.D: Out every interface belonging to the same VRF

questions.explanation_es: La sumarización manual de EIGRP se aplica por interfaz; el resumen solo se anuncia por la interfaz donde se configuró, no automáticamente por todas las interfaces del router.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which two of the following routing protocols rely on a link-state (SPF-based) algorithm to compute the best path? (Choose two.)

options.A: OSPF
options.B: IS-IS
options.C: RIP
options.D: EIGRP

questions.explanation_es: OSPF e IS-IS son protocolos de estado de enlace que ejecutan el algoritmo SPF de Dijkstra; RIP es vector de distancia y EIGRP es un vector de distancia avanzado (DUAL).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What IP protocol number is carried in the header of EIGRP packets?
questions.explanation_es: EIGRP se identifica con el número de protocolo IP 88.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: On a high-speed EIGRP-enabled interface, how often does the router send hello packets by default?

options.A: Every 3 seconds
options.B: Every 5 seconds
options.C: Every 15 seconds
options.D: Every 10 seconds

questions.explanation_es: El temporizador hello por defecto de EIGRP en interfaces de alta velocidad es de 5 segundos.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Which of the following is considered a pure distance-vector routing protocol, without link-state or hybrid characteristics?

options.A: OSPF
options.B: RIP
options.C: IS-IS
options.D: EIGRP

questions.explanation_es: RIP es un protocolo de vector de distancia puro (algoritmo Bellman-Ford); EIGRP es un vector de distancia avanzado con rasgos de estado de enlace, y OSPF/IS-IS son protocolos de estado de enlace.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the default EIGRP hello interval on slower interfaces, such as those below T1 speed?

options.A: 60 seconds
options.B: 10 seconds
options.C: 15 seconds
options.D: 180 seconds

questions.explanation_es: En interfaces lentas (por debajo de T1), EIGRP usa un temporizador hello por defecto de 60 segundos, en lugar de los 5 segundos usados en interfaces rápidas.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Besides per-route metric details, what does the EIGRP topology table contain overall?

options.A: Only the routes currently installed in the IP routing table (RIB)
options.B: A historical audit log of every past successor change
options.C: Every network prefix advertised within the EIGRP autonomous system, along with the neighbors that advertised each one
options.D: The complete OSPF link-state database learned via redistribution

questions.explanation_es: La tabla de topología de EIGRP contiene todos los prefijos anunciados dentro del sistema autónomo EIGRP, junto con los vecinos que los anunciaron, no solo las rutas activas instaladas en la RIB.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What IP protocol number does OSPF use in its packet header?
questions.explanation_es: OSPF utiliza el número de protocolo IP 89; EIGRP usa el 88.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How many distinct OSPF packet types are used for inter-router communication?

options.A: Six
options.B: Four
options.C: Five
options.D: Three

questions.explanation_es: OSPF define cinco tipos de paquetes: hello, DBD, LSR, LSU y LSAck.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which two of the following destination addresses does OSPF use, when possible, for its packets? (Choose two.)

options.A: IP multicast address 224.0.0.10
options.B: IP multicast address 224.0.0.5
options.C: Multicast MAC address 01:00:5E:00:00:0A
options.D: Multicast MAC address 01:00:5E:00:00:05

questions.explanation_es: OSPF usa la dirección multicast AllSPFRouters 224.0.0.5 y su MAC multicast asociada 01:00:5E:00:00:05; 224.0.0.10 y su MAC son de EIGRP.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which statement about enabling OSPF on a router interface is accurate?

options.A: A wildcard mask can only be applied at the interface level, not within the OSPF process.
options.B: OSPF can be enabled either through the network command under the process or through an interface-level command.
options.C: OSPF activates itself automatically on every interface with an IP address once the process starts.
options.D: OSPF can only be enabled through the network command under the OSPF process.

questions.explanation_es: OSPF admite dos métodos de habilitación: el comando network bajo el proceso, o el comando de interfaz ip ospf process-id area area-id; no está limitado a un único método.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which of the following must match between two directly connected routers for an OSPF neighbor adjacency to form?

options.A: The OSPF process number combined with the area name
options.B: The router ID configured on each router
options.C: The OSPF process ID configured on each router
options.D: The hello and dead interval timers configured on the shared interfaces

questions.explanation_es: El process ID de OSPF es de significado local y no necesita coincidir entre routers; en cambio, los temporizadores hello y dead sí deben coincidir para que la adyacencia se establezca correctamente.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: When a default route is injected into OSPF using the default-information originate command, how does it typically appear in the routing table of other OSPF routers?

options.A: As an OSPF external route (O*E1 or O*E2)
options.B: As an OSPF intra-area route (O)
options.C: As an OSPF inter-area route (O IA)
options.D: As a directly connected route

questions.explanation_es: Un default route inyectado con default-information originate se anuncia como una ruta externa de OSPF (tipo E1 o E2), no como una ruta intra-área ni inter-área.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: On an OSPF point-to-point network type, such as a serial link between two routers, what happens regarding the designated router (DR) role?

options.A: No DR or BDR election occurs on that network type.
options.B: The router with the highest interface IP address becomes the DR.
options.C: The router with the highest router ID becomes the DR.
options.D: Both routers alternate holding the DR role periodically.

questions.explanation_es: En redes punto a punto no existe el concepto de DR/BDR, ya que solo hay dos routers y una adyacencia completa se forma directamente entre ellos.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: By default, OSPF calculates an interface's cost using a reference bandwidth of how much?

options.A: 1 Gbps
options.B: 40 Gbps
options.C: 10 Gbps
options.D: 100 Mbps

questions.explanation_es: El ancho de banda de referencia por defecto de OSPF es 100 Mbps, lo cual hace que interfaces de mayor velocidad compartan el mismo costo mínimo de 1 si no se ajusta el valor de referencia.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which interface command prevents a router from ever being elected as the designated router (DR) on that segment?

options.A: ip ospf priority 255
options.B: ip ospf network point-to-point
options.C: passive-interface (configured under the OSPF process)
options.D: ip ospf priority 0

questions.explanation_es: Configurar ip ospf priority 0 en la interfaz excluye al router de la elección de DR/BDR; priority 255 en cambio lo haría más propenso a ganar la elección.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: By default, what network does OSPF advertise for a loopback interface configured with IP address 10.123.4.1/30?
questions.explanation_es: OSPF anuncia las interfaces de loopback como rutas host /32 por defecto, sin importar la máscara configurada en la interfaz.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: When an OSPF ABR advertises reachability for a route between two areas, what actually happens to the original intra-area route information?

options.A: The ABR originates a new Type 3 summary LSA representing that reachability into the other area.
options.B: The ABR forwards the original Type 1 router LSA unchanged into the other area.
options.C: The ABR forwards the route only if both areas use the same area ID.
options.D: The ABR bundles the entire source-area LSDB into a single LSA and floods it.

questions.explanation_es: El ABR no reenvía las LSA de tipo 1 originales entre áreas; en su lugar genera una nueva LSA de tipo 3 (resumen) que representa la alcanzabilidad de esa red en la otra área.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which statement best describes the scope of a single OSPF router's link-state database (LSDB) in a multi-area design?

options.A: Only ABRs maintain any LSDB; internal routers keep none.
options.B: A router maintains LSDB entries only for the areas in which it has at least one active interface.
options.C: Every router in the domain keeps an identical LSDB covering all areas.
options.D: The LSDB is synchronized identically across every router in the OSPF domain because Type 5 LSAs are understood to carry a complete copy of every area's internal topology information, not just external route summaries

questions.explanation_es: Cada router OSPF solo mantiene la base de datos de estado de enlace de las áreas a las que está directamente conectado, no de todo el dominio.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How many OSPF LSA types are used for routing traditional IPv4 traffic?

options.A: Seven
options.B: Six
options.C: Five
options.D: Four

questions.explanation_es: OSPF utiliza seis tipos de LSA para IPv4: tipo 1 (router), 2 (network), 3 (summary), 4 (ASBR summary), 5 (AS external) y 7 (NSSA external).

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the purpose of the age field carried in each entry of the OSPF link-state database?

options.A: To provide version control so the most recently originated LSA is preferred
options.B: To count upward so the LSA is removed from the LSDB once it reaches its maximum age (3600 seconds)
options.C: To record, for troubleshooting purposes, the exact time the LSA was first advertised
options.D: To count down from an initial value and purge the LSA once it reaches zero

questions.explanation_es: El campo age de una LSA se incrementa con el tiempo, y cuando alcanza el valor MaxAge (3600 segundos), la LSA se elimina de la base de datos y se fuerza un nuevo cálculo SPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which LSA type is present in every OSPF area, including the backbone and every non-backbone area?

options.A: AS external LSA (Type 5)
options.B: Router LSA (Type 1)
options.C: Network LSA (Type 2)
options.D: Summary LSA (Type 3)

questions.explanation_es: La LSA de tipo 1 (router LSA) la origina cada router en cada área a la que pertenece, por lo que existe en todas las áreas del dominio OSPF.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: When an ABR receives a Type 2 (network) LSA from a multi-access segment inside one of its attached areas, what does it do with that LSA?

options.A: It floods the Type 2 LSA unchanged into the other attached areas.
options.B: It keeps the Type 2 LSA scoped to the area where it was received and does not forward it into other areas.
options.C: It converts the Type 2 LSA into a Type 1 router LSA before forwarding it.
options.D: It forwards the Type 2 LSA only into the backbone area.

questions.explanation_es: Las LSA de tipo 2 (network) tienen alcance de área única; el ABR no las reenvía a otras áreas, sino que representa esa red mediante una LSA de tipo 3 si es necesario.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: When an ABR receives a Type 3 summary LSA inside one of its non-backbone areas, what does it do with that information?

options.A: It installs the route for the area where it was received but does not directly re-advertise that LSA into another non-backbone area.
options.B: It advertises the Type 3 LSA into the backbone area and flags it as an error.
options.C: It discards the Type 3 LSA without processing it.
options.D: It always re-advertises the same Type 3 LSA into every other attached area.

questions.explanation_es: Un ABR instala la información de la LSA tipo 3 recibida en un área no backbone, pero no la reenvía directamente a otra área no backbone; el tránsito entre áreas no troncales debe pasar por el área 0.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Is it accurate to say that OSPF always selects the mathematically shortest end-to-end path for both intra-area and inter-area destinations?

options.A: No, because inter-area path selection can be suboptimal since a Type 3 LSA only advertises a cost value, hiding the detailed topology beyond the originating ABR.
options.B: Yes, because SPF guarantees a globally optimal path for every route type.
options.C: No, because OSPF never uses SPF for inter-area routes, only for intra-area routes.
options.D: Yes, but only when all areas use the same reference bandwidth.

questions.explanation_es: Dentro de un área, OSPF sí garantiza la ruta más corta real mediante SPF; pero para rutas inter-área, el ABR solo anuncia un costo agregado sin el detalle topológico completo, por lo que la selección puede no ser la óptima global cuando existen múltiples ABR.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Why is segmenting a large OSPF domain into multiple areas considered a form of summarization?

options.A: Because it removes the need for a designated router on multi-access segments
options.B: Because it reduces the total IP address space required by the network
options.C: Because it hides the detailed topology of one area from routers in other areas, exposing only aggregated reachability information via Type 3 LSAs
options.D: Because it compresses the LSA headers exchanged over slow WAN links

questions.explanation_es: Dividir en áreas oculta los detalles topológicos internos de un área frente a las demás, ya que solo se propaga información agregada mediante LSA de resumen, lo cual es conceptualmente una forma de sumarización.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Which command, configured under the OSPF process on an ABR, summarizes routes learned from one area before advertising them into another area?

options.A: The OSPF process command summary-address network prefix-length
options.B: The interface command summary-address network prefix-length
options.C: The OSPF process command area area-id range network subnet-mask
options.D: The interface command area area-id summary-address network subnet-mask

questions.explanation_es: La sumarización entre áreas en un ABR se configura con el comando de proceso area area-id range network subnet-mask; el comando summary-address se usa en el ASBR para sumarizar rutas externas redistribuidas.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How many distinct OSPFv3 packet types exist for inter-router communication?

options.A: Three
options.B: Six
options.C: Five
options.D: Four

questions.explanation_es: OSPFv3 conserva la misma lógica y los mismos cinco tipos de paquete que OSPFv2: hello, DBD, LSR, LSU y LSAck.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What destination address does an OSPFv3 hello packet typically use?

options.A: IPv6 multicast address FF02::6
options.B: IPv4 multicast address 224.0.0.5
options.C: IPv6 multicast address FF02::5
options.D: IPv4 multicast address 224.0.0.10

questions.explanation_es: OSPFv3 usa la dirección multicast de enlace local FF02::5 (AllSPFRouters) para los paquetes hello, equivalente conceptual de 224.0.0.5 en OSPFv2.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How is OSPFv3 enabled on a router interface?

options.A: Automatically on every IPv6-enabled interface once the OSPF process initializes
options.B: With the interface command ospfv3 process-id ipv6 area area-id
options.C: With the command network interface-id under the OSPF process
options.D: With the command network prefix/prefix-length under the OSPF process

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de OSPFv2, OSPFv3 no usa network statements; se habilita directamente en la interfaz con el comando ospfv3 process-id ipv6 area area-id.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: On a router with no IPv4 address configured anywhere, what happens if you configure only an IPv6 link-local address and enable OSPFv3 on that interface?

options.A: OSPFv3 fails to form an adjacency because the router ID defaults to 0.0.0.0 unless one is manually configured.
options.B: The OSPFv3 process refuses to start at all without an IPv4 address present somewhere on the router.
options.C: OSPFv3 automatically derives its router ID from the interface's MAC address.
options.D: OSPFv3 forms the neighbor adjacency normally, since a router ID is optional.

questions.explanation_es: OSPFv3 sigue necesitando un router ID de 32 bits; si no hay direcciones IPv4 disponibles ni se configura manualmente, el router ID queda en 0.0.0.0 y no se forman adyacencias.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: Besides an IPv4 address and enabling the IPv4 address-family, what else is required to run OSPFv3 for IPv4 on a Cisco interface?

options.A: Nothing else; the IPv4 address and address-family are sufficient by themselves.
options.B: The interface must be configured as a passive interface for IPv4 traffic.
options.C: A separate OSPFv2 process must run in parallel on the same interface.
options.D: IPv6 unicast routing must be enabled and the interface still needs an IPv6 link-local address, because OSPFv3 always uses IPv6 for transport.

questions.explanation_es: Aunque OSPFv3 pueda transportar prefijos IPv4 mediante address-family ipv4, el protocolo sigue usando IPv6 como transporte subyacente, por lo que se requiere ipv6 unicast-routing y una dirección link-local IPv6 en la interfaz.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the default administrative distance assigned to routes learned via OSPF on a Cisco router?
questions.explanation_es: La distancia administrativa por defecto de OSPF es 110, comparada con 90 para EIGRP interno y 120 para RIP.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What problem does an OSPF virtual link solve?

options.A: It removes the need for a designated router on a multi-access network.
options.B: It allows two OSPF routers configured with different process IDs to form an adjacency.
options.C: It creates a redundant physical adjacency between two ABRs located in the same area.
options.D: It provides a logical connection joining a disconnected non-backbone area to the backbone (Area 0).

questions.explanation_es: Un enlace virtual conecta lógicamente, a través de un área de tránsito, a un área que no tiene conexión física con el área 0, cumpliendo así el requisito de que todas las áreas lleguen al backbone.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the AllSPFRouters multicast destination address used by OSPFv2?
questions.explanation_es: 224.0.0.5 es la dirección multicast AllSPFRouters usada por todos los routers OSPFv2 para el descubrimiento de vecinos.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: What is the AllDRouters multicast destination address used by OSPFv3?
questions.explanation_es: FF02::6 es la dirección multicast AllDRouters de OSPFv3, usada por routers no DR/BDR para enviar actualizaciones al DR y al BDR.

questions.name: OSPFv2/v3 config
questions.question: How does OSPFv3 differ from OSPFv2 regarding the number of protocol instances that can run on a single link?

options.A: Multiple instances per link are supported only when the link carries IPv4 traffic.
options.B: Both versions restrict a link to a single OSPF process with no distinguishing field.
options.C: OSPFv3 allows multiple independent OSPFv3 instances on the same link, distinguished by an instance ID field; OSPFv2 has no equivalent mechanism.
options.D: OSPFv2 supports multiple instances per link, while OSPFv3 restricts a link to a single instance.

questions.explanation_es: OSPFv3 incorpora un campo de Instance ID que permite ejecutar varias instancias independientes de OSPFv3 sobre el mismo enlace, una capacidad que OSPFv2 no ofrece.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: On an Ethernet (multi-access) exit interface, which type of static route best avoids unintended forwarding behavior if the link fails?

options.A: A recursive static route (specifying only a next-hop IP address)
options.B: A directly attached static route (specifying only the exit interface)
options.C: A fully specified static route (specifying both the exit interface and the next-hop IP address)
options.D: A static route to the null interface

questions.explanation_es: En un enlace Ethernet, una ruta estática completamente especificada (interfaz de salida más next-hop) evita el comportamiento indeseado que puede ocurrir con rutas solo por interfaz (uso de ARP proxy) o rutas recursivas que podrían seguir resolviéndose por una ruta alterna tras una falla.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: What is a floating static route primarily used for?

options.A: As a static route that keeps recursing until it resolves to a directly connected interface
options.B: As a route that is automatically installed once the primary route ages out after 180 seconds
options.C: As a static route configured with an administrative distance lower than the routing protocol it is meant to back up, so it takes over immediately once configured rather than waiting for the primary route to fail
options.D: As a backup route to a primary or dynamically learned route, made less preferred by configuring a higher administrative distance

questions.explanation_es: Una ruta estática flotante se configura con una distancia administrativa mayor que la de la ruta primaria (estática o dinámica), de modo que solo se instala en la RIB si la ruta primaria desaparece.

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: What defines a recursive static route?

options.A: A static route whose next hop is directly connected, requiring no further lookup
options.B: A static route whose next hop must itself be resolved by looking up another route already present in the RIB
options.C: A static route that points only to a null interface for traffic filtering
options.D: A static route where the exit interface and next-hop IP are both explicitly specified

questions.explanation_es: En una ruta estática recursiva, el router solo especifica una IP de next-hop, y debe hacer una búsqueda adicional en la tabla de enrutamiento para determinar la interfaz de salida hacia ese next-hop.

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) can be used to segment routing tables for which type(s) of addressing?

options.A: Both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses
options.B: IPv6 addresses only
options.C: IPv4 addresses only
options.D: MAC addresses only

questions.explanation_es: VRF-lite permite mantener tablas de enrutamiento separadas e independientes tanto para IPv4 como para IPv6 dentro del mismo router físico.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which two ranges represent private-use autonomous system numbers reserved by IANA? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation_es: El rango de 2 bytes reservado para ASN privados es 64.512–65.534, y el rango de 4 bytes reservado para ASN privados es 4.200.000.000–4.294.967.294 (según RFC 6996). Los otros rangos mostrados no corresponden a los bloques oficiales de ASN privados.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which category of BGP path attribute must be understood by every BGP implementation and must be included in every route advertisement sent to peers?

options.A: Well-known mandatory
options.B: Optional transitive
options.C: Optional non-transitive
options.D: Well-known discretionary

questions.explanation_es: Un atributo well-known mandatory (obligatorio y reconocido) debe ser entendido por todas las implementaciones de BGP y debe incluirse en cada actualización enviada a los vecinos (por ejemplo, AS_PATH, ORIGIN y NEXT_HOP). Los atributos discrecionales u opcionales no tienen ese requisito.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how BGP routers normally identify their peers?

options.A: BGP peers are explicitly configured with neighbor statements; BGP does not use multicast hello discovery like IGPs do.
options.B: BGP relies on DHCP option 43 to learn the IP addresses of potential peers.
options.C: BGP neighbors are discovered automatically by sending ARP requests to every directly connected subnet.
options.D: BGP routers automatically discover neighbors using multicast hello packets, similar to OSPF.

questions.explanation_es: BGP no utiliza mecanismos de descubrimiento dinámico basados en multidifusión como los IGP; los vecinos se configuran explícitamente mediante sentencias neighbor en cada extremo de la sesión.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the number of hops that can separate two BGP peers?

options.A: BGP peers must always be directly connected, one hop away from each other.
options.B: Only iBGP sessions can span multiple hops; eBGP sessions can never be configured to do so.
options.C: Because BGP runs over TCP, both iBGP and eBGP sessions can be established between routers that are multiple hops apart, given appropriate underlying reachability.
options.D: BGP requires an IGP to already be running between two peers before any session can form, regardless of hop count.

questions.explanation_es: Una sesión BGP no está limitada a un solo salto: como BGP funciona sobre TCP, tanto sesiones iBGP como eBGP (esta última usando ebgp-multihop) pueden establecerse entre routers separados por varios saltos, siempre que exista alcanzabilidad de capa 3 subyacente.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement about IPv4 unicast BGP sessions is accurate?

options.A: BGP cannot form a TCP session with a peer until the IPv4 unicast address family has been manually enabled.
options.B: IPv4 unicast reachability must be explicitly activated with neighbor activate before the underlying TCP session can even be established.
options.C: The IPv4 unicast address family is enabled by default for a newly configured neighbor, so no extra activation step is needed to form a basic session.
options.D: The IPv4 unicast address family must be created under address-family ipv4 unicast before any neighbor statement can be applied.

questions.explanation_es: La familia de direcciones IPv4 unicast se activa de forma predeterminada para cualquier vecino recién configurado, por lo que no es necesario activarla manualmente para establecer una sesión BGP básica sobre IPv4.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which command displays detailed BGP neighbor information, including the negotiated hello and hold timers, for a specific address family?

options.A: show bgp <afi> <safi> neighbors
options.B: show bgp neighbors
options.C: show ip bgp interface brief
options.D: show bgp <afi> <safi> summary

questions.explanation_es: El comando show bgp <afi> <safi> neighbors muestra información detallada de cada vecino, incluidos los temporizadores de hello y hold negociados para esa familia de direcciones específica.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: According to the BGP RIB model defined in RFC 4271, how many distinct routing information bases does a BGP speaker conceptually maintain?

options.A: One
options.B: Four
options.C: Two
options.D: Three (Adj-RIB-In, Loc-RIB, and Adj-RIB-Out)

questions.explanation_es: Según la RFC 4271, un router BGP mantiene conceptualmente tres bases de información de enrutamiento: Adj-RIB-In (rutas recibidas de los vecinos), Loc-RIB (la tabla BGP local con las mejores rutas seleccionadas) y Adj-RIB-Out (rutas que se anunciarán a cada vecino).

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement best describes what a BGP router advertises to its neighbors for a given prefix, by default?

options.A: It advertises every path it has learned for that prefix so each neighbor can build a full topology map.
options.B: It advertises only the single best path it selected for that prefix, unless the BGP Additional Paths (Add-Path) capability has been negotiated.
options.C: It advertises all iBGP-learned paths but withholds every eBGP-learned path.
options.D: It advertises whichever path has the shortest AS_Path, even if that path was not selected as the overall best path.

questions.explanation_es: De forma predeterminada, un router BGP anuncia a sus vecinos únicamente la mejor ruta que ha seleccionado para un prefijo determinado, no todas las rutas candidatas; para anunciar múltiples caminos es necesario negociar la funcionalidad BGP Additional Paths (Add-Path).

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which BGP command creates a summarized route while suppressing advertisement of its more-specific component routes, shielding downstream routers from flaps of those individual prefixes?

options.A: aggregate-address <network> <subnet-mask> summary-only
options.B: summary-address <network> <subnet-mask>
options.C: aggregate-address <network> <subnet-mask> as-set
options.D: summary-address <network> <mask> <subnet-mask>

questions.explanation_es: El comando aggregate-address <red> <máscara> summary-only crea una ruta resumen y suprime el anuncio de las rutas más específicas que la componen, evitando que los routers en sentido descendente procesen las fluctuaciones (flaps) de cada prefijo individual.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement about establishing a BGP session that carries IPv6 prefixes is accurate?

options.A: IPv6 unicast is enabled by default for every neighbor, exactly like IPv4 unicast, so no additional activation is required.
options.B: BGP cannot exchange IPv6 prefixes under any circumstances; only IPv4 transport and prefixes are supported.
options.C: The address-family ipv6 configuration only changes the output of show commands and has no effect on which routes are actually exchanged.
options.D: The IPv6 unicast address family must be explicitly configured and activated for the neighbor before IPv6 prefixes can be exchanged, unlike the default IPv4 unicast address family.

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de IPv4 unicast, la familia de direcciones IPv6 unicast no se activa de forma predeterminada: es necesario configurarla explícitamente con address-family ipv6 y activar al vecino con neighbor activate para poder intercambiar prefijos IPv6.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: In which scenarios is it generally considered poor practice to let a multihomed site provide transit routing for traffic belonging to other sites? (Choose three.)

options.A: Internet-facing connections at a branch location
options.B: MPLS-based connections at a data center that has been sized for transit traffic
options.C: Internet-facing connections at a data center
options.D: MPLS-based connections at a branch location

questions.explanation_es: El enrutamiento de tránsito suele evitarse en las conexiones a Internet, tanto en centros de datos como en sucursales, y en las conexiones MPLS de las sucursales, ya que esos enlaces normalmente no están dimensionados para cursar tráfico ajeno. En cambio, un centro de datos conectado por MPLS sí puede actuar como punto de tránsito planificado porque su ancho de banda puede dimensionarse para ello.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes using an extended ACL to conditionally match routes (network prefixes) rather than packets?

options.A: Extended ACLs behave identically whether they are filtering packets, IGP routes, or BGP routes.
options.B: Extended ACLs cannot be used at all to filter routing protocol prefixes, only to filter packets.
options.C: The way the source and destination fields are interpreted when matching a route can differ depending on whether the ACL is applied to an IGP or to BGP.
options.D: Extended ACLs can only be used to filter BGP routes; IGPs must always rely on standard ACLs instead.

questions.explanation_es: Cuando una ACL extendida se utiliza para hacer coincidir prefijos de enrutamiento en lugar de paquetes, la forma en que se interpretan los campos de origen y destino puede variar según se aplique a un IGP o a BGP, por lo que la misma ACL no necesariamente produce el mismo resultado en ambos casos.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Given the prefix-list entry "permit 10.168.0.0/13 ge 24", which two prefixes does it match? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation_es: La entrada permit 10.168.0.0/13 ge 24 exige que el prefijo esté contenido dentro del rango 10.168.0.0/13 (10.168.0.0–10.175.255.255) y que su longitud de máscara sea de 24 bits o más. El prefijo base /13 queda excluido porque su longitud (13) es menor que el mínimo exigido (24), y 10.104.0.0/24 queda excluido porque no pertenece al rango de red indicado.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: Which regular expression correctly matches a BGP route whose AS_Path shows that it originated in AS 300 (that is, AS 300 is the last, originating ASN in the path)?
questions.explanation_es: En las expresiones regulares de BGP, el símbolo $ representa el final de la cadena AS_Path, es decir, el AS de origen (el primero en originar el prefijo). Por lo tanto, _300$ coincide con rutas cuyo AS de origen es el 300. El símbolo ^, en cambio, representa el inicio de la cadena, es decir, el AS más reciente en el trayecto.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: If a permit clause in a route map contains no match statements at all, what happens to routes evaluated against that clause?
