questions.question: Which of the following is generally NOT cited as an advantage of Python 3.x when compared with Python 2.x?

options.A: Broader support on newer Cisco platforms
options.B: Simpler syntax that is easier to learn
options.C: A larger base of legacy third-party libraries built up over time
options.D: Compatibility with tools such as virtualenv

questions.explanation_es: Durante mucho tiempo, Python 2.x contó con una base de bibliotecas de terceros más madura y extensa acumulada a lo largo de los años, mientras que Python 3.x se destacaba por su sintaxis más simple, su mejor soporte en plataformas nuevas y su compatibilidad con herramientas como virtualenv.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: Which command is used to enable Guest Shell so that the Python interpreter can be used on a Cisco IOS XE device?

options.A: iox enable
options.B: guestshell enable
options.C: guestshell run python
options.D: guestshell run

questions.explanation_es: El comando guestshell enable habilita el contenedor Guest Shell en un dispositivo Cisco IOS XE, lo que permite ejecutar el intérprete de Python dentro de ese entorno.

questions.name: Python básico
questions.question: True or false: In Python's try/except construct, the else clause defines a block of code that runs only if no exception was raised in the try block.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.explanation_es: La cláusula else en el manejo de excepciones de Python define un bloque de código que se ejecuta únicamente si no se produjo ningún error dentro del bloque try.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Which three protocols form the core of the model-driven programmability stack used to interact with network device data models?

options.A: FTP, TFTP, and SCP
options.B: BGP, OSPF, and EIGRP
options.C: SNMP, Telnet, and SSH
options.D: NETCONF, RESTCONF, and gRPC

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF, RESTCONF y gRPC son los tres protocolos principales de la pila de programabilidad basada en modelos, utilizados para transportar datos de configuración y de estado hacia y desde los modelos de datos del dispositivo.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Between XML and JSON, which data format is generally considered quicker and easier for humans to write by hand?

options.A: Neither format is meant to be written by hand
options.B: Both are equally easy to write
options.C: JSON
options.D: XML

questions.explanation_es: JSON se considera más rápido y sencillo de escribir a mano que XML, ya que su sintaxis es más compacta y tiene menos elementos repetitivos, como las etiquetas de apertura y cierre.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: Within the model-driven programmability stack, which layer is responsible for defining the syntax, semantics, and constraints of the data being exchanged?

options.A: Data models
options.B: Transport layer
options.C: Encoding layer
options.D: Protocol layer

questions.explanation_es: Los modelos de datos son la base de las APIs: definen la sintaxis, la semántica y las restricciones asociadas con su uso, independientemente del protocolo de transporte o del formato de codificación empleado.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: True or false: JSON is generally simpler and more compact than XML, which makes it a good fit for object-oriented systems.

options.A: False
options.B: True

questions.explanation_es: JSON es más simple y compacto que XML, resulta más fácil de analizar gracias a esa simplicidad, y se adapta mejor a los sistemas orientados a objetos.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: What does the very first line of a well-formed XML document typically represent?

options.A: A comment block
options.B: The XML declaration
options.C: A child element
options.D: The root element

questions.explanation_es: La primera línea de un documento XML es la declaración XML, que especifica la versión de XML utilizada, por ejemplo 1.0, y la codificación de caracteres empleada, por ejemplo ISO-8859-1.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: True or false: Similar to XML, a JSON document uses closing end tags to mark the end of each element.

options.A: False
options.B: True

questions.explanation_es: A diferencia de XML, JSON es jerárquico y contiene valores anidados, pero no utiliza etiquetas de cierre; los elementos se delimitan con llaves, corchetes y comas en lugar de etiquetas.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: In JSON syntax, which character is used to separate one key/value pair from the next within an object?

options.A: Pipe
options.B: Semicolon
options.C: Comma
options.D: Colon

questions.explanation_es: La coma se utiliza para separar cada par clave/valor dentro de un objeto JSON, mientras que los dos puntos separan la clave de su valor correspondiente dentro del mismo par.

questions.name: JSON
questions.question: True or false: Omitting a required comma between key/value pairs in a JSON document will cause a parsing error.

options.A: False
options.B: True

questions.explanation_es: JSON exige una sintaxis estricta; la ausencia de una coma separadora entre pares clave/valor produce un error al analizar el documento en la aplicación.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which set of protocols does YANG rely on to actually transport configuration and operational data to and from a device?

options.A: BGP only
options.B: NETCONF, RESTCONF, and gRPC
options.C: SNMP and Syslog
options.D: HTTP and FTP

questions.explanation_es: YANG en sí mismo es solo un lenguaje de modelado; se apoya en protocolos como NETCONF, RESTCONF y gRPC para transportar realmente los datos de configuración y de estado operativo hacia y desde el dispositivo.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which YANG node type represents a sequence of simple leaf values of the same type, without any additional internal structure?

options.A: Container node
options.B: Leaf node
options.C: Leaf-list node
options.D: List node

questions.explanation_es: El nodo leaf-list contiene una secuencia de valores simples del mismo tipo, a diferencia del nodo leaf, que almacena un único valor.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Why is SNMP generally not considered one of the modern data-model components of the network programmability stack, unlike YANG?

options.A: Because it only supports read operations and no writes at all
options.B: Because it does not distinguish between configuration data and operational (state) data
options.C: Because it cannot operate over an IP network
options.D: Because it requires a proprietary Cisco-only agent

questions.explanation_es: SNMP no distingue claramente entre datos de configuración y datos operativos, lo cual es una de las razones por las que no se lo considera un modelo de datos moderno dentro del enfoque programático de red, a diferencia de YANG.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: YANG models that are vendor-neutral and maintained by bodies such as the IETF or the OpenConfig working group are best classified as which type of model?

options.A: Industry standard-based (common) models
options.B: Notification models
options.C: Deviation models
options.D: Native (vendor-specific) models

questions.explanation_es: Los modelos estándar de la industria, o comunes, son independientes del proveedor y de la plataforma, y provienen de grupos de trabajo como el IETF y OpenConfig, a diferencia de los modelos nativos, que son específicos de cada fabricante.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: Which YANG node type defines a sequence of entries, each of which is uniquely identified by one or more key leaves?

options.A: List node
options.B: Leaf-list node
options.C: Container node
options.D: Leaf node

questions.explanation_es: El nodo list define una secuencia de entradas, cada una identificada de forma única mediante una o más hojas clave, lo que permite representar tablas o colecciones de elementos estructurados.

questions.name: YANG
questions.question: True or false: NETCONF can serve as the transport medium that carries YANG-modeled configuration and operational data between a network device and a management application.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.explanation_es: NETCONF puede actuar como el medio de transporte que mueve los datos de configuración y operativos modelados con YANG entre un dispositivo de red y una aplicación de gestión.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: What type of API allows you to build bidirectional integrations that exchange contextual information between Cisco DNA Center (Catalyst Center) and external third-party systems?

options.A: REST-based integration adapter APIs
options.B: SNMP trap listeners
options.C: Syslog forwarding APIs
options.D: CLI screen-scraping scripts

questions.explanation_es: Las APIs de adaptador de integración basadas en REST permiten construir interfaces bidireccionales que intercambian información contextual entre Cisco DNA Center (Catalyst Center) y sistemas externos de terceros.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which Cisco DNA Center capability is responsible for managing software images and the associated image update repository across network devices?

options.A: Network Hierarchy
options.B: Path Trace
options.C: Command Runner
options.D: Software Image Management (SWIM)

questions.explanation_es: Software Image Management, o SWIM, es la funcionalidad de Cisco DNA Center encargada de administrar las imágenes de software y el repositorio de actualizaciones de los dispositivos de red.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: True or false: Cisco DNA Center supports integrating with third-party ecosystem domains such as IT Service Management (ITSM) and IP Address Management (IPAM).

options.A: False
options.B: True

questions.explanation_es: Cisco DNA Center permite la integración con diversos dominios del ecosistema de terceros, como la gestión de servicios de TI (ITSM) y la gestión de direcciones IP (IPAM), además de la generación de reportes.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the typical subdomains found under the 'Know Your Network' request path in the Cisco DNA Center API?

options.A: Environment
options.B: Devices
options.C: Clients
options.D: Sites

questions.explanation_es: Environment no es uno de los subdominios típicos de la ruta Know Your Network en la API de Cisco DNA Center; entre los subdominios habituales se encuentran Devices, Clients y Sites.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which of the following is a common use case for the Cisco vManage API?

options.A: Attaching a configuration template to a device
options.B: Issuing digital certificates for end-user laptops
options.C: Compiling router firmware from source code
options.D: Replacing the physical power supply of a switch

questions.explanation_es: Adjuntar una plantilla de configuración a un dispositivo es un caso de uso habitual de la API de Cisco vManage, junto con el monitoreo del estado de los dispositivos y la consulta y agregación de estadísticas.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: True or false: The RESTful Cisco DNA Center API lets you use standard HTTP verbs such as GET, PUT, POST, and DELETE, combined with JSON, to discover and control the network.

options.A: False
options.B: True

questions.explanation_es: La API RESTful de Cisco DNA Center permite utilizar los verbos HTTP estándar GET, PUT, POST y DELETE junto con la sintaxis JSON para descubrir y controlar la red.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: Which HTTP method is used to submit a username and password when authenticating to the Cisco DNA Center or vManage REST API?

options.A: PUT
options.B: GET
options.C: DELETE
options.D: POST

questions.explanation_es: El método HTTP POST se utiliza para enviar el nombre de usuario y la contraseña al autenticarse contra la API REST de Cisco DNA Center o vManage.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: Which HTTP status code returned by Cisco DNA Center indicates that the requested resource could not be found?
questions.explanation_es: El código de estado HTTP 404 indica que el recurso solicitado no fue encontrado en el servidor de Cisco DNA Center.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: True or false: When an error is caused by a problem on the server side, a REST API typically returns a status code in the 5xx range.

options.A: False
options.B: True

questions.explanation_es: Cuando el error se origina en el servidor, la API REST normalmente devuelve un código de estado en el rango 5xx, indicando que el servidor no pudo completar una solicitud aparentemente válida.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: Which HTTP status code should you expect to receive after a successful authentication attempt against the Cisco vManage or DNA Center API?
questions.explanation_es: Una autenticación exitosa contra la API de Cisco vManage o DNA Center debería devolver un código de estado 200 (OK), confirmando que la solicitud se procesó correctamente.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: True or false: An HTTP 202 status code means the server accepted the request but still needs to perform additional processing before it is fully completed.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.explanation_es: El código HTTP 202 (Accepted) significa que el servidor aceptó la solicitud correctamente, pero todavía necesita realizar acciones adicionales para completarla.

questions.name: Códigos de respuesta REST API
questions.question: True or false: An HTTP 201 status code means that the server was unable to fulfill the request because it was unavailable.

options.A: False
options.B: True

questions.explanation_es: El código HTTP 201 indica que un recurso fue creado exitosamente, no que el servidor esté no disponible; ese significado corresponde al código 503 (Service Unavailable).

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which component of the EEM architecture is responsible for determining when a defined EEM event has actually occurred?

options.A: Tcl interpreter
options.B: Policy director
options.C: Event detectors
options.D: Applet compiler

questions.explanation_es: Los detectores de eventos son el componente de la arquitectura de EEM encargado de determinar cuándo ha ocurrido un evento definido, para luego disparar la política o el applet correspondiente.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which command lets you observe, on the CLI, the actions being executed while an EEM applet is running?

options.A: debug event manager action cli
options.B: show event manager policy active
options.C: debug ip eem
options.D: event manager run applet-name

questions.explanation_es: El comando debug event manager action cli permite visualizar en la CLI las acciones que se están ejecutando mientras corre un applet de EEM.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM architecture component acts as the bridge between the Cisco IOS subsystems used by event detectors and the policies that respond to them?

options.A: EEM applet
options.B: EEM server
options.C: Tcl script
options.D: EEM detector

questions.explanation_es: El servidor de EEM actúa como puente entre los subsistemas de Cisco IOS utilizados por los detectores de eventos y las políticas que responden a dichos eventos.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which EEM event detector generates an event specifically when an administrator manually triggers a policy using the 'event manager run' CLI command?

options.A: None event detector
options.B: Application event detector
options.C: CLI event detector
options.D: Syslog event detector

questions.explanation_es: El detector de eventos none genera un evento cuando el comando event manager run se ejecuta manualmente en la CLI para disparar una política de EEM.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: True or false: An EEM applet can be used to provide a temporary automated workaround for a problem while its root cause is still being investigated.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.explanation_es: Un applet de EEM puede servir como una solución temporal automatizada mientras se investiga la causa raíz de un problema, por ejemplo reiniciando automáticamente una interfaz cuando se detecta una condición intermitente.

questions.name: EEM applets
questions.question: Which command manually triggers an EEM applet to run immediately from the CLI?

options.A: event manager action cli
options.B: event none applet-name
options.C: more flash:applet-name
options.D: event manager run applet-name

questions.explanation_es: El comando event manager run applet-name se utiliza para ejecutar manualmente un applet de EEM desde la línea de comandos.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: What are the three functions represented by the 'AAA' acronym in network access control, and what does each generally address?

options.A: AAA functions require RADIUS and TACACS+ to both be configured simultaneously on every device, since each protocol is understood to independently implement only one or two of the three AAA functions rather than all three together
options.B: AAA refers to three physical RF components (Antenna, Amplifier, Attenuator) used during wireless site surveys to characterize signal propagation, a naming coincidence with no actual relationship to authentication, authorization, or accounting of network access
options.C: Authentication and Accounting are often collapsed into a single verification step in casual usage, since both occur at session establishment, while Authorization is treated as the sole distinct function because it is the only one revisited mid-session when a user's permitted actions actually change
options.D: Authentication confirms a user's identity via credentials, Authorization determines what that authenticated user is permitted to do, and Accounting records what the user actually did, for auditing or billing purposes — three related but distinct functions

questions.explanation_es: Authentication (verificar quién es un usuario, típicamente vía credenciales), Authorization (determinar qué está permitido hacer ese usuario ya autenticado), y Accounting (registrar qué hizo realmente el usuario, para auditoría/facturación) — tres funciones relacionadas pero distintas que juntas gobiernan y registran el acceso a recursos de red.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: How does CoPP typically classify and treat different types of traffic destined to the control plane?

options.A: It classifies traffic into different classes (such as routing protocol traffic, normal management traffic, and undesirable/malicious traffic) and applies a different action (permit, rate-limit, or drop) to each class
options.B: It only takes effect once the CPU is already saturated, functioning purely as an after-the-fact cleanup mechanism that reactively drops queued packets rather than a proactively applied classification policy
options.C: It applies rate limits based mainly on the ingress physical interface a packet arrived on, since class-map matching for CoPP is understood to classify traffic primarily by interface rather than by the packet's actual protocol type or destination port
options.D: It relies solely on the physical ingress interface to decide how to treat control-plane-destined traffic, without inspecting any Layer 3/4 header fields, since CoPP class-maps are believed to only support interface-based matching

questions.explanation_es: CoPP típicamente clasifica el tráfico destinado al plano de control en distintas clases (por ejemplo, tráfico crítico como protocolos de enrutamiento, tráfico de gestión normal, y tráfico indeseable o potencialmente malicioso), aplicando una política diferenciada a cada clase (permitir, limitar la tasa, o descartar), en lugar de tratar todo el tráfico hacia la CPU de forma idéntica.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What is the general purpose of a threat intelligence feed in a network security architecture?

options.A: It is consumed primarily by SIEM platforms to enrich historical log entries with contextual metadata after an event has already occurred, rather than being used by firewalls or IPS devices for real-time detection decisions
options.B: It replaces the need for any firewall or IPS by independently blocking traffic at the network edge through its own built-in enforcement engine, since feeds are sometimes assumed to include active inline blocking rather than being consumed by separate tools
options.C: It provides continuously updated information about known indicators of compromise (IoCs), malicious IPs/domains, and emerging threats, which security tools use to improve detection accuracy
options.D: It focuses on point-in-time compliance audit reports rather than active threat indicators, making it primarily a documentation tool auditors reference annually rather than a continuously updated operational input

questions.explanation_es: Un feed de inteligencia de amenazas provee información continuamente actualizada sobre indicadores de compromiso conocidos (IoCs), direcciones IP/dominios maliciosos y amenazas emergentes, que las herramientas de seguridad (firewalls, IPS, etc.) utilizan para mejorar la precisión de la detección frente a amenazas actuales.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What is the core idea behind the 'zero trust' security model?

options.A: Zero trust grants full trust to a device for the remainder of its session once it has passed an initial authentication check when joining the network, with no further verification of its identity, patch level, or behavior afterward
options.B: Zero trust primarily focuses on strengthening perimeter firewall rules at the network edge, so that once a device or user has passed that perimeter check, subsequent access requests between internal hosts are evaluated less strictly by comparison
options.C: No user, device, or system should be automatically trusted based solely on network location; every access request should be continuously verified regardless of whether it originates inside or outside the traditional network perimeter
options.D: Zero trust removes the need for authentication entirely, since access decisions are made purely on the sensitivity of the data being requested rather than on verifying who or what is making the request

questions.explanation_es: El modelo de zero trust (confianza cero) parte de la idea de que ningún usuario, dispositivo o sistema debe confiarse automáticamente solo por estar dentro del perímetro tradicional de la red; cada solicitud de acceso debe verificarse de forma continua, sin importar si el origen es interno o externo, reduciendo el riesgo de movimiento lateral tras una brecha.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: Why does a thorough Cisco ISE posture assessment (checking things like antivirus status or specific patches) typically require a persistent agent (such as the AnyConnect ISE Posture module) installed on the endpoint, rather than a purely agentless check?

options.A: The agent's role is limited to displaying a corporate splash screen at login, with actual compliance data still collected entirely from network-level probes that inspect DHCP fingerprints and open ports
options.B: ISE posture assessment is defined as an agentless-only capability, so any endpoint-side software used alongside it falls outside the posture workflow itself and is treated as a separate, unrelated endpoint tool
options.C: A persistent agent can inspect detailed, OS-level endpoint state (like specific installed software versions or running processes) that isn't visible from the network alone, and can also re-check compliance on an ongoing basis
options.D: Agentless network probes can already enumerate installed software versions and running processes with the same fidelity as an installed agent, since that information is exposed via standard SNMP polling most endpoints expose by default

questions.explanation_es: Un agente persistente puede inspeccionar el estado del endpoint a nivel de SO (como versiones específicas de software instalado o procesos corriendo) que no es visible solo desde la red, y también puede reverificar el cumplimiento de forma continua.

questions.name: Seguridad de endpoint (NAC/ISE)
questions.question: What is the difference between 'closed mode' and 'monitor mode' when deploying 802.1X on a switch port, particularly during an initial rollout?

options.A: Monitor mode blocks all non-EAP traffic exactly like closed mode, differing only in which syslog severity level is used for its log messages, so the two modes are functionally identical from the connected endpoint's perspective
options.B: Closed mode is intended only for wireless access points, while monitor mode is the default (and only) behavior available on wired switch ports, since enforcement modes are assumed to be tied to the media type rather than independently configurable
options.C: In closed mode, only EAP/802.1X traffic is allowed until authentication succeeds, with all other traffic blocked; in monitor mode, all traffic is allowed to pass regardless of authentication outcome, while the switch still logs what the authentication result would have been, letting administrators validate policy before enabling full enforcement
options.D: Monitor mode actively drops authentication failures the same way closed mode does, but additionally quarantines the failing device's port into a remediation VLAN rather than simply logging what the decision would have been

questions.explanation_es: En closed mode, solo se permite tráfico EAP/802.1X hasta que la autenticación tenga éxito, con todo el demás tráfico bloqueado, dando aplicación completa; monitor mode permite pasar todo el tráfico sin importar el resultado de autenticación mientras sigue registrando cuál habría sido ese resultado, permitiendo que un administrador observe y valide qué pasaría bajo aplicación completa antes de realmente activar el comportamiento de bloqueo de tráfico del closed mode, reduciendo el riesgo de bloquear accidentalmente dispositivos legítimos durante el despliegue inicial.

questions.name: Threat defense
questions.question: What is the primary advantage of a Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) compared to a traditional stateful firewall?

options.A: NGFW abandons stateful connection tracking in favor of a simpler, fully stateless packet-filtering model to reduce CPU load, trading connection-awareness for raw throughput
options.B: NGFW is designed specifically for wireless LAN controllers and has no role in wired perimeter security, since 'next-generation' in this context is sometimes read as referring to newer wireless standards rather than inspection depth
options.C: NGFW forwards traffic based purely on source/destination IP and port, delegating all application-layer inspection to a separate proxy appliance, since it is assumed to only extend a traditional firewall's management interface rather than its inspection depth
options.D: NGFW adds capabilities like application awareness (identifying traffic by the actual application generating it, not just port number) and integrated intrusion prevention on top of traditional stateful filtering, consolidating functions that previously required separate appliances

questions.explanation_es: Un NGFW mantiene la inspección con estado tradicional pero suma capacidades como reconocimiento de aplicaciones (más allá del puerto) y prevención de intrusiones (IPS) integrada, no solo filtrado por IP/puerto.

questions.name: Diagnóstico (debug/traceroute/ping/SNMP/syslog)
questions.question: What information does the 'ping' command's summary output (packet loss percentage, round-trip min/avg/max times) help an engineer quickly assess about a path to a destination?

options.A: Packet loss percentage gives a quick indication of basic reachability/reliability issues along the path, while the round-trip time statistics give a rough sense of latency and its variability, together providing a fast first-pass health check before diving into more detailed tools like traceroute
options.B: Ping reports a binary reachable/unreachable result only, with loss percentage and timing figures added purely for cosmetic display purposes rather than any statistically meaningful measurement of the path's health
options.C: Only the destination's MAC address is reported, since ping is assumed to operate purely at Layer 2 with no visibility into Layer 3 round-trip timing, despite ICMP echo actually running over IP rather than a MAC-only exchange
options.D: Round-trip time statistics stay constant regardless of path congestion, since ICMP echo packets are believed to always be queued ahead of other traffic by every intermediate router, immunizing them from delay variation

questions.explanation_es: El porcentaje de pérdida de paquetes da una indicación rápida de problemas básicos de alcanzabilidad/confiabilidad a lo largo del camino, mientras que las estadísticas de tiempo de ida y vuelta dan una idea aproximada de la latencia y su variabilidad, juntas ofreciendo un chequeo de salud rápido de primera pasada antes de profundizar con herramientas más detalladas como traceroute o capturas de paquetes.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: Why is CoPP generally described as protecting the 'control plane' specifically, as opposed to protecting the 'data plane' of a router or switch?

options.A: The control plane and data plane are processed by the same forwarding ASIC on modern platforms, so CoPP's rate-limiting is understood to be applied at the ASIC's queue scheduling stage rather than specifically protecting the CPU's own processing capacity
options.B: The data plane (forwarding traffic through the device from one interface to another) is typically handled by dedicated, high-speed forwarding hardware (ASICs) that can handle very high traffic volumes, whereas the control plane (the device's own CPU, handling routing protocol processing, SSH sessions, and SNMP) has comparatively limited processing capacity and is much more vulnerable to being overwhelmed
options.C: CoPP's policies apply only to traffic already forwarded through the ASIC, filtering it a second time after it leaves the switch, rather than traffic destined to the CPU itself, reversing which plane CoPP is actually designed to shield
options.D: CoPP throttles the ASIC-based forwarding hardware directly, since the data plane is assumed to be the more CPU-limited of the two planes, when in fact the ASIC's dedicated forwarding pipeline is exactly what lets it handle much higher volumes than the CPU This view also overlooks that ASIC-based forwarding pipelines are purpose-built silicon specifically engineered to sustain line-rate throughput well beyond what a general-purpose CPU handling routing protocol and management sessions could ever process.

questions.explanation_es: El plano de datos (reenviar tráfico a través del dispositivo de una interfaz a otra) típicamente lo maneja hardware de reenvío dedicado y de alta velocidad (ASICs) que puede manejar volúmenes de tráfico muy altos, mientras que el plano de control (la propia CPU del dispositivo, manejando cosas como procesamiento de protocolos de enrutamiento, sesiones SSH, y SNMP) tiene capacidad de procesamiento comparativamente limitada y es mucho más vulnerable a ser saturado por tráfico excesivo destinado a la propia CPU — exactamente el recurso que CoPP está diseñado para proteger.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In network design, what does a 'modular' or 'building block' approach (e.g., separate blocks for campus, data center, WAN edge) primarily achieve?

options.A: It isolates failures and complexity within each functional block, and allows each block to be scaled, upgraded, or troubleshot independently without redesigning the entire network
options.B: It guarantees that no additional hardware will ever need to be purchased as the network grows, since each block is assumed to scale purely through software licensing changes rather than requiring any physical port or chassis capacity increase
options.C: It requires every block to share a single, identical IP addressing scheme, trading design flexibility for a simpler global summarization, rather than allowing each block its own addressing plan suited to its own scale
options.D: It removes the need for any routing between the different blocks, since each block is assumed to be entirely self-contained, when in fact inter-block routing is exactly what ties the modular design together into one network

questions.explanation_es: El enfoque modular (por bloques funcionales) contiene las fallas y la complejidad dentro de cada bloque (campus, data center, WAN, etc.), permitiendo escalar, actualizar o diagnosticar cada uno de forma independiente sin tener que rediseñar toda la red — un principio central del diseño jerárquico de Cisco.

questions.name: vSwitch/OVS
questions.question: How does a vSwitch typically learn which VM (virtual port) is associated with a given source MAC address?

options.A: Only through static configuration, requiring an administrator to manually bind every VM's MAC address to a specific virtual port before it can pass any traffic, with no dynamic learning capability available
options.B: By flooding every frame to every virtual port permanently, since vSwitches are assumed to lack any MAC address table of their own, unlike a physical switch's hardware-based CAM table
options.C: By querying the hypervisor's DNS resolver service for a MAC-to-port mapping record before forwarding each frame, treating MAC learning as a name-resolution lookup rather than a data-plane observation
options.D: Dynamically, similar to a physical switch, by examining the source MAC address of frames received from each virtual port and recording that mapping in its own MAC address table

questions.explanation_es: Al igual que un switch físico, el vSwitch aprende dinámicamente qué puerto virtual corresponde a cada dirección MAC observando las tramas recibidas desde cada puerto y registrando la MAC de origen.

questions.name: Catalyst Center
questions.question: What is the general purpose of Catalyst Center's 'Design' workflow area, as one of the platform's core functional workflows?

options.A: It focuses mainly on defining wireless SSIDs and RF profiles, while site hierarchy and IP address pool planning are instead handled within the separate Provision workflow area rather than within Design itself
options.B: It lets an administrator define the network's intended hierarchy (sites, buildings, floors), global settings (like IP address pools, SSIDs, and common device credentials), and templates, establishing the blueprint that later workflows like Policy and Provision build upon
options.C: It is primarily used to generate topology diagrams and documentation of the network's existing site hierarchy for reporting purposes, after that hierarchy and its IP address pools have already been defined elsewhere in the platform
options.D: It becomes usable only after every device has already been fully provisioned, functioning as a retrospective reporting view rather than an upfront planning tool, overlooking Design's actual role in defining pools and templates beforehand

questions.explanation_es: El flujo de trabajo Design le permite a un administrador definir la jerarquía prevista de la red (sitios, edificios, pisos), ajustes globales (como pools de direcciones IP, SSIDs, y credenciales comunes de dispositivos), y plantillas, esencialmente estableciendo el plano sobre el cual construyen luego otros flujos de trabajo (como Policy y Provision) al desplegar configuración real a los dispositivos.

questions.name: Alta disponibilidad (SSO/FHRP)
questions.question: In terms of standardization, which of these statements about VRRP is correct?

options.A: VRRP originated as an IEEE 802.1Q extension governing trunk negotiation, later informally repurposed by some vendors for gateway redundancy despite never having been formally adopted for that purpose by the IEEE
options.B: VRRP was defined by an IETF RFC (originally RFC 2338, later RFC 3768 and RFC 5798) specifically to provide an open, multi-vendor alternative to Cisco's proprietary HSRP
options.C: VRRP was published only as an internal vendor whitepaper that other manufacturers later reverse-engineered without any accompanying RFC ever being drafted or ratified by the IETF
options.D: VRRP remains a Cisco-only proprietary mechanism with no formal IETF documentation, similar to how GLBP is not published as an open standard, making it functionally indistinguishable from HSRP in terms of standardization

questions.explanation_es: VRRP fue definido por el IETF (originalmente RFC 2338, luego RFC 3768 y RFC 5798) específicamente para ofrecer una alternativa abierta y multi-vendor al HSRP propietario de Cisco, permitiendo interoperabilidad de redundancia de gateway entre equipos de distintos fabricantes.

questions.name: NTP/PTP
questions.question: In what type of environment or use case is PTP's sub-microsecond time synchronization accuracy typically required, as opposed to NTP's millisecond-level accuracy being sufficient?

options.A: PTP's hardware-timestamping requirement makes it unsuitable for any latency-sensitive application, restricting industrial motion control and financial trading systems to NTP-only environments instead of PTP
options.B: Environments such as financial trading platforms (which may have regulatory requirements for precise transaction timestamping), industrial automation/motion control systems, and telecommunications synchronization commonly require PTP's much tighter accuracy, whereas typical enterprise IT log correlation is usually well served by NTP
options.C: General enterprise log correlation typically demands the same sub-microsecond precision as financial trading platforms, making PTP the default choice for ordinary IT infrastructure rather than a specialized tool for latency-critical industries This overlooks that ordinary log correlation only needs timestamps consistent to within a second or two to reconstruct an accurate sequence of events across devices, far looser than PTP's sub-microsecond guarantee.
options.D: PTP and NTP provide numerically identical accuracy specifications, so the choice between them is driven only by licensing cost rather than any actual technical difference in achievable synchronization precision

questions.explanation_es: Entornos como plataformas de trading financiero (que pueden tener requisitos regulatorios de marcado de tiempo preciso de transacciones), sistemas de automatización industrial/control de movimiento, sincronización de telecomunicaciones (por ejemplo, para ciertos estándares de backhaul celular), y algunas aplicaciones científicas/de medición suelen requerir la precisión mucho más ajustada de PTP, mientras que la correlación de logs de TI empresarial típica y las aplicaciones de negocio generales suelen estar bien servidas por la precisión de milisegundos de NTP.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: In Cisco NAT terminology, what does the 'inside global' address specifically represent?

options.A: The translated (typically public/routable) address of an inside host as it appears to devices on the outside network, distinguishing it from 'inside local' (the real, often private, address of that same host as seen on the inside network)
options.B: The physical MAC address burned into the NAT router's inside-facing interface, unrelated to any Layer 3 address translation performed by NAT itself
options.C: A temporary DHCP lease address assigned only during the NAT translation's negotiation phase, discarded once the session table entry is built and no longer relevant to ongoing translated traffic
options.D: The address an inside host uses to refer to a remote outside host, functionally identical to that outside host's own 'outside local' address, collapsing two normally distinct NAT terms into one This conflates two terms that NAT terminology keeps deliberately separate specifically to describe address translation applied to each side of a connection independently.

questions.explanation_es: 'Inside global' representa la dirección traducida (típicamente pública/enrutable) de un host interno tal como la ve un dispositivo en la red externa, distinguiéndose de 'inside local' (la dirección real, a menudo privada, de ese mismo host tal como se ve en la red interna).

questions.name: Policy-based routing
questions.question: Why might an organization use PBR to route certain traffic (e.g., a specific application or a guest subnet) through a security appliance or specific inspection path, while allowing other traffic to follow the normal destination-based routing table?

options.A: PBR allows the organization to selectively force only the traffic matching specific criteria (like a source subnet or application signature) through a particular next hop (such as a firewall/IPS appliance) for mandatory inspection, without redesigning the entire network's destination-based routing
options.B: PBR's route-map is evaluated on the outbound interface after the forwarding decision has already been made by CEF, so it can remark or rate-limit the packet but cannot actually change which next hop receives it
options.C: PBR route-maps can only match on destination prefix, the same criteria the standard routing table already uses, so it is assumed to offer no way to isolate a specific source subnet or application from the rest of the traffic This overlooks that PBR route-maps can reference extended ACLs matching on source address, destination address, protocol, and port simultaneously, not merely the destination prefix a routing table lookup already considers.
options.D: Redirecting only a subset of traffic through an inspection appliance requires a dedicated physical cable run per flow, a requirement assumed to exist because PBR itself is believed to have no software-based redirection mechanism

questions.explanation_es: PBR le permite a la organización forzar selectivamente solo el tráfico que coincide con criterios específicos (como una subred origen o una firma de aplicación) a través de un next-hop en particular (como un firewall/IPS) para inspección obligatoria, sin necesitar rediseñar todo el enrutamiento basado en destino de la red solo para insertar ese punto de inspección para una categoría de tráfico.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What IP address range is reserved for IPv4 multicast addressing, and what does this range represent within the broader IPv4 address space?

options.A: 224.0.0.0 through 239.255.255.255 (Class D address space) is reserved for IPv4 multicast group addresses, representing a portion of the address space set aside specifically for one-to-many/many-to-many multicast communication rather than traditional unicast host addressing
options.B: Only the single address 255.255.255.255 is used for multicast group communication, with no broader range of addresses available for distinguishing between different multicast groups
options.C: The same RFC 1918 private ranges used for unicast addressing double as the multicast range, with no separate block set aside for group communication distinct from ordinary private host addressing This overlooks that RFC 1918 defines private unicast ranges entirely separate from the Class D space IANA carved out specifically for multicast group addressing.
options.D: Multicast addressing in IPv4 was deprecated in favor of IGMP-only signaling, so no dedicated address range remains reserved for it today, with IGMP alone assumed to carry group membership without any Class D address space

questions.explanation_es: El rango 224.0.0.0 a 239.255.255.255 (espacio de direcciones Clase D) está reservado para direcciones de grupo multicast IPv4, representando una porción del espacio de direcciones apartada específicamente para comunicación multicast uno-a-muchos/muchos-a-muchos en lugar de direccionamiento de host unicast tradicional.

questions.name: NAT/PAT
questions.question: What does the 'outside local' address represent in Cisco NAT terminology, and in what scenario does it differ from the 'outside global' address of the same outside host?

options.A: 'Outside local' and 'outside global' always refer to identical values in every NAT deployment, since only inside addresses are ever assumed to be eligible for translation, never the outside host's own address
options.B: 'Outside local' is how an outside host's address appears from the inside network's perspective, which differs from 'outside global' (the outside host's real address as seen from the outside network itself) specifically in scenarios where the outside address is also being translated, rather than the more common case where only the inside address is translated
options.C: 'Outside local' exists only in IPv6 NAT66 deployments, with no equivalent concept defined anywhere in IPv4 NAT terminology, since IPv4 NAT is assumed to only distinguish inside local/global without any outside-facing counterpart This misreads NAT terminology as an IPv6-specific concept, when in fact 'outside local' and 'outside global' are both classic IPv4 NAT terms describing how an outside host's address is perceived from each side of the translation.
options.D: 'Outside local' identifies a Layer 4 port number reserved for the NAT translation table entry, unrelated to IP address translation itself and closer in concept to a PAT port assignment

questions.explanation_es: 'Outside local' es cómo se ve la dirección de un host externo desde la perspectiva de la red interna, lo cual difiere de 'outside global' (la dirección real del host externo tal como se ve desde la propia red externa) específicamente en escenarios donde la dirección externa también se está traduciendo (por ejemplo, en algunos diseños de NAT bidireccional o de direcciones superpuestas), en lugar del caso más común donde solo se traduce la dirección interna.

questions.name: CoPP
questions.question: Which of the following best describes how CoPP determines whether traffic is allowed to reach a router's control plane?

options.A: It is enabled by default on all Cisco platforms and requires no configuration
options.B: It applies a policy-map, attached to the control-plane interface, that classifies and rate-limits or drops traffic destined to the route processor's CPU
options.C: It filters traffic using a standard ACL applied inbound on every physical interface
options.D: It relies on the forwarding ASIC to silently drop any packet addressed to the router's own IP address

questions.explanation_es: CoPP se implementa aplicando un policy-map a la interfaz virtual control-plane, que clasifica el tráfico destinado a la CPU del route processor y le aplica una acción (permitir, limitar la tasa, o descartar) según la clase a la que pertenezca.

questions.name: AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS)
questions.question: In a TACACS+ deployment, what does 'authorization' typically control that plain authentication does not?

options.A: How long the TCP session to the TACACS+ server stays open
options.B: Whether a user's identity is verified against a username and password
options.C: Which encryption algorithm is used to protect the TACACS+ packet body
options.D: Which specific commands or services an already-authenticated user is permitted to use

questions.explanation_es: La autenticación solo verifica la identidad del usuario; la autorización es un paso posterior y separado que determina qué comandos o servicios específicos puede usar ese usuario ya autenticado.

questions.name: NGFW/FMC/AVC
questions.question: In Cisco Firepower/FTD, what is the primary role of Application Visibility and Control (AVC)?

options.A: Encrypting all traffic that passes through the firewall using TLS 1.3
options.B: Identifying and classifying traffic by the actual application generating it, regardless of port number, so policy can be applied based on that application
options.C: Automatically patching vulnerable applications running on protected hosts
options.D: Load-balancing traffic across multiple FTD appliances in a cluster

questions.explanation_es: AVC identifica y clasifica el tráfico según la aplicación real que lo genera, independientemente del número de puerto, permitiendo aplicar políticas basadas en esa aplicación en lugar de solo en IP/puerto.

questions.name: ACLs
questions.question: Which type of ACL can filter traffic based on source IP, destination IP, protocol, and Layer 4 port number in a single statement?

options.A: Reflexive ACL only
options.B: VLAN ACL only
options.C: Standard ACL
options.D: Extended ACL

questions.explanation_es: Una ACL extendida puede filtrar por dirección IP origen, dirección IP destino, protocolo y puerto de Capa 4 en una sola sentencia; una ACL estándar solo puede filtrar por dirección IP origen.

questions.name: Seguridad de REST API
questions.question: What is the main purpose of using OAuth 2.0 access tokens with a short expiration time?

options.A: To allow a single token to authenticate an unlimited number of different users
options.B: To eliminate the need for HTTPS on API endpoints
options.C: To reduce the impact of a leaked token, since it becomes unusable once it expires
options.D: To increase the amount of data that can be transmitted per API call

questions.explanation_es: Un token de acceso con vida corta reduce el impacto si se filtra o es robado, ya que deja de ser utilizable poco después, limitando la ventana de tiempo en la que un atacante podría usarlo.

questions.name: eBGP
questions.question: By default, how many IP hops away can an eBGP neighbor be before the session requires 'ebgp-multihop' to be configured?

options.A: eBGP peers are expected to be directly connected (one IP hop away); reaching a neighbor more than one hop away requires 'ebgp-multihop' to be configured
options.B: eBGP always requires exactly two intermediate hops regardless of configuration
options.C: Any number, since eBGP has no hop-count restriction by default
options.D: eBGP sessions can only be established between loopback interfaces

questions.explanation_es: Por defecto, eBGP espera que los vecinos estén conectados directamente (a un salto IP); para establecer una sesión eBGP hacia un vecino a más de un salto de distancia hace falta configurar 'ebgp-multihop'.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which LACP mode combination will NOT form an EtherChannel bundle?

options.A: Active and active
options.B: Passive and passive
options.C: On and on
options.D: Active and passive

questions.explanation_es: Con passive y passive, ninguno de los dos extremos inicia activamente la negociación LACP, por lo que el canal nunca llega a formarse; al menos un lado debe estar en modo active.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Which IGMP version introduced the source-specific membership reports required by SSM (Source-Specific Multicast)?

options.A: IGMPv3
options.B: IGMPv2
options.C: IGMPv4
options.D: IGMPv1

questions.explanation_es: IGMPv3 introdujo los reportes de membresía con filtrado por fuente (listas include/exclude), una capacidad necesaria para que SSM funcione; no existe una versión IGMPv4.

questions.name: APIs Catalyst Center
questions.question: Which HTTP method is typically used to retrieve a list of devices from the Catalyst Center Intent API?

options.A: DELETE
options.B: PUT
options.C: GET
options.D: POST

questions.explanation_es: GET es el método HTTP estándar para recuperar datos sin modificarlos, por lo que es el que se usa para consultar la lista de dispositivos desde la API de Catalyst Center.

questions.name: Diseños de red (2-tier/3-tier/fabric/cloud)
questions.question: In a traditional 3-tier campus design, which layer is primarily responsible for high-speed backbone switching between distribution blocks?

options.A: Core layer
options.B: Distribution layer
options.C: Edge layer
options.D: Access layer

questions.explanation_es: La capa core es responsable del switching troncal de alta velocidad entre los distintos bloques de distribución, sin realizar la política/agregación que corresponde a la capa de distribución.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which QoS mechanism actively drops packets before a queue becomes completely full, in order to avoid TCP global synchronization?

options.A: Weighted Random Early Detection (WRED)
options.B: Low Latency Queuing (LLQ)
options.C: Traffic shaping
options.D: Classification and marking

questions.explanation_es: WRED descarta paquetes de forma aleatoria y anticipada antes de que la cola se llene por completo, evitando la sincronización global de TCP que ocurriría si muchos flujos TCP reaccionaran al mismo tiempo a un descarte por cola llena (tail drop).

questions.name: VRF
questions.question: What does 'VRF-lite' specifically refer to, as opposed to a full MPLS VPN-based VRF deployment?

options.A: A cloud-only version of VRF available exclusively on virtual routers
options.B: A VRF implementation limited to exactly two routes per table
options.C: A VRF that only supports IPv6 addressing
options.D: Running VRFs on a router without requiring MPLS or a dedicated PE/CE architecture to exchange routes between VRFs and the rest of the network

questions.explanation_es: VRF-lite permite correr múltiples VRFs en un router sin necesitar MPLS ni una arquitectura PE/CE dedicada para intercambiar rutas entre VRFs y el resto de la red, a diferencia de un despliegue de VPN MPLS completo.
